40844.title: rbdmap: replace rbdmap with systemd unit generator
40844.author: huww98
40844.body:
Replace original rbdmap bash script with rbdmap-generator, which is a systemd unit generator that generates one rbdmap@.service for each RBD image on boot or `systemctl daemon-reload`.

This generator is written in Python3, and its behavior closely follows systemd-cryptsetup-generator(8). It is designed to be fully compatible with the original /etc/ceph/rbdmap config file.

Apart from original functions, this generator supports several new features:

* Support adding systemd unit options (e.g. x-systemd.requires=) from /etc/ceph/rbdmap config file. The design closely follows systemd-fstab-generator(8)

* Support noauto, nofail options. They have the same semantic as in systemd-cryptsetup-generator(8)

* Previous "id=admin,options='lock_on_read,queue_depth=1024'" can now be written as "id=admin,lock_on_read,queue_depth=1024", which is more nature.

We have some additional advantages compared with the original script:

* Other units may acquire dependency to a specific RBD device, may through the rbdmap@.service units, or the standard .device and blockdev@.target units.

* We do not have to deal with mount and umount in the script. The mount unit created by systemd-fstab-generator(8) will automatically pull in and wait until RBD device mapping finished.

* Furthermore, we may support on-demand RBD mapping. For example, when working with automount, the mount unit triggered by access to the mount point will in turn trigger the RBD device mapping automatically.

However, there are still some breaking changes:

* Manually invoke `rbdmap` command is not supported. They may be replaced with `systemctl start|stop rbdmap@*.service`. `rbdmap unmap-all` has no replacement.

* There is no easy way to override the config file path.

Hooks in /etc/ceph/rbd.d/ are still supported but should be considered deprecated. Administrators should use systemd unit file to deploy hooks.

Signed-off-by: 胡玮文 <huww98@outlook.com>

43859.title: librbd/crypto: don't decrypt image uninitialized data
43859.author: orozery
43859.body:
By convention, librbd returns zeros when reading uninitialized image data.
When using encryption, this convention is not guaranteed.
Specifically, this can happen when non-sparse reads are issued to the OSDs,
such in the case where the reads are smaller than `rbd_sparse_read_threshold_bytes`.
To overcome this, this commit adds a check to bypass decryption in case
the data read from the OSD is all zeros.

Signed-off-by: Or Ozeri <oro@il.ibm.com>

49761.title: rbd/config: replace ImageCtx::config with ImageConfigProxy
49761.author: pereman2
49761.body:
The following changes removes ConfigProxy from the ImageCtx in favor ImageConfigProxy. Every time a ImageCtx is created, CephContext's ConfigProxy is copied into ImageCtx cascading a copy of ConfigProxy's internal md_config_t copy. On the other hand ImageConfigProxy stores a reference to md_config_t as this instance can perform configuration operations through different ConfigValue instances. Therefore, this implementation can be thought of keeping md_config_t as a schema while `ConfigValues values` inside ImageConfigProxy stores the state of the specific ImageCtx.

After performing some tests it was visible the action of opening a file was a bottlelneck for applications who would want to open and close several images periodically to perform some actions. The following test was performed by creating, opening and closing 10k images on a pool, returning the following results:

|method|total open/close(ms steady_clock)|total create/open/close(ms)|num imag| 
|-------|----------------|---------|-|
|ImageConfigProxy|14252|39534|10000|
|ConfigProxy|50846|80182|10000|
|**diff**|**3.56x**|**2.02x**|10000|


Signed-off-by: Pere Diaz Bou <pdiazbou@redhat.com>

51326.title: [WIP] librbd: fix busy looping caused by remote request ETIMEDOUT handling logic
51326.author: pkalever
51326.body:
* librbd: notifier convert ETIMEOUT errors to EBUSY
    
Currently the local client gets ETIMEOUT errors from both notifier and
RPC, so its not possible to distinguish the notifier errors from real RPC
timeout errors and take appropriate actions in both the cases. Hence its
better to return a different error from notifier so that the local client
can now differentiate between the cause and can take necessary action.

* librbd: retry the operation which was not marked complete previously

In case if the previous operation returned a failure and is not marked
complete (i.e if error is ETIMEDOUT or ERESTART) then rather than just
retuning the previous error code again and again in a loop, retry the
operation each time.




Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/59563
Signed-off-by: Prasanna Kumar Kalever \<prasanna.kalever@redhat.com\>

51540.title: rbd_mirror: introduce a timeout for remote cluster OSD operations
51540.author: pkalever

52373.title: mds: add ceph.dir.bal.mask vxattr for MDS Balancer
52373.author: yongseokoh
52373.body:
tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/61777

**Introduction**
This PR introduces the ceph.dir.bal.mask vxattr, which is an option to rebalance a subtree within specific active MDSs. Similar to the CPU mask, this feature enables load balancing of specific directories across multiple MDS ranks. It is especially useful for fine-tuning and improving performance in various scenarios. Previously, the bal_rank_mask in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/43284 supports isolating unpinned subtrees under the root directory ('/') to a specific MDS rank. However, with this new option vxattr, it becomes possible to isolate specific subdirectories to designated MDS ranks. By introducing the ceph.dir.bal.mask vxattr, this PR empowers Ceph administrators with enhanced control and flexibility for optimizing performance and fine-tuning their deployments.

**Use Cases**
The first is when it is difficult to pin a subdir to one MDS rank. The /home/images directory exists. There are /0 to /99 directories under it, and 10 million image files are stored in each directory. In this case, it is difficult to pin the entire images directory to one MDS rank. Also, pinning the huge 100 directories manually or using ephemeral pinning is not an easy task. Therefore, efficient resource management is possible by using ceph.dir.bal.mask.

Second, when there are several large directories such as /home/images, performance can be optimized by distributing them to different MDS rank groups using ceph.dir.bal.mask. Since the existing mdsmap’s bal_rank_mask isolated the entire ‘/’ directory to specific ranks, it can affect performance due to each other's migration overhead. For example, mdsmap’s bal_rank_mask is set to 0xf and /home/images and /home/backups large directories exist. If the load on /home/images instantaneously increases, metadata distribution occurs across ranks 0 to 3. Thus, users of /home/backups may be affected by noisy neighbors unnecessarily. If the two directories are set to MDS rank 0-1 (ceph.dir.bal.mask 0x3) and 2-3 (ceph.dir.bal.mask 0xC) respectively, the effect on each other can be minimized. Like this, it can be used efficiently for various directories.

**How to use**
```
# / root is distributed within MDS rank 0 to 3
# it overrides mdsmap bal_rank_mask value
setfattr -n ceph.dir.bal.mask -v 0x0f /

# /home/images subdir is distributed within MDS rank 1 and 2
setfattr -n ceph.dir.bal.mask -v 0x06 /home/images

# /home/images subdir is distributed within MDS rank 3 and 4
setfattr -n ceph.dir.bal.mask -v 0x18 /home/backups

# remove values and they will obey parent the value or mdsmap bal_rank_mask
setfattr -n ceph.dir.bal.mask -v -1 /home/images
setfattr -n ceph.dir.bal.mask -v -1 /home/backups

# /home/images is placed only on MDS rank1 (similar to ceph.dir.dir)
setfattr -n ceph.dir.bal.mask -v 0x02 /home/images
```

60137.title: rgw: cls_timeindex: avoid dup ext key (object name) indexes
60137.author: trociny
60137.body:
The object expirer gets an expiration hint (a cls_timeindex entry keyed by
the expiration time and the object name) every time X-Delete-At/After is set
on an object. Updating it adds a new hint but leaves the old one, so stale
hints pile up in the `obj_delete_at_hint.*` omap.

Originally a stale hint was harmless: the expirer passed `hint.exp_time` to
`RGWRados::delete_obj()`, which returned `-ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED` unless the
object's delete_at still matched. That check was lost in the zipper conversion
(72d1a363263, pacific), so on reef/squid the object is deleted at the
*earliest* time ever set (this tracker). On main and tentacle,
`RadosObject::handle_obj_expiry()` checks `is_expired()` before deleting
(0e0222d0162), so the early deletion no longer happens there, but the stale
hints still accumulate and each one costs a head object read when processed.

This PR makes the ext key (object name) unique in cls_timeindex: an ext index
`2_<key_ext>` -> time index is maintained, and adding an entry for an existing
key_ext removes the old one. Trim removes the ext index only if it still points
to the trimmed entry, so entries left over from before the upgrade (no ext
index) don't break tracking of the newer ones; such legacy entries are cleaned
up when their time comes, as before.

For reef/squid a separate, rgw-only fix (restoring the `expiration_time`
precondition in `garbage_single_object()`) is proposed, as it does not
depend on the OSDs being upgraded.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68380

60490.title: Include cleanup: reduce header bloat
60490.author: MaxKellermann
60490.body:
This is a continuation of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/60253 (and contains many of its commits). It is a demonstration of what can be done do reduce header bloat.
Ceph build times are painfully slow and each compilation unit takes about 2 GB RAM, which means parallel builds require excessive amounts of CPU and RAM. This is because the header dependency tree is very large.
This draft PR shows a few ideas how to improve this:
- include only headers that are needed
- split headers so includers can decide what parts they need
- un-inline functions/methods so their dependencies don't need to be included in the public header and the compiler doesn't need to generate code in each compilation unit that includes the header

Prior to this PR a clean build of `ceph-mds`:
```
3657.90user 222.19system 2:46.14elapsed 2335%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 3838844maxresident)k
0inputs+0outputs (24major+81216038minor)pagefaults 0swaps

 Performance counter stats for 'time ninja -C build/debug ceph-mds':

      3,891,960.89 msec task-clock:u                     #   23.424 CPUs utilized             
                 0      context-switches:u               #    0.000 /sec                      
                 0      cpu-migrations:u                 #    0.000 /sec                      
        81,140,096      page-faults:u                    #   20.848 K/sec                     
 9,183,874,937,949      cycles:u                         #    2.360 GHz                       
 9,098,969,848,371      instructions:u                   #    0.99  insn per cycle            
 2,021,603,305,694      branches:u                       #  519.431 M/sec                     
    53,365,675,475      branch-misses:u                  #    2.64% of all branches           

     166.151033259 seconds time elapsed

    3657.906470000 seconds user
     222.190450000 seconds sys
```
After this PR:
```
2621.21user 152.68system 2:05.10elapsed 2217%CPU (0avgtext+0avgdata 3271296maxresident)k
0inputs+0outputs (0major+56495236minor)pagefaults 0swaps

 Performance counter stats for 'time ninja -C build/debug -k50 ceph-mds':

      2,784,514.32 msec task-clock:u                     #   22.258 CPUs utilized             
                 0      context-switches:u               #    0.000 /sec

        56,476,974      page-faults:u                    #   20.283 K/sec                     
 6,628,349,851,908      cycles:u                         #    2.380 GHz

    41,054,543,018      branch-misses:u                  #    2.83% of all branches           

     125.103906411 seconds time elapsed

    2621.212510000 seconds user
     152.683572000 seconds sys
```
This is a speedup of 28%, and much more can be done (still a lot of header bloat, and type erasure might also help a lot).

Note that this is a quick'n'dirty draft PR. Only `ceph-mds` builds and all other executables will fail, some due to pre-existing bugs because includes were missing, others because I didn't adapt to splitted headers yet.

61126.title: MonClient: Add auxiliary connections and enhance quorum handling
61126.author: NitzanMordhai
61126.body:
This commit introduces auxiliary connections (aux_list) in MonClient
to improve the robustness of monitor connectivity and quorum detection.

Key changes:
 * Added support for multiple auxiliary connections, enabling MonClient
   to fetch MonMaps and validate quorum status independently of the active connection.
 * Improved handling of half-dead monitors (monitors that appear responsive but are
   out of quorum) by leveraging auxiliary connections to verify their quorum state.
 * Subscribed to quorum change events, ensuring prompt updates and better cluster responsiveness.
 * Transitioned from relying on a single active connection to utilizing multiple monitor connections,
   reducing the risk of cluster misbehavior due to a faulty monitor.

These changes address scenarios where a half-dead monitor caused disruptions and make MonClient more
resilient in dynamic cluster environments by not relay just on active
connection.

61140.title: rgw: allow controlling chain data replication
61140.author: clwluvw
61140.body:
When chain replication is enabled, an object that has been replicated to a destination zone can be further replicated to other zones. Disabling this option prevents chain replication, avoiding potential performance issues and redundant logging caused by circular replication patterns between zones. This can be useful in scenarios where chain replication is unnecessary or undesirable for optimizing sync operations.

Introduced a new zonegroup feature called "data-sync-disable-chain-replication" to disable this type of replication for the new deployments. Currently AWS also doesn't support such a replication: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-what-is-isnot-replicated.html

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/69310

61202.title: common: migrate ceph_json to Glaze
61202.author: chardan
61202.body:
common: ceph_json: migrate backend from spirit_json to boost.json

This PR replaces the spirit_json backend with Glaze's implementation, as well providing 
various code cleanups and updates. Adds support for some common use-cases of parse(), such
as string_view.

Observed large speedup on JSON read-heavy paths while keeping the existing JSONObj compatibility surface intact. In release microbenchmarks against main, parse/tree-walk cases improved by roughly 5.3x-8.0x, array traversal by 6.8x-7.6x, and combined encode/decode by about 4.3x. Pure encode paths were essentially unchanged; this migration buys much faster parsing without trading away write-side performance.

I do believe this is a very worthwhile project, as in addition to greatly consolidating the implementation we see observable effects when going through the extant API:

Compatibility API
```
case                         speedup vs. baseline

parse_tree/8                 7.96x
find_nested_scalar/8         7.99x
decode_rows/8                6.18x
array_elements/8             7.64x
encode_rows/8                1.00x
encode_decode_rows/8         4.30x
parse_tree/128               7.49x
find_nested_scalar/128       7.19x
decode_rows/128              5.28x
array_elements/128           6.76x
encode_rows/128              1.03x
encode_decode_rows/128       4.31x
```

But I've long maintained that the design of ceph_json's API is an inherent hindrance. I decided to extend local entry points directly into the back-end as revisiting all of this requires considerable effort. While migrating some of the call sites belongs to another project, I did go for some of the lower-hanging fruit, and as an enticement:

Direct API
```
case                         speedup vs. baseline

OPA result bool              47.17x
Keystone nested secret       32.32x
cephfs mirror notify         28.05x
Swift ACL string arrays      22.97x
JWKS keys traversal          58.73x
PG stats array traversal     63.09x
```

I am of course happy to provide benchmarking code and methodology.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74810

61862.title: rgw: add multisite configuration for cross-zonegroup replication
61862.author: cbodley
61862.body:
# realm default and zonegroup overrides

defines the configuration for cross-zonegroup replication at the realm and zonegroup level. the default behavior is set by the realm, and individual zonegroups can override this to enable/disable cross-zonegroup replication to/from other zonegroups

# opt-in vs opt-out

the realm configuration supports three models:
* opt-out model where cross-zonegroup replication is "enabled" in the realm but "forbidden" for specific zonegroup pairs
* opt-in model where replication is "allowed" in the realm but only "enabled" for specific zonegroup pairs
* no cross-zonegroup replication when "forbidden" by the realm

the realm uses a tristate `enum CanSync` to represent the default, while the zonegroup uses two sets ("enable" and "forbid") to represent the overrides

# import vs export

zonegroups can override the realm behavior both for import and export. while this can duplicate information (that is, disabling A's import from B is the same as disabling B's export to A), one form will generally be simpler than the other. for example, consider a realm with zonegroups A, B, C with cross-zonegroup replication disabled to/from C. to represent this with imports only:
```
realm:
  "cross_zonegroup": "enabled"
zonegroup A:
  "cross_zonegroup_import": { "forbid": {"C"} }
zonegroup B:
  "cross_zonegroup_import": { "forbid": {"C"} }
zonegroup C:
  "cross_zonegroup_import": { "forbid": {"A", "B"} }
```
using both imports and exports, the configuration can be localized to zonegroup C:
```
realm:
  "cross_zonegroup": "enabled"
zonegroup C:
  "cross_zonegroup_export": { "forbid": {"A", "B"} },
  "cross_zonegroup_import": { "forbid": {"A", "B"} }
```

# wildcards

the wildcard string "*" can be used to match all peers, allowing the example above to be simplified as `"forbid": {"*"}`. but more importantly, wildcards adapt as zonegroups are added/removed from the realm. so if another zonegroup D is added to the realm above, that use of wildcards would automatically disable its replication to/from C

# TODO:
- [x] add similar configuration for same_zonegroup replication policy
- [x] radosgw-admin commands to modify this configuration

62599.title: [DNM] rgw: bucket snapshots
62599.author: yehudasa
62599.body:
This PR implements RGW bucket snapshots.

The RGW bucket snapshots provides an integrated snapshot mechanism that leverages the S3 object versioning system. 

Functionality:

New operations:
 - Enable snapshots on bucket
 - Create snapshot
 - Delete snapshot (partially implemented)
 - List snapshots
 - List objects (snapshot range)

A snapshot has a name and an ID. The name is user-defined, and needs to be unique, and the ID is defined by the system and is monotonically increasing.

When accessing an object, if a snapshot-id is provided, the object that is returned is the object instance that belongs to this snapshot-id. If the object did not exist when this snapshot was created (as in: never existed, or existed prior but was removed), an does-not-exist error is returned.

Listing buckets is extended to support snapshot (or snapshot ranges -- as in snapshot diffs). When a snapshot id is provided, the system will return only the object instances that are new in that snapshot (that is: didn't exist in the previous snapshot, but do exist in this snapshot).
A snapshot-range operation provides a snapshot diff operation: shows all the objects that didn't exist in the first snapshot, and exist in the second snapshot.
These listings also show which objects existed, but were removed in the specified range.
If the first snapshot in the range is not specified, the system will return the view of the bucket as it existed when the
specified (as in the second) snapshot was taken.

The system can also return the stats for any snapshot: how many objects and total size of objects that were created in the snapshot, and what are the number of objects and their total size that existed when this snapshot existed. 

New REST APIs have been created in order to support the new functionality, and boto extensions were defined for these APIs.

As it is implemented now the feature is zone-local, and is not visible to multisite.

Some considerations:

Buckets maintain a snapshot manager that keeps track of the existing snapshots. Every object instance created is assigned with the next snapshot ID.
~~When snapshots are enabled on a bucket, the bucket (if not versioned) is being set as version-suspended.~~
A new bucket state is added to signify a "versioned index", which is separate from the bucket versioned state. So a bucket can be at a versioned-disabled state (as is: has never been set to versioned), but the index itself can be versioned-enabled, which is needed in order for this feature. Note that currently the feature is only implemented for the RADOS backend.
The `rgw_obj_key` now has a new snapshot-id field. This allows creating multiple null-versioned objects with the same name (but different snapshot-ids).
Currently, the snapshot-id on the key is set only if the object has a null version. That is not to say that versioned objects are not snapshotted. The key itself (as it is now), is only used to locate the object instance and to identify, and for versioned objects the object instance id (version-id) is enough. We don't add the snapshot-id to the object key in the versioned case because if we did, we'd need to always go through the olh in order to be able to access the objects.
The object metadata has a new snap_id field that is used to determine to which snapshot the object belongs to.

As it is implemented currently, listing does a naive filtering in order to show objects that belong to the requested snapshots range (whether one is specified or not). This means that the different listing and diff operations iterate over all the object instances in the bucket. Bucket sharding is still in effect, so this is not different than regular listing, other than that the returned number of objects may very well be less than all the objects in the bucket. There are optimizations that can be done, but these are left to be done as a follow-up work.

63527.title: blk/spdk/NVMEDevice.cc: apply pci_whitelist only for PCIe transports
63527.author: next0262
63527.body:
## Fix SPDK NVMe Probe Misclassification for TCP Transport in Ceph OSD Startup

When running Ceph OSD with SPDK NVMe-oF over TCP using the following `vstart.sh` configuration:

```
../src/vstart.sh --debug --new -x --localhost --bluestore \
--bluestore-spdk "trtype:tcp adrfam:IPv4 traddr:127.0.0.1 trsvcid:4420 subnqn:nqn.2019-02.io.spdk:cnode0,\
trtype:tcp adrfam:IPv4 traddr:127.0.0.1 trsvcid:4420 subnqn:nqn.2019-02.io.spdk:cnode1,\
trtype:tcp adrfam:IPv4 traddr:127.0.0.1 trsvcid:4420 subnqn:nqn.2019-02.io.spdk:cnode2"
```

i got error from osds :

```
2025-05-25T06:10:07.459+0000 7f552e7fdf40 -1 bdev() open failed to get nvme device with transport address 127.0.0.1 type 3
2025-05-25T06:10:07.459+0000 7f552e7fdf40 -1 bluestore(/app/build/dev/osd0) mkfs failed, (1) Operation not permitted
2025-05-25T06:10:07.459+0000 7f552e7fdf40 -1 OSD::mkfs: ObjectStore::mkfs failed with error (1) Operation not permitted
2025-05-25T06:10:07.459+0000 7f552e7fdf40 -1 ERROR: error creating empty object store in /app/build/dev/osd0: (1) Operation not permitted
```

The code incorrectly sets local_pci_device = true for a TCP transport address (127.0.0.1) due to this logic:

```
bool local_pci_device = false;
int rc = spdk_pci_addr_parse(&addr, trid.traddr);
if (!rc) {
  local_pci_device = true;
  opts.pci_whitelist = &addr;
  opts.num_pci_addr = 1;
}

```
spdk_pci_addr_parse() does not validate whether the transport is actually PCIe or not. This causes spdk_nvme_probe() to be called with NULL for the first argument even in TCP mode:

`r = spdk_nvme_probe(local_pci_device ? NULL : &trid, ctxt, probe_cb, attach_cb, NULL);`

To ensure correct behavior, the following change was introduced:

```
if (trid.trtype == SPDK_NVME_TRANSPORT_PCIE) {
  // Only classify as local PCIe device if the transport is actually PCIe
  int rc = spdk_pci_addr_parse(&addr, trid.traddr);
  if (!rc) {
    local_pci_device = true;
    opts.pci_whitelist = &addr;
    opts.num_pci_addr = 1;
  }
}

```
This guards against misclassifying TCP transports as local PCIe devices, and ensures that spdk_nvme_probe() is invoked correctly for TCP configurations.

With this fix, the Ceph OSDs bring up successfully as expected.

```
$ ./bin/ceph -s
cluster:
  id: 56e8c6d7-c426-487e-9a09-101ac4c09ab7
  health: HEALTH_OK

services:
  mon: 3 daemons, quorum a,b,c
  mgr: x(active)
  mds: 1/1 daemons up, 2 standby
  osd: 3 osds: 3 up, 3 in

data:
  volumes: 1/1 healthy
  pools: 3 pools, 145 pgs
  objects: 24 objects, 451 KiB
  usage: 82 MiB used, 2.9 GiB / 3 GiB avail
  pgs: 145 active+clean
```

64427.title: mgr/cephadm: unset MON flag during upgrade
64427.author: shraddhaag
64427.body:
This PR unsets the specified mon flags before an upgrade starts and sets them after an upgrade. This will be used to disable availability tracking before an upgrade and enable it again after the upgrade is complete. The code is written in an extensible way, such that any further usecases will only have to make a single line change to achieve the same. 

Scenarios handled: 


|Type|Resolution|
|-----|-----------|
| Full upgrade | flag unset before upgrade; flag reset after upgrade. |
|Staggered upgrade| flag unset and reset for each upgrade step triggered by user.|
|Upgrade stopped by user manually using `ceph orch upgrade stop`| flag is reset before command exits|
|Upgrade fails| flag is reset before command exits|

64435.title: [AGENT OPTIMIZATION] mgr/cephadm: Add load distribution and compression for agent metadata
64435.author: rkachach
64435.body:
Fixes https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77958

Based on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/64278

## Enhancements to Prevent Spikes in Cephadm Agent Metadata Reporting

This PR introduces several improvements to the Cephadm Agent to make metadata reporting more efficient, scalable, and customizable. In large clusters, synchronized reporting can cause traffic spikes and overload the cephadm module and hence the ceph-manager. To address this, the agent now uses adaptive logic to automatically determine reporting intervals (`agent_refresh_rate`), jitter windows, and startup delays based on cluster size. These enhancements help smooth network load, reduce reporting bursts, and improve overall scalability.

In addition this PR adds support for optional compression of Cephadm Agent metadata payloads to reduce bandwidth consumption. This is especially beneficial in large clusters where frequent metadata reporting can result in significant network overhead.  

Testing has shown that enabling compression yields a reduction of over 80% in payload size, significantly improving efficiency without impacting functionality.


### Motivation
Static refresh rates and missing jitter logic previously led to uneven traffic and potential burstiness, especially during agent restarts or in large clusters. This change introduces a more scalable, self-tuning model that adjusts automatically to the cluster size.

### Key Enhancements

- **Automatic refresh rate**: User now can use automatic refresh rate calculation adjusting the behavior to the cluster size.
- **Smarter Jittering**: Agents now support jitter mechanism to spread metadata sending over time, reducing bursts.
- **Configurable Startup Behavior**: Agents can be configured with randomized startup delays to avoid startup bursts.

### Jitter calculation key Changes
- Automatically derive `avg_concurrency` as `sqrt(N)/2`  with a minimum of 2 agents/sec.
- Dynamically compute `agent_refresh_rate` based on `num_agents // avg_concurrency`, with a minimum of 20s.
- Set jitter to 50% of the refresh rate to evenly spread metadata reports across time.
- Apply the same heuristic to the startup delay to avoid initial burst load.

### Theoretical Behavior

Agent metadata activity follows a [binomial](https://randombooks.org/the-binomial-distribution.html) concurrency model, where each of the `N` agents is independently active with probability `p = D / T` at any given moment, where:

- `N`: Number of agents  
- `D`: Average task duration (seconds)  
- `T`: Agent refresh interval (seconds)  

The expected number of concurrent agents is:

`μ = N × (D / T)`

The 99th percentile can be used to estimate the maximum concurrency as following:

`P99 ≈ μ + 2.33 × sqrt(N × p × (1 - p))`

Simulation confirm that this model provides a reliable upper bound for burst behavior, with observed peaks consistently less than **< 2×Average** when number of agents is higher than 100. This enables safe, efficient provisioning without requiring significant over-provisioning.

With the new (default) configuration, we get the following numbers for `D = 2sec`:

| Num Agents | Avg Concurrency Heuristic | Refresh Rate (s) | Expected Avg Concurrency | Std Dev | Max Estimated Concurrency (P99) | P99 / Avg Ratio |
|------------|----------------------------|------------------|---------------------------|---------|---------------------------|------------------|
| 10         | 2                          | 20               | 1.00                      | 0.95    | 3.21                      | 3.21             |
| 50         | 3                          | 34               | 2.94                      | 1.62    | 6.72                      | 2.29             |
| 100        | 5                          | 40               | 5.00                      | 2.18    | 10.08                     | 2.02             |
| 200        | 7                          | 57               | 7.02                      | 2.38

65360.title: os/bluestore: Reshuffle Objects in class BlueStore into namespace bluestore
65360.author: Jayaprakash-ibm
65360.body:
Refactors BlueStore internals by moving `struct Blob`, `struct Onode`, `struct ExtentMap`, `struct Extent` `struct SharedBlob` and related helpers from the `class BlueStore` into the `namespace bluestore`.

Currently, several BlueStore primitives are defined as nested types inside class BlueStore.

This creates unnecessary coupling between the objects and the BlueStore class. As more functionality is added around BlueStore, this can make it harder to:

- reuse BlueStore primitives from other components
- break circular dependencies
- extend BlueStore without increasing the size and complexity of BlueStore.h
- understand and navigate deeply nested definitions.

The reshuffle is intended to provide a cleaner separation between the BlueStore implementation and its core data structures.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80442

65747.title: osd: Optimized EC missing list not updated on recovering shard
65747.author: bill-scales
65747.body:
Shards that are recovering (last_complete != last_update) are using pwlc to advance last_update for writes that did not effect the shard. However simply incrementing last_update means that the primary doesnt send the shard log entries that it missed and consequently it cannot update its missing list.

If the shard is already missing object X at version V1 and there was a partial write at V2 that did not update the shard, it does not need to retain the log entry, but it does need to update the missing list to say it needs V2 rather than V1. This ensures all shards report a need for an object at the same version and avoids an assert in MissingLoc::add_active_missing when the primary is trying to combine the missing lists from all the shards to work out what has to be recovered.

The fix is to avoid applying pwlc when last_complete != last_update, this forces the primary to send the log to the recovering shard which can then update its missing list (and discarding the log entries as they are partial writes).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73249

65815.title: mgr/cephadm: Prevent verbose asyncssh logging unless DEBUG is enabled
65815.author: pdvian
65815.body:
The redirect_log was previously configured to unconditionally capture
the asyncssh log content (log_string.getvalue()) and include it in
exception messages whenever a connection failed.

This caused verbose, low-level connection logging to be included in
exception output, even when the primary orchestrator log level was
set to `INFO` or `WARNING`. This made ceph cluster logs noisy,
often triggering frequent mon elections.

This commit makes two changes:
1.  Explicitly sets the asyncssh_logger level within the redirect_log
context manager using the new asyncssh_log_level module option.
2.  The verbose log_content is now only extracted from the StringIO
stream and appended to the final exception message if the effective
log level of the asyncssh logger is set to INFO.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73381

Signed-off-by: Prashant D <pdhange@redhat.com>

66061.title: cephadm: uca prototype
66061.author: phlogistonjohn
66061.body:
## What's uca?

uca is a tool that brings some of cephadm's capabilities to systems
that are not part of a ceph cluster. The goal is run certain commands
and automation without having to ssh into a ceph cluster (admin) node
first.

At present the command supports a shell subcommand that works similar
to `cephadm shell`. It also has a direct wrapper for `ceph` command line
tool similar to `cephadm shell ceph ...` but with a few additional
abilities.

## What's uca mean?

Naming is hard. I had to call it something.
* uca could stand for "Userspace Ceph Admin"
* uca could stand for "micro ceph admin" (yeah yeah u ain't micro)
* uca could stand for "Uncanny Cephadm Approximate"

Choose one you like or suggest your own. The name is also not set in
stone yet anyway.

## Why?

For a while (~2 years or so) I have wanted a tool like this. In my
previous experience working on k8s systems I always appreciated
that I could run `kubectl` or `oc` on my system to issue commands
and submit resources to the cluster. It's just a matter of having
the right keys and the ability to send packets to the API really.

At some point it dawned on me that the same is true of Ceph. Ceph
has cephx keys and APIs (rados). The tooling is a bit different,
a bit more "dispersed" but the Ceph project already packages things
in to containers and cephadm already knows how to execute those
containers in a way that allows you to manage the ceph cluster.

## How's it work?

uca is basically a very stripped down version of cephadm. It shares
the libraries cephadm uses but it is limited to running commands
that make sense outside of a ceph node, so no systems management
stuff. But the containers, yeah, we can do that.

Unlike cephadm, uca is designed to work with multiple ceph clusters.
The `uca cluster ...` subcommands allow one to list, add, remove, etc
clusters. You can mark a cluster as default to make uca commands
use that cluster without additional arguments.

Do note that it requires "line of sight" to the Ceph cluster you
want to manage, as the tools within the container will need to
connect to rados/the mons in the ceph cluster.

## Who can use it?

I designed it for my own use cases and have been using it on and off for
a couple of months now. Consider it developer-pre-preview.

Eventually, I see it useful for both developers as well as ceph cluster
admins. Imagine issuing commands from your laptop based on yaml
files stored in a git repo instead of having to copy them to an admin
node first.

## How do I get started?

If you want to give it a whirl you need to build it manually at
the moment. Run:
```
./src/cephadm/build.py --main-script uca.py  /tmp/uca
```
and it will produce a python "zipapp" at /tmp/uca. Run
```
/tmp/uca -h
```
to see the help.

To initialize a cluster config from a host you can ssh into, run:
```
/tmp/uca cluster ssh-init --make-default  root@my.host.example.com
```
(see the help for other params)

You can also manually initialize a cluster using `uca cluster init`
and providing it with config and keyring files.

Now, as an example, run:
```
/tmp/uca ceph status
```
Or perhaps:
```
/tmp/uca ceph orch ls
```

You can enter the shell and use additional tools, like `rados` for
example:
```
$ /tmp/uca shell
[...]# rados lspools
cephfs.cephfs.meta
cephfs.cephfs.data
.mgr
.smb
```

Have fun!

66231.title: [WIP] src/script: add script to store pool availability status
66231.author: shraddhaag
66231.body:
This commit adds a script, pool-status-check.sh, to enable testing of the data availability feature. The script specifically stores the ceph status output and pool's data availability output in a log file every 10 mins to a log file. This log file can be used to analyse the reliability of the feature. The script ensures multiple instances of the same script are not run.

Before running the script make sure it has appropriate permissions: 
```
chmod u+rwx pool_status_check.sh
```

Command to run the script such that the terminal is not blocked and losing SSH connection will not interrupt the script:

```
nohup ./pool_status_check.sh &
```

Command to stop the script:
```
./pool_status_check.sh --stop
```
Output: 
```
[root@ceph-node-0 ~]# cat nohup.out 
Script already running (PID 1215533). Exiting.
[root@ceph-node-0 ~]# ./pool_status_check.sh --stop
Stopping ceph_pool_status process with PID 1215533...
Stopped.
[1]+  Terminated              nohup ./pool_status_check.sh
[root@ceph-node-0 ~]# ll /var/log/ceph_pool_status/
total 4
```

Each entry in the log file will look like this:

66446.title: pybind/rbd: fix Python 3.12+ sub-interpreter crashes in callbacks
66446.author: tchaikov
66446.body:
Python 3.12+ introduced significant changes to sub-interpreter isolation
which cause crashes when callbacks are invoked from C code in a different
interpreter context than where the callback was created. This affects both
progress callbacks and AIO oncomplete callbacks when used in ceph-mgr's
rbd_support module, which runs in a sub-interpreter.

This patch implements a CallbackWrapper that uses PyThreadState_Swap() to
switch to the correct interpreter context when callbacks are invoked:

Implementation:
- Captures the interpreter state when callback is created (in Python code)
- Switches to that interpreter when callback is invoked (from C code)
- Switches back to the original interpreter after callback completes
- Optimized: skips swap if callback invoked in same interpreter (25% faster)
- Generic: single wrapper class handles all callback types (*args, **kwargs)
- Zero overhead on Python < 3.12 (no wrapping needed)

The wrapper automatically fixes:

Progress callbacks (6 sites):
- RBD.remove()
- RBD.trash_remove()
- RBD.migration_execute()
- RBD.migration_commit()
- RBD.migration_abort()
- Image.flatten()

AIO oncomplete callbacks (all AIO methods):
- RBD.aio_open_image()
- Image.aio_close()
- Image.aio_read/write/discard/write_zeroes/flush()
- Image.aio_mirror_image_create_snapshot()
- Image.aio_mirror_image_get_info()
- Image.aio_mirror_image_get_mode()

Benefits:
- Fixes crashes in ceph-mgr rbd_support module on Python 3.12+
- Minimal overhead: 0.037 µs per callback invocation

Benchmark results (10,000 callback invocations, Python 3.13):
- With optimization: 0.374 ms (0.037 µs per call)
- Without optimization: 0.502 ms (0.050 µs per call)
- Improvement: -25.4%

Real-world overhead remains negligible:
- Image flatten (100 callbacks): ~0.004 ms
- Migration (200 callbacks): ~0.007 ms
- Bulk AIO (1000 ops): ~0.037 ms

Refs: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73930
Refs: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73857
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72713

66573.title: tracing/eBPF: add radostrace for dynamic RADOS client tracing
66573.author: taodd
66573.body:
This is the initial PR to integrate the cephtrace into ceph source tree, enabling Ceph to take advantage of the capabilities of eBPF.
I presented some real production examples and a demo, showing the value we are already getting from the tools in cephalocon2025, you can find the  details at:
https://cephalocon2025.sched.com/event/27f3z/efficient-ceph-performance-troubleshooting-in-production-using-ebpf-dongdong-tao-canonical
and cephtrace project details at https://github.com/taodd/cephtrace

As the first step, this PR introduces radostrace, an eBPF-based tracing tool that provides real-time visibility into RADOS client operations. radostrace attaches dynamically to any running librados-based client (QEMU/RBD, cinder/glance, RGW, cephfs-mirror, etc.) with low-overhead. It also establishes eBPF infrastructure in Ceph that can be extended to trace OSD operations, BlueStore internals, MDS operations, and more. (I plan to send follow-up PRs to introduce osdtrace, kfstrace once this is merged)

  **Key features:**
  - Captures per-operation latency, object names, pool/PG, target OSDs, operation types, and extent info
  - Uses uprobes on `Objecter::_send_op` and `Objecter::_finish_op` - no code modification needed
  - DWARF parser extracts struct offsets at runtime, works with any Ceph build
  - Production-safe: eBPF programs are kernel-verified before execution
  - Requires Linux kernel 5.8+ (for BPF ring buffer support)

  **Example output:**
```
          pid     client     tid  pool   pg           acting          WR    size    latency        object[ops]
          12345   1234       1     2   f2           [1,4,7]          W    4096      892         rbd_data.1a2b3c.0000000000000001 [write][0, 4096]
```

  ## Changes

  1. **tracing/eBPF**: Core implementation
     - `radostrace.bpf.c`: eBPF program for uprobe attachment
     - `radostrace.cc`: Userspace loader, DWARF parsing, output formatting
     - `dwarf_parser.cc/h`: Extracts function addresses and struct member offsets from debug info
     - `bpf_utils.h`, `bpf_ceph_types.h`: BPF helper utilities and type definitions
     - Includes libbpf and bpftool as submodules

  2. **doc/dev/radostrace.rst**: Documentation covering usage, output format, and architecture

  3. **qa/standalone/tracing/radostrace.sh**: Integration tests for the tool

  ## Build

  Enabled by default with `WITH_=ON`:
  ```bash
  ./do_cmake.sh
  cd build && ninja radostrace
  sudo ./bin/radostrace

  Test plan

  - ninja radostrace builds successfully
  - ./bin/radostrace --help shows usage
  - sudo ./bin/radostrace traces RADOS operations from rados bench or rbd bench
  - qa/standalone/tracing/radostrace.sh tests pass
  - Verified on x86_64 (arm64 support included but untested, planning to test it soon, and will update it here)

66716.title: bluestore: add support for multi-stream SSDs(such as FDP SSDs)
66716.author: Cici-Lii
66716.body:
This patch introduces a new feature enabling Ceph to use multi-stream devices (e.g., FDP SSDs) for data storage.
The Linux kernel now supports data lifetime hints via the i_write_hint field in inode structure.
We modified the CephFS kernel client to pass these hints from the kernel and transmit them over the network to the Ceph server.
The CephFS kernel client patch will be submitted later, in alignment with Linux kernel requirements.
This patch updates the Ceph server to accept data lifetime hints from the network and use them to guide data placement on multi-stream devices (e.g., FDP SSDs).
As a result:
Data with different lifetime hints are stored in different regions of the multi-stream device.
Data with same lifetime hints are stored in same regions.
This feature reduces SSD garbage collection (GC) pressure, lowers write amplification, and improves device endurence.

66768.title: mds: add tracing infrastructure and basic flows
66768.author: salieri11
66768.body:
## MDS Request Tracing Infrastructure

### Summary

This PR implements a hierarchical request tracing infrastructure for the MDS, enabling detailed performance analysis of client request processing. When OpenTelemetry tracing is enabled, the MDS captures timing information for each phase of request handling and makes it available via a new admin socket command.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73701

### Features

- **Hierarchical Span Tracing**: Captures nested function call timing with parent-child relationships
- **Async Span Support**: Properly tracks asynchronous operations (like journal commits) that outlive their parent spans
- **Sliding Window Storage**: Maintains recent traces in memory with configurable retention window
- **Clear-on-Dump Semantics**: Traces are atomically extracted and cleared when dumped, preventing memory growth
- **OTEL Span ID Compatibility**: Uses OpenTelemetry span IDs for Jaeger correlation

### Usage

Dump traces via admin socket:

`ceph daemon mds.<name> trace dump`

**NOTE: after each dump, traces are completely pruned, please remember to save the dump output!**

### Configuration

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `jaeger_tracing_enable` | `false` | Enable OpenTelemetry tracing (required for trace generation) |
| `mds_trace_sliding_window_sec` | `10` | Trace retention window in seconds (1-30) |

### Example Output
```json
{
    "trace_id": "89a470995cd418dad345a74a78357005",
    "name": "mds:client_request",
    "start_time": "2025-12-10T18:07:08.496362+0000",
    "end_time": "2025-12-10T18:07:09.932454+0000",
    "duration_ms": 1436.09,
    "result": 0,
    "attributes": {
        "mds.client_id": "4158",
        "mds.op_name": "unlink",
        "mds.reqid": "client.4158:37",
        "mds.path": "myfile"
    },
    "spans": [
        {
            "span_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
            "parent_span_id": "",
            "name": "handle_unlink",
            "start_time": "2025-12-10T18:07:08.496713+0000",
            "end_time": "2025-12-10T18:07:08.500989+0000",
            "duration_ms": 4.28
        },
        {
            "span_id": "f6e5d4c3b2a1",
            "parent_span_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
            "name": "path_traverse",
            "duration_ms": 0.58
        },
        {
            "span_id": "112233445566",
            "parent_span_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
            "name": "journal_wait",
            "duration_ms": 1430.5,
            "async": true
        }
    ]
}
```
### Instrumented Operations

**Request Handlers** (`Server.cc`):
- `handle_client_getattr`, `handle_client_lookup_ino`, `handle_client_open`
- `handle_client_openc`, `handle_client_readdir`, `handle_client_file_setlock`
- `handle_client_file_readlock`, `handle_client_setattr`, `handle_client_setlayout`
- `handle_client_setxattr`, `handle_client_removexattr`, `handle_client_fsync`
- `handle_client_mknod`, `handle_client_mkdir`, `handle_client_symlink`
- `handle_client_link`, `handle_client_unlink`, `handle_client_rmdir`
- `handle_client_rename`, `handle_client_lssnap`, `handle_client_mksnap`
- `handle_client_rmsnap`, `handle_client_renamesnap`, `handle_client_readdir_snapdiff`

**Path & Lock Operations** (`MDCache.cc`, `Locker.cc`):
- `path_traverse`, `rdlock_path_xlock_dentry`, `rdlock_two_paths_xlock_destdn`
- `acquire_locks`, `rdlock_snap_layout`, `create_lock_cache`

**Other Operations**:
- `cap_release`, `prepare_stray_dentry`, `issue_lease`, `journal_wait` (async)

New test class `TestMDSTrace` in `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_misc.py`:

66866.title: rgw/keystone: enforce application credential access rules in Swift auth
66866.author: senolcolak
66866.body:
## Summary

Enforce Keystone application credential access rules for Swift authentication and align RGW behavior with current Keystone and keystonemiddleware semantics.

This PR now consolidates the access-rule enforcement and configuration scope discussed in #67721.

## Implementation

- Negotiates access rules with Keystone using `OpenStack-Identity-Access-Rules: 1.0`.
- Parses rules from `application_credential.access_rules`, preserving the distinction between an absent field and a present-but-empty rule list.
- Matches accepted service type, HTTP method, and request path using keystonemiddleware-compatible path semantics.
- Validates that a matching service type is present in the validated token service catalog.
- Enforces rules consistently on Keystone validation and token-cache paths.
- Validates access rules before the service-token authorization bypass is considered.
- Returns `401 Unauthorized` when access-rule validation fails, matching keystonemiddleware invalid-token behavior.
- Adds startup-only `rgw_keystone_verify_access_rules` and `rgw_keystone_accepted_service_types` options. Enforcement defaults to enabled and the accepted service type defaults to `object-store`.
- Documents configuration, behavior, empty-rule semantics, and restart requirements.

## Tests

- Extends C++ unit coverage for access-rule parsing and matching.
- Adds fake-Keystone protocol and RGW workunit coverage for negotiation, cache hits and misses, service catalog validation, empty and absent rules, service-token behavior, and configurable accepted service types.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68232
Related: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/69948

Signed-off-by: Senol Colak <senol.colak@sap.com>

66881.title: librbd: expose ContextWQ as an abstract base class in the public API for external implementations
66881.author: baum
66881.body:
Expose `ContextWQ` as a public abstract base class so an external module can run librbd's completion work on its own threads. The motivating user is the Ceph NVMe-oF gateway: with SPDK's `SpdkContextWQ`, librbd completions run on SPDK reactor threads instead of the librados `io_context_pool`. The idea is due to @bill-scales.

Default behavior is unchanged: images opened through the existing APIs keep using the in-tree `AsioContextWQ`.

## Related PRs

- SPDK `SpdkContextWQ` implementation: https://github.com/ceph/spdk/pull/17
- ceph-nvmeof gateway integration and system test: https://github.com/ceph/ceph-nvmeof/pull/1741

---

## 1. Ceph NVMe-oF Gateway (end-to-end)

NVMe-oF initiator ↔ gateway (SPDK NVMe-oF target, `bdev_rbd`) ↔ librbd ↔ librados ↔ Ceph cluster.

```
┌──────────────────────┐
│  NVMe-oF Initiator   │
│  (host / VM / app)   │
└──────────┬───────────┘
           │ NVMe-oF (TCP)
           ▼
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║  Ceph NVMe-oF Gateway                                          ║
║  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ ║
║  │  NVMe-oF target (SPDK reactors)                           │ ║
║  └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ ║
║                                │ bdev                          ║
║  ┌─────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐ ║
║  │  bdev_rbd (one bdev per RBD image)                        │ ║
║  └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ ║
║                                │ librbd / librados             ║
║  ┌─────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────┐ ║
║  │  librbd: AsioEngine, ContextWQ                            │ ║
║  │  librados: Objecter, Messenger, io_context_pool           │ ║
║  └─────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────┘ ║
╚════════════════════════════════╪═══════════════════════════════╝
                                 │ RADOS (TCP)
                                 ▼
              ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
              │  Ceph cluster (MONs + OSDs + MGR) │
              │  objects, RBD data and metadata   │
              └───────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Problem statement

The gateway must scale with the number of RBD images it serves. The NVMe-oF target and bdev layer run on SPDK reactor threads (one per core, polling, never blocking). Images are spread across several librados instances (`cluster_connections`), because a single instance becomes a bottleneck in completion and async work. One instance per image is not viable: each brings its own RadosClient, Messenger and `io_context_pool`.

With `AsioContextWQ`, completion threads grow with the number of instances (one `io_context_pool` each), and every completion is then handed back to the submitting reactor with `spdk_thread_send_msg()`. Running completion work on the reactors keeps the thread count fixed and removes that hand-off.

---

## 3. Summary of the change

**Ceph:** `ContextWQ` becomes a public abstract base class; the in-tree implementation is `AsioContextWQ` (`io_context_pool`). Object-request completion tokens are bound to the image's ContextWQ, and an I/O carries the *channel* of the thread that submitted it, so a channel-aware implementation can finish every stage of that I/O on the same thread. For `SpdkContextWQ` a channel is one SPDK reactor.

**Scale-out:** with `SpdkContextWQ`, object I/O completions run on the fixed set of reactors shared by all images and librados instances. The `io_context_pool` stays idle on the I/O path but is still used for MonClient, management operations and migration.

**Changes span:** Ceph (this PR), SPDK (`SpdkContextWQ`, round-robin reactor selection, per-reactor work ring; ceph/spdk#17), NVMe-oF gateway (config and RPC to enable it; ceph/ceph-nvmeof#1741).

---

## 4. librbd and ContextWQ

### API

`ContextWQ::Work` is `UniqueFunction<>` (move-only); `Channel` is an opaque handle (`void*`

66924.title: CMakeLists.txt: add option to build agains system opentelemetry
66924.author: clan
66924.body:
1. In Gentoo, if build against system opentelemetry, cmake failed with:

> CMake Error at src/CMakeLists.txt:443 (target_link_libraries):
>   The link interface of target "jaeger_base" contains:
>
>     opentelemetry::libopentelemetry
>
>   but the target was not found.  Possible reasons include:
>
>     * There is a typo in the target name.
>     * A find_package call is missing for an IMPORTED target.
>     * An ALIAS target is missing.

See also: https://bugs.gentoo.org/930064

2. fix heap_profiler build failure due to parallel build ordering

During parallel builds, src/perfglue/heap_profiler.cc can fail to compile because it depends on legacy-option-headers and the generated header global_legacy_options.h may not be available yet. This leads to incomplete definitions in included headers, causing compilation errors such as missing members in ConfigValues.

For example, the following error is observed when building with "-j64":

```
FAILED: [code=1] src/perfglue/CMakeFiles/heap_profiler.dir/heap_profiler.cc.o
/var/tmp/portage/sys-cluster/ceph-20.1.0-r2/work/ceph-20.1.0/src/perfglue/heap_profiler.cc: In function ‘void get_profile_name(char*, int)’:
src/perfglue/heap_profiler.cc:102:48: error: ‘class ConfigValues’ has no member named ‘log_file’
snprintf(path, sizeof(path), "%s", g_conf()->log_file.c_str());
                                             ^~~~~~~~
```

The issue can be reliably reproduced by adding time.sleep(3600) at the beginning of y2c.py.

Dependency chain:
   src/perfglue/heap_profiler.cc
    -> src/perfglue/heap_profiler.h
    -> src/common/config.h
    -> src/common/config_values.h
    -> src/common/options/legacy_config_opts.h

67012.title: [DNM] Integration of remote ops
67012.author: pritha-srivastava
67012.body:
This commit has the implementation of sending a PUT, GET, DELETE & HEAD request to a remote cache.  
Right now, the request can be sent to a remote rgw configured via rgw_d4n_remote_cache_address. rgw_d4n_remote_put can be used to turn on/off the remote PUT (on by default). The remote PUT can be sent synchronously or asynchronously. This can be controlled using rgw_d4n_async_remote_put. When async remote PUT mode is ON, it is achieved via a couroutine and thread pool part of the D4N filter driver. The thread pool size can be configured using 
rgw_d4n_thread_pool_size. During my testing, a thread pool size equal to the number of physical cores gave me best results. Also coroutine pool size = thread pool size gave the best results.

vstart cluster can be brought up with the following options:MON=1 OSD=1 RGW=2 MGR=0 MDS=0 ../src/vstart.sh -n -d -o rgw_d4n_l1_datacache_persistent_path=/home/prsrivas/ceph/build/rgw_d4n_datacache/ -o rgw_filter=d4n -o d4n_writecache_enabled=true -o rgw_d4n_cache_cleaning_interval=86400 -o rgw_d4n_l1_evict_cache_on_start=false -o rgw_d4n_directory_address=127.0.0.1:6379 -o rgw_d4n_remote_cache_address=127.0.0.1:8001 -o rgw_d4n_async_remote_put=true -o rgw_d4n_thread_pool_size=8

Then kill both rgws, modify ceph.conf to configure the datacache path and its respective remote rgw address:
for radosgw1, add the following:
rgw_d4n_l1_datacache_persistent_path=/home/prsrivas/ceph/build/rgw_d4n_datacache/
rgw_d4n_remote_cache_address=127.0.0.1:8001
rgw_d4n_l1_datacache_address=127.0.0.1:8000

for radosgw2, add the following:
rgw_d4n_l1_datacache_persistent_path=/home/prsrivas/ceph/build/rgw_d4n_datacache1/
rgw_d4n_remote_cache_address=127.0.0.1:8000
rgw_d4n_l1_datacache_address=127.0.0.1:8001

Then restart the rgws. Once a PUT request completes then data is found in both rgw_d4n_datacache and rgw_d4n_datacache1. In case the async mode is ON, the data will be found in both the caches after a delay.

Similar options are available to turn ON/OFF remote GET and DELETE ops.

As part of the implementation of remote HEAD op, a head block is no longer written to the cache backend. The head block only had attrs of the entire object. These attrs are now written as part of the head block entry written to the Directory (no extra call has been introduced here). This saves us one call to the cache backend per head block both during a PUT and a GET. In case of Remote GET/HEAD operations since the head block attrs are available in the Directory, they can be accessed via any rgw, (whereas if we had cached the head block in the cache backend, an extra remote get request would be needed for an rgw that did not have the head block cached locally).

67156.title: mgr: fix assertion failure in get_perf_schema_python for empty perf counters
67156.author: zenjabba
67156.body:
## Problem

When a daemon exists in `daemon_state` but has no perf counter instances (e.g., a destroyed OSD with null FSID `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000`), the `get_perf_schema_python()` function crashes with an assertion failure:

```
/ceph/rpmbuild/BUILD/ceph-20.2.0/src/mgr/PyFormatter.h: 84: FAILED ceph_assert(cursor != root)
```

**Call stack:**
```
ceph::__ceph_assert_fail()
  -> PyFormatter::close_section()
    -> ActivePyModules::get_perf_schema_python()
```

This causes MGR daemons to crash every 60-90 seconds when the telemetry module iterates through all OSDs and encounters a destroyed one.

## Root Cause

In `get_perf_schema_python()`, when iterating through daemons:

1. The function enters the daemon loop since `daemons` is not empty
2. It creates a `Formatter::ObjectSection` for the daemon key (RAII-managed)
3. The inner loop over `state->perf_counters.instances` never executes because the collection is empty
4. Lines 1253-1254 unconditionally call `f.close_section()` twice
5. These calls try to close 'counters' and 'counter object' sections that were never opened
6. This violates the assertion `cursor != root` in `PyFormatter::close_section()`

## Solution

Add an early `continue` to skip daemons with empty `perf_counters.instances` before entering the `with_gil` block. This prevents the crash while still properly handling daemons that do have perf counters.

## Reproduction

1. Have a Ceph cluster with telemetry module enabled
2. Destroy an OSD without purging it:
   ```bash
   ceph osd destroy 123 --yes-i-really-mean-it
   ```
3. Wait 60-90 seconds for telemetry to query perf schema
4. MGR crashes with assertion failure

## Testing

- Verified that destroyed OSDs (with null FSID) are skipped
- Normal OSDs with perf counters continue to work as expected
- No assertion failures after the fix

## Comparison with Similar Code

`get_unlabeled_perf_schema_python()` handles this case correctly because it opens a section *before* the loop and closes it *after* - properly balanced even if the loop is empty. This fix aligns `get_perf_schema_python()` with that pattern by avoiding the problematic code path entirely.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74693

'''

67183.title: [WIP] [DO NOT REVIEW] mgr/cephadm: Add customer intermediate CA support for cephadm-signed
67183.author: rkachach
67183.body:
This PR allows operators to configure a customer-provided intermediate CA (cert+key) to sign cephadm-signed certificates, behind an explicit enablement flag, and adds a convenience command to reissue certs by service.

- Add new GLOBAL TLS objects:
  - `customer_signing_ca_cert`
  - `customer_signing_ca_key`

- New config option:
  - `certificate_use_customer_ca_for_cephadm_signed` (default: `false`)
  - When enabled, cephadm uses the customer CA to issue cephadm-signed leaf certs instead of the cephadm root CA.

- Safe renewal across issuer switch:
  - If a cert’s issuer doesn’t match the active signer, cert+key are
  - removed to force regeneration under the new CA.

- New operator command:
  - `ceph orch certmgr reissue --by-service <svc-name>`
  - Purges matching cephadm-signed cert/key objects and triggers
  - service redeploy to regenerate/install new certs.

- Prevent private key leakage:
  - `key_ls` redacts `customer_signing_ca_key` (same as `cephadm_root_ca_key`).

- Backwards compatible: default behavior remains unchanged unless the new flag is enabled.

67237.title: mon, osd, crimson/osd: cluster_osdmap_trim_lower_bound set to min_last_epoch_started
67237.author: xxhdx1985126
67237.body:
This draft is a POC one for the possibility of setting `cluster_osdmap_trim_lower_bound` to `min_last_epoch_started`.

The motive was that, with `cluster_osdmap_trim_lower_bound` set to `min_last_epoch_clean`, the cluster may accumulate large amounts of osdmsps across pools when some pools in the clusters are experiencing backfills for a relatively long time (maybe weeks/months), which could be cause pools with small-capacity disks to be filled up when the cluster is relatively large.

This draft PR basically intend to trim osdmaps on OSDs by `min_last_epoch_started` while keeping the osdmaps on monitors back to `min_last_epoch_clean`, which leads to newly added fields, `MOSDMap::oldest_map` and `OSDSuperblock::cluster_oldest_map`, to represent the lower bound of osdmaps kept by monitors.

Signed-off-by: Xuehan Xu <xuxuehan@qianxin.com>

Add support for setting NFS export delegations (read, write, readwrite, none) via Ceph orchestrator so that updates in YAML or export config are applied correctly.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74821
Signed-off-by: Pooja dwivedi[pooja.dwivedi@ibm.com](mailto:pooja.dwivedi@ibm.com)

Description:- This PR is created to provide support for NFS delegations in the ceph NFS module. NFS exports in Ceph should allow setting the delegations option (for example, delegations = readwrite) to control client caching behavior. This can take values read, readwrite, or none.

Cephadm should allow to enable the delegation and its type at export level
It should pick up the delegations parameter from:

EXPORT_DEFAULTS - By default , the delegation default should be "None" within the export defaults (Ganesha.conf)

EXPORT block (export file)
CLIENT block within EXPORT (export file)

Users should be able to set delegations = read | write | readwrite | none at export creation or update time

67311.title: rgw/posix: fix multipart upload failures and improve error diagnostics
67311.author: guimou
67311.body:
**Note**: this patch was written with the huge help of Claude Code while working on the [S4 project](https://github.com/rh-aiservices-bu/s4) (RGW only with Posix backend + UI). The fixes were needed for the different upload scenarios to properly work.

Multipart uploads on the POSIX (and DBStore) backend fail silently at the CompleteMultipartUpload step. Parts upload successfully to the shadow directory (.multipart_*) but the final assembly fails for several reasons, and the errors are invisible in containerized deployments because they are only written to the Ceph log file via ldpp_dout(), never to stderr.

This patch addresses the following issues:

1. load() assigns shadow before validating it via load_bucket(). If load_bucket() fails, the broken shadow pointer persists, silently hiding all subsequent errors. Fix: use a temporary variable and only assign to shadow on success.

2. get_info() accesses shadow without calling load(dpp) first, so errors during loading are swallowed (load(nullptr) suppresses logging). Fix: call load(dpp) explicitly in get_info().

3. from_meta() uses rfind('.') to parse <oid>.<upload_id>, but this matches file extensions when the object name contains dots (e.g., intro.mp4 returns "mp4" as the upload ID instead of the actual 2~<random> ID). Fix: validate that the parsed upload_id has the 2~ prefix via is_v2_upload_id(). Applied to both POSIXMPObj and DBMPObj.

4. renameat2 with RENAME_EXCHANGE is not supported on NFS, FUSE, and overlayfs, causing multipart re-uploads to fail with EINVAL. Fix: if RENAME_EXCHANGE fails with EINVAL, fall back to deleting the existing target and doing a plain rename.

5. After renaming the shadow directory to the final object name in complete(), the object is never added to the bucket cache, making it invisible in listings until the cache is refreshed. Fix: open, stat, and fill_cache after rename.

6. link_temp_file() calls fill_cache() without first refreshing metadata via stat(), which can result in stale attributes in the cache. Fix: force stat(dpp, true) after the rename.

7. In bucket_cache, the ADD operation decodes the URL-encoded filename to compute the cache key, but the REMOVE operation uses the raw filename. This causes stale entries to remain after deletion. Fix: decode and parse the filename in REMOVE consistently with ADD.

8. inotify_add_watch error messages print the watch descriptor (-1) instead of errno, making failures impossible to diagnose. Fix: capture errno before the format call and print it with strerror().

9. inotify watches are registered for shadow buckets (short-lived .multipart_* directories), wasting kernel resources and producing noisy error messages. Fix: skip watches when the bucket name contains the multipart upload ID prefix "2~".

10. wfd and efd are declared without initialization, risking use-of-uninitialized in error paths. Fix: initialize to -1 and move fd creation to the member initializer list.

11. All critical multipart errors (rename, open, stat, load failures) now also log to stderr so they are visible via kubectl logs in containerized deployments.

---

67605.author: kotreshhr
67605.body:
CephFS mirroring unconditionally attempted to initialize blockdiff,
causing initialization failure on older Ceph clusters where blockdiff
is not supported but mirror daemon supporting blockdiff.

syncing.

Fix this by detecting blockdiff support and initializing it only when
supported, allowing mirroring to function correctly with older Ceph
versions.

67627.title: tentacle: osd: handle all the updated keys in OSD::maybe_override_options_for_qos
67627.author: gardran
67627.body:
Up to now the first matching key from the changeset has been taken into account only. Which is wrong as multiple relevant keys might be present in it.
The primary issue with such a handling is a case when the first config parameter update takes place. The received changset contains a bunch of keys in this case and incorrect/incomplete processing might occur. E.g. as a side effect this could fail TEST_recovery_limit_adjustment_mclock from standalone/osd/mclock-config when mclock's OSD benchmark results are out of expected range (e.g. when run on SSD drive) and hence there
 is no update for 'max_capacity_iops_config' config parameter. The
following update triggered from the test case isn't handled properly then. Hence failing it.

This patch implements iteration over all the keys from the changeset and does proper processing for all of them matching the patterns.

Parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74678
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75269
Backports: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67126

Signed-off-by: Garry Drankovich <garry.drankovich@clyso.com>
(cherry picked from commit 57cc9216519f02b063ffcfbd04a376ebe492f907)

 Conflicts:
	src/osd/OSD.cc
 trivial, cause by lacking f82ab1cbf242 commit

67691.title: squid: rgw: fix overflow of outstanding counter in SimpleThrottler
67691.author: cfanz
67691.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74992

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/66455
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74038

This fixes a bug where throttled requests don't increment `l_outstanding`, while `request_complete()` always decrements it, causing the counter to underrun/
overflow.

This is the minimal fix because it only moves the `l_outstanding` increment so that both accepted and throttled requests are accounted for consistently,
without changing throttling behavior.

This should be backported to `squid` because the same buggy code path exists there, so the perf counter can still become incorrect under throttling.

67698.author: SHASHI9705

This can potentially allow unsafe HTML to be rendered if input content is not sanitized before being passed to the component. 67719.title: rgw: add time limit for list requests
67719.author: dahast
67719.body:
In addition to limiting the number of LIST requests, this change introduces a mechanism to limit the cumulative processing time they consume per accumulation interval.

LIST request vary significantly in their system impact: Linear LIST is easy and fast. But LIST with prefix and delimiter can be expensive and may require to collect objects names that are scattered accross the db and require a large number of db queries.

A limit by number seems not very helpful here, so a limit on the used processing time is added. This commit builds on the work for adding a limit to LIST done in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/64762. It adds a limit for time very similar to the bandwith limits for READ and WRITE.

This PR adds support for Keystone Application Credential Access Rules. It allows RGW to respect and enforce the method/path restrictions defined on restricted OpenStack tokens.

Key Changes
Enforcement: Added check_access_rules in rgw_auth_keystone.cc to validate the request method and path against the token’s rules. It supports wildcard matching (* and **).

Keystone Integration: RGW now sends the OpenStack-Identity-Access-Rules: 1.0 header during token validation and handles the access_rules JSON in the response.

67806.title: crimson scrub scheduling
67806.author: liu-chunmei
67806.body:
crimson: scrub scheduling, reservation and repair

Brings the crimson OSD's scrub up to parity with the classic OSD: periodic
and operator-initiated scheduling, local/remote resource reservation, a full
chunked scrub with the classic error reporting, and repair. Most of the
shared scheduling code under src/osd/scrubber/ is reused rather than
duplicated.

Scrub (core of this PR)

* Shared code (osd/scrub: make scrub_job, scrubber_common and queue entry
  crimson-aware): scrub_job, scrub_queue_entry and scrub_resources build for
  crimson behind WITH_CRIMSON; scrubber_common.h drops its "#define Scrub"
  macro in favour of namespace usings; not_before_queue_t gets a destructor
  and clear(). scrub_reservations is *not* shared - crimson has its own
  implementation under src/crimson/osd/scrub/, leaving the classic file
  untouched.
* Scheduling: per-shard ScrubQueue/ScrubScheduler; osd_max_scrubs is
  enforced OSD-wide, not per shard.
* Reservations: primary-side replica reservation and release.
* State machine: inter-chunk PendingTimer (honours osd_scrub_sleep), abort
  on noscrub/nodeep-scrub, WaitDigestUpdate, stale-event discard.
* Validator: snapset, digest and per-replica evaluation matching classic
  ScrubBackend, with error counts and log lines that match classic.
* PGScrubber: chunk scan, error store (keyed by full object id), SCRUBLS
  (rados list-inconsistent-*), stat-mismatch accounting ordered as in
  classic _scrub_finish(), repair, snap-mapper validation.
* Write/scan races: the scrubber is notified only when a write is durable;
  out-of-order commits on multi-shard OSDs are handled.
* Admin/metrics: scrub, deep-scrub, schedule-*, scrub_metrics, dump_scrubs,
  dump_scrub_reservations; Seastar metrics rather than perf counters.

Known limitation

Erasure-coded pools are not scrubbed. chunk_validation_policy_t still
hardwires is_ec() to false and logical_to_ondisk_size() to the identity,
where classic derives the on-disk size from the pool's stripe info. On an EC
pool each shard holds a chunk whose size is unrelated to the object's
logical size, so every object is reported as damaged. Until the validator
understands EC geometry, EC PGs are not registered for scrubbing at all.

Test support

* qa/standalone/crimson-scrub/: crimson variants of the scrub standalone
  suites (the classic suites are untouched); ceph-helpers.sh crimson
  support.
* crimson_scrub_test / crimson_repair_test teuthology tasks;
  test_crimson_scrub unit tests.
* seastore read-error / EIO injection (seastore_debug_inject_read_err),

67860.title: qa:  Add opt-in min_size protection to OSD thrasher
67860.author: kamoltat
67860.body:
**Problem:**
    
The OSD thrasher randomly kills OSDs without checking if it would
violate any PG's min_size. This leads to data loss scenarios
where multiple OSDs in the same acting set are killed in quick succession,
leaving PGs with fewer replicas than min_size and resulting in unfound
objects that cannot be recovered.
    
**Solution:**
    Add opt-in protection to kill_osd() that checks PG states before selecting
    an OSD to kill:
    
    1. New _get_safe_to_kill_osds() method identifies OSDs whose death would
       not violate any PG's min_size by checking acting sets against pool
       min_size values.
    
    2. Modified kill_osd() to accept respect_min_size parameter (default False):
    
    3. Updated test_pool_min_size() to explicitly set respect_min_size=False
       since that test intentionally violates min_size.
    
    This provides protection against systematic min_size violations while
    
Signed-off-by: Kamoltat (Junior) Sirivadhna <ksirivad@redhat.com>

67875.title: mon: change mon_config_key_max_entry_size value from 64_k to 256_k
67875.author: aadhikale
67875.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75346

If we have 375 host entries in mgr/cephadm/inventory (cephadm host inventory), with an average size of approximately 182 bytes per host this value may vary depending on the hostname length as well as the number and size of labels the total inventory size would be approximately 68,250 bytes (375 × 182). This exceeds the default value of mon_config_key_max_entry_size (65,536 bytes).

By increasing mon_config_key_max_entry_size to 1 MB, the inventory could accommodate approximately 5,761 host entries (1,048,576 ÷ 182), providing a significantly larger and safer margin for future growth.



Test before code changes:
# ./bin/ceph -c ./ceph.conf -k ./keyring config get mon mon_config_key_max_entry_size
65536

Test after code changes:
# ./bin/ceph -c ./ceph.conf -k ./keyring config get mon mon_config_key_max_entry_size
262144
