71553.title: rbd-mirror: detect split-brain when incomplete local snapshot lacks remote snap
71553.author: VinayBhaskar-V
71553.body:
Currently, if a local non-primary mirror snapshot is incomplete (!m_local_mirror_snap_ns.complete) and its corresponding remote mirror snapshot was deleted on the primary cluster before the image replayer could finish syncing, `scan_remote_mirror_snapshots` fails to catch this case.

Instead of detecting the split-brain, the replayer logs that all remote snapshots are synced and transitions to idle. On subsequent sync cycles, the orphaned incomplete local snapshot gets falsely marked as complete without syncing its remaining objects, causing subtle data corruption and deferring the split-brain detection to later steps.

Fix this by explicitly checking in scan_remote_mirror_snapshots() whether an incomplete local snapshot (m_local_snap_id_end) exists without a matching remote snapshot target (m_remote_snap_id_end == CEPH_NOSNAP). If so, set split_brain = true immediately to halt replay and flag the error early.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80281

71562.title: umbrella: mgr/cephadm: batch MDS upgrades when fail_fs is set
71562.author: kginonredhat
71562.body:
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78304

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70873

**Summary**

When `fail_fs` is enabled the filesystem is already failed, so MDS daemons are safe to upgrade together. Stop breaking after the first MDS in `_to_upgrade` so they are queued in one pass instead of one per upgrade cycle.

`fail_fs` is already on umbrella, but without this change MDS are still redeployed one daemon per upgrade cycle, so the "rapid multi-rank mds upgrade" path is incomplete.

71571.title: crimson/os/seastore: introduce BlockIODriver and NVMeIODriver transport abstractions
71571.author: fultheim
71571.body:
Preparation for the SPDK I/O path (#69516), split out per review so the shared-path change can be reviewed and merged on its own.

Two refactors, no behaviour change, no new dependencies:

- `BlockIODriver`: the raw block I/O that `BlockSegmentManager` did through `seastar::file` moves into `KernelBlockIODriver` behind a small transport interface (open/close/read/write/writev). The segment manager keeps its logic and calls the driver.
- `NVMeIODriver`: same for `NVMeBlockDevice`; the kernel NVMe passthrough path becomes `KernelNVMeIODriver`, and the raw NVMe command structs move to `nvme_command.h`, which drops the `linux/nvme_ioctl.h` dependency from the RBM device header.

Both factories return the kernel implementation unconditionally in this PR; the SPDK implementations arrive in #69516 and select themselves only when `seastore_spdk_transport_id` is set.

Tested with the seastore unit tests (transaction manager, journal, RBM, segment manager) against both backends.

71572.title: crimson/os/seastore: zero-copy DMA buffers for the SPDK I/O path
71572.author: fultheim
71572.body:
Depends on #69516 (merged). Split out of #69516 per review.

With the SPDK backend in place, this PR makes the path zero-copy by handing SeaStore's own buffers to the device already DMA-registered:

- Zero-copy read/write: extent and journal buffers are allocated through a small `seastore_dma_alloc` helper that returns SPDK DMA memory when `seastore_spdk_transport_id` is set and page-aligned heap memory otherwise. Cache, extent placement, the journal (circular and segmented) and RBM staging buffers use it; `Device::alloc_io_buffer()` lets each device type choose. The helper reads the option on every call (no cached static), so tests that toggle the option see the change.
- Journal record metadata is encoded in place into a DMA buffer via a new `bufferlist::append_buffer()`, which seeds the append carriage with a caller-provided raw so the encode lands directly in it. Covered by new `bufferlist` unit tests.

With `seastore_spdk_transport_id` empty the only change is that these buffers are page-aligned heap allocations, as before.

## Testing

Zero-copy on the write path was confirmed with `perf` under sustained random writes at steady state (device overwritten many times, GC active): the SeaStore->SPDK submit path carries no payload `memcpy`; data extents and in-place-encoded journal metadata reach the controller as DMA-registered buffers via passthrough SGL, and the non-DMA bounce fallback never triggers.

**Summary**

```
Upgrade aborted - Got unexpected daemon type "nvmeof".
Viable daemon types for this command are: ['mgr', 'mon', 'crash', 'osd', 'mds', 'rgw',
'rbd-mirror', 'cephfs-mirror', 'ceph-exporter', 'iscsi', 'nfs', 'node-proxy']

71587.title: RADOS snapshot rollback
71587.author: bill-scales
71587.body:
Currently RADOS implements a snapshot feature that allows point-in-time
copies of a set of objects to be created. Snapshot creation is an O(1)
operation, deferring the actual work of cloning objects to a just-in-time
process when the object is next written. All snapshots of a RADOS object
are stored on the same OSDs as the head object which makes it easy to
implement this process within the OSD daemon.

RADOS also implements a rollback I/O operation which will restore a
RADOS object to a previous point-in-time snapshot. Clients wishing to
rollback a set of RADOS objects must iterate across these objects
issuing rollback I/O operations and need to deal with how to make this
rollback appear atomic. This implementation of rollback is O(number of
objects), unless the client implements its own just-in-time processes
for deferring when it issues rollback operations.

This PR implements a new RADOS snapshot rollback feature
that provides the ability to revert all objects in a pool to the state
captured in a previously created snapshot with similar performance to
taking a snapshot (O(1) time to start the rollback, similar overheads to
snapshots for read/write I/Os whilst the rollback completes), without
requiring client coordination, and without blocking client I/O while the
rollback occurs.

See doc/dev/osd_internals/rados-snapshot-rollback-design.rst for the full
design document and rados-snapshot-rollback-work-breakdown.rst for the
work breakdown

---
Status:

3 days work, mainly designed and coded by IBM Bob with a lot of direction and testing by Bill.

Highlights:
* Concept works!
* Pool level snapshots can be rolled back, JIT read/write paths work, snap trimmer processes rollbacks as a background task
* New CLIs, APIs written, tested and documented, including python bindings
* New unittests written and tested.
 
 Work is incomplete, the todo list:

* There is one late breaking design issue that is fixed in the design (workitem 22) but not coded (1/4 day)
* There needs to be more testing of self-managed snapshot rollbacks, the changes to librbd and the changes to ceph_test_rados to test this in teuthology runs (1 day)
* More testing of snap trimmer (mixtures of rollback + trimmed snapshots, multiple rollbacks and deleting a snapshot as it is being rolled back) (3/4 day)
* Need to complete tidying up the 100 commits and finishing a full review of the changes (2 days)
* Run teuthology QA runs and screen results (2 days)
* Getting the PR reviewed and merged (1 week+ of other peoples time)

71609.author: eameh-LF
71609.body:
Small trial of the man page as the single source for command reference, as discussed with Anthony D'Atri and Ville O. Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80355

The rbd snapshots page restated the `rbd snap create` command that the rbd(8) man page already documents. This change marks the entry in `doc/man/8/rbd.rst` with two RST comments and includes that slice into `doc/rbd/rbd-snapshot.rst` at build time, so the command description is written once and rendered on both the prose page and the man page. The markers are comments, so nothing new appears in the roff output. Author comments at both ends explain where the text comes from so nobody re-adds it by hand.

Checked on main with `admin/build-doc`: the man build is clean with `-W`, and the html build produces no new warnings. (The html build on main already emits one unrelated autodoc warning about `DriveGroupSpec`/`ArgumentSpec`, present without this change.)

Draft on purpose: the point is to see it rendered in the Read the Docs preview and decide whether to apply the pattern more widely. It fits rbd(8) and radosgw-admin(8) directly, since their man pages list commands as individual entries; ceph(8) is written in prose sections and would need a different approach.

71611.title: umbrella: qa/cephfs: wait for MgrMap client registration before mgr fail
71611.author: karthik-us1
71611.body:
test_mgr_eviction expects that failing the active mgr evicts its CephFS MDS sessions. Eviction depends on ceph mgr fail blocklisting MgrMap.active_clients, which the mon only learns from mgr beacons.

After subvolume create, the volumes module registers the new libcephfs client address in the mgr process immediately, but that address may not be in MgrMap yet until the next beacon (mgr_tick_period, default 2s). If mgr fail runs in that window, the mon blocklists a stale client list and the live MDS session is never blocklisted. The failed mgr then respawns without a clean CephFS close, so the session lingers past the test's 30s wait (MDS session_timeout is ~61s).

Fix the race by waiting until each mgr MDS session nonce appears in mgr dump active_clients before calling mgr fail, so blocklisting covers the sessions the test asserts are evicted.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76047

(backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80161)
(cherry picked from commit 13da5431ece1a77105889af404d8f8fcf920b812)

71628.title: mgr/cephadm : Verify MTU configuration before adding hosts to the bootstrapped cluster
71628.author: djagdale4
71628.body:
## Fixes: [Tracker #80384](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80384)

## Description

When adding a host, cephadm now sends a Don't Fragment (DF) ping from the active manager host to the new host, sized to the manager's effective MTU. If the ping detects a mismatch, the host is still added and a warning is printed — it never blocks the operation.

---

## Local Testing

### Before

Despite the MTU mismatch, the host was added successfully without any warning.

```text
[root@ceph-node-00 ~]# nmcli device show ens3 | grep MTU
GENERAL.MTU:                            9000
[root@ceph-node-00 ~]#
logout

[root@ceph-node-01 ~]# nmcli device show ens3 | grep MTU
GENERAL.MTU:                            1500
[root@ceph-node-01 ~]#
[root@ceph-node-01 ~]#
logout

[root@ceph-node-00 ~]# cephadm shell
[ceph: root@ceph-node-00 /]# ceph orch host add ceph-node-01 192.168.100.101
Added host 'ceph-node-01' with addr '192.168.100.101'
```

### After

**1. Host addition using CLI**

```text
[ceph: root@ceph-node-00 /]# ceph orch host add ceph-node-02 192.168.100.102
```

Host was added successfully, followed by an MTU mismatch warning:

```text
Added host 'ceph-node-02' with addr '192.168.100.102'
WARNING: MTU check from ceph-node-00 to ceph-node-02 (192.168.100.102) failed, possible MTU mismatch: MTU validation failed for host 192.168.100.102. Could not send 9000 byte packet without fragmentation. PING 192.168.100.102 (192.168.100.102) 8972(9000) bytes of data.
--- 192.168.100.102 ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 2045ms
```

**2. Host addition using YAML**

Created `/tmp/hosts.yaml`:

```text
[ceph: root@ceph-node-00 /]# cat > /tmp/hosts.yaml <<EOF
service_type: host
hostname: ceph-node-02
addr: 192.168.100.102
EOF
[ceph: root@ceph-node-00 /]# ceph orch apply -i /tmp/hosts.yaml
```

The host was added successfully and the same MTU warning was printed.

```text
Added host 'ceph-node-02' with addr '192.168.100.102'
WARNING: MTU check from ceph-node-00 to ceph-node-02 (192.168.100.102) failed, possible MTU mismatch: MTU validation failed for host 192.168.100.102. Could not send 9000 byte packet without fragmentation. PING 192.168.100.102 (192.168.100.102) 8972(9000) bytes of data.
--- 192.168.100.102 ping statistics ---
3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss, time 2046ms
```

**3. Cephadm log verification**

```text
[ceph: root@ceph-node-00 /]# ceph log last 30 cephadm | grep -i mtu
2026-11-02T07:59:43.401684+0000 mgr.ceph-node-00.ldpgca (mgr.214100) 688 : cephadm [WRN] MTU check from ceph-node-00 to ceph-node-02 (192.168.100.102) failed, possible MTU mismatch: MTU validation failed for host 192.168.100.102. Could not send 9000 byte packet without fragmentation. PING 192.168.100.102 (192.168.100.102) 8972(9000) bytes of data.
```

Confirmed that the MTU mismatch warning was recorded in the cephadm logs.

71650.author: Doracly
71650.body:
install-deps.sh: keep ceph-build-deps after dependencies installation
    
When running install-deps.sh to install packages for Ubuntu, a lot of necessary stuff is installed via apt with the help of the metapackage ceph-build-deps that depends on those packages.
In a separate step this metapackage is removed again, but that leaves the other packages in place with the mark "they are not needed any more", and might be auto-removed at some later point, breaking the build.
    
This behavior seems inferior to keeping the "self built" package ceph-build-deps in place and not accidentally removing the dependencies every now and then.
    
Signed-off-by: Dominik Raddatz <dominik.raddatz@clyso.com>

71665.title: common/options: build option tables in place
71665.author: tchaikov
71665.body:
y2c.py generates each get_{name}_options() as one braced list:
```c++
  return std::vector<Option>({ Option(...)..., Option(...)..., ... });
```
This is expensive in two ways.

Every Option backing the initializer_list is live at once in a single frame. `-fstack-usage` reports 746192 bytes for `get_global_options()` (857 entries) and 404736 for `get_rgw_options()` (458), far larger than any other function in these libraries.

`initializer_list` elements are `const`, so vector cannot move out of them. Every Option is built on the stack, copied to the heap, then destroyed, duplicating each name, description, tag and service string.

Use `reserve()` and `emplace_back()` instead. `emplace_back()` returns a reference to the new element, so the `.set_...()` chain applies to it directly: each Option is built in the vector, with no stack temporary and no copy.

On x86-64 (gcc 14.2.0, `-O2` `-fstack-clash-protection` `-fstack-protector-strong`) `get_global_options()` goes from a 746192 to a 1136 byte frame, from 445856 to 85884 bytes of `.text`, and compiles in 3.5s instead of 18.8s. `get_rgw_options()` goes from 404736 to 3792 bytes of frame.

The frame size also breaks unwinding on arm64. A frame that large makes gcc emit stack-clash probing as a loop, and gcc 14 (up to at least Debian's 14.2.0-19) gets the unwind info for that loop wrong by the callee-save size [0]. gdb, C++ exceptions, and full tcmalloc taking a heap-growth backtrace then read garbage instead of the return address. Where pointer authentication is enforced this traps, and `ceph-mon/ceph-osd` have been seen dying with SIGILL at startup, even for `--version` [1]. A small frame avoids the probing loop without waiting for a compiler fix to reach stable distros.

The generated definitions do not change: `--raw` output (for pasting option definitions elsewhere, not used by the build) and the generated legacy option headers are byte-identical across all 13 tables, and the .cc differs only in how each Option is appended.

[0] https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=119610
[1] https://bugzilla.proxmox.com/show_bug.cgi?id=7941

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81551

71682.title: systemd: stop OSDs before monitors again
71682.author: tchaikov
71682.body:
When a host runs both a monitor and OSDs, nothing orders ceph-osd@.service against `ceph-mon@.service`, so on reboot or poweroff systemd stops them in parallel. A stopping OSD first sends `MOSDMarkMeDown` and waits up to `osd_mon_shutdown_timeout` (5 seconds) for the monitors to commit it. If the local monitor is shutting down at the same time, that wait can expire, and the OSD exits while the osdmap still has it up. Clients on other hosts keep sending it requests until a later map marks it down, and their I/O stalls in the meantime [0]. Stopping the OSDs by hand before rebooting avoids the stall.

7f4acf45dd0 fixed this by adding `ceph-mon.target` to `After=` in `ceph-osd@.service`. d88c834ea44 dropped it while rewriting the ordering of all daemon units, and added `After=ceph-mon.target` to `ceph-osd.target` instead. That orders the target, not the `ceph-osd@` services that are part of it, so OSDs and monitors are stopped in parallel again.

This went largely unnoticed because Ceph recommends running monitors on separate hosts from OSDs [1]. Hyperconverged Proxmox VE clusters, however, commonly run a monitor next to the OSDs on every node, and that is where it was reported.

Put `ceph-mon.target` back in `After=` of `ceph-osd@.service`. Because `ceph-mon@.service` is `Before=ceph-mon.target`, systemd now stops the OSDs first, then `ceph-mon.target`, then the monitors.

This does not introduce regressions. It restores the ordering ceph-osd@.service had between 7f4acf45dd0 and d88c834ea44. `ceph-osd.target` already has After= and Wants= on ceph-mon.target, so hosts without a monitor get no new dependency. `ceph-mon@.service` is a simple service, so at boot the OSDs only wait for the monitor process to start, not for it to join quorum. `systemd-analyze` verify reports no ordering cycle with the change, and stopping units with this ordering in a single transaction shows the monitor now waiting for the OSD.

[0] https://bugzilla.proxmox.com/show_bug.cgi?id=7827
[1] doc/rados/configuration/mon-config-ref.rst

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/18516

71683.title: rbd: do not fail ls -l and du on partially removed images
71683.author: tchaikov
71683.body:
"rbd rm" first moves the image to the trash, which removes the `rbd_id` object for its name, and only then trims the data. If the removal is interrupted after the move, the image stays in the trash with source `REMOVING`. `list2()` still returns it, after all the regular images, but it can no longer be opened by name: opening it fails with `-ENOENT`.

"rbd ls -l" prints an error for such an image and moves on, and "rbd du" skips it silently, but both leave the `-ENOENT` in `r`. These images come last, so usually nothing overwrites it, and the command exits with an error after printing a complete listing. Callers that check the exit status fail as well. Proxmox VE's RBD storage plugin runs "rbd ls -l --format json", so every operation that lists the pool fails until someone finishes the removal by hand [0].

Don't let `-ENOENT` from opening an image fail either command. For "rbd du <image>", only count the image as found once it has been opened, so a partially removed image is reported as not found instead of being printed as an empty table.

Tested with the following steps on a vstart cluster:
```shell
  ceph osd pool create rbd 8
  rbd pool init rbd
  ceph osd pool create data 8
  rbd pool init data
  rbd create -s 64M --data-pool data rbd/victim
  rbd bench --io-type write --io-size 4M --io-total 32M rbd/victim
  ceph auth get-or-create client.rm_ro mon 'profile rbd' \
    osd 'profile rbd pool=rbd, profile rbd-read-only pool=data' \
    -o keyring.rm_ro
  rbd --id rm_ro --keyring keyring.rm_ro rm rbd/victim
  rbd ls -l; echo $?
  rbd ls -l --format json; echo $?
  rbd du; echo $?
  rbd du victim; echo $?
```
The client can't write to the data pool, so "rbd rm" moves the image to the trash and then fails to trim it. Before this change, "rbd ls -l", "rbd ls -l --format json" and "rbd du" print the listing and exit with 2. With it they exit with 0, and "rbd du victim" reports the image as not found. `test_trash_partially_removed` in `cli_generic.sh` runs the same steps: it fails without this change and passes with it.

[0] https://bugzilla.proxmox.com/show_bug.cgi?id=7817

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/52910

71686.title: doc/cephfs: design for credential isolation in snapshot mirroring
71686.author: vshankar
71686.body:
Add a design document detailing multi-tenant credential management and path-jailed isolation for CephFS snapshot mirroring.

The proposal replaces cluster-wide root credentials and eliminates dynamic key-minting in ceph-mgr via a two-track model:

- Orchestrated (Rook/CSI, Dashboard): Uses exported base64 subvolume templates to pre-create matching secondary directory layouts, paired with orchestrator-provisioned path-jailed MON keys.
- Standalone (cephadm/CLI): Preserves an O(1) bootstrap token workflow by pre-authorizing keys on the MON and restricting MGR to read-only token packaging.

Also covers cephfs-mirror libcephfs connection pooling and future daemon- to-daemon RPC replication.

- PosixAioSingleBufferCompletion: single-aiocb write+read round trip,
  the aiocbp[0]/EV_ONESHOT path (already correct before this PR).
- PosixAioMultiIovecCompletion: a genuinely multi-segment bufferlist
  forces submit nseg iovecs
  Build the write from page-aligned segments, so aio_write() does not
  rebuild them into one contiguous buffer, and assert before submitting
  that the IOContext holds a single aio_t with one iovec per segment.
- PosixAioConcurrentCompletion: queues several independent aio_t's on
  one IOContext before a single aio_submit(), giving genuine queue
  depth on the kqueue (multiple concurrent kevent registrations, not
  just multiple iovecs within one lio_listio() call). This is closer
  to the actual failure mode EV_ONESHOT guards against: a persistent
  completion re-firing and being misattributed to a different,
  already-completed and already-freed aio_t. Asserts exact queue
  depth (aio_write()'s fast path pushes exactly one aio_t per call
  for writes at this size) before submitting, and checks each
  segment's content individually so a misattributed completion would
  show up as a specific segment mismatch rather than a generic
  length failure.

71706.title: common/options: clarify osd_max_backfills vs osd_recovery_max_active
71706.author: anthonyeleven
71706.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82125

## Description

`osd_max_backfills` and `osd_recovery_max_active[_hdd|_ssd]` are routinely confused because the names imply they do the same thing. They operate at different granularities:

- **`osd_max_backfills`** is a per-OSD *reservation* limit on whole PGs: it caps how many PGs may be backfilling at once (concurrency), not the rate of each one. An erasure-coded PG must reserve a slot on every shard's OSD simultaneously, so wide EC pools stall on it even when the disks are idle.
- **`osd_recovery_max_active[_hdd|_ssd]`** is a per-OSD limit on individual object operations in flight. Despite the "recovery" name it throttles *backfill* data movement as well as log-based recovery, so it sets the *rate*, not the concurrency.

This rewrites the `fmt_desc` of all four options to state which controls concurrency and which controls rate, notes that `osd_recovery_max_active` governs backfill as well as recovery, and cross-links the pair via `see_also`.

It also harmonizes `osd_max_backfills` onto the same `desc`/`fmt_desc`/`note` shape as the recovery options — it previously had a `long_desc` and no `fmt_desc`, so its detail did not render in the config reference. The read/write detail moves into `fmt_desc`; the mClock caveat becomes a `note`.

Documentation-only; no behavior change.

71721.title: test/erasure-code: PoC GF(2^8) linear hash for EC parity scrub verification
71721.author: aainscow
71721.body:
EC deep scrub currently uses CRC32c to check parity consistency, but CRC32c is only compatible with parity shard 0 (the XOR parity).  For plugins with m>1 the generator matrix rows for parities 1..m-1 contain non-unity GF(2^8) coefficients, so CRC's lack of GF(2^8) linearity (H(α·X) ≠ α·H(X)) means CRC-encoded hashes do not match the actual parity data.  No existing test exercised this gap or validated any alternative.

This commit adds a GFLinearHashSupport test to
TestErasureCodePlugins.cc as a proof of concept for a GF(2^8) inner-product sketch as a replacement/complement to CRC32c.  The sketch computes four independent GF(2^8) inner products (one byte per lane) packed into a uint32_t, giving 1/2^32 collision probability matching CRC32c, but satisfying H(α·X) = α·H(X) so it is compatible with every row of the EC generator matrix.

The test mirrors the structure of the existing CRCEncodeDecodeSupport test, swapping calculate_crc for calculate_gf_hash, and extends it to check all parity shards rather than just parity 0.  It also includes a CRC negative-control assertion that confirms CRC does fail for higher parity shards, making the motivation for the GF approach explicit.

Test results on the full plugin suite (163 configurations):
  86 PASSED  - all ISA reed_sol_van/cauchy (all k/m), all Jerasure
               reed_sol_van/reed_sol_r6_op w=8, and SHEC.  GF hash
               matches actual parity data for every parity shard.
  77 SKIPPED - bit-matrix/packet codecs (liberation, blaum_roth,
               liber8tion, cauchy_orig/good w/ packetsize), w=16/w=32
               Jerasure, Clay (sub-chunks), and LRC (composite layers).
               These use a different encoding structure than byte-level
               GF(2^8) and are noted for future work.
   0 FAILED

The PoC uses an inline carry-less GF(2^8) multiply (poly 0x1d, matching the ISA-L field) with no new dependencies.  A production implementation would obtain the scalar multiply from each plugin.

Assisted-by: IBM Bob v2.1.0

71736.title: cmake: stop nasm feature probes from unlinking /dev/null
71736.author: mmgaggle
71736.body:
`cmake/modules/CheckNasm.cmake` probes the installed nasm for AVX2 /
AVX512 / VPCLMUL support by assembling three sample sources with
`-o /dev/null`. nasm removes its output file when assembly fails, and a
failing probe is the normal case on an assembler that lacks one of
those instruction sets: the probe fails, nasm calls `remove()` on its
output path, and when the configure step runs as root that unlinks
`/dev/null`. The next process to redirect to `/dev/null` recreates it
as a regular file, after which anything depending on the device node
misbehaves (in practice, sshd stops accepting new connections until the
node is recreated from a console).

Point the three probes at a scratch file under
`build/CMakeFiles/CheckNasm` instead of `/dev/null`, so a failed probe
deletes only that scratch file. No change to what the probes detect.

Found while configuring an unrelated branch as root on a build host.

71745.title: mds: defer dirfrag snap purge progress until commit completes
71745.author: LiShengG
71745.body:
A fetch currently advances the live fnode's snap_purged_thru while its stale_items removals are still only in memory. A later metadata operation can journal that fnode before the dirfrag is committed. After a crash, replay restores the advanced watermark without the removals, allowing a subsequent fetch to skip stale snapshot keys that remain in OMAP.

Keep the fetch's purge target separate from the live fnode. Capture the OMAP header and removal set together under mds_lock, write the header in the final batch, and publish the watermark only after commit success. Preserve the target across outstanding fnode projections, and give purge work discovered after commit capture a later dirty version.

Only a full fetch without cached snapshot dentries or decoding errors can certify purge progress. Named-key reads may remove keys they examine but must not advance the watermark for the whole dirfrag.

Add CephFS regression coverage for journal replay before the removals are committed and for partial fetches followed by a full fetch. The tests use the existing fetch path and configuration, without readdir pipelining.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80496

71757.title: rgw: fix rgw_zone_create() returning after first zone spec
71757.author: joshjan20
71757.body:
rgw_zone_create() loops over rgw_specs to create each zone, but 'return created_zones' was nested inside the loop (inside 'if rgw_spec.rgw_zone is not None:'), so the function returned as soon as the first spec was successfully processed. Any additional specs in the list were never passed to RGWAM(...).zone_create() at all.

This is triggered by 'ceph rgw zone create -i <file>' when the input file contains multiple '---'-separated zone specs, a case explicitly supported by _parse_rgw_specs(). Only the first zone actually gets created, and the command still reports success, the caller (_cmd_rgw_zone_create) formats a pluralized message ('Zones ..., ... created successfully') that only makes sense if multiple zones can in fact be returned.

The sibling function _cmd_rgw_realm_bootstrap loops over all specs with no early return, the correct, established pattern this function should also follow.

Fixed by moving the return outside the loop, so every spec in rgw_specs is processed before the function returns.

Adds regression tests confirming all specs are processed (not just the first) when multiple zones are requested, and that the single-spec case continues to work correctly.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80499
Signed-off-by: joshjan20 <joshjan20@gmail.com>
Co-authored-by: Kobi Ginon <kginon@redhat.com>

71762.title: mds: purge snapshots from data pools removed via rm_data_pool
71762.author: dparmar18
71762.body:
When a data pool that still has references helds against its objects is removed
from a fs with `ceph fs rm_data_pool` before its snapshots are deleted,
SnapServer::_commit's destroy path iterates only the pools currently in the
mdsmap (data_pools). The removed pool is no longer listed there, so its snapids
are never added to need_to_purge and SnapServer::check_osd_map never asks the
mon (via MRemoveSnaps) to remove them. The snap trimmer therefore never trims
the clones, leaving orphaned clone and whiteout-head objects in the pool with
no cleanup path.

Therefore, track the file system's data pools in the SnapServer and on each
mdsmap update also record any pool that has left data_pools while snapshots
still exist, keyed by the last_snap at removal (the highest snapid that may
reference it). SnapServer::_commit then purges these removed-but-referenced
pools alongside the current data pools on every snapshot destroy, and drops a
pool once no live snapshot at or below its threshold remains. Both containers
persist in the SnapServer state, so the track record survives mds restart and
tableserver failover.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77438
Signed-off-by: Dhairya Parmar <dparmar@redhat.com>

71763.title: test/rgw: fix ENETUNREACH connecting to any-address acceptor on non-linux
71763.author: wjwithagen
71763.body:
The test `BeastFrontendShutdownClose, ShutdownsButDoesNotCloseSocket` 
binds its test acceptor to tcp::v4() (0.0.0.0) and then connects client sockets directly to` acceptor.local_endpoint()`. Linux silently rewrites a `connect()` to the any-address as a connect to 127.0.0.1, but this is Linux-specific behavior, not part of the POSIX socket API. FreeBSD's TCP stack correctly rejects 0.0.0.0 as a connect target and returns `ENETUNREACH`, causing the test to fail with:
```
  C++ exception with description "Network is unreachable
  [system:51 ...boost::asio::detail::reactive_socket_connect_op...]"
```
Bind the acceptor to the explicit loopback address instead of the any-address so `acceptor.local_endpoint()` returns a connectable endpoint on every platform. This does not change test semantics -- the acceptor still listens on an OS-assigned ephemeral port.

71764.title: common/TrackedOp: clamp negative op ages instead of wrapping to ~4.29e9
71764.author: dvanders
71764.body:
`OpTracker` samples `now` once, before taking the shard locks and walking the
in-flight lists. An op registered after that sample therefore has an initiation
time later than `now`, and because `utime_t` keeps seconds in a `__u32`, the
subtraction wraps instead of going negative: a -0.5ms age is reported as
`4294967295.99`.

On a busy daemon this is routine rather than an exotic race. It surfaces in four
places:

- `dump_historic_ops` / `ops` report `age: 4294967295.99`, so anything parsing
  those dumps sees a request that looks stuck for 136 years.
- `check_ops_in_flight()` can emit `slow request 4294967295.999526 seconds old`
  into the cluster log and the SLOW_REQUEST health detail.
- `dump_ops_in_flight(print_only_blocked=true)` treats a brand new op as blocked,
  because the wrapped age compares greater than `complaint_time`.
- `get_age_ms_histogram()` adds a ~4.29e9 ms sample to the histogram.

Clamped to zero at all four sites via a small file-local helper. An op's age
cannot meaningfully be negative.

Re-sampling the clock per op would also work and be marginally more accurate, but
it adds a clock read to a hot path walked under the shard locks, which does not
seem worth it to avoid a sub-millisecond skew.

Found while writing a tool that parses `dump_historic_ops` to attribute MDS
request latency; it reported a healthy-but-busy MDS as deadlocked.

Verified on a running MDS: 3725 ops sampled across 25 dumps under 16-client load,
zero wrapped ages, and a minimum observed age of exactly `0.0` -- i.e. the clamp
firing on the ops that previously read `4294967295.99`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80500

71766.title: os/bluestore: fix heap-use-after-free in ~FileWriter() on abrupt destruction
71766.author: wjwithagen
71766.body:
Running tests with unittest_bluefs fails on FreeBSD about 1 in 200... 
After some gdb sessions compiled the test with ASAN. 
And set
    `export ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_stack_use_after_return=1:abort_on_error=1:halt_on_error=1`

We see the following:
fsync() only submits aios via _flush_bdev(); it does not call _drain_writer()/aio_wait() and therefore does not guarantee that submitted aios have completed. close_writer() correctly drains before destroying the FileWriter, but a FileWriter destructed directly (e.g. process crash, or BlueFS_wal.wal_v2_simulate_crash's deliberate `delete writer` without close_writer(), which is a realistic simulation of an actual crash) skips this drain.

This leaves a race: KernelDevice::_aio_thread() can still be processing a completion (get_return_value() / try_aio_wake()) on an aio_t that ~FileWriter()'s IOContext teardown has already freed via the pending_aios/running_aios list destruction, producing a heap-use-after-free. Confirmed via AddressSanitizer with both an allocation-site and free-site stack trace pointing at KernelDevice::aio_write() vs. IOContext::~IOContext() from FileWriter::~FileWriter() called from
BlueFS_wal.wal_v2_simulate_crash. Also independently reproduced (via gdb core, mutex_debug_impl::try_lock_impl() -> EINVAL on a corrupted mutex) on two separate FreeBSD hosts.

Fix: call IOContext::aio_wait() on each iocv[] before deleting it in ~FileWriter(), mirroring what _drain_writer() already does for the close_writer() path. On the normal close_writer() path this is a no-op (num_running is already 0), so there is no performance impact; confirmed via unittest_bluefs/unittest_bluefs_ex timing before and after (no measurable difference) and 1000 iterations of wal_v2_simulate_crash under ASan with no further failures (previously failed within ~124 iterations).

This looks not to be FreeBSD-specific -- it's a generic lifecycle race in BlueFS/KernelDevice
FreeBSD's stricter libthr pthread implementation and ASan's instrumentation simply surface it more reliably than default Linux glibc/pthread timing.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80501

71767.title: tentacle: Bump NFS Version in Ceph
71767.author: fivetime
71767.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81803

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67906
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75630

## Why tentacle needs this

The tentacle image still installs NFS-Ganesha from the SIG `nfsganesha-5` repo, i.e. 5.9. Ganesha 5.9 answers `GET_DIR_DELEGATION` with `OP_ILLEGAL`, and Linux 6.19+ clients request directory delegations by default, so readdir on a CephNFS export fails intermittently with `EREMOTEIO`. The fix (nfs-ganesha issue 1385, returning `NFS4ERR_NOTSUPP`) is only in 9.11 and later; no 7.x or 8.x release has it.

Reproduction and before/after numbers from a 7.0 kernel client (5.9: 2 failures in 15 rounds of `ls`; 9.16: 0 in 60, with the `NOTSUPP` reply visible in the `nfs4_xdr_status` tracepoint on every mount) are in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80503.

The concern behind https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77291 (moving to 7.0 because of nfs-ganesha issue 1400) is fixed in `libntirpc-7.2-3`; production data for 9.16 with `libntirpc-7.2-5` on v20.2.4 is in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77291#note-2.

## Notes

- Straight `git cherry-pick -x` of the single commit in #67906; it applies cleanly to current tentacle and changes one line.
- The parent tracker is 75630 because that is the ticket whose "Pull request ID" is 67906, which is how the releng audit finds it. 80503 describes the user-visible bug.
- I am not a member of the Ceph organization, so CI needs someone to add `ci-approved`.

This replaces #71599, which was closed before the problem above was described.

71787.title: mgr: add perf counters and logging for GIL contention
71787.author: NitzanMordhai
71787.body:
Measures how long mgr threads wait for the GIL (average and max), counts
waits over 5ms, and logs a rate-limited sample of them with the module and
Python function involved. Waits are attributed to the module, either by
tagging the thread directly or, for threads a module starts itself, from
the outermost Python frame under mgr_module_path.
  
Also switches the remaining raw PyEval_SaveThread()/RestoreThread() pairs
to without_gil_t so their waits are counted.

### Example output

  `ceph daemon mgr.x perf dump mgr` on an idle vstart cluster:

  ```
  "mgr": {
      "gil_acquire_lat": {
          "avgcount": 79,
          "sum": 0.012754997,
          "max_inc": 0.004310491,
          "avgtime": 0.000161455
      },
      "gil_reacquire_lat": {
          "avgcount": 309,
          "sum": 0.054896731,
          "max_inc": 0.007915636,
          "avgtime": 0.000177659
      },
      "gil_slow_waits": 5
  }
  ```
  
  - `avgcount`/`avgtime`: how many waits and their average.
  - `max_inc`: the longest single wait.
  - `gil_slow_waits`: waits longer than 5ms.

The matching slow waits in the mgr log (`debug_mgr 20`):

  ```
  mgr log_slow_wait without_gil_t::acquire_gil: module 'progress' waited 0.005956708s for the GIL, python frame: config_notify (src/pybind/mgr/progress/module.py:502)
  mgr log_slow_wait without_gil_t::acquire_gil: module 'prometheus' waited 0.006342889s for the GIL, python frame: __init__ (src/pybind/mgr/prometheus/module.py:834)
  mgr log_slow_wait without_gil_t::acquire_gil: module 'prometheus' waited 0.005969628s for the GIL, python frame: __init__ (src/pybind/mgr/prometheus/module.py:834)
  mgr log_slow_wait without_gil_t::acquire_gil: module 'progress' waited 0.007915636s for the GIL, python frame: config_notify (src/pybind/mgr/progress/module.py:502)
  mgr log_slow_wait without_gil_t::acquire_gil: module 'progress' waited 0.007898027s for the GIL, python frame: config_notify (src/pybind/mgr/progress/module.py:502)
  ```
  
  The 0.007915636s wait from `progress` is the `max_inc` shown in the dump.
  
  At `debug_mgr 5`, at most one of these lines is logged per second. Each one
  also says how many slow waits were skipped since the last line, and the
  longest of them with its module.


Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78711

71802.title: mds: block client mutations when the journal grows too big
71802.author: joscollin
71802.body:
When client sessions stall and prevent journal trimming, the MDS journal
can grow without bound. Replaying an oversized journal uses unbounded
memory and can crash the MDS.

This adds mds_log_hard_limit_factor. When the journal reaches the hard
limit, which is the factor times mds_log_max_segments, new client
mutating requests are parked until trimming brings the journal back
under the limit. The hard limit is kept above the warn threshold, so
MDS_TRIM is raised before clients are blocked. Between the warn threshold
and the hard limit, new mutations are delayed in proportion to the backlog.

While the limit is reached, the MDS raises MDS_JOURNAL_HARD_LIMIT as a
health error, and the monitor refuses "mds fail" and "fs fail" unless
--yes-i-really-mean-it is given.

This also fixes a trim stall. Expired segments waiting for a major segment
were counted as already gone, so trim stopped at the ceiling and the
journal stayed above max_segments.

QA: adds tasks.cephfs.test_journal_limits. It checks that a create blocks
while the limit is held, that MDS_JOURNAL_HARD_LIMIT is raised, that mds
fail is refused and the refusal names the new code, and that parked creates
complete once trimming resumes.

Known limitations: MDS_TRIM is always raised with the hard limit, so the
integration test cannot isolate the monitor's refusal logic. Steady-state
trimming can differ slightly from before when expired segments are waiting
for the next major segment. 

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73868

71813.title: crimson/osd: fix throttle deadlock between client and background ops
71813.author: mohit84
71813.body:
When crimson_osd_scheduler_concurrency is set, client and background ops 
share the same OperationThrottler slot pool (max_in_progress). 
This causes a circular deadlock:

  - Client ops hold slots waiting for replica acks (wait_repop/SendReply)
  - Background ops (RecoverySubRequest, RepRequest) need slots to
    deliver those acks
  - All slots consumed → permanent deadlock

Additionally, budget_available() in BudgetBlocked state incorrectly
returns false when budget_retry_releaser already holds a slot, causing
an infinite BudgetBlocked → BudgetAvailable → BudgetBlocked loop

71814.title: tools/ceph-dencoder: link librados
71814.author: Doracly
71814.body:
## `ceph-dencoder` is missing `librados`

`ceph-dencoder` links `cls_log_client` and friends, which are declared with a bare
`add_library(... STATIC ...)` and no `target_link_libraries`, so they rely on consumers
to supply `librados`. This stays latent: nothing in `ceph_dencoder.cc` references them,
so their archive members are normally never extracted. Once one is pulled in, its
`librados::ObjectOperation` references are undefined.

## How this was found

`ninja tests` fails to link `ceph-dencoder` with mold, with both clang and GCC. The same
command lines link with GNU ld 2.46 and lld 21.1.8, which do not extract these members.
With this commit, it links under mold as well.

mold's behaviour was reported as https://github.com/rui314/mold/issues/1657 and is fixed
upstream (not yet released); the dependency is still worth declaring, as older mold versions
will be around for a while.

## Testing

Debug build with clang 21.1.8 and mold 2.40.4: without this commit, `ninja tests`
fails to link `ceph-dencoder` with undefined `librados::ObjectOperation` references;
with it, it links and `ceph-dencoder list_types` lists 666 types. A GCC 15 build with
mold fails the same way without the fix.

Dashboard MOTD expiration accepts values such as `2days` and `1d2h`, but silently interprets them as `2d` and `1d`. This can expire a message earlier than the supplied duration suggests.

71824.title: rgw/kvrgw:
71824.author: benhanokh
71824.body:
KV-RGW: S3 Server over FoundationDB.

## Summary
A new model for RGW that replaces RADOS head objects with entries in an external KV store, decoupling S3 object identity from storage-tier naming.

 - DB-Agnostic KV Contract: Defines key formats, value structures, and operations, with FoundationDB (FDB) and TiKV as reference examples.
  - No Bucket-Index: Enables listing via KV range scans, eliminating dual updates and resharding.
  - Atomic KV Transactions: Replaces multiple non-atomic operations across BI, Head Objects, OLH, Storage Tier, and Tail Objects.
  - Decoupled Storage Tier: Decouples RGW from the storage tier, allowing the data store to function as a simple blob store (write, read-range, punch-hole).

## Motivation
The 1:1 mapping between S3 objects and RADOS objects creates
compounding problems:
- small-object overhead
- versioning complexity(OLH)
- EC metadata amplification
- costly deletes
- bucket-index as a secondary mechanism with all its pain
- storage-tier lock-in.

RGW already uses head objects as a de facto KV system — this design replaces them with areal one.

# Benefits
 - Simplify PUT and Put-Overwrite
 - Eliminates the versions cost and enables unlimited versions per-object
 - Decouples Data from MD (removes EC metadata amplification)
 - Inexpensive deletes
 - No bucket-index overhead
   - Enables unlimited objects per-bucket
   - Efficient Scalable Listing 
 - Full Data sharing for S3-Copy and Dedup
 - Supports S3-Rename naturally 
 - Support multiple storage-tiers/classes in parallel
 - Enables Small object packing (TBD)
 - Opens the door for S3-Over-RDMA of unstructured data (where obj-size is unknown at GET time) 

## Status
The POC is now functional and ready for testing. 
Performance testing indicates that it surpasses current RGW over RADOS performance, with mutation and listing of small objects showing an order of magnitude increase in speed.

Supported S3 commands:
 • CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, HeadBucket, ListBuckets
 • PutObject (incl. x-amz-tagging)
 • GetObject (incl. byte-range)
 • HeadObject
 • ListObjects, ListObjectsV2
 • DeleteObject, DeleteObjects
 • CopyObject
 • PutObjectTagging, GetObjectTagging, DeleteObjectTagging
 • PutBucketVersioning, GetBucketVersioning
 • GetObject --version-id
 • DeleteObject with --version-id
 • ListObjectVersions
 • Conditional Operations (Conditional Write, Conditional Read, Conditional Delete)
 • Multipart - (create-multipart-upload, upload-part, complete-multipart-upload, list-multipart-uploads, list-parts, abort-multipart-upload, Conditional Operations, versions )

Stub / not stored:
- GET ?acl (static XML for s3cmd info). 
- ACL and ownership APIs are no-ops or disabled (DisableACLs). 
- PutBucketPolicy, GetBucketPolicy, DeleteBucketPolicy
 
Not supported:
- encryption
- object lock
- lifecycle
- ACLs

## Key components include:
 - libkvrgw.so: 
 The C++ S3 engine provided as a shared library containing FDB metadata, the blob DataStore, sweeper/GC, and the admin socket.
 - kv-rgw-backend --perf: 
 A CLI driver for the engine used for benchmarking (bypassing S3 frontend).
 It runs a stdin command loop calling KvRgwServiceImpl directly without HTTP or versitygw.
  Using --perf uses PerfDataStore (no real disk) to isolate FDB/metadata measurement.
 - Frontend: A versitygw Go frontend exposes the S3 API, with Nginx load-balancing front-ends on port 9080.

Dependencies:
 - versitygw (https://github.com/versity/versitygw) is not vendored.
 This repository implements versitygw's Backend in frontend/ and calls libkvrgw.so.
 It is pinned in frontend/go.mod and downloaded during go build.
 - FoundationDB (https://github.com/apple/foundationdb/releases) is not built from this repo.
 Use upstream 7.3 client+server RPMs extracted into third_party/fdb/ (see scripts/fetch_fdb.sh). CMake links libfdb_c.so; reload.sh runs fdbserver from that tree via docker. 
 Download FoundationDB 7.

71826.title: qa: restructure erasure-code thrash suites with pool-config separation
71826.author: CJamesIBM
71826.body:
### **Summary**

Consolidates 6 separate erasure-code thrash suite directories into two unified suites (`thrash-erasure-code`and `thrash-erasure-code-big`) by introducing a 'pool-config' approach which separates pool/profile configuration from workload definitions. This enables a proper teuthology matrix expansion across all EC Profiles and optimization flags without unnecessary duplication.

**_Note:_**`thrash-erasure-code-big` remains as a unique suite as it was the only one using a different cluster setup. Interestingly, despite it's name, the cluster it uses is actually smaller.

### **Motivation**

Previously, the test suite has 6 independent `thrash-erasure-code-*` directories:

| Old Suite | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `thrash-erasure-code` | Default jerasure profiles |
| `thrash-erasure-code-big` | Different cluster with select profiles |
| `thrash-erasure-code-isa` | ISA plugin profiles (x86_64-only) |
| `thrash-erasure-code-shec` | SHEC plugin |
| `thrash-erasure-code-overwrites` | Overwrite-enabled pools |
| `thrash-erasure-code-crush-4-nodes` | CRUSH rule variants |

Each suite duplicated the same cluster setups, thrasher configs, mon election/msgr-failures/objectstore/recovery-overrides setup, and `ec_optimizations` on/off toggles. Adding a new profile or workload required editing multiple directories. 

### **What Changed**

**New `pool-config` override mechanism (`rados.py`, `radosbench.py`)**

Both task files now support a `use-pool-config: true` key. When set, pool configuration (`ec_pool`, `erasure_code_profile`, `erasure_code_crush`, `erasure_code_overwrites`, `fast_read`, `min_size`) is read from `overrides.ceph.pool-config` in the teuthology context rather than being hardcoded in each workload YAML. Task level config still takes precedence over `pool-config ` values.

### **New shared profile library (`qa/erasure-code-profile/`)**

18 profile YAML files for various plugin/parameter combinations. Each file writes into o`verrides.ceph.pool-config`. ISA profiles include the `arch: x86_64` guard. These are the source for all profile definitions - suite level profile files are symlinks back to here.

### **New shared matrix (`qa/erasure-code/)`**

- `%` 
- `ec_optimizations/`
  - `off/` — `off.yaml` + `profile/` symlinks (18 profiles)
  - `on/` — `on.yaml` + `profile/` symlinks (15 profiles)
- `fast/`
  - `fast.yaml` — `fast_read: true`
  - `normal.yaml` — `fast_read: false`

### **Unified `thrash-erasure-code` suite**

The suite now has a single `erasure-code` dimension (a symlink to `qa/erasure-code/`) which expands as a full matrix across all 18 profiles `x` 2 optimization states `x` 2 `fast_read` states. The old workloads that embedded profile configuration inline (e.g. `ec-rados-plugin=jerasure-k=2-m=1.yaml`) are replaced with 7 generic workloads that defer to `pool-config.`

| New Workload | Replaces |
|---|---|
| `rados-default.yaml` | `ec-rados-plugin=*.yaml` (profile-specific workloads) |
| `rados-small-obj.yaml` | `ec-small-objects.yaml`, `ec-small-objects-fast-read.yaml` |
| `rados-small-obj-delete.yaml` | `ec-small-objects-many-deletes.yaml` |
| `rados-bench.yaml` | `ec-radosbench.yaml` |
| `rados-overwrites.yaml` | `ec-small-objects-overwrites.yaml` (from overwrites suite) |
| `rados-snaps-overwrites.yaml` | `ec-snaps-few-objects-overwrites.yaml` |
| `rados-pool-snaps-overwrites.yaml` | `ec-pool-snaps-few-objects-overwrites.yaml` |

### **Restructured `thrash-erasure-code-big` suite**

Retains its own inline `erasure-code/ec_optimizations/` tree with a reduced profile set (profiles compatible with a 12-OSD cluster), but profile files are now symlinks to `qa/erasure-code-profile/` rather than inline copies. The old inline `workloads/` with per-profile files is replaced with a single `rados-default.yaml` using `use-pool-config: true`.

### **Removed suites**

`thrash-erasure-code-isa`, `thrash-erasure-code-shec`, `thrash-erasure-cod

service_id: all-available-devices
service_name: osd.all-available-devices

  - aartikl-2

71836.title: cmake: add sysctl(hw.physmem)/core-count fallbacks and clang memory tuning for FreeBSD
71836.author: wjwithagen
71836.body:
cmake_host_system_information() can return 0 or an unusable value for
TOTAL_PHYSICAL_MEMORY and NUMBER_OF_LOGICAL_CORES on FreeBSD. Add
FreeBSD-specific fallbacks that query sysctl directly when the cmake
query fails, and reserve 15% headroom for OS/filesystem cache pressure
(ZFS ARC in particular doesn't reliably shrink fast enough under
sudden build-time memory pressure).

Also lower MAX_COMPILE_MEM/MAX_LINK_MEM when building with clang
(using the CLANG variable introduced in wip-clang-copy-dt-needed):
upstream's 3500/4500 MiB defaults are tuned against gcc, and were
observed causing real swap thrashing under clang at the default pool
depth. 1800/1000 MiB is an empirically-derived correction from one
machine's workload; revisit if jobs still end up swapping.

Depends on wip-clang-copy-dt-needed for the CLANG variable.
https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71836

71840.title: cmake: use -Og for C and Clang 21+ debug builds
71840.author: Doracly
71840.body:
Debug builds compiled C files and all Clang code at `-O0`; only GCC C++ got `-Og` (since 8e742424a7f).

- Clang 21's `-Og` adds `-fextend-variable-liveness`, which keeps user variables live through the optimizer. Before 21, Clang's `-Og` is just `-O1`, so Clang 16-20 stay at `-O0`.
- C files now get `-Og` too, with both compilers. For example, gf-complete's SIMD region multiply (used by the jerasure plugin) runs about 15x faster than at `-O0`, and CRUSH's `crush_do_rule` about 1.3x (GCC 15.2, Ceph's compile flags for those files). The C and C++ compilers are checked separately, since they can differ.
- At `-Og`, GCC can't honor xxHash's `always_inline` hints (Cyan4973/xxHash#943), so `xxhash.c` would fail to build. Debug builds now define `XXH_NO_INLINE_HINTS` for C, as xxHash recommends; rgw already defines it for its C++ users.

`-DCMAKE_<LANG>_FLAGS_DEBUG=-O0` still overrides the default. GCC's C++ compile lines are unchanged, and CI's clang-19 builds are unaffected.

Tested with GCC 15.2 and Clang 21.1.8: in Debug, all C files get `-Og` with both compilers, and Ceph's C++ files get it with Clang 21 too; Release keeps `-O3`. All C files compile at `-Og` with both compilers. The only new diagnostic is a GCC `-Wunused-result` warning in `libcephfs_proxy/libcephfsd.c`; C isn't built with `-Werror`.

71849.title: jfw rgw op fusion combined
71849.author: chardan
71849.body:
Refactors RGW operation and REST dispatch paths to reduce repeated branching, avoid
avoidable string copies, and split related operation families out of rgw_op.cc.

  - centralizes HTTP argument classification and enables string_view/transparent lookup
  - avoids extra copies in root S3 POST action parsing
  - simplifies REST manager resource routing
  - splits ACL, forwarding, object-attrs, and object-lock code out of rgw_op.cc

```
Area                                      Speed vs. Baseline   Allocations vs. Baseline
HTTP long-key get() via string_view       54.4% faster         100% fewer, -1 alloc/op
Cached exists("uploadId")                 98.3% faster         unchanged, 0 allocs/op
Cached sub_resource_exists("uploadId")    98.3% faster         unchanged, 0 allocs/op
HTTP arg classification on append         57.4% faster         unchanged
REST route, empty frontend prefix         75.8% faster         50% fewer, -1 alloc/op
REST route, nonempty frontend prefix      52.5% faster         unchanged
Root S3 POST action parse                 76.9% faster         76.5% fewer, -26 allocs/op
```

Cleanups:
rgw_op.cc is massive and terrifying. This steps toward cleaning it up:
* rgw_op_acl.cc‎ - moves ACL operations out of rgw_op.cc
* rgw_op_forward.cc: isolates multisite forward-to-master helper
* rgw_op_obj_attrs.cc: isolates RGWGetObjAttrs 
* rgw_op_obj_lock.cc: isolates bucket/object lock operations
* rgw_op_internal.h: adds private cross-file helpers 

Tests:
RGW tests: adds focused C++ coverage for REST routing, HTTP args, POST parsing, and tar EOF behavior.

Supercedes:
https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70676

71860.title: mgr: skip pickling for remote() calls within the same interpreter
71860.author: NitzanMordhai
71860.body:
mgr_subinterpreter_modules defaults to empty, so almost every mgr
module shares the main Python interpreter. Despite that,
MgrModule.remote() always pickled args/kwargs and the return value,
and spun up a temporary PyThreadState for the call, regardless of
whether caller and callee were actually in different interpreters.

Add PyModule::shares_interpreter() to detect when caller and target
share an interpreter, and a direct-dispatch path
(ActivePyModule::dispatch_remote_direct(), reached via
ActivePyModules::shares_interpreter()) that calls the target method
directly under the already-held GIL in that case, skipping both the
pickling and the thread-state churn. The existing pickled path is
unchanged for genuinely cross-interpreter calls.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78710

During upgrade, the auth_allowed_ciphers setting was being changed without considering the currently configured ciphers. This behavior added aes cipher to auth_allowed_ciphers when auth_allowed_ciphers was set as only aes256k is currently in use.
This introduced unnecessary health warnings when upgrading, for example, from squid-19.2.6 to tentacle-20.2.4

Modify the upgrade logic to check if 'aes' is in the current ciphers: if present, use all ALLOWED_CIPHERS; otherwise use only SERVICE_CIPHER. This preserves existing cipher configurations during the upgrade.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80295

When the cluster already allowed the legacy 'aes' cipher before the

71866.title: cephadm: keep mgr ports in sync when modules are enabled/disabled
71866.author: yaelazulay-redhat
71866.body:
ceph orch ps  - was showing stale or incorrect port information for `mgr` daemons after enabling or disabling mgr modules (e.g., dashboard, prometheus). This fix ensures the displayed ports always reflect the actual active module endpoints.

Code Fixes:
-----------
Changes in src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/services/cephadmservice.py:
- Extract and refactor _get_mgr_service_ports: The logic for reading active mgr module ports was inline inside prepare_create, using check_mon_command({'prefix': 'mgr services'}). It was extracted into a static helper method and refactored to read directly from mgr.get('mgr_map')['services'] instead -- which is faster and consistent with how get_dependencies reads the same data. The method is now shared by both prepare_create (existing use) and get_dependencies (new use).

- Extract `_get_mgr_service_ports`: The logic for reading active mgr module ports from `mgr_map['services']` was inline inside `prepare_create`. It was extracted into a static helper method so it can be reused by both `prepare_create` (existing use) and `get_dependencies` (new use). Returns the port numbers currently registered by active mgr modules (e.g., `[8443, 9283]`).

-  Override `get_dependencies` in `MgrService`: The base class returns `[]` for all Ceph daemons. The serve loop compares `get_dependencies()` output against `last_deps` (saved after the previous reconfig). If they differ, a reconfig is triggered. By overriding this method in `MgrService`, we make the serve loop aware of mgr port changes. Returns a sorted list such as `['port:8443', 'port:9283', 'sd_port:8765']`.

- Override `generate_config` in `MgrService`: After a reconfig completes, the result of `generate_config` is saved as `last_deps`. The inherited implementation returns `[]` as deps. If `[]` is saved but `get_dependencies` returns `['port:8443', 'sd_port:8765']`, they would always differ, causing an infinite reconfig loop. This override ensures that what is saved as `last_deps` matches what `get_dependencies` will return in the next iteration.

Changes in `src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/serve.py`:

- Update mgr cache on reconfig: The existing logic skipped the cache update for all Ceph daemon reconfigs. A new `elif` branch for mgr reconfigs fetches the existing cached `DaemonDescription`, updates only its `ports` field, and saves it back. This makes `ceph orch ps` reflect the correct ports immediately after a reconfig, without showing a misleading "starting" status.

Changes in `src/cephadm/cephadm.py`:

- Update `unit.meta` on reconfig: `unit.meta` is a per-daemon file on the host that stores metadata including ports.  It is read periodically by `cephadm ls` and fed back into the orchestrator cache. Previously it was only written on initial deployment, so every periodic cache refresh would overwrite the corrected ports with stale data from `unit.meta`. This change updates the `ports` field in `unit.meta` during reconfig, ensuring the cache refresh confirms the correct state rather than reverting it.

Changes to src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/tests/services/test_mgr.py:

- Updated _prepare helper: The original mocked check_mon_command to feed services data to prepare_create. Since our _get_mgr_service_ports now reads from mgr.get('mgr_map') instead of check_mon_command, the mock was replaced with mock_store_set('_ceph_get', 'mgr_map', ...) which sets the data in the right place.

- Added test_get_dependencies_changes_when_module_enabled: A new test that verifies get_dependencies returns different dep strings before and after a module is enabled. This directly tests the core sync mechanism -- the serve loop compares get_dependencies output against last_deps to detect port changes and trigger a reconfig.

to run new tests:
cd src/pybind/mgr
tox -e py3 -- cephadm/tests/services/test_mgr.py -v

backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80072
possibly a backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69043

71870.title: mgr: mgr thrasher for teuthology - and expend testing covarage for mgr
71870.author: NitzanMordhai
71870.body:
We already thrash OSDs and mons, but nothing thrashes the mgr. This
adds a task that does the same thing mon_thrash does: kill or fail
over a mgr, check that another one takes over, then bring the killed
one back as a standby. It uses ThrasherGreenlet (like mds_thrash and
rbd_mirror_thrash) so it can stop right away instead of waiting out a
full revive_delay when the test ends.

Also checks the mgr modules still work after each round: self-tests
still pass, calls between modules still work, and nothing that was
enabled gets disabled along the way (including always-on modules like
crash and devicehealth, which needed special handling since 'mgr
module ls' lists them separately).

Adds kill_mgr()/fail_mgr() to CephManager, next to revive_mgr().

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78712

71877.title: smb: support checking case sensitivity settings of a cephfs volume
71877.author: phlogistonjohn
71877.body:
Currently based on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71504 for testing purposes. Main code is independent of that PR however.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80799

Add a new option to the cephfs share configuration to detect and either warn on or reject (sub)volumes that are not configured as case-insensitive. 
The resource spec gains a new option `case_insensitive` with values of `warn`, `ignore`, or `require`. When set to warn (the default - a backwards compatible option) it will add warnings to the resource results that are emitted by the apply or share create commands. Ignore simply ignores the case sensitivity of the subvolume (similar to the current behavior). The require option will reject any subvolumes that are not case insensitive and produce an error rather than a warning (failing any update operation).

An imperative command line switch --case-insenstive is added for the share create command.

Unit and integration tests are included.  

Example of a warning on a resource + a warnings summary block from the `apply` command:
```
   ...

  {
      "resource": {
        "resource_type": "ceph.smb.share",
        "cluster_id": "cluster1",
        "share_id": "subvol",
        "intent": "present",
        "name": "Sub Volume",
        "readonly": false,
        "browseable": true,
        "cephfs": {
          "volume": "cephfs",
          "path": "/",
          "subvolumegroup": "g1",
          "subvolume": "sv1",
          "provider": "samba-vfs"
        },
        "acl_support": "disabled"
      },
      "state": "created",
      "warnings": [
        "CephFS subvolume is case sensitive; case insensitive mode is recommended"
      ],
      "success": true
    }
  ],
  "success": true,
  "warnings_summary": {
    "count": 1,
    "recap": [
      "CephFS subvolume is case sensitive; case insensitive mode is recommended"
    ]
  }
}
```
The warnings recap exists to help readers avoid missing a warning is many resoruces are being operated on at once. If the number of warnings exceeds a fixed value (5) it will add a special message to the recap to indicate that more warnings are present and the section for each resource should be reviewed.

71883.title: common,auth,msg: fix portability problems a stricter toolchain turns up
71883.author: dvanders
71883.body:
Split out of #71232, which reviewers asked to see in smaller batches.
This is the first of seven; it is based on main and does not depend on
any of the others.

Nothing here is macOS-specific — there is not a single platform
conditional in the series. These are things the tree gets away with under
libstdc++ and a slightly older clang, and which a stricter standard
library or a newer compiler rejects:

- headers that relied on an include arriving transitively
- `BoundedKeyCounter`'s nested iterator not satisfying the C++20 iterator
  concepts it is used through
- `SimpleRADOSStriper::truncate` declared with a signature the definition
  does not match
- `CachedStackStringStream`'s cache as a function-local static in a header
- `std::execution::seq` passed to an algorithm overload that does not take
  an execution policy

Each is a single self-contained commit.  (A seventh, making
`platform_errno.h` includable from C, was dropped: #71442 made the same
change.)

71886.title: libcephfs_proxy: build it on Linux only
71886.author: dvanders
71886.body:
Split out of #71232, which reviewers asked to see in smaller batches.
Based on main; independent of the other six.

`libcephfsd` shares a single libcephfs mount between processes over a Unix
socket and is written to Linux throughout: it marshals fscrypt's UAPI
structures by size from `<linux/fscrypt.h>`, holds an unnamed file open
with `O_TMPFILE` and names it later with `linkat(AT_EMPTY_PATH)`, and asks
`recvmsg()` for `MSG_CMSG_CLOEXEC`. None of that has a Darwin spelling, and
`O_TMPFILE` and `AT_EMPTY_PATH` are absent on FreeBSD too, so the component
cannot have been building anywhere but Linux.

Gate it the way the mount helper immediately above it in
`src/CMakeLists.txt` already is, rather than spreading conditionals through
it — @phlogistonjohn's suggestion on #71232, and the right one.

Two fixes come along because neither is about Darwin:

- `cephfs_proxy` compiles `proxy_helpers.c`, which hashes with EVP, so it
  needs OpenSSL; only the daemon was being given it
- `<endian.h>` was included in two files that use nothing from it, while
  `<limits.h>`, which `proxy_mount.c` takes `PATH_MAX` from, was not
  included at all

71888.title: common,osd,rgw: fill in the Darwin side of the compatibility layer
71888.author: dvanders
71888.body:
Split out of #71232, which reviewers asked to see in smaller batches.
Based on main; independent of the other six. The macOS build also needs
@tchaikov's #72482 (endian macros) and #72484 (unversioned object class
libraries).

`src/include/compat.h` and friends already carry a Darwin branch; it is
just missing pieces. This fills them in, and fixes a few things that are
not additions:

- `compat.h`: the definitions the Darwin branch was missing, the `fadvise`
  fallback, and `ENOKEY`; `numa.h` including it for `cpu_set_t`
- `compat.cc`: `__STDC_WANT_LIB_EXT1__` defined before the first
  `<string.h>`, not after
- `blkdev.cc`: the three helpers the Darwin branch does not define
- `tcp_info.cc`: stubbed, as on Windows — Darwin's
  `struct tcp_connection_info` shares no fields with Linux' `tcp_info`
- `admin_socket.cc`: the raise hook gated on a new `HAVE_TIMER_CREATE`
  rather than on `!WIN32`, since POSIX per-process timers are what it
  actually needs; where they are absent, `raise --after` fails with
  `-ENOTSUP` (as on Windows) and the corresponding tests are skipped
- `auth/Crypto.cc`: the `/dev/urandom` fallback opened in the right
  namespace
- `rgw_file`: two reads of the stat timespecs going through the same
  `HAVE_STAT_ST_MTIMESPEC_TV_NSEC` guard the writes in the same file
  already use

The `entity_addr_t` encoding fix on the BSDs that was here has been
dropped in favour of @wjwithagen's #71445, which fixes it the same way.
Likewise the Darwin endian fallbacks and a `ClassHandler.cc` change to skip
versioned `libcls_*.dylib` names, in favour of #72482 and #72484, which
remove the need for them.

71889.title: macos: build and run Ceph natively on Apple silicon
71889.author: dvanders
71889.body:
The last of the seven PRs #71232 was split into. Based on main and
mergeable on its own, but it is the one that only means something with
the other six in: #71883, #71884, #71885, #71886, #71887, #71888.

The goal is a local vstart cluster on a MacBook, so Ceph development can
happen there without a Linux VM. With the full series the client
libraries, the mon, the OSD (memstore only), the mgr, the MDS, the RGW and
the offline tools build with Apple clang, and `vstart.sh --memstore`
brings all five daemons up. RADOS, RBD, S3 and CephFS through `ceph-fuse`
all work against it. BlueStore is out of scope: it needs libaio or
io_uring and the Linux block layer.

What is here:

- `arch/arm.c`: probe the ARM CPU features through `sysctl` on Darwin,
  which has no `getauxval` — this is what actually enables hardware crc32c
  and NEON gf-complete once #71887 has cmake recognising arm64
- `FindFUSE.cmake` and `client/fuse_ll.cc`: build `ceph-fuse` against
  macFUSE, which ships the vanilla libfuse3 API rather than the old
  Darwin-specific one the `__APPLE__` branches assumed
- `do_cmake_macos.sh`: a configure helper, companion to `do_freebsd.sh`
- `doc/dev/macos.rst`: rewritten. The page still described a 2018 build —
  a brew clang because Xcode's was too old for C++17, hand-written paths
  into `/usr/local/Cellar`, and the conclusion that FUSE and librados
  applications were the practical uses. None of that holds.

The doc covers the dependencies, the submodules that must not be cloned
shallow, the extra packages the mgr, the MDS and the RGW each want, and
the handful of Darwin behaviours that read as bugs the first time: a full
memstore looking like a hang, mgr commands hanging when no mgr is running,
and radosgw aborting in the Objective-C runtime because it forks without
exec.

71895.title: mgr/dashboard: yield GIL in NotificationQueue after each batch
71895.author: afreen23
71895.body:
NotificationQueue.run() drains its queue and notifies listeners in a tight loop without ever releasing the GIL. Under burst conditions (e.g. cluster-log events) this causes GIL convoy behavior where other mgr module threads wait 400ms+ for a turn.

Add time.sleep(0) after each batch of notifications to force a GIL release, capping the uninterrupted hold time to one batch regardless of queue depth.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80547

71901.title: cmake: add WITH_PCH option to build with precompiled headers
71901.author: Doracly
71901.body:
Adds `WITH_PCH`, an opt-in precompiled header (PCH) for the targets measured
to benefit from one. A core payload of `std`, `fmt`, `boost` and Ceph
infrastructure headers goes to all of them; `rgw`, `osd`, `mon`, `mds`,
`librbd`, `rbd-mirror` and the latter two's unit tests add a few of their own
entry headers, such as `mon/Monitor.h`. The header lists, the per-target
figures and the rule for adding an entry are at the end of `src/CMakeLists.txt`.

In a Debug build it takes about 30% off the compile CPU of a whole build with
Clang and about 15% with GCC, with or without tests; the listed targets lose a
quarter to two thirds with Clang and a tenth to over a third with GCC. With
Clang, ASAN and TSAN builds gain about the same. The PCHs add about 2GB to the
build tree with Clang and 9GB with GCC.

The option defaults to OFF, so CI and ordinary builds still compile without a
PCH and keep catching translation units that stopped including what they use.
With `WITH_PCH=OFF` nothing changes.

### Compilers and caches

`WITH_PCH` supports Clang and GCC; `cmake` refuses it with any other compiler.

ccache caches objects built against a PCH only with `pch_defines` and
`time_macros` in its sloppiness. With `WITH_CCACHE`, the PCH targets compile
through a small generated script that appends both to `CCACHE_SLOPPINESS`
without touching `ccache.conf`; all other targets and external projects keep
plain ccache. Clang also gets `-Xclang -fno-pch-timestamp` with `WITH_CCACHE`,
or every rebuilt PCH would make the objects built against it miss.

GCC needs two more fixes (gcc 15.2, ccache 4.12.3, sccache 0.13.0):

- After a change to a macro only, ccache and sccache could return the old PCH:
  CMake builds it from a stub source, both caches can key on its preprocessed
  text, and that has no `#define`s. ccache guards against this for Clang only.
  `-dD` on the PCH targets puts the `#define`s into that text; it doesn't
  change objects.
- ccache hashes the old `.gch` as an input of the compile replacing it, and
  GCC's PCH differs on every build, so every PCH rebuild in an existing tree
  made all objects of the target miss. The script deletes the old `.gch` first.

sccache needs neither the script nor `-fno-pch-timestamp`.

CMake marks its PCH header as a system header, which hides the warnings of
every header in the payload. `WITH_PCH` empties `CMAKE_PCH_PROLOGUE`, so they
are reported as without a PCH.

A PCH is built with its target's compile settings, and the compiler can use it
for a source file whose own settings differ, without a warning. Such files are
therefore compiled without the PCH: `rgw/rgw_iam_policy.cc` (an include
directory), `common/version.cc` (a definition) and, with GCC,
`common/config.cc` and `common/options.cc` (`-fno-var-tracking-assignments`).

The first two commits fix what a PCH exposes: `mon/ConfigMap.cc` relied on
including `common/dout.h` after `#undef dout_prefix` to restore the default,
but the PCH has already included it; `MergeDiff.cc` redefined
`_LARGEFILE64_SOURCE` after the PCH's `<features.h>` had set it, which warns.

### Testing

- Clang: compiled IR of all ~1,200 translation units built against a PCH,
  Debug and Release, compared with the build without it: no difference changes
  behaviour. Unit tests give the same results with and without PCH, also in
  ASAN and TSAN builds. With ccache, a rebuild is served entirely from the
  cache, and a changed macro in a payload rebuilds the PCH and its users.
- GCC: with a macro defined only in a payload header and checked by a
  `static_assert`, macro-only changes, switching back, `touch` and real
  changes all build correctly with ccache and with sccache; without `-dD`,
  both return the stale PCH. A fresh tree is served entirely from ccache,
  byte-identical to the cold build.

No CI job exercises this code, deliberately: some build has to compile without
a PCH.

Measured on one machine (AMD Ryz

71902.title: cmake: use a scratch object in CMakeFiles for the nasm probes
71902.author: wjwithagen
71902.body:
https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71121 switched the nasm probes in CheckNasm.cmake from writing
to /dev/null to mktemp-generated temp files, so nasm cannot delete
/dev/null on a failed probe when running as root.

It uses `mktemp --suffix=.o`, a GNU coreutils extension. On FreeBSD
(and other systems with a BSD mktemp) configure fails with:

    mktemp: unrecognized option --suffix=.o

The temp files are also never removed, so every configure leaves
three files behind in /tmp.

This drops mktemp altogether: all three probes write to a fixed
scratch object in CMakeFiles, which is removed after the probes.
The /dev/null protection stays, and nothing is left behind.

Tested on FreeBSD 14.4 and 15.1 (clang 19): configure succeeds,
the nasm capability messages are unchanged, and no temp files remain.

References: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79569
References: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71121

71920.title: mds: fix missing entries in readdir_snapdiff replies
71920.author: LiShengG
71920.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes five MDS `readdir_snapdiff` reply-handling bugs that
can omit entries from snapshot diffs:

- Preserve the encoded entry count when discarding a new entry
  without rolling back the previous name group.
- Report dirfrag completion only after all entries, including any
  pending deletion, have been emitted.
- Set the existing `waiting` out-parameter when opening an uncached
  remote inode so the request stays pending instead of receiving an
  empty reply. Also avoid dereferencing the missing inode in the
  debug log.
- Send the first same-name group of a reply whole even if it exceeds
  the byte budget, instead of rolling it back into an empty, non-final
  reply that leaves the client without a resume position.
- Roll back a same-name group that an uncached remote dentry would
  otherwise split across two replies, so that the replacement entry
  is not skipped.

The fixes are split into five commits, with regression coverage for each case.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80635
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80639
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80640
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81447
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81506

71921.title: mds: report intra-object shrink in file blockdiff
71921.author: LiShengG
71921.body:
`MDCache::aggregate_snap_sets()` sized each changed object extent from the newer clone. When a file is truncated inside an object and then grown back without rewriting, the discarded tail lies beyond the newer clone's size and is omitted from blockdiff, so a cephfs-mirror peer keeps stale bytes in that range while the file sizes still match.

Size the extent from the larger of the two clones, and clamp the aggregated extents to the newer snapshot's EOF so that a shrink does not report ranges past the end of file.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79753
