72093.title: librbd: don't wait for in-flight reads in diff-iterate
72093.author: tchaikov
72093.body:
diff-iterate flushes the image before it runs, so that in-flight writes show up in list-snaps and in the object map. This flush waits for all older in-flight operations, including reads.

QEMU calls rbd_diff_iterate2() for each block status query, and a backup queries block status before copying each chunk. So each query waits for the backup's own reads, and only about one read is in flight at a time. In Proxmox bug 7909, backups of images with fast-diff on HDD OSDs became about three times slower after a QEMU update.

Reads do not change what diff-iterate reports, so this change adds a flush that only waits for older operations that may write, and uses it in diff-iterate. The new flush skips reads, flushes and list-snaps. As far as I can tell, list-snaps is the only tracked operation that uses AIO_TYPE_GENERIC, so the new flush identifies it by that type. Skipping an older flush should be fine, because the flush from diff-iterate still flushes the cache after the older writes finish.

I tested it on a vstart cluster with 20 ms of injected OSD latency. qemu-storage-daemon backed up a 1 GiB image with fast-diff using 16 workers. The numbers are the average of 3 runs:

| librbd | backup throughput | reads in flight |
| ------ | ----------------: | --------------: |
| before |         159 MiB/s |             1.8 |
| after  |        1221 MiB/s |            12.0 |

With rbd_clone_copy_on_read, a read on a clone may start a copyup, which updates the object map. If the copyup starts after the flush, neither the old flush nor the new one waits for it. If it starts before the flush, both wait for it. So this change does not make that case better or worse.

Refs: https://bugzilla.proxmox.com/show_bug.cgi?id=7909

72095.title: rgw/s3vector: background vector-index rebuild with distributed locking
72095.author: galsalomon66
72095.body:
Purpose:

The background subsystem's job is to keep each vector index structure (the
 vector index LanceDB builds over the `data` column)  fresh as
rows are inserted and deleted — **without** rebuilding on every mutation, and
**without** two RGW instances rebuilding the same table at once.

It does this with three decoupled mechanisms:

1. **Per-table pending-mutation flag** — the write path inserts the table key into a
   mutex-protected `pending_mutations` set; it never blocks on the rebuild.
2. **A per-instance background worker loop** — drains the pending set, checks rebuild
   thresholds, and spawns rebuild coroutines.
3. **A distributed lock stored as an S3/RADOS object in the vector bucket** — the
   only cross-instance coordination point, so that across N distributed RGWs
   exactly one rebuilds a given table at a time. The delete-rebuild decision reads
   ground-truth ghost rows (`num_deleted_rows` from LanceDB table stats), which are
   shared across instances and self-reset on compaction — no cross-instance delete
   counter is persisted.

The write path does only the triggering ; all the heavy work happens
asynchronously on the background workers.

##  User request arrives (the write path)

The subsystem is namespaced `rgw::s3vector` and initialized once per RGW process
(`init()` creates the singleton `s_manager` and starts its workers).

**PutVectors** : after the rows are upserted into LanceDB
via `lancedb_table_merge_insert`, and only on success, the handler calls:

```cpp
notify_index_update(dpp, ns, vector_bucket_name, index_name, num_rows);
```

**DeleteVectors**: symmetrically, after
`lancedb_table_df_delete` succeeds:

```cpp
notify_index_delete(dpp, ns, vector_bucket_name, index_name,
                    configuration.keys.size());
```

(`ns` is a `bucket_namespace_t` carrying the tenant and namespace key.)

**What notify actually does** (`notify_index_mutation`): it is *not* a queue push — it
inserts the table's key into a mutex-protected `pending_mutations` unordered_set.
The `row_count` parameter is accepted but used only for logging; the set records
*presence* (a boolean flag), not a count.
The cost to the user request is a brief `std::lock_guard` acquisition plus a set
insert — negligible, and it never blocks a rebuild.

**Lifecycle notifications go through a lock-free queue instead**
(`message_t` on a `boost::lockfree::queue`, capacity 8192):

- `notify_session_create` — on vector-bucket create and
  lazily whenever a connection is opened without a cached session.
- `notify_session_delete` — on vector-bucket delete.
- `notify_index_remove` — on index delete and on cascade paths during
  bucket teardown.


## 1. Async Architecture - Big picture

The subsystem is a single long-lived `Manager` object (`s_manager`, a
`std::unique_ptr<Manager>`). It owns **two** Boost.Asio `io_context`s and the threads
that run them, and it drives all work through **coroutines** (`boost::asio::spawn` +
`yield_context`). The data plane (RGW request handlers) never touches the rebuild
machinery directly — it only **enqueues notifications**, which the background
coroutines later consume.

```
                         RGW request handlers (data plane)
                                   |
         notify_index_mutation()   |   notify_index() / notify_session()
         (mark table as pending)   |   (push control message)
                                   v
   +---------------------------+   +-------------------------------+
   | pending_mutations (set)   |   | messages (lock-free queue)    |
   | per-table presence flag   |   | REMOVE / SESSION_CREATE /     |
   | last_rebuild_epoch (map)  |   | SESSION_DELETE                |
   +-------------+-------------+   +---------------+---------------+
                 |                                 |
   == main_loop_io_context ==          == io_context (worker pool) ==
   [1 dedicated thread: s3v-

72096.title: rgw, qa: test injection points and a workunit for overwrite races
72096.author: mmgaggle
72096.body:
Reproducers for races between writers of one key that leak RADOS objects or lose data, found with a formal model of RGW overwrites and multipart uploads (https://github.com/mmgaggle/ceph/tree/cdbbbb09245535782e91503ad45b0cc7a423e10d/src/test/formal/p/rgw_overwrite).

- `rgw_inject_delay()` holds a request at a named point when `rgw_inject_delay_pattern` names it and `rgw_inject_delay_sec` is positive; a request coroutine waits on a timer, so the frontend keeps serving. Points: `write_meta_before_head_write`, `copy_obj_before_write_meta`, `complete_mp_after_head_write`, `delete_obj_before_head_delete`.
- `rgw_debug_inject_mp_meta_delete_err` makes a multipart completion's delete of its meta object fail, after the head write.
- `qa/workunits/rgw/test_rgw_overwrite_races.py`: each case holds one request at a point while another changes the key, then deletes every key, drains GC, and expects no RADOS object of the bucket to remain (or the object to read back whole). It sets its knobs at runtime with `ceph config set`.

| Case | Tracker | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_losing_complete` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80897 | rgw: a completion that loses the head race sends its parts to GC |
| `test_delete_racing_put` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80898 | rgw: guard a delete's head removal on the ID tag it read |
| `test_losing_copy` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80899 | rgw: a copy that loses the head race drops its tail references |
| `test_delete_racing_dedup`, `test_copy_to_itself_racing_dedup` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80901 | open |

Every case fails on main, and passes with its fix on a vstart cluster. The workunit is not added to a qa suite yet, since the dedup cases fail until https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80901 is addressed. s3-tests counterparts, for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80895, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80896, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80900 and https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80903, are in https://github.com/mmgaggle/s3-tests/tree/wip-rgw-overwrite-races.

Four cases for conditional requests, added later:

| Case | Tracker | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `test_cond_delete_racing_put` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80898 | #72100 |
| `test_conditional_puts_race` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80906 | #72109 |
| `test_if_match_losing_race` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80906 | #72109 |
| `test_refused_complete_keeps_parts` | https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80907 | #72109 |

## Versioned buckets and other scenarios

The injection points and the workunit now cover versioned buckets. The existing points miss versioned races, because a versioned write links its version to the olh after its head write, and a versioned DeleteObject links a delete marker or unlinks a version without reaching `delete_obj_before_head_delete`.

- New points: `write_meta_before_olh_link`, `delete_obj_before_olh_link`, `delete_obj_before_unlink_instance` and `unlink_instance_before_olh_update`.
- `rgw_inject_delay_pattern` accepts a comma-separated list of points, so a case can hold two requests at different points.
- New option `rgw_debug_inject_link_olh_log_err_key`: the olh link of that object name fails after the bucket index links the version.
- The workunit can create a bucket with versioning enabled or suspended. With versioning suspended, each key first gets an olh, so its null version shares the olh's head object. Cleanup removes every version and delete marker.
- The seven head-race cases also run with versioning suspended. New cases cover conditional writes and deletes racing at the olh link, two If-None-Match writes of a null version, a DeleteObject of the null version racing a PutObject, olh link failures, a copy onto itself in a suspended bucket and racing a tagging or ACL update, and a listing during a stalled PutObject in versioned buckets.

The workunit passes with the whole series applied. Its versioned cases need the versioning follow-ups on #72098, #72100, #72101, #72103, #72115 and #72118,

72097.title: cls/rgw: a skipped or canceled completion keeps the entry's version
72097.author: mmgaggle
72097.body:
`rgw_bucket_complete_op` sets `entry.ver = op.ver` before it acts on the op. A cancel, or an op skipped because its epoch is not newer than the entry's, then lowers the entry's version; a cancel sets it to its own {-1, 0}. A later completion from an older epoch passes the epoch check and overwrites the newer entry, and with no pending op left, no listing repairs it: ListObjects keeps listing an object the head no longer holds, or a key that answers 404.

Set the version only when the op is applied. `8b27472bbd8a` moved the assignment above the cancel branch while reworking cancellation to clean up `remove_objs`.

Three new `ceph_test_cls_rgw` cases complete ops out of epoch order; they fail without the fix. With it, `ceph_test_cls_rgw` and `ceph_test_cls_rgw_stats` pass on a vstart cluster (replicated pools).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80894

## Versioned buckets

Versioned writes still complete through `rgw_bucket_complete_op`, on the version's own instance entry, and a null version's ops are redirected from the key's version marker to the null instance entry. The change reaches both. A new cls_rgw test, `index_stale_complete_keeps_newest_null_version`, checks the null instance entry the way the existing test checks a plain entry.

72098.title: rgw: keep a write whose index completion fails, and clean up after lost head races
72098.author: mmgaggle
72098.body:
Three fixes to how `write_meta`'s callers handle a write that did not take effect.

- **Keep a write whose index completion fails after the head write** (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80902). `_do_write_meta` treats an error from `index_op->complete` like a lost race, after the head is written, and callers then undo what the new head names: PutObject deletes the tail, a copy drops its references, a completion skips its meta delete. On main this is reachable since `a67a233ccbd`, where a FIFO-bilog bucket flushes its bilog batch before the completion op. Keep the write, leave the pending op for a listing to repair, and still remove the entries the write replaces, with a cancel without a tag. After this, `meta.canceled` means the head was not written.
- **A copy that loses the head race drops its tail references** (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80899). `copy_obj` rolls back its references on the source's tail only when `write_meta` returns an error; a lost race returns 0 with `meta.canceled` set, and the source's tail outlives the source.
- **A completion that loses the head race sends its parts to GC** (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80897). `RadosMultipartUpload::complete` ignores `meta.canceled`; its parts become unreferenced and are never collected.

The last two rely on the first: without it, `meta.canceled` can be set after the head was written, and cleaning up would free data the head names.

The workunit cases `test_losing_copy` and `test_losing_complete` in #72096 fail on main and pass with this change on a vstart cluster. The index-completion failure has no cluster reproducer, since it needs a bilog flush to fail; it was checked with a formal model of these paths (https://github.com/mmgaggle/ceph/tree/cdbbbb09245535782e91503ad45b0cc7a423e10d/src/test/formal/p/rgw_overwrite).

## Versioned buckets

A write in a versioned bucket, or of a null version over a key with an olh, links its version to the olh after its head write and index completion. A new commit keeps such a write when the bilog flush or the datalog entry fails after the index has linked the version, or when `update_olh` fails after it, as this PR already does for a failed index completion. Before, `set_olh` returned the error and the caller undid what the now current version names.

The bilog or datalog entry that failed is not written, so multisite sync can miss the change, as for a failed index completion.

Validated on vstart with the new `rgw_debug_inject_link_olh_log_err_key` option of #72096: a PutObject with versioning enabled and suspended, and a CompleteMultipartUpload followed by an abort. Each leaves a current version that cannot be read without the new commit, and reads back whole with it.

72100.title: rgw: guard a delete's head removal on the ID tag it read
72100.author: mmgaggle
72100.body:
`55f5b762c67` ("fix conditional Delete and MultiDelete") replaced the delete's call to `prepare_atomic_modification(removal_op=true)`, which added a `cmpxattr` on the ID tag, with `check_preconditions`, which adds nothing to the op. A delete that races an overwrite now removes the new head, then sends the manifest it read, the old one, to GC. The new object's tail, or a completion's parts, is never collected.

Guard the removal with `append_atomic_test` again. DeleteObject already answers the lost race's `-ECANCELED` with success; answer it the same way in multi-object delete, which reported it as an error before `55f5b762c67` as well.

The workunit case `test_delete_racing_put` in #72096 fails on main (the PutObject's tail remains after GC) and passes with this change on a vstart cluster.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80898

With the removal guarded, a delete can lose the race to a write that replaced the head. DeleteObject answers that with success, which is right for an unconditional delete. A conditional one (If-Match, If-Match-Size, If-Match-Last-Modified-Time, If-Unmodified-Since) cannot claim its condition held, so the second commit answers its lost race with 409 ConditionalRequestConflict, in DeleteObject and in multi-object delete, and adds that error (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80906). The guard also closes a conditional delete deleting an object that fails its If-Match; the workunit case `test_cond_delete_racing_put` in #72096 fails on main and passes with this change.

## Versioned buckets

In a bucket whose versioning is suspended, a DeleteObject of the null version logs the removal of the null instance, and whoever applies the olh log removes its head. If a PutObject wrote the key's head and linked a new null version in between, that removal took the new version's head: the version stayed current and lost its data. A new commit makes `apply_olh_log` cancel a pending removal when a later entry links the same instance as a version, with "null" and the empty instance treated as the same key.

Validated on vstart with the injection points of #72096: the workunit case `test_suspended_delete_null_racing_put` fails without the new commit and passes with it.

Not covered here:
- when the guarded removal inside `apply_olh_log` loses a race, the error is treated as a race with another applier, and the rewritten head stays until the log is applied again;
- a conditional DeleteObject with `versionId=null` checks its condition apart from the unlink, which needs a cls condition on `unlink_instance`, like the one #72118 adds to `link_olh`.

72101.title: rgw: a copy onto itself writes only over the head it copied
72101.author: mmgaggle
72101.body:
A metadata-only copy of an object onto itself (`copy_itself`) reads the source's manifest, then writes it back with `keep_tail`. The destination has its own `RGWObjectCtx`, so `write_meta` reads the head afresh and guards on whatever ID tag it finds then. An overwrite between the two steps replaces the head and sends the old tail to GC; the copy then writes that tail back into the head. GC deletes the tail the head names, and the overwrite's own tail leaks.

Add `MetaParams::id_tag_guard`, a `cmpxattr` on the ID tag the caller read, placed before `prepare_atomic_modification()` sets the new one, and skip the exclusive create for a guarded write, which would recreate a head deleted meanwhile. `copy_obj` guards a copy onto itself on the source's ID tag. A copy that fails the guard is answered as success, like any lost race.

The s3-test `test_object_copy_to_itself_racing_put` (https://github.com/mmgaggle/s3-tests/tree/wip-rgw-overwrite-races), with the injection points in #72096, fails on main (GET stops after the head's 4 MiB, ENOENT on the tail) and passes with this change on a vstart cluster.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80900

## Versioned buckets and attribute updates

Attribute updates: PutObjectTagging, PutObjectAcl and the other `set_attrs` callers give the head a new ID tag and keep the object. A copy onto itself that raced such an update failed its guard and was answered success without writing, so its new metadata was lost. A new commit makes a copy onto itself that loses its guard read the head again and retry, up to twice, and answer 500 InternalError if it still loses. Reported in review by @mheler.

Versioned buckets: with versioning enabled, a copy onto the same key writes a new instance, so it is never a copy onto itself. With versioning suspended and another version current, the source resolves to that version and the copy takes references on its tail. With the null version current, the copy is a copy onto itself of the olh's head, and the guard applies.

Validated on vstart with the injection points of #72096: `test_copy_to_itself_racing_tagging` and `test_copy_to_itself_racing_acl` fail without the new commit and pass with it; `test_suspended_copy_to_itself` and `test_suspended_copy_null_to_itself` pass. The P model (#72110) checks the tagging race on main, with this guard, and with the retry: only the retry holds.

72102.title: rgw: re-link an index entry whose pending op expired
72102.author: mmgaggle
72102.body:
A bucket listing drops a pending index op older than `rgw_pending_bucket_index_op_expiration` and repairs the entry from the head it reads. If a write stalled past the expiry before its head write, the listing repairs the entry from the old head, or removes it for a new key. The write then writes its head, and its index completion fails with `-EINVAL` because its tag is gone; the completion is asynchronous and the error is dropped, so the index keeps listing the old object, or nothing.

When a completion comes back `-EINVAL`, run a fresh index transaction for the key in the completion manager's thread: prepare a new pending op, read the head, and complete from the head as it is now, with its epoch. A delete whose head is still gone completes with its own epoch, and anything else cancels; `remove_objs` go along either way. A racing write or delete either sees the new pending op or is ordered by epoch, as for any write. Applying the late completion in `cls_rgw` when its epoch is newer would not do: an entry a delete has removed keeps no epoch, so it would bring the deleted object back.

Also factor the head-to-entry conversion out of `check_disk_state` into `head_dir_meta()` for the re-link to share.

The s3-test `test_listing_during_stalled_put` (https://github.com/mmgaggle/s3-tests/tree/wip-rgw-overwrite-races), which holds a PutObject past a short pending-op expiry with the injection points in #72096, fails on main and passes with this change on a vstart cluster. The design was checked with a formal model (https://github.com/mmgaggle/ceph/tree/cdbbbb09245535782e91503ad45b0cc7a423e10d/src/test/formal/p/rgw_overwrite) in listing scenarios with writers that stall, including a new key's first write and a racing delete.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80903

## Versioned buckets

A versioned write's pending op sits on the version's instance entry, or for a null version over a key with an olh, on the null instance entry behind the key's version marker. Neither ListObjects nor ListObjectVersions repairs those entries, so the loss this PR fixes does not occur there, and the re-link does not run for them. Validated on vstart with workunit cases that list a bucket during a stalled PutObject, with versioning enabled and suspended.

72103.title: rgw: record a multipart completion before its head write
72103.author: mmgaggle
72103.body:
Once a completion writes the head, it deletes the upload's meta object. If RGW dies between the two, or the delete fails, the meta object survives with its part list. A retried completion then writes the head again and sends the replaced manifest, the same parts, to GC; an abort, or lifecycle's, sends the parts to GC directly. Either way the completed object loses its data.

In every bucket, write the completion's tag, the ID tag its head will carry, and the version instance it writes to the meta object (`user.rgw.mp_completion_tag`, `user.rgw.mp_completion_instance`) before the head write, and remove them if the head write fails for sure. The instance is the completion's own with versioning enabled, which RGWCompleteMultipart generates before complete(), and "null" otherwise, which names the key's head object and is read without following the olh. A completion or abort that finds a record reads that instance's head:

- if the head carries the tag, the earlier completion took effect. A completion with the same part list answers success, with the version id the earlier completion wrote, and the caller deletes the meta object; an abort deletes only the meta object.
- otherwise the head was never written, or was replaced and its parts sent to GC. A completion answers NoSuchUpload rather than write a head over those parts, and an abort proceeds as before.

The cost: a retry after a crash between the record and the head write is refused, and the upload has to be aborted and uploaded again. It does not help a holder whose lock lapses before its head write.

The s3-tests `test_multipart_complete_retry_after_meta_delete_error` and `test_multipart_abort_after_meta_delete_error` (https://github.com/mmgaggle/s3-tests/tree/wip-rgw-overwrite-races), which make the meta delete fail with the debug option in #72096, fail on main and pass with this change on a vstart cluster. The design was checked with a formal model (https://github.com/mmgaggle/ceph/tree/cdbbbb09245535782e91503ad45b0cc7a423e10d/src/test/formal/p/rgw_overwrite) with a crash, or a failed meta delete, in the multipart scenarios.

## Versioned buckets

The first version of this change skipped versioned buckets, and checked the record against the current version. With versioning suspended, a retry then replaced the null version and sent its parts to GC. With versioning enabled, a retry wrote a second version that shared the first one's parts, and an abort sent the parts of the completed version to GC; a check against the current version also missed a completed version that a later write made noncurrent. The record now names the instance, and every bucket records it.

The s3-tests `test_multipart_complete_retry_after_meta_delete_error_versioned`, `test_multipart_abort_after_meta_delete_error_versioned` and `test_multipart_abort_after_overwrite_versioned`, and the retry and abort tests with `_suspended`, fail without the record and pass with it. The P model (#72110) checks the record skipped, checked against the current version, and naming the instance, with versioning enabled and suspended: only naming the instance holds in every scenario.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80896

72104.title: mds: stop a session close from flooding the OSDs with deletes for delegated inos
72104.author: xiubli
72104.body:
When a session closes, the MDS deletes the first object of every inode
number still delegated to it, and issues all of those deletes at once.
Only a kernel client with async dirops uses delegated inos, but every
client is sent them, so most of those deletes are for objects that never
existed. With `mds_client_prealloc_inos=16384`, 128 libcephfs clients
disconnecting issued about 2.1 million deletes, and the journal writes
queued behind them in the OSDs: `sync_fs` from another client took up to
30s on bluestore, and a client mounting meanwhile timed out.

This PR:

- **mds: bound the deletes in flight when purging delegated inos** —
  all closing sessions share one budget, `mds_purge_inodes_max_ops`
  (default 512, 0 = no limit).
- **mds: free unused delegated inos when a client closes its session** —
  on a clean close with nothing in flight, delegated inos the client never
  used go back to the inotable instead of being purged. Evicted, timed out
  and killed sessions still purge all of them.
  `mds_session_close_free_unused_delegated_inos=false` turns it off.
- PendingReleaseNotes and doc updates.

## Test results

128 libcephfs clients disconnect at once; one active MDS, 3 OSDs.

```
| Metric                         | Before     | After    |
|--------------------------------|------------|----------|
| Object deletes                 | 2.15M      | 57K      |
| Worst `sync_fs`, bluestore     | 29.9s      | 76ms     |
| Wait before next run, bluestore| 22-57s     | 0.2s     |
| Worst `sync_fs`, memstore      | 1.3s       | 35ms     |
```

The remaining 57K deletes are purge queue deletes for the files the
workload unlinked. The purge limit was chosen from a sweep of 256-16384
on bluestore: 512 kept `sync_fs` under 80ms and drained as fast as no
limit; 2048 and above let the journal stall again.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80904

72109.title: rgw: answer a conditional request that loses the race with a conflict
72109.author: mmgaggle
72109.body:
Depends on #72100; the first two commits are #72100's.

A conditional request that loses the race for the head is answered as `done_cancel` maps the error, and the mapping is wrong both ways (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80906):

- With `If-Match: *`, `-ECANCELED` becomes success, though the write never happened. Racing a PutObject with If-Match on the old ETag, both are answered 200 while the head holds the other write, and no order of the two explains both answers. `If-None-Match: *` answers `-ENOENT` the same way.
- With If-Match on an ETag, `-ECANCELED` has no S3 error and is answered 500 UnknownError.

Answer each of these with 409 ConditionalRequestConflict, as S3 does for a conditional request that loses to a concurrent operation; the error is added in #72100, which answers a conditional delete's lost race the same way. The answers that already say what happened, 412 and 404, stay.

A completion with `If-None-Match: *` that loses the race to create the key is refused, and its upload stays, but the cancel of its index op has already removed its parts' index entries (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80907). Decide the answer first, and cancel without `remove_objs` when the write is answered with an error.

The workunit cases `test_conditional_puts_race`, `test_if_match_losing_race` and `test_refused_complete_keeps_parts` in #72096 fail on main and pass with this change on a vstart cluster. The fixes were checked in a formal model of these paths before they were written.

## Versioned buckets

This branch now contains the new commit on #72100, which keeps a null version's head when it is linked after a DeleteObject of the null version logged its removal. The answer this PR gives a conditional request that loses a race, 409 ConditionalRequestConflict, is the one S3's API model gives a conflicting operation during a conditional write. #72118 now answers a conditional write refused at its olh link the same way.

72110.title: test/formal: add a P model of RGW overwrites and multipart uploads
72110.author: mmgaggle
72110.body:
A [P](https://p-org.github.io/P/) model of RGW's write paths, which found the races fixed in #72097 through #72103 and #72109.

`src/test/formal/p/rgw_overwrite` models PutObject, DeleteObject, CopyObject with a shared tail, conditional requests (If-Match, If-None-Match: *), part uploads, multipart completion and abort, lifecycle's abort, bucket listings and their repair, dedup, a logrecord reshard, the bucket index entry and its header stats, `cls_refcount` and GC, each step at the granularity of a RADOS operation. Its specifications check that no head's data is deleted, that the index lists what the head holds, that the stats match the index, that nothing leaks, and that every request is answered. The checker searches the interleavings of a few requests on one or two keys, with faults: a crash after the head write, a failed meta delete, a failed index completion, a request that stalls past the pending-op expiry, a completion lock that lapses under its holder.

Each mechanism the code relies on is a flag, as on main by default; turning one off reproduces the code before the commit that added it, and the checker finds the bug that commit fixed (for example #75375's without lock renewal). On main the model finds fourteen problems. The first eleven are filed as https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80894 to https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80903; its README traces each to the code and lists the proposed fix. It also checks those fixes alone and all together, with and without failing index completions: every scenario holds but dedup's (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80901, open). Findings 12 to 14, on conditional requests, reproduce on a cluster too (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80898, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80906, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80907); their fixes are #72100 and #72109.

The models are not part of the build: they need the .NET 8 SDK and the P tool. `./run.sh rgw_overwrite 20000 <jobs>` checks all 213 cases against `expect.txt`; all match. The reproducers on a cluster are in #72096 and #72097.

72111.title: cephadm: staged switch — stage a redeploy while the daemons serve, switch them with one restart
72111.author: FredNass
72111.body:
With `mgr/orchestrator/fail_fs = true`, `ceph orch upgrade` fails a CephFS filesystem and then redeploys its MDS daemons one `cephadm deploy` call at a time. Each call spends most of its time on work that does not need the filesystem to be down — starting cephadm on the host, a throwaway container to look up the uid/gid in the target image, writing the unit files, `daemon-reload` — and the filesystem is only set joinable again once cephadm's own daemon cache has noticed the new image.

Measured on a 4-host reef 18.2.8 cluster with three filesystems (19 MDS, `mds_join_fs` set, `fail_fs = true`), image already present on every host, upgrade run three times from the same starting point — stock, with #69334 / #70873 applied, and with this PR on top (`upgrade_staged_switch = true`). Downtime is `fs fail` → `fs set joinable true` in the cephadm log; the wait for `up:active` after that is the same in all three and is not counted.

| filesystem | MDS | stock 18.2.8 | + #69334 / #70873 | + this PR |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `cephfs` | 12 (6 active + 6 standby-replay) | 349 s | 67.7 s | **11.4 s** |
| `cephfs2` | 4 (3 active + 1 standby) | 357 s | 40.1 s | **8.3 s** |
| `cephfs3` | 3 (2 active + 1 standby) | 357 s | 36.7 s | **6.3 s** |
| MDS phase, all three | | 6 min 00 s | 3 min 07 s | **1 min 40 s** |

Stock fails every filesystem at the start of the MDS phase and re-joins them only once the last MDS is upgraded, so each one is down for the whole phase whatever its size. With #69334 (one filesystem at a time) the window scales with the number of MDS of that filesystem. With the staged switch what is left inside the window is the stop/start and the MDS boot, plus a few seconds for the largest filesystem.

This PR moves everything that does not need the daemons to be down out of the outage window, as a daemon-type agnostic mechanism with an MDS policy.

## cephadm binary

- `cephadm deploy --stage` (also `_orch deploy` with `params.stage=true`): everything a redeploy does — config, keyring, `unit.run/stop/poststop/meta/image`, sysctl, systemd units, `daemon-reload` — but the unit files are written as `unit.*.staged` next to the live ones and the running unit is never touched. Before writing anything, the daemon's own entrypoint is run with `--version` in the target image, so an image that cannot execute on this host fails here, with the daemon still up. Refused for the agent, for daemons with sidecar containers, and for daemons never deployed on the host.
- `cephadm switch-staged --name X [--expected-image I] [--rollback]`: checks the staged `unit.image` is the expected one and that the image is still present locally, then `stop` → rename live files to `unit.*.prev` and staged files into place → clean cgroup → `reset-failed` → `enable` → `start`. `--rollback` puts the `.prev` files back and parks the new ones as `.staged` again. Idempotent.

Both work for any containerized daemon type and can be used by hand.

## mgr/cephadm

- `cephadm/staged_switch.py`: `StagedSwitchRunner` drives one group per `serve()` pass through *stage* (all hosts in parallel, daemons still serving) → *down* (`policy.take_down`) → *switch* (`switch-staged` on all hosts in parallel) → *verify* (`policy.verify` against the **monitors**, not cephadm's cache) → *restore* (`policy.restore`, then a refresh of cephadm's daemon cache for the hosts involved) → *settle* (`policy.settled()`: until the group has settled — for a policy that needs it, its daemons caught up with what they missed during the switch — the runner keeps it in a persisted `settling` phase, polls it for up to 30 s per pass, does **not** pause the upgrade and has **no timeout**, and reports why in `ceph orch upgrade status`; the next group is chosen only afterwards. `--limit` accounting is saved with the transition to that phase. The default `settled()` answers right away, so the MDS policy is unchanged). On a staging or take-down failure nothing has been restarted: `UPGRADE

72112.title: osd: resume a withheld PG creation for a backfill target
72112.author: mmgaggle
72112.body:
An OSD over the PG hard limit (mon_max_pg_per_osd *
osd_max_pg_per_osd_hard_ratio) withholds creating a PG and records it in
pending_creates_from_osd. Once it has room, resume_creating_pg() forces a
pg_temp change for the PG so that its primary peers again and resends.
For a backfill target (an OSD in the PG's up set but not its acting set)
that did not happen, and the PG stayed activating+remapped until an OSD
restart or a repeer:

- consume_map() discarded the record at every new OSDMap unless the OSD
  was in the acting set. The first commit keeps it while the OSD is in the
  up or acting set (is_up_acting_osd_shard()).
- With an acting set of the primary alone, the pg_temp requested was
  [primary, CRUSH_ITEM_NONE], which a replicated pool maps back to the same
  acting set. The second commit adds a second up OSD instead, as
  "pg repeer" does.

The new standalone test covers both: an OSD at the limit becomes a
backfill target (with the replica still acting, or with the primary alone
after the replica dies), then gets room. On main both cases stay
activating; with the first commit only, the second does.

Both cases were found with a P model of PG peering and of the OSD's PG
creation (https://github.com/mmgaggle/ceph/tree/wip-formal-p-pg-models,
src/test/formal/p/pg_statechart), and reproduced on a vstart cluster.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/23117

72113.title: osd/PeeringState: take only an accepted notify as GetInfo's reply
72113.author: mmgaggle
72113.body:
GetInfo::react(MNotifyRec) erased the sender from peer_info_requested
before proc_replica_notify() looked at the notify. proc_replica_notify()
discards a notify the peer sent before its current up_from (the
has_been_up_since() check from https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/12990), so such a notify ended
GetInfo's wait for the peer without providing its info. When that peer
is the only surviving OSD of an interval that went read-write, the
primary chose the authoritative log without it and activated without
the writes acknowledged in that interval.

This erases the peer from peer_info_requested only once
proc_replica_notify() has accepted its notify.

The new unittest_peeringstate test, StaleNotifyCompletesGetInfo, drives
the sequence through PeeringState: osd.1 alone acknowledges a write,
fails, and returns while the primary (osd.0) is behind on maps, flapping
once more so that its first notify predates its up_from. That notify
reaches osd.0 in GetInfo before osd.2's reply. On main osd.0 goes active
without the write; with this change it waits for osd.1.

Found with a P model of PG peering
(https://github.com/mmgaggle/ceph/tree/wip-formal-p-pg-models,
src/test/formal/p/pg_peering).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80927

72114.title: rgw: refuse the S3 APIs that rgw does not implement
72114.author: mmgaggle
72114.body:
A request for an S3 API that rgw does not implement is not refused. The op_*() methods of the S3 bucket and object handlers test the sub-resources they serve, and run any other request as the plain bucket or object operation for its method, answering success:

- DeleteBucketMetricsConfiguration, and the configuration deletes for analytics, inventory, intelligent-tiering and metadata tables, run as DeleteBucket and delete an empty bucket (204).
- PutObjectAnnotation and UpdateObjectEncryption run as PutObject and replace the object's data with the request body; RenameObject runs as PutObject with no body and leaves an empty object at the destination (200).
- DeleteObjectAnnotation runs as DeleteObject and deletes the object (204).
- The Get and List calls run as ListObjects or GetObject (200).

Tools that manage bucket configuration, such as Terraform, call the configuration deletes when they remove one. #46263 fixed this for DeleteBucketEncryption and DeleteBucketReplication by serving those sub-resources; each API added to S3 since then falls through the same way.

This refuses a request whose query names one of these APIs' sub-resources with 501 NotImplemented, which S3 clients read as a feature the endpoint lacks. The list comes from AWS's Smithy model of S3. The check is in the init() of the S3 bucket and object handlers, so the S3 website handlers, whose query strings belong to the site, are unaffected; HEAD and OPTIONS requests are left alone. The GET calls, which answered a bucket listing, now answer 501 too.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80921

Validated on a single-host vstart cluster: the s3-tests reproducers test_bucket_config_delete_keeps_bucket (metrics, analytics, inventory, intelligent-tiering), test_object_annotation_put_keeps_object, test_object_annotation_delete_keeps_object, test_update_object_encryption_keeps_data, test_rename_object_keeps_destination and test_bucket_metrics_configuration_get_unconfigured (ceph/s3-tests#763) fail on main and pass with this change, and test_s3.py as the rgw suite runs it shows no new failures.

## Versioned buckets

None of the refused subresources is used by versioned requests. s3-tests `test_unimplemented_api_versioned_ok` and `_suspended` check that tagging, ACL, HEAD and ListObjectVersions requests with a version id still work, and that a refused subresource answers 501.

72115.title: rgw: a conditional delete that finds no object is answered 404
72115.author: mmgaggle
72115.body:
A DeleteObject with If-Match that finds no object is answered 204 No Content: delete_obj returns -ENOENT before it checks the condition, RGWDeleteObj_ObjStore_S3::send_response answers -ENOENT as success, and a removal that finds the head already gone ends in complete_del, whose return replaces the -ENOENT. For general purpose buckets S3 answers such a delete 404 Not Found, including one that a concurrent delete beat (S3 User Guide, "How to perform conditional deletes"). With If-Match used to release a lease, two clients releasing the same lease are both told they released it.

This answers the -ENOENT of a delete that carries If-Match as 404 NoSuchKey, on both paths, and in a versioned bucket, where check_preconditions returns -ENOENT when there is no current version. A delete without If-Match still succeeds for a missing object, and so does one with only x-amz-if-match-size or x-amz-if-match-last-modified-time, which S3 documents as 204. DeleteObjects reports a key whose ETag condition finds no object as a NoSuchKey error.

s3-tests' test_delete_object_if_match, test_delete_object_current_if_match and test_delete_object_version_if_match assert the 204; ceph/s3-tests#764 updates them.

The P model of RGW overwrites (#72110) checks this answer (S3Answers, finding 15).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80922

Validated on a single-host vstart cluster: test_delete_object_if_match_no_object (ceph/s3-tests#763) fails on main and passes with this change; with the companion s3-tests change all 12 conditional-delete tests pass, and test_s3.py as the rgw suite runs it shows no other new failures.

## Versioned buckets

In a versioned or suspended bucket whose current version is a delete marker, the conditions were checked against the olh's own head: If-Match: * passed, and a second delete marker was linked. S3 answers 412 Precondition Failed for a delete marker, If-Match: * included. A new commit answers any delete condition 412 there. DeleteObjects takes the same path.

s3-tests `test_delete_object_if_match_delete_marker` and `_suspended` fail without the new commit and pass with it. `test_delete_object_current_if_match` must expect 412 on the delete marker, and remove the delete marker rather than the version before it retests If-Match: *; ceph/s3-tests#764 needs that change too.

72116.title: rgw: send a multipart completion's part history to GC after its head write
72116.author: mmgaggle
72116.body:
RadosMultipartUpload::complete sends each part's past prefixes to GC (cleanup_part_history) while it checks the parts, before the head write. A completion refused after that - InvalidPart or EntityTooSmall for a later part, or a precondition or lost race in write_meta - leaves the upload, and its meta object still lists those prefixes as the part's history. Once GC has deleted them, the next upload of that part number writes its head at the base prefix again (process_first_chunk falls back to a random prefix only when the exclusive create fails), and cls_rgw_mp_upload_part_info_update refuses it with -EEXIST, answered 409 BucketAlreadyExists. Every retry takes the same prefix, so the part cannot be uploaded again for the life of the upload.

This collects the history while checking the parts and sends it to GC only once the head is written. A completion refused before that leaves the history for a later completion or an abort to collect; if rgw dies between the head write and the GC send, the meta object is still there, and a retry or an abort collects the history the same way. cleanup_part_history keeps its behaviour for its other callers.

The P model of RGW overwrites (#72110) checks this change (historyAfterHead, finding 16), alone and with the other proposed fixes for RGW overwrites.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80923

Validated on a single-host vstart cluster with short GC timers: test_multipart_upload_part_after_refused_complete (ceph/s3-tests#763) fails on main and passes with this change, and test_s3.py as the rgw suite runs it shows no new failures.

## Versioned buckets

The part history is the same in every bucket kind, and no head manifest names a past prefix, so moving the history after the head write is correct with versioning enabled and suspended. With #72103 applied, a completion that replays an earlier one returns before it sends the history to GC; whichever of the two merges second needs to send it on that path.

72117.title: rgw: compare If-Match and If-None-Match entity tags whole
72117.author: mmgaggle
72117.body:
The conditional headers compare the object's ETag as a prefix of the header value (if_match_str.compare(0, etag.length(), etag)): in check_preconditions for writes and deletes, and in the read path for GET, HEAD and a copy's source. So any value that starts with the ETag matches it - an If-Match of the ETag with more characters after it is accepted, and an If-None-Match refuses it - a list of entity tags matches only when the first is the object's, and a weak tag never matches.

This adds rgw_etag_matches(), which reads the header as RFC 7232 does: a comma-separated list of entity tags, each quoted or not, compared whole; If-Match compares strongly, so W/"..." does not match it, and If-None-Match weakly. The callers still handle "*". It is used in the four places, and for the If-Match of a delete by version. unittest_rgw_etag covers it.

Related: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64439 (If-Match not unquoted).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80924

Validated on a single-host vstart cluster: test_put_object_if_match_etag_with_suffix (ceph/s3-tests#763) fails on main and passes with this change, unittest_rgw_etag passes, and test_s3.py as the rgw suite runs it shows no new failures.

## Versioned buckets

Every conditional path for a version, and for a delete marker, compares entity tags through `rgw_etag_matches()`. s3-tests `test_versioned_if_match_whole_etag` and `_suspended` check GET, HEAD, PUT and DELETE with a version id. Other storage backends (d4n, posix, dbstore, motr) still compare by prefix.

72118.title: rgw: link a conditional write's version only over the version it checked
72118.author: mmgaggle
72118.body:
In a versioning-enabled bucket a conditional write is not atomic. The write goes to a new instance head, which nothing guards (set_attr_id_tag requires an empty instance), and its condition is checked only against the current version as get_current_version_state read it, before set_olh makes the new version current. Another write can become current in between, so two PutObjects with If-None-Match: * on a new key both succeed, and so do two If-Match writes on one ETag, a completion with either header, and two conditional deletes that each write a delete marker. S3 lets the first succeed and refuses the others. Applications that use If-None-Match: * for a lock or to create exactly once get two winners.

This checks the condition again where the new version becomes current: rgw_bucket_link_olh, the one cls op on the index shard that holds the key's olh entry, and already the place that refuses a stale link (unmod_since). rgw_cls_link_olh_op gains an optional condition, and its encoding goes to v6:

- NO_CURRENT: the key has no current version, or its current version is a delete marker. A key with no olh entry but a plain entry from before versioning has a current version.
- CURRENT_IS: the current version is the given instance, the one the write checked its condition against.

A link that fails its condition is refused with CLS_RGW_ERR_PRECONDITION_FAILED; set_olh does not retry it. The condition held when the write checked it, so a concurrent request changed the current version: rgw answers the refusal 409 ConditionalRequestConflict, as S3's API model answers a conflicting operation during a conditional write. A condition that fails when it is checked is still answered 412. The error is defined as in #72100, so the two merge cleanly. _do_write_meta passes the condition for a conditional write to a versioned key, and delete_obj for a conditional delete marker.

Points for review:

- The refused instance is left as any failed link leaves one: not listed, found and removed by "radosgw-admin bucket check unlinked", with its data objects deleted by the writer. Removing it at once instead would be a follow-up.
- Multisite: the refused write logs the instance's ADD in the bilog but no LINK_OLH. A secondary that syncs the ADD writes the instance without linking it, waiting for a LINK_OLH that never comes (fetch_remote_obj), so no zone makes the refused version current; if it fetched before the source deleted the data, it holds the same kind of unlinked instance. As for any condition, only the zone that accepted the request enforces it.
- Mixed versions: an OSD that has not been upgraded decodes the v6 op as v5 and links without the condition, as today.

## Versioning suspended

With versioning suspended, a write of the null version over a key with an olh writes the olh's own head, then links. With If-None-Match: * that head write took no guard, so two such writes could both write the head, and the one refused at its link had already replaced the head of the one answered success; the key read back as neither object. The head write is now guarded on the ID tag it read for these writes too, and a write that loses the guard is answered 409. A write that reads the head only after another's head write, but before that write links, still passes its guard.

Validated on vstart with the injection points of #72096: `test_suspended_if_none_match_puts_race` fails without the guard and passes with it, and it and `test_versioned_cond_delete_racing_put` fail with the earlier 412 answers and pass with 409.

72119.title: client: fix create reply decoding when mds_allow_async_dirops is off
72119.author: xiubli
72119.body:
The userspace client cannot do async creates and discards the delegated
inode numbers the MDS sends it, but it still advertises
`CEPHFS_FEATURE_DELEG_INO`. The MDS therefore parks
`mds_client_delegate_inos_pct` (50% by default) of each libcephfs
session's preallocated inode numbers in a delegated set the client never
uses, which leaves only half of `mds_client_prealloc_inos` for its
synchronous creates.

Depends on #70682: without it the client decodes the bare created inode
number as an `openc_response_t` and every create fails.

### Changes

- **client: don't ask for delegated inode numbers**: stop advertising
  `CEPHFS_FEATURE_DELEG_INO` until the client learns async creates. The
  MDS then keeps the whole preallocated range for synchronous creates
  and replies with the bare created inode number.
- **mds: flush the log when a request refills the preallocated inos**:
  the refilled numbers cannot be handed out until the event is safe, and
  an early-replied request does not flush the log, so a session could
  run dry meanwhile and fall back to inotable allocation, which forbids
  an early reply. Flush once per refill.

The decode fix for `mds_allow_async_dirops=false` ("client: decode the
create reply by its length") was dropped from this PR because it
duplicates #70682.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80931

72123.title: mds: optionally drop a client's writeable range without journaling it
72123.author: xiubli
72123.body:
When a client gives up its write caps on a file and nothing else about the
inode is dirty, `Locker::_do_cap_update()` still journals a full inode update
only to erase that client's writeable range. Every file that is created and
closed without data (IO500 mdtest-easy, untarring empty files, lock/marker
files) therefore costs **two** journal events: the openc and this "cap update",
each with its inode projection, parent dirfrag fnode and journal completion.

The range in the journal is only used after an MDS failure, to decide which
files need their size probed on the OSDs. A journal that still holds a range
the client no longer has is the state every file is already in between the
client dropping its write caps and the cap update committing; it can only make
recovery probe a file that did not need it, never lose data.

This PR adds `mds_defer_client_range_shrink` (default **off**). When it is set
and shrinking the range is the only change, the MDS drops the range in memory
and leaves the journal alone:

- only when the inode is not projected, so a pending update cannot bring the
  old range back when it is applied;
- the current inode is replaced with a modified copy, not changed in place;
- the dropped range reaches the disk with the next commit of the inode's
  dirfrag, at the latest when the log segment holding the file's events
  expires.

**Trade-off:** until that commit, an MDS failure makes recovery probe the size
of such a file if its client no longer holds caps on it, the same as for a file
whose writer died. Hence the option defaults to off.

### Results

mdtest-style run on a single-MDS vstart cluster, 8 libcephfs clients, 240k
empty files in a private directory per client plus 120k 3901-byte files in one
shared directory, 10s between phases, 3 runs each:

|                                          | origin/main   | option on               |
|------------------------------------------|---------------|-------------------------|
| easy create ops/s                        | 9896 ± 463    | 13641 ± 141 (**+37.9%**) |
| MDS CPU per create (µs)                  | 149.9 ± 6.1   | 122.8 ± 1.7 (**−18.1%**) |
| journal events per create                | 1.81          | 1.26                    |
| overall score, 8 phases (geomean, kIOPS) | 24.51 ± 0.97  | 25.48 ± 0.45 (+4.0%)    |


Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80936

72129.title: rgw: cloud transition and restore of compressed and encrypted objects
72129.author: mheler
72129.body:
Compressed objects were transitioned to the cloud as RGW's own compressed stream, making the cloud copy unreadable by anything other than RGW. Transitions now decompress objects before sending them to the cloud and remove the compression attribute from the stub. Permanent restores recompress the object using the restore storage class's compression setting. Temporary restores leave the object as-is in the cloud, since expiration copies its attributes back to the stub.

Encrypted multipart objects previously lost their part lengths during transition. As a result, restoring them could return corrupted data when using CBC or fail to decrypt when using GCM. The stub now retains the part lengths. Objects that were already tiered by older releases remain affected.

Encrypted objects are still uploaded in their stored form and marked with `x-amz-meta-rgwx-source-encrypted`. Their encryption attributes are kept only on the retained head object, so they are skipped when `retain_head_object` is false.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68015

72131.title: mds: reduce the MDS CPU spent per create and unlink
72131.author: xiubli
72131.body:
Under metadata-heavy workloads such as IO500 mdtest, the MDS is bound by its
  single dispatch thread holding `mds_lock`. This series removes or amortizes
  three costs that thread pays on every create and unlink.

  ### Changes

  - **mds: build the path in check_access() only for path-restricted caps** —
    `Session::check_access()` runs for most client requests, often more than
    once per request, and every time it built the inode's full path by walking
    all of its ancestor dentries. The path is only compared against grants that
    are limited to a path, and common caps such as `allow *` or `allow rw` have
    none. Add `MDSAuthCaps::path_restricted()` and build the path only when some
    grant is path-restricted. Covered by a new case in `unittest_mds_authcap`.
  - **mds: fill in the path check_access() passes to is_capable() for logging**
    — the trimmed path `is_capable()` prints at debug level 10 was never filled
    in, so that line always showed an empty path. It is now filled in when level
    10 is gathered.
  - **mds: complete safe journal events in batches under one mds_lock** —
    every journaled event had its own Journaler completion, and each one took
    `mds_lock` on its own. One journal flush typically covers tens to hundreds
    of events, so the finisher thread took and dropped the fair `mds_lock` that
    many times in a row, each hand-off costing a futex wake-up and a context
    switch on the MDS's bottleneck thread. The completions now wait in an
    MDLog-side queue in journal order, and the first kick after a flush commits
    completes the safe ones in batches, each under one lock acquisition.
    - The batch size is bounded by `mds_log_safe_batch_max` (default 8), and
      optionally by time with `mds_log_safe_batch_max_us` (off by default). Both
      can be changed at runtime.
    - Completion order is unchanged, and no event completes before the journal
      has made it safe.
    - The log's safe position still advances after each completion.
    - `pre_finish()` still runs before `mds_lock` is taken, so the
      `journal_committed` op event keeps its meaning.
    - When the journaler shuts down, the queued completions are completed with
      its error instead of being leaked.
  - **mds: journal the removal of purged strays in batches** — after the
    PurgeQueue takes a stray, StrayManager journaled one EUpdate per stray to
    remove its dentry, so every unlink cost the MDS two journal events. Purged
    strays are now queued per stray dirfrag and journaled together as one
    EUpdate, once 64 are queued for a dirfrag or 10ms after the first one.
    - A stopping rank journals each purged stray at once.
    - Before `shutdown_pass()` caps the log, it journals whatever is still
      queued and waits for strays still on their way to the PurgeQueue or
      queued for delayed eval.

    Journal events per unlink go from 1.91 to 1.03 (easy) and from 1.85 to
    1.02 (hard).

  ### Results

  Single-MDS vstart cluster, libcephfs clients, median of 3 runs. These are the
  numbers in the commit messages.

  **Whole series**, 8 clients, 480k empty files in all in a private directory per
  client and 48k 3901-byte files in one shared directory, 5s between phases:

  |                                         | before | after           |
  |-----------------------------------------|--------|-----------------|
  | easy create ops/s                       | 8978   | 10690 (+19.1%)  |
  | hard create ops/s                       | 5276   | 5285 (+0.2%)    |
  | easy unlink ops/s                       | 9048   | 10989 (+21.5%)  |
  | hard unlink ops/s                       | 8819   | 10035 (+13.8%)  |
  | MDS CPU per create (µs)                 | 183.0  | 167.2 (−8.6%)   |
  | MDS CPU per unlink (µs)                 | 202.8  | 171.1 (−15.6%)  |
  | shared-dir create p99 (ms)              | 10.70  | 6.78            |
  | overall sc

72135.title: .github/workflows: check-license diff inspect files directly
72135.author: nizamial09
72135.body:
as per copilot

> The job is failing because the workflow tries to fetch the full pull request diff with gh pr diff, but GitHub rejects it when the diff is too large:
> 
> Failing step: .github/workflows/check-license.yml
> Error: HTTP 406: Sorry, the diff exceeded the maximum number of lines (20000) Why it fails
> The current workflow does this:
> 
> ```
> DIFF=$(gh pr diff ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} -R ${{ github.repository }}) if echo "$DIFF" | grep -qi "GNU General Public License"; then
>   echo "Error: Incompatible license 'GNU General Public License' found in PR diff."
>   exit 1
> fi
> ```
> For large PRs, gh pr diff can fail before the license check even runs, so the job exits early.
> 
> Suggested fix
> Avoid relying on the full rendered PR diff. Instead, inspect the changed files directly from the pull request files API and search only the patch text for license additions.
> 
> A more robust approach:
> 
> ```
> - name: Check PR files for License env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} run: | pr_number=${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} repo=${{ github.repository }}
> 
>     gh api "repos/$repo/pulls/$pr_number/files" --paginate --jq '.[].patch' |
>       grep -qi "GNU General Public License" && {
>         echo "Error: Incompatible license 'GNU General Public License' found in PR changes."
>         exit 1
>       } || true
> ```

72138.title: osd/ECTransaction: do not re-clone data a truncate has already backed up
72138.author: aainscow
72138.body:
An op on a Fast EC, that does both the following:

1. Truncates the object to a size that is not 4K-aligned on some shard, and
2. Writes to the same 4k page that involved the truncate.

This generates the following transaction on the shard:

1. clone_range head -> rollback object, from the truncate point (rounded
down to 4K) to the old end of the shard
2. truncate head to the exact new size
3. truncate head up to the next 4K boundary (logically a zero-write)
4. clone_range head -> rollback object for the range being written
5. write

Step 4 copies from the head after steps 2 and 3, so where its range overlaps step 1's it replaces the saved data between the truncate point and the 4K boundary with the zeros from step 3.

If the op is rolled back (a divergent log entry after an OSD failure), those bytes are restored as zeros. The object size is correct. Damage on a data shard shows on read; damage on a parity shard only on scrub, a
degraded read or recovery.

This can be exposed in CephFS and RBD, the latter only if sub-4k block sizes are used (e.g. 512b).

For CephFS, this can be hit directly from a file operation.

For RBD, it much more unlikely, but theoretically can be hit if:

512b blocks
Snapshot copy-on-write queues writes
Queued write contains trim operation that happens to be at end of object and is misaligned. (Turns into truncate)
Queued write contains an over-lapping write.
In practice, RBD scenario may be vanishingly rare when combined with the need for a rollback.

Tests: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72140 (test/osd: Add new EC Truncate tests) demonstrates this defect, rolling back truncate-then-write ops through the PG's backend, and depends on this PR.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80962

72139.title: osd/ECUtil: zero the gap between extents that share a page
72139.author: aainscow
72139.body:
Before encoding, pad_and_rebuild_to_ec_align() pads each extent of each shard with zeros to whole pages, and inserts the result back into the shard's extent map. When two extents of a shard lie in the same page, each is padded over the other, and the one inserted second replaces the data of the first with zeros. The zeroed data is encoded into the parity and written to the shard.

The extents to write normally cover whole pages, because the write plan reads the rest of any page that is partly written. Gaps are left where there is nothing to read: above the new end of an object that a truncate in the same op shrinks, and in a page above the old end of the object. So a truncate followed by a write further into the page holding the new end loses the data below the new end, and two writes to a page above the end of the object lose all but one of them.

Fill each such gap with zeros before padding, so that the extents merge into one. The gap reads as zeros, as the padding already assumes.

Fixes https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80963

72147.author: LiShengG

72155.title: os/memstore: do not replace the target of a clone_range with its source
72155.author: aainscow
72155.body:
BufferlistObject::clone() shares the source's data rather than copying it when the range is all of the source at the same offset. That replaces all of the target's data, so it is only right when the target is no longer than the range. When the target is longer, the clone truncates it to the length of the source: cloning the whole of one object to the same offset in a larger object makes the larger object a copy of the smaller one, instead of leaving the rest of it alone.

EC rollback hits this. When an op truncates a shard to a size that is exactly the length of a later write's range starting at offset 0, the write stashes that range by cloning it from the head into the rollback object, which already holds the data that the truncate stashed. With MemStore that clone discards the truncate's stash, so rolling the op back leaves the shard truncated.

Take the shortcut only when the target is no longer than the range, and add a store_test that reproduces the problem; without the fix it fails for MemStore and passes for BlueStore.

This is not a production bug, where memstore is used, however it is a problem for the EC Unit tests.

72156.title: cls/rbd: reject updates to removed group snapshots
72156.author: pkalever
72156.body:
**Problem**

Two group mirror enable operations can overlap. Each operation creates a group snapshot in the `CREATING` state. The snapshot key and its `snap_order` key are created together.

One operation can finish first and remove the other operation's incomplete snapshot. This removes both keys. The slower operation can later finish its image snapshots and try to update the removed group snapshot to `CREATED`.

`group_snap_set()` previously accepted this update and recreated only the snapshot key. It did not recreate the `snap_order` key because order keys are created only for new snapshots in the `CREATING` state.

This left incomplete metadata and caused group snapshot listing to fail with `EINVAL`.

There is also a separate cleanup problem in `group_snap_unlink()`. When the last image was removed from a group snapshot, it removed the snapshot key but left its `snap_order` key behind.

**Solution**

This PR contains two changes:

1. Make `group_snap_unlink()` remove both the snapshot key and its  `snap_order` key.

2. Before `group_snap_set()` updates a snapshot outside the `CREATING` state, require the snapshot key to exist. If the key is missing, log an error and return `EINVAL`.

This allows updates to existing snapshots, including `CREATED -> CREATED` metadata updates, but prevents an update from recreating a removed snapshot.

The tests verify that:

- `group_snap_unlink()` removes both snapshot keys.
- A removed snapshot can be created again through the `CREATING` state.
- A new snapshot cannot be added directly in the `CREATED` state.

**Reproduction steps**

Use an unfixed `cls_rbd` build and a fresh group with mirroring disabled.

1. Start the first group enable operation under GDB:

```
gdb --args ./bin/rbd --cluster site-a mirror group enable pool1/group1 snapshot --debug-rbd=0
```

2. Stop before the incomplete group snapshot is marked complete:

```
break GroupEnableRequest::update_primary_group_snapshot
run
```

Wait for the breakpoint.

3. From another terminal, run a second enable operation and let it finish:

```
./bin/rbd --cluster site-a mirror group enable pool1/group1 snapshot --debug-rbd=0
```

The second operation creates its own snapshot and removes the incomplete snapshot belonging to the paused operation.

4. Continue the paused operation:

```
continue
```

With the unfixed code, the paused operation recreates the snapshot key without its order key.

5. Check the group status:

```
./bin/rbd --cluster site-a mirror group status pool1/group1 --debug-rbd=0
```

The incomplete metadata produces an error similar to:

```
librbd::mirror::GroupGetInfoRequest: failed to list group snapshots of group '10338ac90fa2': (22) Invalid argument

rbd: failed to get mirror info for group 'group1': (22) Invalid argument
```

With this change, the paused operation receives `EINVAL` and cannot recreate the removed snapshot. The group snapshot metadata remains valid.

72165.title: qa/standalone/mon: add wait time for port to bind
72165.author: ljflores
72165.body:
Currently, the test forwards the mon address
to a different port, and immediately tries

The result is that the ping fails, as the port
forwarding command and ping to the monitor all

72166.title: log: load the test prefix hook atomically and only once
72166.author: aainscow
72166.body:
`Log::_flush()` runs on the log thread and did `prefix_hook ? prefix_hook() : nullptr` on a plain global. `PGBackendTestFixture` sets the hook in `SetUp()` and clears it in `TearDown()` on the gtest thread. In a Debug build the global is read twice, and if `TearDown()` clears it between the check and the call, the log thread calls address 0. That is the SIGSEGV in thread `log` with a two-frame backtrace seen in `unittest_backend_basics`.

This makes the hook a `std::atomic` and reads it once into a local before testing and calling it.

**Reproducer (not included):** add a `usleep(2000)` between the check and the call, then run `unittest_backend_basics --gtest_filter='BackendSizes/TestBackendBasics.*/Replicated_*'`. It crashes within a few tests with the same signature as CI. With this fix and the same sleep after the single load, 3 repeats run without a crash. The full `unittest_backend_basics` passes (888 tests).

While this is only used by a single test harness, out of paranoia I am running it through a QA batch, as its not that urgent. 

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80565

72170.title: mgr/DaemonState: prune empty DeviceState in with_device_create
72170.author: stzuraski898
72170.body:
`with_device_create` created a `DeviceState` and ran a callback but never checked whether the device was still `empty()` afterward, unlike its sibling `with_device_write`, which erases the device in that case.

In the current codebase, this asymmetry is dormant: the only two callers—`set-life-expectancy` in `DaemonServer.cc` and the startup `device/*` key loader in `Mgr.cc`—always populate the device before returning, so the new check never fires in practice. The fix is therefore a consistency cleanup: it makes `with_device_create` honor the same post-callback invariant as `with_device_write`, ensuring that any future caller that passes a no-op or emptying callback does not leave a stale entry in the devices map.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80655
Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus)

72171.title: mgr/DaemonState: safely parse wear_level metadata without atof ambiguity
72171.author: stzuraski898
72171.body:
DeviceState::set_metadata parsed the wear_level metadata value with atof(), which returns 0.0 on failure and cannot signal an error. A non-numeric or empty wear_level string was therefore silently coerced to a valid-looking 0.0f, discarding the -1.0 "unknown" sentinel and reporting corrupt or missing wear data as a pristine device. Use strict_strtof() instead and leave wear_level unchanged when parsing fails, so unparseable values preserve the -1.0 unknown sentinel.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80659
Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus)

72172.title: mgr/DaemonState: validate life expectancy bounds to prevent inverted ranges
72172.author: stzuraski898
72172.body:
The device life-expectancy range was recorded without enforcing that the minimum precedes the maximum, so an inverted range could enter through the `device set-life-expectancy` CLI handler or be reloaded from persistent device metadata. In `DeviceState::get_life_expectancy_str()`, the unsigned `utime_t` subtraction `life_expectancy.second - now` then underflows and produces nonsensical duration output. The same subtraction already underflows on the “no upper bound” path, where the maximum is zero, although that value is currently discarded. This dates back to when the prediction became a range in `4920bbd6cb49`, where no `min <= max` check was added.

The fix rejects a `"from"` value that comes after `"to"` in the `device set-life-expectancy` CLI handler with `-EINVAL`, preventing an inverted range from being entered interactively. It also hardens `get_life_expectancy_str()` by guarding the subtraction: the lower bound is computed first, and `">min"` is returned whenever there is no upper bound or the range is inverted (`max <= min`); the maximum is computed only when a valid upper bound exists. This neutralizes a bad range regardless of its source—the CLI, a reload from `config-key`, or any future writer—without mutating the stored state, while also eliminating the unused underflow on the no-upper-bound path. The permissive low-level setter remains unchanged.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80660
Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus)

72173.title: mgr/DaemonState: prevent empty hostname bucket creation in by_server map
72173.author: stzuraski898
72173.body:
DaemonStateIndex::_insert and _erase accessed by_server[dm->hostname] through operator[], so a daemon whose metadata had not yet arrived (empty hostname) created and populated the by_server[""] bucket, violating the invariant that by_server is keyed only by real hostnames. That contaminated bucket leaked into get_by_server(""), with_daemons_by_server() and list_devids_by_server(""), corrupting the mgr host view. This behaviour dates back to the original implementation in ac30e6cee2b2. The fix gates both the by_server insert and erase on a non-empty hostname; the daemon is still tracked in `all` and gains a by_server entry once update_metadata() supplies its real hostname.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80661
Assisted-by: Claude Code (Opus)

72174.title: mgr/DaemonState: release lock before callbacks in with_devices2 to avoid GIL inversion
72174.author: stzuraski898
72174.body:
with_devices2 held the DaemonStateIndex shared_lock across its cbi() and per-device cb() callbacks, which reacquire the Python GIL via ActivePyModules::get_python. Holding the index lock while a callback blocks on the GIL inverts the lock/GIL acquisition order against threads that hold the GIL and take a unique_lock on the index, deadlocking the mgr. Copy the devices map under the shared_lock and release it before invoking the callbacks, so no lock is held during any callback, matching the snapshot-then-release fix applied to with_daemons_by_server in b4304d521f61.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80662
Assisted-by: IBM Bob

72175.title: crimson: support reference wrappers in error assertions
72175.author: tchaikov
72175.body:
Backport fmt's transparent std::reference_wrapper<T> formatter for system fmt before 11.1.0. fmt 11.1.0 introduced the native implementation in upstream commit https://github.com/fmtlib/fmt/commit/1f87b1c58d2d466b283f282211b732a4e3987659.

72176.title: cephfs-shell: drop compatibility with cmd2 < 1.0.1
72176.author: tchaikov
72176.body:
cephfs-shell branched on cmd2's reported version so it could support cmd2 as old as 0.7.9, plus a distro-sniffing DFLAG workaround for how Ubuntu 22.04's cmd2 package reports its version as "0.0.0". None of that applies anymore.

qa/suites/fs/shell installs cephfs-shell as a distro package with no cmd2 pin, and the distros that suite actually rotates through (qa/suites/fs/shell/distro -> .qa/distros/supported: Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, CentOS 9 Stream, Rocky 10) all ship cmd2 2.3 or newer. Every threshold in the code (0.9.6, 0.9.13, 0.9.23, 0.10.0, 1.0.1) predates all four by several years, and the comment justifying the oldest branch, "we use cmd2 v0.7.9 with teuthology," is stale: nothing in the current qa suite pins that version.

Drop the version checks and always take the modern-cmd2 path. This also drops the runtime dependency on the distro and packaging modules, which existed only for the version sniffing.

72180.title: rgw/s3vectors: Allow Objects in Vector Buckets
72180.author: soumyakoduri
72180.body:
This PR enables object storage in vector buckets, allowing LanceDB data to be stored directly in the VectorBucket instead of using regular S3 bucket.

1) A new boolean config option "**rgw_s3vector_data_s3_bucket**" is added to control storage selection for rgw backend.
- false (default): Store LanceDB files directly in the vector bucket.
- true: Store LanceDB files in a separate S3 bucket with the same name. That S3 bucket must exist before the vector bucket is created.

storage mode is selected based on this option value during VectorBucket creation and will remain the same through out that bucket lifecyle. Configuration changes affect only newly created vector buckets; they do not migrate existing data. The local filesystem backend is unaffected.

2) This PR also handles changes to allow vector-bucket and S3 bucket share same bucket-instance namespace.

With this, S3 and vector buckets retain separate entrypoints and listings while sharing the bucket-instance metadata namespace. Distinct bucket IDs keep their data separate, even when their names match. Native vector objects are accessible through internal RGW operations, not through the S3 object API.

Below is the feature status for native vector buckets:

**TODO: (will be addressed as follow-up)**
Resharding 
Vector Bucket Policies
User-selected storage through bucket tags/attrs (apart from admin controlled config options)
Quota,
chown,
Bucket and Owner stats,
Usage accounting,

**NA:**
S3 SetACL API - Not exposed for vector buckets; the default owner ACL is retained
Multisite replication - Disabled for vector metadata and data
Lifecycle, object expiration, cloud transition and restore - Not supported for native vector storage

GC and deduplication are expected to use the existing bucket-agnostic mechanisms; they should be working for vector buckets as well.

Signed-off-by: Soumya Koduri <skoduri@redhat.com>
