72187.title: qa/rbd: report concurrent workunit failures
72187.author: popododo0720
72187.body:
## Summary
- Collect every concurrent pass exit status so create, map, write, read, comparison, unmap, and removal failures fail the workunit.
- Limit cleanup and reads to images created by this workunit, and discard the ownership reservation if creation fails.
- Atomically publish the device ID after writing. Readers hold a shared image lock and recheck readiness; teardown holds the exclusive lock and withdraws readiness before unmapping. Keep lock files until cleanup to protect stale readers.
- Limit comparison to the source data length and explicitly propagate each read failure, including when callers test the function status.

Concurrency coverage: creates, writes to different images, reads, and removals still overlap across passes. Reads and teardown of the same image are deliberately serialized, so the workunit no longer exercises unmapping a device during an active read of that device.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76990

## Testing
- `bash -n qa/workunits/rbd/concurrent.sh qa/workunits/rbd/test_concurrent_failure.sh`
- `bash qa/workunits/rbd/test_concurrent_failure.sh`: all 14 checks passed. Injected create, map, missing-device-ID, write, initial/middle read, actual data corruption, unmap, and removal errors exited 2. Single-pass success, concurrent success, and a mapped-but-unwritten peer exited 0. Held-reader/teardown overlap and stale-reader checks passed. Every workunit case preserved an unrelated image and mapping.
- The fixture substitutes sysfs/device paths, mocks RBD operations, and uses real sparse-file writes, reads, and `cmp`.
- Additional fixture stress: 24 passes across 3 iterations passed.
- Negative controls: removing the comparison length limit, publishing readiness before writing, ignoring a middle read failure, or removing the reader lock each caused the regression tests to fail.
- `git diff --check`
- Real kernel RBD validation: using existing development binaries and a separate localhost, one-OSD, no-auth memstore vstart cluster, ran `concurrent.sh -i 1 -c 1 -d 0` and `concurrent.sh -i 1 -c 2 -d 0`. Both exited 0 with real RBD create/map/write/read/compare/unmap/remove operations; the concurrent run mapped two images. Only cluster config/admin identity and redundant root `sudo` were wrapped; RBD, kernel devices, `dd`, and `cmp` were real. Both runs left zero images, mappings, and temporary files. The isolated runtime and kernel module were removed, and the pre-existing development cluster retained zero pools. The default 100-by-5 workload and teuthology/CI suites were not run locally.

72199.title: mgr: explicit interfaces for cross-module KV reads and remote() calls
72199.author: NitzanMordhai
72199.body:
Modules exchange data in two informal ways today: `remote()`, which lets any module call any method of another module (private and inherited ones included), and raw `config-key` reads of another module's `mgr/<module>/` keys. Neither has a contract, so internal methods and key layouts quietly become APIs. This PR gives both paths an explicit interface. It is a contract between modules, checked in CI, not a performance change and not a security boundary.

- mgr: add `SharedStorePolicy`. A module declares, in a `SHARED_STORE` class attribute, which prefix of its KV store which other modules may read. The owner stays the only writer.
- mgr: add `MgrModule.get_store_ex(module, key)`, checked against the owner's policy and read from the local KV cache. An invalid `SHARED_STORE` fails the module load, and an unknown reader name is logged.
- mgr: add a `@remote_export` decorator for the methods a module offers to `remote()`, read when the module loads. A method stays exported in a subclass that overrides it. `MgrModule` marks `self_test()` and `can_run()`. `ceph mgr api ls [<module>]` lists the exports. Nothing is refused at runtime.
- mgr: add `check_remote_calls.py` and a `check-remote-calls` tox env. It flags `remote()` calls to methods the target module doesn't export, `config-key` commands on another module's keys, and `config-key get` of a module's own key through `mon_command` (use `get_store()`). Existing findings are in a baseline file, so only new ones fail.
- mgr: roll back the KV cache when the mon rejects a `set_store()`. The cache was updated before the mon replied, so a rejected value stayed visible to `get_store()`, and now to `get_store_ex()` readers too.
- mgr/orchestrator: export the `Orchestrator` interface, so cephadm, rook and test_orchestrator export it, and replace the `remote('orchestrator', '_select_orchestrator')` call with an exported `select_orchestrator()`.
- mgr/cephadm: seed `prometheus.yml` with `get_store()`/`set_store()` instead of `config-key` commands through the mon.

The orchestrator and cephadm commits are examples of clearing baseline entries. The remaining entries (about 100, mostly volumes, progress, mirroring, nfs and snap_schedule methods) are cleared by each module's owners in follow-up PRs: mark the called methods with `@remote_export` and drop the module's lines from the baseline.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80847
Assisted-by: IBM-Bob:ClaudeSonnet
Assisted-by: Claude

72210.title: osd/OSDMap: report balance metrics per device class in ceph osd df
72210.author: manya-dogra
72210.body: Ceph osd df currently calculates MIN/MAX VAR and STDDEV across all OSDs in the cluster. In clusters with different device classes such as HDD, SSD, and NVMe, each class can have different utilization patterns. Using one cluster-wide average can make OSDs within a device class appear more or less balanced than they actually are. This change updates ceph osd df and ceph osd df tree in both plain-text and JSON/XML formats to calculate and report average utilization, MIN/MAX VAR, and weighted STDDEV separately for each CRUSH device class. This makes it easier to check the balance of OSDs within each device class. 72211.title: monitoring: compare NVMe-oF gateway CPU in percent
72211.author: banlor
72211.body:
The NVMe-oF gateway reactor counter accumulates busy seconds. Its per-second rate is a fraction, but `NVMeoFHighGatewayCPU` compares that fraction with the configured threshold of 80. In the full-rule replay, a gateway at 90% stayed silent after 15 minutes.

Scale the averaged rate by 100 in both the Ceph mixin source and shipped rules. The configured threshold stays 80, and the 10-minute `for`, labels, and annotations are unchanged. The regression exercises two gateways, multiple reactor threads, the pending period, and the exact 80% boundary.

| Gateway load | Before, at 15m | After, at 15m |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 90% | no alert | alert |
| 80% | no alert | no alert |
| 50% | no alert | no alert |

`promtool test rules tests_alerts/test_nvmeof_cpu.yml` and `promtool check rules prometheus_alerts.yml` pass. The existing all-alert fixture has the same unrelated failures on base and this branch under promtool 3.15.0; the isolated regression passes and is registered with both tox and CTest. The new CTest registration was exercised in isolation, not through a full Ceph build. Jsonnet generation produces the same changed NVMe-oF expression, while the repository's checked-in YAML already differs from generated output in unrelated rules.

AI tools assisted with the patch, tests and review. Found while studying alert rules across projects; the study reports results only in aggregate. This is a source-backed synthetic replay of ceph-nvmeof 1.7.23, not a claim about a live gateway.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81134

72216.title: rbd-fuse: avoid freeing option defaults with libfuse3
72216.author: popododo0720
72216.body:
## Summary
`rbd-fuse -p rbd mnt` can crash in `free()` inside `fuse_opt_parse()` when built against libfuse3. Unlike libfuse2, libfuse3 frees the previous `%s` option value before replacing it; the pool and namespace defaults currently point at string literals.

- Initialize the string option fields to null, so the parser only replaces null or allocated strings.
- Apply the existing default pool (`rbd`) and namespace (empty string) when initializing the filesystem, using const pointers for those defaults.
- Add a CTest regression that invokes the real executable with short, long, empty, and repeated pool/namespace options. It requests `-V` after the options to exercise FUSE parsing without mounting or connecting to a cluster. `--version` would exit earlier during Ceph argument parsing.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/71594

## Testing
- Reproduced the unfixed executable's SIGSEGV with libfuse 3.14.0, with `free()` and `fuse_opt_parse()` in the stack.
- Compiled and linked the updated `rbd-fuse.cc` separately against libfuse 2.9.9 and 3.14.0, reusing existing local Ceph build dependencies.
- `bash -n src/test/rbd_fuse/options.sh`
- `src/test/rbd_fuse/options.sh <rbd-fuse-binary>`: all 12 option combinations passed for each library version (24 total invocations).
- The same regression failed against the unfixed libfuse3 executable at `-p rbd`.
- Validated the actual CTest registration block in a minimal CMake harness: the test passed for both library versions and was excluded with either `WITH_FUSE=OFF` or `WITH_RBD=OFF`.
- `git diff --check`
- Live cluster validation on 2026-10-01: three-node Ceph 20.2.2 cluster (3 MONs and 3 OSDs), using Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 clients and the same updated executables described above.

72219.title: tools/ceph-erasure-code-tool: fix crashes and wrong decode output
72219.author: sunyuechi
72219.body:
- **stop when ec_init() fails** — it returns 1 on error, but three
  subcommands only checked `r < 0` and went on with a null plugin,
  crashing with SIGSEGV.
- **reject a stripe unit the plugin cannot use** — the given stripe unit
  was used as the chunk size as is. cauchy_orig needs k*w*packetsize
  aligned chunks and wrote past the buffers when given 4096. Reject a
  stripe unit that `get_chunk_size()` would round up.
- **decode shard files by shard id** — encode names files by shard id,
  decode remapped the numbers through `get_shard()` again. With lrc the
  chunks landed in the wrong places even with every shard present.
- **decode whole stripes** — the range to rebuild came from the shards
  given, so without shard 0 the output lost the first chunk, and without
  the shard holding the tail it lost the last. Round the range out to
  stripe boundaries, as encode always writes whole stripes.
- **refuse plugins that need sub-chunks** — clay does not implement the
  shard_id_map interface and aborted with "Not implemented for this
  plugin". Report an error instead.

test_ceph-erasure-code-tool.sh covers each case.

72220.title: erasure-code/lrc: fix decode of multi-layer losses
72220.author: sunyuechi
72220.body:
- **retry layers after a layer recovers chunks** — layers were walked
  once, so with k=4 m=2 l=3 losing a data chunk and its local parity
  returned -EIO and the PG went down.
- **decode chunks that are neither in nor out** — a missing chunk that
  was not wanted was read from an empty buffer and hit
  `ceph_assert(size == ptr.length())`.

TestErasureCodeLrc covers both cases.

72228.title: osd: keep FastEC peering from resetting an acting shard without backfill
72228.author: vitaly-goot
72228.body:
With `allow_ec_optimizations`, peering can keep a shard that is behind the log tail in the acting set, or pick it as an async recovery target, without making it a backfill target. `activate()` then resets that shard to empty (`last_backfill` MIN), nobody backfills it, and the PG goes active+clean one shard short. The next write to the PG trips

```
FAILED ceph_assert(is_backfill_target(peer))
```

in `PrimaryLogPG::should_send_op()`. The tracker has the full sequence from the logs: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81183

### What changed since the first version

Alex's review asked for reproducers before anything else, for the GetMissing re-check to wait for the logs it had requested instead of leaving them in flight, for the three-round cap to fail closed, for one helper shared by `choose_acting()` and `GetLog`, and for the `consider_adjusting_pwlc()` change to go. This version does all of that; the replies on the review threads have the details. The reproducers come first in the series so they can be read, and run, on their own.

### The commits

1. **test/osd: reproduce peering leaving an acting shard empty without a backfill.** Three `PeeringStateTest` cases that fail on main:
   - `Issue81183_PwlcRollForward` (2+2): pwlc covers a shard when the acting set is chosen, `proc_master_log()` then rolls it to the write that was in flight, and `activate()` resets the shard without a backfill. On main the PG ends active+clean with shard 1 empty.
   - `Issue81183_ContiguityTail` (2+3): `auth_log_shard` has a longer log than `get_log_shard`, so a shard whose head lies between the two tails is taken as an async recovery target and reset.
   - `Issue81183_FourShardsBehind` (5+5): four nonprimary shards come back behind the tail in one interval. On main all four are reset; with the first version of this PR the fourth was still lost.

   The fixture also gets a check that runs after every activation: a shard sitting at `last_backfill` MIN has to be a backfill target.
2. **osd: judge optimized EC contiguity against the log the primary builds.** `calc_ec_acting()` compared each shard with `auth_log_shard`'s tail, but the primary builds its log from `get_log_shard` and GetLog only extends it back to that shard's tail. `choose_acting()` now uses the later of the two tails, and `GetLog`'s `request_log_from` loop uses the same bound through `log_tail_after_getlog()`, so a shard the acting set accepts is a shard GetLog really requests logs back to.
3. **osd: choose the acting set again for shards behind the log tail.** GetMissing notes every acting and async recovery shard that is behind the tail and not a backfill target, on entry and again as each requested log arrives. Once all requested logs are in it goes back to GetLog once, where `choose_acting()` makes those shards backfill targets. There is no round limit any more: a shard found behind a second time in the same interval is a cluster error and the PG goes `Incomplete` instead of activating with a shard it would wipe; it tries GetLog again when new peering info arrives.

### How it was tested

- `unittest_peeringstate`: 58/58 with the fix. On main the three new tests fail (55/58), and the first version of this PR fails `Issue81183_FourShardsBehind` exactly as described in the review (one shard left empty after three rounds).
- On a 55-OSD test cluster (11 hosts, 8+3 pool with `allow_ec_optimizations`, a v20.2.4-based tree with these commits on top): three runs of the procedure that reproduces the bug on stock, every OSD SIGKILLed under load, restarted host by host, with a messenger delay on the first host back. Result: no PG left clean with an empty shard, 726 backfill starts and all of them to real backfill targets, the re-choice fired in 15 PGs and never a second time on the same shard, no asserts. On stock the same procedure gives 6 PGs with an empty shard and 4 OSD asserts in one run. Three more all-OSD kills under a different write pattern and no delay were

72229.title: osd: Improve debug for PeeringState state machine crashes
72229.author: bill-scales
72229.body:
Currently when the PeeringState state machine crashes because of an invalid state transition it provides no debug about which state it was previously in or the stimulus that caused the crash. Add this information to the abort message.

The state machine is hierarchical, make sure that we capture the innermost state (which is exited first) rather than the outermost state (which is exited last) before entering the crashed state.

---

Here's a test to show what the new output looks like using adeliberate bug to cause a peering state machine crash when local recovery reservations are acquired:

--- a/src/osd/PeeringState.h
+++ b/src/osd/PeeringState.h
@@ -1222,7 +1222,7 @@ public:

   struct WaitLocalRecoveryReserved : boost::statechart::state< WaitLocalRecoveryReserved, Active >, NamedState {
     typedef boost::mpl::list <
-      boost::statechart::transition< LocalRecoveryReserved, WaitRemoteRecoveryReserved >,
+      //BUG!      boost::statechart::transition< LocalRecoveryReserved, WaitRemoteRecoveryReserved >,
       boost::statechart::custom_reaction< RecoveryTooFull >
       > reactions;
     explicit WaitLocalRecoveryReserved(my_context ctx);

Procedure to cause a crash with this state transition:

Start cluster
Take one osd down
Create object with rados put
Bring osd up, PG will try and recover

New assert:

`/ceph/src/osd/PeeringState.cc: 5445: ceph_abort_msg("bad state machine event in state 'Started/Primary/Active/WaitLocalRecoveryReserved': epoch_sent: 31 epoch_requested: 31 LocalRecoveryReserved")
`
The new assert shows the previous state and the stimulus that caused the state machine to crash

72236.title: osdc/Objecter: re-target forced-OSD direct reads when the PG changes
72236.author: aainscow
72236.body:
Split sub-reads and single-chunk EC direct reads are pinned to one shard OSD with CEPH_OSD_FLAG_FORCE_OSD. If that OSD leaves the acting set, the Objecter is supposed to fail the sub-read with -EAGAIN so that the parent op is retried at the primary (or, for a single direct read, redrive it to the primary). In vstart testing with thrashing, a localized or balanced EC split read with a sub-read outstanding to a shard OSD that died or was marked down never completed, even after the OSD came back and every PG was active+clean. The client log showed the sub-op move to the homeless session and every later map report 'no change'. It reproduced 3 times out of 3.

The causes were in the Objecter's retargeting. _calc_target() only re-targets such a sub-read on a change of primary unless the target is marked used_replica, and it clears used_replica whenever it recomputes a target, so even a correctly marked target lost it after the first resend. A resend after a primary change rebuilt the pgid without the forced shard, so the shard OSD parked the read waiting for a PG that never appears. A new interval that left the acting set alone (for example a min_size change) did not resend the read, although a non-primary OSD drops direct reads from an earlier interval.

Unit tests with a real Objecter then found two more ways the same path fails when a map lands while _op_submit() has dropped its lock: later sub-reads were sent using the parent's target from the older map, and the parked sub-read completed with -EAGAIN through _check_op_pool_dne() while still registered for a map check, which aborts the client. A deterministic test of that race needs a hook in the Objecter, so #72289, which is stacked on this PR, adds the hook and the test. Any client using localize or balance reads on EC pools (librbd, CephFS, librados) is affected; for stretch pools these are the normal read paths.

```
           e1: read issued      e2: osd.1 marked down     e3: osd.1 back up
           ---------------      ---------------------     -----------------
BEFORE
  +---------------------+    +-----------------------+    +-----------------+
  | sub-read -> osd.1   |    | _calc_target():       |    | still no change |
  |   (shard 1)         |--->|   primary unchanged   |--->| seen for the op |
  | FORCE_OSD,          |    |   -> NO_ACTION        |    |                 |
  | EC_DIRECT_READ      |    | op parked in the      |    | parent read     |
  |                     |    |   homeless session    |    | NEVER completes |
  +---------------------+    +-----------------------+    +-----------------+

AFTER
  +---------------------+    +-----------------------+    +-----------------+
  | sub-read -> osd.1   |    | FORCE_OSD target:     |    | parent read     |
  |   (shard 1)         |--->|   any new interval    |--->| retried at the  |
  | FORCE_OSD,          |    |   counts as a change  |    | primary (osd.0) |
  | EC_DIRECT_READ      |    | osd.1 not at shard 1  |    |                 |
  |                     |    |   -> -EAGAIN          |    | read completes  |
  +---------------------+    +-----------------------+    +-----------------+
```
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81194

72237.title: test: shrink benchmark iterations under any sanitizer
72237.author: Doracly
72237.body:
e16e6398b1e cut the bufferlist benchmark rounds to 2 under ASan. This extends that to all sanitizers and to three more benchmarks:

- `test/sanitized_bench.h` provides `sanitized_bench_rounds(n)`, which returns `min(n, 2)` when `CEPH_SANITIZED` is defined and `n` otherwise.
- The top-level `CMakeLists.txt` defines `CEPH_SANITIZED` whenever `WITH_ASAN`, `WITH_ASAN_LEAK`, `WITH_TSAN` or `WITH_UBSAN` is enabled. The compiler macros aren't enough, since UBSan has none of its own.
- It is used in the bufferlist benchmarks (replacing `asan_bench_rounds()`), `bluestore_blob_t.csum_bench`, `Transaction.GetNumBytesBench*` and `MemoryIsZeroPerformance`.

Only loops that repeat the same work are shortened; the distinct cases (sizes, steps, checksum types, …) still run in their outer loops. Builds without a sanitizer are unchanged.

### Effect under TSan

GCC 15.2, Debug build with `-DWITH_TSAN=ON`; each binary run directly (not via ctest), before and after on the same machine and base:

| Test | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `unittest_bufferlist` | 26.4 min | 33.1 s |
| `unittest_bluestore_types` | 225 s | 201 s |
| └ `bluestore_blob_t.csum_bench` | 24.9 s | 0.43 s |
| `unittest_transaction` | 19.0 s | 0.21 s |
| `unittest_memory` | 14.5 s | 0.19 s |

`unittest_bufferlist` used to be by far the longest unit test under TSan, roughly 7x the next one, so a TSan run of all unit tests took at least ~26 min regardless of `-j`. Now the longest remaining tests take about 4 min, and the run scales with the number of jobs.

### Coverage

The shortened loops still exercise every case at least once. Before and after this change, TSan reports races at the same code locations in these binaries (on current main they hit the known `mempool::get_pool()` race); only the number of repeated reports drops.

72241.title: mgr/dashboard: fix ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH caused by unhandled SSLWantWriteError
72241.author: nmunet
72241.body:
Problem
===

Large static files served by the Ceph Dashboard over HTTPS intermittently fail to download completely. Clients see ERR_CONTENT_LENGTH_MISMATCH (Chrome) or unexpected EOF while reading (curl). tcpdump confirms the TCP RST originates from the server side, mid-response.

The failure is intermittent because it only occurs when the kernel TCP send buffer is full and the non-blocking ssl.SSLSocket.write() call cannot proceed immediately. At that point Python raises ssl.SSLWantWriteError (or ssl.SSLWantReadError during TLS renegotiation). Neither is a subclass of io.BlockingIOError:

Cheroot's BufferedWriter._flush_unlocked only catches io.BlockingIOError, so the SSL want-* exception propagates uncaught to Cheroot's connection handler, which closes the socket and sends a TCP RST to the client with the response body incomplete. This affects Cheroot 10.x and 11.x; neither version fixes the BuiltinSSLAdapter path.

Fix
===

Add _SSLStreamWriter (subclasses cheroot.makefile.StreamWriter) which overrides _flush_unlocked to also catch ssl.SSLWantWriteError and ssl.SSLWantReadError, treating both as n=0 (no bytes consumed, retry the write on the next loop iteration) — the same semantics io.BlockingIOError already implements for plain non-blocking sockets.

Add _SSLBuiltinAdapter (subclasses cheroot.ssl.builtin.BuiltinSSLAdapter) which overrides makefile() to return _SSLStreamWriter for write-mode sockets. CherryPyMgr.create_adapter is updated to use _SSLBuiltinAdapter instead of BuiltinSSLAdapter.

Testing

Verified by running 50 sequential throttled downloads (--limit-rate 50k) of main.js (~1.16 MB compressed) against a live cluster. Before the fix, random requests terminated short of the advertised Content-Length. After the fix, all 50 complete with a consistent byte count matching Content-Length.

72251.title: rgw: fix crash in RGWWatcher::reinit()
72251.author: jhoblitt
72251.body:
This revives the stale-closed PR ceph/ceph#68207 ("rgw: fix crash in
RGWWatcher::reinit()") by @abhishek593. That PR was never reviewed and was
closed by the stale bot on 2026-07-15, not rejected. The bug it fixes is still
present on `main`. The original commit is carried here unchanged (authorship
preserved as @abhishek593); this PR only adds a second `Fixes:` reference and a
second `Signed-off-by:`. Full credit for the fix goes to Abhishek Bansal.

`RGWWatcher::reinit()` crashes with SIGSEGV or stack smashing (SIGABRT) when OSD
watch connections break during normal operation. There are three bugs in the
`reinit()`/`handle_error()` interaction:

1. Missing `return` after scheduling a retry when `unregister_watch()` fails.
   Execution falls through to `register_watch()` with the old watch not cleaned
   up.
2. No guard against duplicate `C_ReinitWatch` callbacks. Each `handle_error()`
   unconditionally schedules a new reinit, so rapid watch failures queue
   multiple redundant reinit cycles.
3. The `retries` counter is never reset on success, so a long-running watcher
   that recovers many times over its lifetime eventually crosses the
   `retries > 100` threshold and calls `abort()`. This is the specific
   denial-of-service reported as [tracker #80992](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80992): a radosgw aborts even though
   every earlier watch episode recovered.

The fix adds the missing `return`, uses an atomic `reinit_pending` flag to
deduplicate `C_ReinitWatch` scheduling, and resets `retries` after a successful
re-registration. Change (3) resolves [#80992](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80992); the PR also carries [#73564](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73564), the
watch2 segfault it was originally filed for.

72252.title: crush,osd: ignore device class shadows in stretch peering
72252.author: dvanders
72252.body:
Stretch peering resolves each OSD's site through the pool's CRUSH rule. With a device-class rule, that gives the shadow bucket (dc1~ssd), which never matches the real bucket the monitors record as the surviving site in degraded stretch mode. As a result, every PG of such a pool goes inactive when a site is lost, and it stays inactive after the site returns until someone runs force_healthy_stretch_mode.

This adds CrushWrapper::get_nonshadow_parent_of_type(), which maps a shadow bucket back to its original, and uses it in stretch_set_can_peer() and calc_replicated_acting_stretch(). Other callers of get_parent_of_type() only compare the results with each other, so they are left unchanged.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81216

Testing:
  - New unit test CrushWrapperTest.get_nonshadow_parent_of_type; all 25 tests in unittest_crush_wrapper pass.
  - vstart repro on 18.2.8 (2 sites, 5 mons, 8 OSDs, pools on class ssd and class ssd-meta rules, one site killed and then restored). Active PGs per pool, out of 16:

|  | site down | site restored |
| :--- | :---: | ---: |
| before the fix | 0/16 active  | 0/16 active, stuck in recovering stretch mode |
| after the fix  | 16/16 active | 16/16 active+clean, healthy stretch mode on its own |

72253.title: cls/otp: use liboath's signed otp_pos for the replay index
72253.author: jhoblitt
72253.body:
`otp_instance::verify()` computed its replay-guard index from the **return
value** of `oath_totp_validate2()`, which liboath documents as the *absolute
value* of the matched position in the search window. The signed position (past
negative, future positive) is delivered only through the `int *otp_pos` output
parameter, which the call passed `nullptr` and discarded.

For a code matched N steps in the past (true step `current_step - N`), the index
was recorded as `current_step + N` -- `2*N` steps ahead of the true step.
`last_success` then jumped ahead and the `index <= last_success` guard refused
legitimate codes for the intervening steps, including the true current step;
within the window an earlier code could also outrank a later one. No code outside
the TOTP window is ever accepted, so this does **not** bypass MFA.

The fix captures the signed position via `&otp_pos` and computes the matched step
directly (`index = (secs - time_ofs) / effective_step_size(otp) + otp_pos`), which equals
liboath's own matched counter.

**Overlap:** ceph/ceph#72250 (fix for [tracker #80948](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80948), the division-by-zero on a
stored `step_size` of 0) edited the same `index = ...` statement and has merged; this
is rebased onto it and keeps its `effective_step_size(otp)` divisor.

72254.title: squid: rgw/rados: guard against dir suggest during reshard
72254.author: jhoblitt

squid backport of commit 461be1cd3d5 ("rgw/rados: guard against dir suggest
during reshard", ceph/ceph#59609).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82185

On squid, bucket listing sends `cls_rgw_suggest_changes` to repair stale index

(`o.assert_exists()` + `cls_rgw_guard_bucket_resharding(o, -ERR_BUSY_RESHARDING)`)
at both squid listing call sites in `RGWRados::cls_bucket_list_ordered` and the
`check_updates` path. Clean cherry-pick (`-x`); no conflict.

72255.title: rgw: bound rgw_cache_expiry_interval to prevent timespan overflow
72255.author: jhoblitt
72255.body:
`rgw_cache_expiry_interval` (a uint of seconds) is widened to a `ceph::timespan`
(a 64-bit **unsigned** nanosecond count) at both use sites — `ObjectCache::set_ctx()`
in `src/rgw/rgw_cache.h` and `RGWChainedCacheImpl::init()` in
`src/rgw/services/svc_sys_obj_cache.h` — via `expiry = std::chrono::seconds(secs)`.
That multiplies by 1e9 and overflows 2^64 for any value above
`floor((2^64-1)/1e9) = 18446744073` s, silently corrupting the expiry:

- `18446744074` -> ~0.29 s (near-instant expiry, cache re-fetch storm)
- any multiple of 2^55 -> `0`, which the `if (expiry.count() && ...)` guard treats as
  "expiry disabled", so entries never expire
- `2^64-1` -> ~584 years (effectively never)

This PR adds `min`/`max` bounds to the option in `src/common/options/rgw.yaml.in`. Every
config set path goes through `Option::validate()`, so an out-of-range value is rejected at
set time, covering both use sites with one bound. The cap uses `17_G` (18253611008 s,
~578 years — the largest 2^30-second multiple whose nanosecond widening stays below 2^64),
because the option codegen only emits a `max` via the `min`/`max` unit-literal form (same
pattern as `mds_max_snaps_per_dir`). Matches the `rgw_*_max_objs` `min:` precedent in
https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72160.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81218

A self-contained C++17 reproducer that performs the exact conversion is included in the
tracker ticket.

72256.title: rgw: clamp bucket creation shard count to rgw_shards_max()
72256.author: jhoblitt
72256.body:
`init_default_bucket_layout()` stored a new bucket's index shard count from
`rgw_override_bucket_index_max_shards` (or an explicit `CreateBucket` request)
without clamping it to `rgw_shards_max()` (65521). Bucket-index shard selection is
`(hval % 65521) % num_shards`, so any count >= 65522 leaves shard indices 65521 and
above permanently unreachable (dead). The reshard path and the `RGWRados` runtime
member already clamp this value; only the creation path was unguarded. This clamps it
with `std::min(..., rgw_shards_max())` — a no-op for counts <= 65521 — matching the
existing clamp behavior rather than a hard option maximum that would reject an existing
admin config on upgrade. Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/70980

72260.title: osd: keep a newer entry's missing item for skipped partial writes
72260.author: vitaly-goot
72260.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81225

With `allow_ec_optimizations`, `PGLog::_merge_object_divergent_entries()` can undo the missing entry that `merge_log()` has just added for a newer authoritative update of an object. This happens on a shard where every divergent entry of the object is a partial write that skipped the shard.

It is a regression from #68727 (f4237ca47e0, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75962). Since that change, the "more recent entry found, already merged" case requires a kept entry (`!entries.empty()`). These objects therefore fall through to case 2 or 3 with the skipped entry's `prior_version`. Example: shard 2 of a 4+2 pool, a divergent 10'100 (prior_version 10'99) that skipped it, and 11'110 in the authoritative log:

| Missing item after `merge_log()` added 11'110 | After the divergent merge |
|---|---|
| need 11'110, have 10'99 (object was not missing) | removed (case 3: have == prior_version) |
| need 11'110, have 9'50 (object already missing) | need lowered to 10'99 (case 3) |
| need 11'110, have 0 (both entries create the object) | removed, and the object deleted (case 2) |
| need 11'110, have 11'105 (a newer partial write 11'105 also skipped the shard, then 11'110 wrote it) | need lowered to 10'99, below have (case 3) |

The fourth row comes from Alex Ainscow's fault-injection testing on a 4+2 pool: it tripped the "unexpected need for missing item" assert in `MissingLoc::add_active_missing()`, the assert of https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73249, with a different cause.

Only nonprimary shards are affected, because partial writes always write shard 0 and the parity shards. In the current interval the primary still recovers the object, because it computed the peer's missing before this merge. But the shard persists the wrong missing set. If the PG re-peers before the object is recovered, the object is not recovered on that shard. The tracker has the sequence and the logs.

Affected:
- main;
- umbrella (v21.1.0, v21.1.1);
- tentacle, since #70570 (merged after v20.2.4).

It needs backports to umbrella and tentacle before tentacle's next release.

### Fix

When every divergent entry skipped the shard and the log has a newer entry for the object, return before cases 2 and 3. The divergent entries never touched the object on this shard, and missing already reflects the newer entries. Without a newer entry the merge still rolls missing back, as #68727 intended.

### Testing

Unit tests in `src/test/osd/TestPGLog.cc`:
- New: `PGLogTest.merge_log_skipped_partial_write_then_newer_entry` runs the three rows above through `merge_log()` on shard 2 of a 4+2 pool. It also runs the case #68727 fixed (no newer entry: need goes back to `prior_version`).
- Updated: test case 7 of `PGLogTest.merge_object_divergent_entries_partial_writes` was meant to cover case 1 with a partial write. Its log did not index objects, so case 1 never ran. The log is now indexed, and the test also checks `need`.

Both fail without the fix and pass with it, and the rest of `unittest_pglog` passes. These runs used a v20.2.4 tree with the tentacle backport of #68727 (#70570). On main, `_merge_object_divergent_entries()` differs only in whitespace and in `trim_after_remove()`, which this path does not reach.

TODO: `unittest_pglog` result on this branch.

### Review notes

- The new check sits next to case 1 rather than widening it. Case 1 clears `have`, marks the object dirty and removes it, which is right for an object the divergent entries changed. Here they did not change it. If the newer entries also skipped the shard, the object is not in missing, and removing it would drop data that nothing recovers.
- `entries` is empty only when every non-error divergent entry was skipped, so `last` is the newest skipped entry.

72261.title: rgw: require positive values for five quota/usage duration options
72261.author: jhoblitt
72261.body:
Five `type: int` RGW duration options in `src/common/options/rgw.yaml.in` have no lower
bound, so a non-positive value drives a radosgw thread into a busy loop or makes the quota
stats cache unusable:

- `rgw_usage_log_tick_interval` <= 0: the usage-log `SafeTimer` event is always already due,
  so the timer thread flushes and re-arms with no pause.
- `rgw_user_quota_sync_interval` <= 0, and `rgw_user_quota_bucket_sync_interval` <= 0 on
  Squid: `cond.wait_for(seconds(N))` returns immediately, so the sync thread spins. On
  Tentacle/main the `uint64`/`std::max`/`std::chrono::seconds` conversion turns 0 and small
  negatives into a 1 s wait and larger negatives into an immediate return (spin).
- `rgw_bucket_quota_ttl` <= 0: cached expiration never exceeds now, so cached stats are
  never used and every quota check hits the backend.
- `rgw_user_quota_sync_wait_time` <= 0: the minimum-time-between-full-syncs throttle is
  defeated and a full sync runs every cycle.

None of these values has a documented "disable" meaning at 0, so this adds `min: 1` to each.
Confirmed with a self-contained C++17 reproducer that compiles the real wait/timer/TTL
expressions against bad values and controls (attached to the tracker ticket).

Tracker: [https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81226](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81226)

72262.title: rgw: match the whole token against "*" in IAM policy parsing
72262.author: jhoblitt
72262.body:
`ParseState::do_string()` in `src/rgw/rgw_iam_policy.cc` tested only the first
character of a `Principal`, `NotPrincipal`, `Action` or `NotAction` token
against `'*'` (`*s == '*'`) instead of comparing the whole token to `"*"`. Any
`*`-prefixed token (e.g. `"*:GetObject"`, `"*evil"`) silently collapsed to the
full wildcard: every action granted/denied, or `Principal` = everyone. This
compares the whole token with `std::string_view{s, l} == "*"`, matching the
`parse_principal_()` precedent. Reproducer included.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81229

72263.title: rgw: enforce the aws4 payload-hash verdict for whole-body ops
72263.author: jhoblitt
72263.body:
`read_all_input()` and `get_json_input()` call `do_aws4_auth_completion()` but
discard its return. That call recomputes SHA256 over the body and compares it to
the signed `x-amz-content-sha256`, returning `-ERR_AMZ_CONTENT_SHA256_MISMATCH` on
a mismatch. Discarding it accepts a signed request whose body does not match its
claimed hash, for every op that reads its whole body this way (CreateBucket,
ACL/tagging/policy PUTs, CompleteMultipartUpload, DeleteObjects, more). Regression
from 0214b4a7afb (v17.1.0); v16.2.15 enforced it. This PR propagates the return.
Reproduced live on v19.2.6 and v20.2.4.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81230

72265.title: mds: ceph.dir.pin.distributed.tree to spread large directories deep in a tree over the active ranks
72265.author: xiubli
72265.body:
`ceph.dir.pin.distributed` spreads the dirfrags of the directory it is set on over the active ranks, but a directory below it stays on the rank of the parent dirfrag it lives in. A large shared directory deeper in the tree, such as IO500's `mdtest-hard` (created two levels below the only directory a run may set attributes on), is therefore served by one rank.

This series adds `ceph.dir.pin.distributed.tree`: every directory below it that gets fragmented has its own dirfrags distributed over the ranks. Fragments are mapped by their ancestor at the minimum distribution depth and dealt out to the ranks in turn, so later splits never move a fragment. The nearest export pin or distributed pin on the way up still wins.

Spreading one directory's fragments over several ranks exposed three ways in which clients send requests to a rank that has to forward them; the series fixes those too:

- the auth listed every replica of a dirfrag in DirStat, not only the ones the balancer replicated for reads; clients sent LOOKUPs to replicas without the dentry;
- libcephfs `choose_target_mds()` sent non-auth requests to the lowest-rank cap instead of the fragment auth when the dirfrag was not replicated;
- the balancer read-replicated hot dirfrags of ephemerally pinned (distributed or random) directories.

72266.title: osd/scrub: keep operator scrub requests made before the PG is clean
72266.author: sunyuechi
72266.body:
Since 3cde1421504, `scrub_requested()` returns early for a PG that is
not registered (not clean yet), so a `ceph pg scrub/deep-scrub/repair`
issued while the PG is recovering or backfilling is dropped, while the
command reports success.

Set the target's urgency anyway; `update_targets()` keeps it when the
PG registers. `scrub-abort` on such a PG now removes the request instead
of reporting an error.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81622

72269.title: rbd-mirror: support dynamic mirror group membership changes
72269.author: pkalever
72269.body:
This series allows images to join or leave enabled mirrored groups while mirroring continues. It preserves snapshot order and transfers image ownership between standalone and group replayers.

- cleanup: name shared ImageMap updates as entities
  Renames shared ImageMap helpers because they now manage both images and groups. This is a naming only change.

- rbd-mirror: manage replayers during group membership changes
  Keeps entries for group images at weight zero and transfers ownership between standalone and group replayers.

- librbd: detach images from mirrored groups
  Converts a detached group image to standalone mirroring.

- librbd: add images to enabled mirror groups
  Enables non-mirrored images in standalone mode first, then uses one consistent path to attach images to enabled groups.

- librbd: recover interrupted group membership changes
  Makes attach and detach safe to retry after failures or daemon restarts and restores saved membership during forced promotion.

- rbd-mirror: process group membership snapshots in order
  Rebuilds membership from saved snapshots and keeps replayer ownership in the correct order.

- qa/rbd: make mirror tests reliable with large images
  Makes status checks tolerate short ownership transitions and compares large mirrored images without export files.

72270.title: rgw: check a copy source with the source bucket's tenant and owner
72270.author: jhoblitt
72270.body:
RGWCopyObj / RGWPutObj authorized a copy *source* object with inputs taken from
the request's *destination* bucket: `read_obj_policy()` used `s->bucket_tenant`
and `s->bucket_owner`, and `verify_bucket_permission()`'s cross-account gate used
`s->bucket_owner`. A requester who owns the destination bucket could therefore
CopyObject / UploadPartCopy a private source object in another tenant/account and
read its contents, though a direct GetObject on it is denied. The source check
now uses the source bucket's tenant and owner. The `x-amz-expected-bucket-owner`
check (which names the destination) is unchanged, and the ordinary object-read
path is unaffected (read bucket == target bucket), so tracker #67464 is not
regressed.

Reproduced live against radosgw v19.2.6 and v20.2.4; reproducer in the tracker
ticket.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/PLACEHOLDER

72271.title: rgw: guard copy-source and destination bucket-policy parse against std::terminate
72271.author: jhoblitt
72271.body:
`get_iam_policy_from_attr()` throws `rgw::IAM::PolicyParseException` on an
unparsable bucket policy. Two copy-path callers in `src/rgw/rgw_op.cc` do not
catch it, so the exception escapes and `std::terminate()` aborts radosgw:
`read_obj_policy()` (the copy source's policy, parsed before any permission
check) and `RGWCopyObj::verify_permission()` (the destination's policy). A
policy valid in its own tenant can fail to parse under another tenant during a
cross-tenant copy ([#59169](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/59169),
[#59221](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/59221)), so any such request is a
DoS. This wraps both parses in the same try/catch `read_bucket_policy()` uses:
deny with `-EACCES`, letting admin/system users through to repair the bucket.

Overlaps textually with [#72270](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72270)
([tracker #81248](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81248)), which edits the same
`read_obj_policy()` statement; whichever merges second must rebase.

72284.title: crimson: spread replication off the primary reactor
72284.author: knrt10
72284.body:
OSD-to-OSD sends all went through the primary reactor's one cluster
session. A replicated write was accepted there, forwarded to the PG's
reactor, and the reply was sent back out through it.

Each reactor now keeps its own session to a peer OSD and sends from
there. The client nonce records the sending reactor so the peer keeps
those sessions apart. The replica replies on the connection the request
arrived on, which already belongs to the primary's reactor.

The peer still accepts on the osdmap port and forwards each op to the
reactor that owns the PG, the same way it already handles client ops.
No PG-to-reactor map is exchanged, and the client path is unchanged.

Fixes: http://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80545

72289.title: osdc/Objecter: pause order-reads-writes ops on a full pool
72289.author: aainscow
72289.body:
An `ORDER_READS_WRITES` (`CEPH_OSD_FLAG_RWORDERED`) read must not complete before
writes submitted ahead of it. On a full pool the Objecter pauses those writes, but
it lets the RWORDERED read through, so the read overtakes them.
`ceph_test_rados` aborts with `finished tid 1 when last_acked_tid was 3` when an OSD
goes failsafe-full. The same abort reproduces on a replicated pool by pulsing a
`max_objects` quota under `ceph_test_rados`. This is not specific to EC or stretch
pools. The code is the same on main, Tentacle and Squid, and has been since
Octopus.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81205

### Cause

`op_target_t::respects_full()` treats RWORDERED ops like writes, so
`_scan_requests()` force-resends them when a pool fills or gets space again.
`target_should_be_paused()`, however, folds the full-pool check into the PAUSEWR
condition, and only `CEPH_OSD_FLAG_WRITE` ops test that condition. An RWORDERED
read already in flight when the pool fills is therefore resent at once.

c4b73f19a7b ("osdc/Objecter: resend RWORDERED ops on full",
https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/19133) also made `_op_submit()` pause every op that
`respects_full()`. c0482d7afaa ("osdc/Objecter: remove duplicated pause check code",
v15.1.1) removed that check as a duplicate. Since then, RWORDERED reads submitted
while the pool is full are not paused either.

### Fix

`target_should_be_paused()` now pauses every op that `respects_full()` while its
pool or the cluster is full. The RWORDERED read waits with the writes ahead of it.
Once the pool has space, `_scan_requests()` resends them in tid order.

What does not change:
- PAUSEWR on its own still pauses only writes.
- `FULL_TRY` and `FULL_FORCE` ops are still sent.
- Reads without `CEPH_OSD_FLAG_RWORDERED` are not affected.

As before c0482d7afaa, the in-tree RWORDERED readers now wait while their pool is
full:
- `Filer::_probe()`, which Journaler recovery and so cephfs-journal-tool use. The
  MDS's Objecter ignores pool full, so the MDS is not affected.
- The OSD's tier promotes, copy-gets and proxied RWORDERED reads.

### Dependency

**This PR is stacked on #72236.** The fix itself is one hunk in
`Objecter::target_should_be_paused()` and stands alone. The tests extend that PR's
`unittest_objecter_direct_reads` (`TestSplitOpMapChange`, a real Objecter driven
through maps and replies). Until #72236 merges, this PR also shows its commits.
The last five commits belong here:
- `osdc/Objecter: pause order-reads-writes ops on a full pool`
- `test/osdc: check that RWORDERED reads do not overtake writes on a full pool`
- `osdc/Objecter: reword the comments on forced-OSD and direct-read targets`
- `osdc/Objecter: let a test run code in the injected relock delay`
- `test/osdc: land a map while a split read's first sub-read relocks`

The last three follow up #72236, whose production code stays as approved. Review
asked for its timing-dependent race test to go, and a deterministic replacement
needs a hook in the Objecter. The hook turns the `sleep(1)` of
`objecter_debug_inject_relock_delay` into a function object that defaults to the
same sleep, so nothing changes when the option is off.

### Testing

New tests in `unittest_objecter_direct_reads`:
- `RWOrderedReadWaitsForWriteOnFullPool`: a write and then an RWORDERED read
  submitted while the pool is full. Neither is sent until the pool has space, and
  then the write goes before the read.
- `RWOrderedReadResentAfterWriteWhenPoolFull`: the pool fills with both in flight.
  Nothing is resent until it has space, and then the write goes before the read.
- `RWOrderedFullTryReadSentOnFullPool`: an RWORDERED read with `FULL_TRY` is still
  sent on a full pool.
- `ECSplitReadNewIntervalDuringSubmit`: raises min_size from inside `_op_submit()`'s
  relock window for the first sub-read of a split read, on the same thread. Neither
  sub-read is sent with its old target, and the next change to the PG redrives the
  whole read to the primary.

All nine tests in the binary

72290.title: osd/PeeringState: cap pwlc at the log head when the primary activates
72290.author: aainscow
72290.body:
In an optimized EC pool, a partial-write-last-complete (pwlc) range can outlive
the write it covers when peering rolls that write back. A nonprimary shard then
moves its `last_update` and log head to a version that no longer exists. The next
write reuses that version number, and the shard aborts in
`PGLog::IndexedLog::add` (`e.version.version > head.version`). Alternatively, the
shard is later chosen as the log source and is never recovered.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81283

### What goes wrong

After a peered-only interval keeps a sub-stripe write, the unwritten nonprimary
shards get a pwlc range ending at that write. When the next interval rolls the
write back, the stale range survives in two places:

- **On the primary.** The new primary merges peers' pwlc in `update_peer_info()`
  during GetInfo, before GetLog has chosen the log. It therefore takes a range
  ending at the write that is about to be rolled back. Nothing trims the
  primary's own copy afterwards. When the primary is its own log source,
  `proc_master_log()` does not run. `activate()` then stamps the range with the
  new epoch, which makes it win every later merge, and sends it to the shards.
- **On a nonprimary shard.** Each one keeps its own copy and re-applies it in
  `update_peer_info()`. If no primary-capable shard of the new interval saw the
  write, the primary sends no range for it. The shard then re-applies its stale
  copy right after the primary's MInfoRec has rewound its log.

The tracker has a step-by-step trace from the unit test.

### Fix

The primary's log is authoritative once it activates, so no pwlc range may end
past its head.
- `activate()` trims pwlc to `pg_log.get_head()` before it stamps the epoch and
  sends the ranges. That also covers ranges merged in WaitUpThru, and ranges from
  peers whose log head already matched.
- A nonprimary shard trims its own pwlc to the primary's `last_update` in
  `update_peer_info()` before applying it.
- When a replica applies the range for its own shard from an MLogRec, that range
  is capped at the sender's `last_update`. With the `activate()` change a primary
  no longer sends such a range, so this cap is defensive: it protects replicas
  during an upgrade, when the primary may still run older code.

The cap must come after all the merges and before the epoch is stamped. pwlc
epochs are unchanged, so the tie-break in `update_peer_info()` is unchanged too.

### Why #71579 is not enough

#71579 trims the copy of the range that the primary holds for each peer with
divergent entries, in `proc_replica_log()`. It does not trim:
- the primary's own merged copy, which it took from those peers in GetInfo
  before the rollback was known;
- the copy each nonprimary shard keeps for itself.

In a trace of the k4m2 test on main, #71579 rolls the peers' ranges back from 5'2
to 5'1. The primary still activates with (5'1, 5'2] for shards 1-3.

### Testing

New tests in `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`:
- `RolledBackPeeredWriteLeavesNoStalePwlc`: the primary-side case.
- `RolledBackPeeredWriteLeavesNoStaleReplicaPwlc`: the nonprimary-side case. The
  write reaches no other primary-capable shard.

Both raise min_size to k + 1, so that losing two shards leaves the PG peered but
not active. They check pwlc and every shard's log head before the next write, so a
regression fails the test rather than aborting the binary. They skip k2m1
configurations, as intended. The test commit also adds
`OSDMapTestHelpers::set_pool_min_size()` and `ECPeeringTestFixture::set_pool_min_size()`.

Results:
- With the fix: all non-skipped configurations pass, and the whole binary passes
  (206 passed, 24 skipped).
- With the PeeringState change reverted: all 16 non-skipped configurations fail
  on the intended checks. The stale range ends past the head, and a nonprimary
  log head differs from the primary's.

The tests do not deep-scrub the object afterw

72291.title: rgw: let CopyObject re-encrypt objects
72291.author: mheler
72291.body:
Changing rgw_crypt_sse_algorithm to aes-256-gcm only affects new writes, and a copy onto the same object that sets encryption headers was refused, so there was no way to move existing objects off aes-256-cbc. Accept that copy, so it rewrites the object under the configured cipher.

CopyObject now also applies the destination bucket's default encryption,  the way PutObject does.

POSIX, DBStore and D4N don't run the copy through the encrypt and compress filters, so they now refuse a copy that would need the data rewritten instead of copying it unchanged.

Adds s3tests for both cases and an rgw/crypt-reencrypt qa suite that writes objects under aes-256-cbc, switches to aes-256-gcm and re-encrypts them.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81284

72292.title: osd/PrimaryLogPG: redirect non-sparse EC direct reads that hit -EIO to the primary
72292.author: aainscow
72292.body:
An EC direct read, used by balanced and localized reads, reads only the shard on
the OSD it is sent to, so that OSD cannot rebuild the data around a medium error.
The read must be sent back to the primary, which can decode it from the other
shards. For a non-sparse read (`CEPH_OSD_OP_READ`) this does not happen: the
client gets -EIO, and every retry hits the same bad sector.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81286

### What goes wrong

In `PrimaryLogPG::do_read()`, the `ec_direct_read()` branch calls
`ECBackend::objects_read_local()`. That returns the object store's -EIO unchanged,
and `do_read()` passes it straight back as the op result. It does not call
`rep_repair_primary_object()`, as the replicated branch of the same function does.

The Objecter only resubmits to the primary on -EAGAIN, and `SplitOp` returns the
first non-EAGAIN error from its sub-reads. So a single direct read and a split
read both fail with -EIO, and the primary is never asked.

This affects any client using `read_from_replica` balance or localize on an
optimized EC pool, for example librbd with `rbd_read_from_replica_policy`.

### Fix

On -EIO, the non-sparse EC direct-read branch of `do_read()` now calls
`rep_repair_primary_object()`, as the replicated path does. With #71910 that
replies -EAGAIN, and the Objecter (or `SplitOp`) resubmits the read to the
primary without the direct-read flags. -EAGAIN from `do_osd_ops()` means the reply
has already been sent, so `execute_ctx()` just closes the context; that is
existing behaviour.

Replicated pools and EC reads that are not direct reads are unchanged.

### Relationship to #71910

#71910 fixes the sparse-read side: `do_sparse_read()` calls
`rep_repair_primary_object()` on -EIO or on a full-object CRC mismatch. That
function asserted the pool was not erasure coded, so a medium error hit by a
localized RBD read aborted the OSD. #71910 replaces the assert with an -EAGAIN
reply whenever the OSD is not the primary or the pool is erasure coded. It does
not touch the non-sparse `do_read()` path, which this PR fixes. The change here is
three lines, and it relies on #71910's version of `rep_repair_primary_object()`.

72296.title: script: add ceph-core-bundle, a core dump debugging tool
72296.author: aainscow
72296.body:
`src/script/ceph-core-bundle` turns a ceph core dump into a self-contained, debuggable bundle: the core, the exact binaries and debuginfo it needs (matched by the GNU build-ids recorded in the core), a gdb wrapper and a pre-generated backtrace report. It needs only python3 (stdlib), cpio, tar and zstd/xz: no container, root or ceph install.

```
ceph-core-bundle 1790361071.14248.core.gz     # check the core, build a package
ceph-core-bundle /a/<run>/<job>               # every core of a job, one package
ceph-core-bundle --in-place ./cores           # turn a directory of cores into the package
cd core-<...> && ./gdb --list && ./gdb 1      # pick a core; cores/<name>/report.txt has backtraces
```

The build is identified from the core itself (ceph version strings and build-ids), so a bare core works; teuthology `config.yaml` is used as a hint when present. Files come from:
- chacra via shaman (CI builds)
- download.ceph.com (official releases)
- container images for containerized daemons (cephadm records `CONTAINER_IMAGE` in each daemon's environment, so the core names its image), or found by sha1/version once a CI build has expired; private registries use the normal podman/docker login
- debuginfod, distro mirrors/koji/vault/EPEL and Launchpad for distro libraries
- `--debug-repo URL` for any other yum repository

Bundles work with gdb on Linux and macOS (Homebrew gdb), and in IDEs such as CLion (`./gdb --clion` prints the setup). `--tar` packs a bundle for copying elsewhere.

### Main options
- `--in-place DIR`: turn a directory of cores into the package, leaving the original files alone
- `--verify-only`: just check cores for truncation/damage (exit 1 if bad)
- `--tar`: also write a `.tar.zst` of the package for copying elsewhere
- `--lean`: skip debuginfo for distro libraries (smaller)
- `--image`, `--debug-repo`: extra sources, e.g. for downstream builds

`ceph-core-bundle --help` lists the rest.

### Measurements (OSD cores from teuthology, empty cache, trial200)
| | CentOS 9 | Ubuntu noble | Rocky 10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| downloaded | 686 MB | 1926 MB | 694 MB |
| of which ceph (chacra) | 447 MB | 1850 MB | 451 MB |
| build time | 156–253 s | 991 s | 206 s |
| bundle on disk (compressed DWARF) | 843 MB | 440 MB | ~800 MB |
| `--tar` | ~300–400 MB | 301 MB | 278 MB |

Ubuntu downloads more because ceph's `-dbg` debs group many binaries' debuginfo into a few large packages, each of which has to be streamed in full.

### Testing
Exercised against teuthology cores from CentOS 9, Rocky 10, Ubuntu jammy and noble (classic and crimson OSDs, radosgw-admin, ceph_test_rados, default and debug flavors), with and without teuthology metadata, with chacra unavailable (image + `--debug-repo` paths), and with deliberately truncated cores for the core check, with multi-core packages and `--in-place`. Bundles were debugged with gdb on Ubuntu 24.04, Rocky 10 and macOS (arm64).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81297

72301.title: rgw: reject a malformed percent-escape in the request path
72301.author: jhoblitt
72301.body:
`url_decode()` cannot report a malformed percent-escape: a bad hex digit empties the result and a trailing `%` is silently dropped. `RGWREST::preprocess()` and `rgw_rest_transform_s3_vhost_style()` route on that value, so `GET /bucket/%zz` is served as ListBuckets and a request for key `k%` acts on key `k` — radosgw acts on a resource the URL does not name. This adds a strict `url_decode()` overload that reports the failure, and rejects a malformed request path with 400. The existing `url_decode()` is unchanged, so the copy-source guard from #63521 (tracker [#71458](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/71458) / CVE-2025-48052) still holds. Reproduced on v19.2.6 and v20.2.4.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81301

72302.title: rgw: require at least one concurrent aio for the bucket index
72302.author: jhoblitt
72302.body:
Setting `rgw_bucket_index_max_aio = 0` broke every bucket-index operation,
and silently. On the `CLSRGWConcurrentIO` path (Squid) the issue loop sent no
op and the op returned success with no work done — a listing came back empty
while the objects existed. On the `shard_io` path (Tentacle, main) the send
gate `outstanding.size() >= max_concurrent` (`0 >= 0`) waited for a completion
before sending anything, so the op hung. The option was never floored; only
the admin `--max-aio` flag was. Add `min: 1`, which `Option::validate()`
enforces on every config path.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81302
