72304.title: rgw: require at least one concurrent aio in bypass-gc bucket removal
72304.author: jhoblitt
72304.body:
The admin REST bucket-removal op (`RGWOp_Bucket_Remove::execute`) forwards
`bypass-gc` to `RGWBucketAdminOp::remove_bucket` without ever calling
`set_max_aio()`, so `RGWBucketAdminOpState::max_aio` keeps its default of `0`
and reaches `RadosBucket::remove_bypass_gc()` unclamped. With a budget of `0`
the purge (a) never releases the first object's tail stripes — the loop
condition `max_aio--` is false before the body runs, so those stripes are
orphaned in the data pool while the head and index entry are removed and
nothing is queued to GC — and (b) then runs with a negative budget, so the
in-loop drains never fire and the deletes run unbounded. `radosgw-admin` is
unaffected (it seeds the budget from `--max-concurrent-ios`, default 32); only
the admin REST path is exposed.

The fix clamps the budget to at least 1 at the point of use, matching the
bucket-index-check paths that already clamp the same value with
`std::max(1, ...)`.

Distinct from the pre-existing "fails once a tail stripe is gone" defect
([#24789](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/24789) /
[#40587](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/40587),
[ceph/ceph#28789](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/28789)), which is about
`drain_aio` propagating ENOENT for an already-missing stripe.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81304

72305.title: rgw: reject a bad port in an [ipv6]:port frontend endpoint
72305.author: jhoblitt
72305.body:
`parse_endpoint()` in `src/rgw/rgw_asio_frontend.cc` parses the port of an
`[ipv6]:port` endpoint with `parse_port()` and the address with
`make_address_v6()`, passing both the same `error_code`. The IPv6 branch never
checks the code after `parse_port()`; it relies on the single implicit check
when the function returns. But `make_address_v6()` (boost asio's `inet_pton`)
clears the `error_code` on entry, so a successful address parse overwrites the
error `parse_port()` set, and the bad port is silently accepted.

`parse_port()` returns the value `strtoul()` read truncated to 16 bits even on
error, so the endpoint binds the wrong port: `endpoint=[::1]:notaport` listens
on port 0 and `endpoint=[::1]:70000` on port 4464. The `ipv4:port` form is
correctly rejected because the IPv4 branch returns as soon as `parse_port()`
sets the code, before `make_address_v4()` can clear it.

This mirrors the IPv4 guard in the IPv6 branch: check `ec` immediately after
`parse_port()` and return.

The defect has been present since the IPv6 branch was added in
[#24887](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/24887) (the fix for
[tracker #36662](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/36662)); it is present at
v19.2.6, v20.2.4 and main. See also
[tracker #39038](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/39038).

A userspace reproducer compiling `parse_port()`/`parse_endpoint()` verbatim
against real `boost::asio` confirms `[::1]:notaport` is accepted (ec=ok, port 0)
while `127.0.0.1:notaport` is rejected; with the fix the IPv6 case is rejected
too.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81305

72306.title: rgw: check_disk_state removes a multipart part's index entry from the right shard
72306.author: jhoblitt
72306.body:
`RGWRados::check_disk_state` walks a head object's manifest and removes each
multipart part's bucket-index entry. It builds the part's `rgw_obj` with
`raw_obj_to_obj`, which leaves `index_hash_source` empty, so `get_hash_object`
falls back to the part's own name and the removal is routed to
`hash(part-name)`'s index shard.

The multipart writer indexed the part on a different shard:
`MultipartObjectProcessor::prepare_head` sets
`head_obj.index_hash_source = target_obj.key.name`, so the entry was written to
`hash(head-name)`'s shard. On a bucket with more than one index shard the delete
reaches a shard that holds no such entry, `cls_rgw`'s `bucket_complete_op` logs
"not on disk, no action", and the part's entry is left behind. It only works on
a single-shard bucket.

Point the removal at the head object's shard by setting the part obj's
`index_hash_source` to `manifest->get_obj().key.name` (the same `target_obj` the
writer hashed) before `delete_obj_index`. Only shard selection for the
manifest-part removal changes; the entry key and the non-multipart path are
untouched.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81121

A reproducer (`repro.sh`) is attached to the tracker ticket; it leaves a stale
part index entry on a multi-shard bucket before this change and removes it
after.

72307.title: cls/rgw: encode 65536 without truncation in encode_packed_val
72307.author: jhoblitt
72307.body:
`encode_packed_val` (`src/cls/rgw/cls_rgw_types.h`) chooses its on-wire width
from the value's magnitude. The two-byte branch was taken for
`0x100 <= val <= 0x10000` and writes `(uint16_t)val`, but `0x10000` (65536) does
not fit in 16 bits, so it was stored, and decoded, as `0`. `65535` round-trips in
the two-byte form and `65537` round-trips in the four-byte form; `65536` was the
only affected value. The bound dates from b1578ba705a (v0.67) and is unchanged on
main.

`encode_packed_val` encodes the pool and epoch of `rgw_bucket_entry_ver` and the
`index_ver` of index and bilog entries, so an epoch or index version of exactly
65536 was silently lost.

Tighten the two-byte branch to `val < 0x10000` so 65536 falls through to the
four-byte branch and is written as a `uint32_t`. The change is encode-only:
`decode_packed_val` is driven by the width tag the encoder wrote and is
unchanged, so a peer or an older build decodes the four-byte form the same way,
and every other value keeps the width it had before. This is not a data
migration — a value previously stored as the truncated two-byte `0` is already
corrupt on disk and is unaffected; the fix prevents new truncation.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80995

A C++ reproducer (`repro_packed_val.cc`) and live `radosgw-admin bi put/bi list`
round trips (65536 -> 0 before; 65535/65537 fine, on v19.2.6 and v20.2.4) are
attached to the tracker ticket.

72308.title: rgw: size the aws-chunked trailer buffer to fit a signed trailer and reject oversize
72308.author: jhoblitt
72308.body:
`AWSv4ComplMulti::complete()` read the aws-chunked trailer section into a
256-byte buffer, capping each `recv_body` at `trailer_buf_size - tbuf_pos - 1`.
The reserved byte shrank the request to zero at `tbuf_pos == 255`, and a
zero-length `recv_body` returns 0, so the `tbuf_pos == trailer_buf_size` limit
check was unreachable and an over-long trailer was silently truncated at 255
bytes rather than rejected. Signed uploads then failed 403
SignatureDoesNotMatch (a signed SHA512 trailer is ~290 bytes, so it never fit),
and unsigned uploads were accepted with the declared checksum never compared.

This sizes the buffer to 1024 bytes so the largest well-formed trailer fits,
sizes the `static_vector` so the copy and reads stay in bounds, and drops the
reserved byte so an over-long section trips the limit check and returns 409
LimitExceeded. Reproducer (Go S3 client) is attached to
https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81122.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81122

72309.title: rgw: reject malformed aws-chunked chunk sizes
72309.author: jhoblitt
72309.body:
`AWSv4ComplMulti::ChunkMeta::create_next` parsed each aws-chunked chunk-size
token with `std::strtoull` and checked neither sign nor overflow, so `-1` and
17-digit sizes wrapped `data_length` to 2^64-1. That hides the next chunk
boundary: an unsigned multi-chunk PUT is answered 200 and silently stores a
corrupted object (signed form → 400 `XAmzContentSHA256Mismatch`). On main
be1f82f94964 (#63326) had removed the only guard, leaving the size
unvalidated. This parses the size explicitly — optional leading CRLF, 1..16 hex
digits, required `;`/CRLF boundary — and rejects the rest with 400 before any
data is stored. Valid signed/unsigned uploads, chunk extensions and the final
zero chunk are unaffected.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81123

72310.title: cls/lock: don't clean an expired ephemeral lock from a read-only method
72310.author: jhoblitt
72310.body:
`get_info` and `assert_locked` are registered read-only (`CLS_METHOD_RD`;
`RdTag` / `RdPromoteTag` on main). When they read an ephemeral lock whose
holders have all expired, `read_lock()` removes the now-empty object with
`cls_cxx_remove()`. The OSD rejects that write from a non-`WR` method and
fails the whole class call with `EIO` (`PrimaryLogPG`: "tried to update
object but is not marked WR"), so both methods answer `EIO` instead of the
lock's state and the cleanup is lost. Present since ephemeral locks landed in
`a289f2d8654` (v14.1.0); verified at v19.2.6, v20.2.4 and main.

This gates the removal on a `may_write` flag the callers pass: the
write-capable methods (`lock`, `unlock`, `break_lock`, `set_cookie`) still
clean the drained object; the read-only methods skip the removal and report
the lock as empty. The next `lock` replaces the drained lock, and that holder's
unlock removes the object.

[#56575](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/56575) logged this same failure in
2022 but was closed by a test-only change
([ceph/ceph#47148](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/47148)) that lengthened
the test's lock durations so the lock never expired; the class behaviour was
never corrected.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80993

72311.title: RGW NSFS,Posix - Split NSFS FSEnt to it's own files
72311.author: dang
72311.body: Like Posix, split NSFS FSEnt classes to their own files.  This also adds a common location for shared defines and methods.

72312.title: mon: return get_cipher_type's error code to auth command callers
72312.author: jhoblitt
72312.body:
`AuthMonitor::get_cipher_type` returns `-EINVAL` for an unknown key type,
`-ENOTSUP` for AES256KRB5 without quorum `FEATURE_CEPHX_AUTH_AES256K`, and
`-EPERM` for a policy-refused type. Its five callers in `prepare_command`
(`auth add`, the pending-key command, `auth get-or-create[-key]`, `fs
authorize`, `auth rotate`) overwrote that code with `-EINVAL`, so a client
could tell a policy refusal or a missing feature from a bad argument only by
parsing the status text. This returns `key_type` unchanged instead.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80998

72314.title: rgw: stop leaving refcount tags behind on shared tails
72314.author: mheler
72314.body:
Every time an object is copied and the copy deleted, cls_refcount keeps the copy's tag in a retired list on every tail object, forever. On EC pools that whole xattr goes into each pg log  entry, so osd_pglog grows quickly once an object has been copied many times.

This series has cls_refcount remember which tag owns the tails. Copies get unique tags, which are removed outright when the copy is deleted. CopyObject and dedup pass the source tail tag. Objects fetched by sync get a tail tag of their own instead of keeping the source's. Objects without a tail tag, and appendable objects, have their data copied (CopyObject) or are skipped (dedup) instead of sharing tails.


Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81312

72318.title: rgw/libfdb: reduce result and encoding copies
72318.author: chardan
72318.body:
> Superseded by #72319, which includes all changes from this pull request in the combined core libfdb update. Please review #72319.

## Summary

Reduce temporary allocation and copying at libfdb's FoundationDB result, encoding, and content key boundaries.

- Add raw point/range reads with callbacks that retain the owning future while borrowed bytes are in use.
- Traverse paged and disjoint selections with a cursor, preserving forward/reverse order.
- Decode Ceph buffers without an intermediate string and keep typical scalar encodings in inline storage owned by the call.
- Normalize owned range bounds without redundant key copies, retaining reserved-key clamping.
- Reuse compiled content key prefixes through `key(prefix, ...)`, `append()`, and `/=`, with explicit aliasing restrictions and tests of the byte encoding.

These memory improvements are now included in #72319 alongside the core error, commit, option, and recovery changes. The earlier staged-proxy change #71554 is already merged.

## Validation

- Focused core, query, content, and Ceph suites pass independently at this branch boundary.
- Core: 48 cases; query: 16; content: 12, including 7,359 assertions; Ceph: three passed and one intentional cautionary example skipped.
- The content key examples, arbitrary-byte encoding, reusable-prefix behavior, and reserved key bounds are covered by the corresponding tests.
- Builds ran sequentially with six jobs and the existing Ceph dependency cache; no full Ceph build was run.

Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-6
Signed-off-by: Jesse F. Williamson <jfw@ibm.com>

72319.title: rgw/libfdb: strengthen core commit and error handling
72319.author: chardan
72319.body:
Fixes libfdb commit() API, strongly improves consistent error vs. failure behavior.

FoundationDB has precise rules around commit behavior that must be handled differently by any given application. libfdb's commit() behavior was too simple, making following through on certain conditions quite tedious. Additionally, mapping FoundationDB error values to enumeration was previously incomplete because of the labor involved-- this has finally been done. 

Note: this unfortunately does introduce a breaking change. :-/ I tried really hard to avoid that, but it's really the best thing I could come up with-- other alternatives, like leaving the tagged (but correct) version in with the very tedious default just wasn't reasonable-- fortunately as we're not really much "out in the wild" yet this is the time to make a break change if it's got to happen! :-)

This change combines the error, commit, recovery, and option improvements with the result and encoding memory improvements previously submitted in #72318.

- Add `fdb_errors.h` with named native and local error codes, standard error categories, and a `std::system_error`-derived exception.
- Submit `commit(txn)` once; `commit(with_result, txn)` returns `std::expected<void, std::error_code>`. A later versionstamp failure remains separate from confirmed commit.
- Share recovery across managed operations, preserve application exceptions and FoundationDB's native retry/timeout budgets, and expose typed `retry_if` decisions with the original error and body/commit phase.
- Preserve ordered and repeated option applications, and restore nonpersistent options after native recovery.
- Add raw point/range reads whose callbacks retain the owning future while borrowed bytes are in use; preserve forward/reverse traversal of paged and disjoint selections.
- Reduce temporary allocation and copying in Ceph buffer decoding, scalar encoding, and owned range normalization, retaining reserved-key clamping.
- Reuse compiled content key prefixes through `key(prefix, ...)`, `append()`, and `/=`, with documented aliasing restrictions and encoding tests.

This is the combined core update against `main` and supersedes #72318. Experimental stdexec/Asio implementations remain a separate extension in #72320, which builds on this core update.

## API Migration

**Breaking API (application programming interface) changes:** `option_map` and map-style option access, the old commit/transactor result records, and `fdb_error_value` are removed.

Use sequence insertion for repeated options, `replace_all()` for in-place updates, and `erase()` followed by `emplace_back()` for an explicit final override. Use `libfdb_exception::code()` for the authoritative error. Manual commit callers own recovery; managed transactors use the native retry preparation and optional policy.

Managed replay includes uncertain commit outcomes by default. Applications can stop on those outcomes through `retry_if`, and must account for effects that an earlier attempt may already have committed.

The examples cookbook, standalone demo, tests, and core callers use the updated interfaces. Optional concurrency types remain in #72320.

Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-6
Signed-off-by: Jesse F. Williamson <jfw@ibm.com>

72320.title: rgw/libfdb: experimental stdexec and Asio concurrency
72320.author: chardan
72320.body:
## Summary

Add experimental, opt-in asynchronous FoundationDB operations with directly composable stdexec senders and native Asio deferred operations. Builds on the combined core libfdb improvements in #72319, which supersedes #72318. This optional concurrency extension is reviewed separately.

- `NVIDIA_STDEXEC` preserves sender/receiver composition, completion types, environment queries, and stop semantics.
- `ASIO` exposes native deferred operations and associated-executor delivery without a stdexec dependency.
- Share owning point/range results, watches, commits submitted once, and managed replay with staged publication after confirmed commit.
- Add asynchronous read versions, commit/range size estimates, and partition planning with owning selections and bounded pending requests.
- Rearm cancellation across request transitions, preserve lifetime when completion is inline, and bound replay operation storage.
- Expose native handles and the Ceph wait boundary without introducing a common scheduling framework. Include the opt-in `bench_fdb_concurrency` target.

## Review Dependency

Depends on #72319; merge the core update first. This branch is based on its current head and adds three concurrency commits. [Review the concurrency-only delta](https://github.com/chardan/ceph/compare/e90e2f8f678993498c7d808a95ecc97a6abe3ba4...264e7b474bc2b553169eb12b603afb5d7aea2e7e).

Both pull requests target `ceph/ceph:main`. Until the core update lands, this pull request's Files changed view also includes its prerequisite core changes.

## Enabling

The extension is experimental and disabled by default. Configure `WITH_RADOSGW_FDB=ON` and select `LIBFDB_EXPERIMENTAL_CONCURRENCY=ASIO|NVIDIA_STDEXEC`; `OFF` keeps ordinary core consumers independent of either backend.

Link `rgw_fdb_execution` and include `rgw/fdb/experimental/concurrency.h`. The older `rgw/fdb/execution.h` include forwards to it. Only `NVIDIA_STDEXEC` fetches the pinned stdexec headers; no NVIDIA hardware or CUDA is required. Replace the retired `EXPERIMENTAL_NVIDIA_STDEXEC` option with this selector.

## Validation

- Native stdexec: 89 cases; native Asio: 41 cases. Both pass against an isolated FoundationDB 7.3.71 cluster.
- Each backend passes all six benchmark workload smoke checks and rejects an invalid workload.
- Both benchmark consumers and native documentation fixtures compile. All 138 published C++ blocks exactly match the compilation fixtures, with backend guards.
- Sequential target-graph checks cover disabled FoundationDB, core only, Asio, stdexec, invalid selectors, and disabled/conflicting header use.
- The earlier Clang address/undefined/vptr sanitizer results cover the pre-cleanup implementation. This cleanup was checked with fresh builds and native tests; the sanitizer runs were not repeated. Leak detection remains excluded for a separately reproduced native-client allocation; broad switched-stack coverage remains limited.
- Builds use the existing Ceph dependency cache, six explicit jobs, and a host resource guard. Benchmark runs checked functionality; no performance comparison or full Ceph build was performed.

Signed-off-by: Jesse F. Williamson <jfw@ibm.com>

72322.author: chardan
72322.body:
Replace `std::list<>` where its node stability and splice semantics are not
needed in common helpers and encoding machinery. Transient sequences now use
contiguous storage or a FIFO container matching the operation; obsolete list
scaffolding is removed.

The encoding changes retain the existing wire representation. Tests cover
vector/deque compatibility, queue-removal ordering, JSON sequence decoding,
and concurrent readahead registration.

## Series

These six related PRs target `main` and share the encoding, callback, and fixture-registration
prerequisites they need. Each subsystem contains its own container conversions, fixture generators,
and consumers.

- #72322: common helpers and encoding.
- #72323: Objecter and librados result APIs.
- #72324: OSD, object-store, CRUSH, and Crimson conversions.
- #72325: monitor, manager, MDS, messenger, and authentication conversions.
- #72326: RGW and CLS conversions.
- #72327: librbd, client, journal, and tool conversions.

The Objecter/librados, storage, and cluster-service topics share the prerequisite commits from
#72322. RGW and tools also include the client API prerequisite from #72323. Required commits remain
in each branch so CI can build it before the prerequisite PR merges.

## Scope and compatibility

- Chooses containers according to actual access and lifetime semantics.
- Preserves wire formats and compatibility adapters where required.
- Keeps librados interface changes additive; existing callers retain their behavior.
- Includes focused regression tests for behavior affected by each conversion.

## Performance summary

The representative queue-removal path becomes substantially cheaper by
eliminating per-node allocation and intermediate materialization. The measured
gain belongs to that isolated machinery; complete Messenger latency still
includes teardown, bookkeeping, reference release, and logging.

72328.title: osd, rgw: export traces for slow requests
72328.author: ideepika
72328.body:
Tracing every op is too expensive to leave on: with jaeger_tracing_enable,
OSD CPU per op rises by about 22%. The ops worth tracing are the slow ones,
and the op tracker already records a timestamped timeline for every op.

This exports a trace only for ops slower than a threshold, built after the
op completes from the events the op tracker already recorded, so faster ops
cost nothing extra.
d
What it adds:
- OSD: a trace per slow op (osd_op_trace_slow_threshold, off by default),
  with a span per phase that took a noticeable share of the op, and ops that
  stay stuck traced before they complete. Traced ops show a trace_id in
  dump_historic_ops.
- One trace per request: every OSD derives the trace id from the reqid and
  the cluster fsid, so the primary's op and the replicas' sub-ops land in one
  trace with nothing new on the wire. sub_op_commit_rec now names the
  replica, so the trace shows which replica held up a write.
- RGW: slow requests traced end to end (rgw_trace_slow_threshold), with the
  trace context passed to the OSD, including bucket index updates.
- Searchable attributes: role, pool, pool_name, pg, object, op_type, ops,
  bytes.
- Rate limit by trace id (osd_op_trace_max_per_sec, rgw_trace_max_per_sec),
  so every daemon keeps the same slow requests and traces arrive whole.
- Destination: jaeger_agent_host, and OTLP/HTTP export (trace_exporter=otlp,
  trace_otlp_endpoint) for Jaeger v2, Grafana Tempo and the OpenTelemetry
  Collector, both changeable at runtime. Jaeger UDP stays the default.

Testing: unittest_tracked_op covers phase building, request trace ids and
the op tracker's slow-op path; tested on vstart with Jaeger v2.

Docs: doc/jaegertracing rewritten around slow-op traces; release notes
updated.

Contribution Guidelines
- [x] Signed-off-by on every commit
- [x] Docs and PendingReleaseNotes updated
- [x] Unit tests added

72329.title: rgw: add radosgw-admin bucket admin-lock/admin-unlock
72329.author: notque
72329.body:
adds `radosgw-admin bucket admin-lock` and `bucket admin-unlock`. while a bucket is admin-locked only admin and system users can change it: its configuration, the retention, legal hold or acl of objects in it, governance bypass, or deleting the bucket. everyone else, the bucket owner included, gets 403 AccessDenied. reading and writing objects works as before, including setting retention at write time. it's off unless an admin sets it.

this is for audit logs and other records that have to stay unchanged for a set time, the kind of retention SEC 17a-4, FINRA or HIPAA rules and ISO 27001 or SOC 2 audits look for. object lock covers the objects, but the bucket owner can still undo the setup around them: lift a legal hold, use governance bypass, add an expiration rule, open up the policy or acl, or delete the bucket once retention runs out. aws and gcp handle this for audit buckets with controls above the bucket owner (organization policies, locked retention policies). rgw has nothing above the bucket owner, so this puts a flag on the bucket that only an admin can set or clear.

how it works:
- one list of op types, checked in rgw_process and librgw right before verify_permission, next to where admins already get to override permission errors
- swift bulk delete checks the flag before removing a container
- delete and multi-delete don't honor governance bypass on a locked bucket unless the requester is an admin
- `bucket stats` shows `admin_locked`. on multisite secondaries the commands need `--yes-i-really-mean-it`, same as bucket suspend
- rgws without this change don't know the flag and ignore it, the release note says to finish the upgrade before relying on it

same shape as bucket suspend (#69645).

## Testing

all on vstart (`MON=1 OSD=1 RGW=1`, memstore) with `rgw_enable_static_website=true` and a zonegroup sync group so the website and replication ops get routed. everything below came out as expected.

`qa/workunits/rgw/test_rgw_bucket_admin_lock.py` passes. bucket owned by a normal user, object lock on with a governance default retention, then `bucket admin-lock`:
- AccessDenied for put/delete bucket policy, put bucket acl, put versioning, put/delete lifecycle, put object lock config, put/delete tagging, put/delete public access block, put/delete ownership controls, put/delete cors, put/delete encryption, put/delete website, put request payment, put logging, put notification config, put/delete replication, delete bucket
- AccessDenied for put object retention, put object legal hold, put object acl
- delete object and delete objects with governance bypass are refused
- put object (plain and with retention headers), get and list still work
- the rgw log has one "is admin-locked" line per denied request (28)
- after `bucket admin-unlock` the owner can change policy, lifecycle, tagging, cors and legal hold again, and the governance bypass delete works
- with the admin-lock step removed the test fails at the first check (put_bucket_policy), so it's testing the lock

by hand:
- owner gets AccessDenied putting a bucket policy on a locked bucket. same user with `--admin` can, with `--admin` removed it's AccessDenied again, after unlock the owner can
- swift (`test:tester`): container POST with `X-Container-Read` or `X-Versions-Location`, PUT on the existing container with metadata, DELETE, and bulk-delete of the container all get 403 while locked, and the container is still there after the bulk-delete. object PUT/GET/DELETE work. after unlock POST and DELETE work.

also:
- `test_rgw_bucket_suspend.py` passes
- `src/test/cli/radosgw-admin/help.t` passes under cram
- all 38 `unittest_rgw_*` tests pass, and `run-cli-tests` passes apart from the rbd ones (rbd isn't in my build, `WITH_RBD=OFF`). the rest of make check is left to jenkins
- no compiler warnings in the changed files

not tested: librgw/nfs, multisite, teuthology (added `qa/suites/rgw/verify/tasks/bucket-admin-lock.yaml`, will rely on ci after ok to test).

72330.title: cmake: build Boost.Context with TSan fiber support
72330.author: Doracly
72330.body:
Under `WITH_TSAN`, Boost.Context switches coroutine stacks without telling TSan, so TSan's per-thread state no longer matches the active stack. Coroutine tests crash with `ThreadSanitizer:DEADLYSIGNAL … nested bug in the same thread`, and sometimes hang in TSan's nested-bug handler until the ctest timeout.

This builds Boost.Context for TSan the way it is already built for ASan (ucontext backend plus `BOOST_USE_TSAN`), so every stack switch is reported to TSan.

### Commits

1. **cmake/boost: build Boost.Context with TSan fiber support:** the fix itself.
2. **cmake: reject WITH_TSAN combined with WITH_ASAN or WITH_ASAN_LEAK:** the existing check in `FindSanitizers.cmake` passed a list instead of a variable name to `IN_LIST` and never fired. The conflict now stops configure with an error that names the options.

### Testing

**Crash rate** (`unittest_*` run repeatedly in separate processes):

| test | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| `unittest_rgw_async_utils` | 46 / 60 crashed | 0 / 50 |
| `unittest_yield_completion` | 60 / 1500 crashed | 0 / 1500 |

`unittest_yield_completion` crashes in about 0.3% of runs on an idle machine and about 10% under heavy CPU load. `unittest_rgw_async_utils` is the reliable reproducer. The other 26 tests that use Boost.Context did not crash in 10 runs each without the change.

**Configure:**
- no sanitizer: b2 command lines unchanged
- `WITH_TSAN` and `WITH_ASAN`: the stage/install commands get `libs/context/build … context-impl=ucontext define=BOOST_USE_{TSAN,ASAN}`, and the headers command gets neither
- `WITH_ASAN`+`WITH_TSAN` and `WITH_ASAN_LEAK`+`WITH_TSAN`: fail at configure with the new message

**Builds and test runs:**
- TSan: a full `unittest_*` ctest run has no crashes or timeouts.
- ASan: all 28 Boost.Context-using unit tests still pass.

72334.title: build/cmake: fix CEPH_GIT_VER in a detached linked worktree
72334.author: supriti
72334.body:
GetGitRevisionDescription.cmake.in switches GIT_DIR to the common git dir to find branch refs in a linked worktree. The detached HEAD case then reads HEAD from that common dir too, which is the HEAD of the main worktree, not of the worktree being built.

If the main worktree is on a branch, ceph_ver.h gets

  #define CEPH_GIT_VER ref: refs/heads/<branch>

and ceph_ver.c fails to compile. If the main worktree is detached, the build silently embeds the main worktree's commit.

Use @HEAD_FILE@, which is already a copy of the worktree's own HEAD.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81316

72336.title: rgw/sts: log trust-policy denials with request prefix
72336.author: kchheda3
72336.body:
The trust-policy deny/pass messages in `RGWSTSAssumeRole::verify_permission()` and `RGWSTSAssumeRoleWithWebIdentity::verify_permission()` were logged with `ldout()`, so they carry no `req <id>` prefix. When a request authenticates successfully and is then denied by the role's trust policy, searching the logs by request id shows the authentication but not the denial, and the 403 looks unexplained.

Switch the four `ldout(s->cct, 0)` calls to `ldpp_dout(this, 0)`, matching the neighbouring error paths in the same functions. Log-only change; no behaviour change.

72346.title: mgr/MgrCap: clear grants on profile-evaluation parse failure
72346.author: stzuraski898
72346.body:
MgrCap::parse cleared grants only on the grammar-parse failure path,
violating the "no grants are kept after parsing failed" invariant
(https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/6350bee5c873cb1cef0ca1345b89bff66817e0c1) when a grammar-valid capability failed profile evaluation.
This was introduced in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/9193d8762347af65bebdaea673175113f7ccd01a ("mgr: validate that profile caps
are actually valid"), which added the profile-evaluation failure return
without a matching grants.clear(); the result was that an authorization
object retained unvalidated grammar-parsed grants after parse() returned
false (e.g. "profile does-not-exist" or "profile rbd badkey=x").

Restructure parse() so both failure paths fall through to a single
grants.clear()/return false, without weakening profile validation.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81015
Assisted-by: Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8)

72348.title: mgr/MgrCap: memoize profile expansion for zero-grant profiles
72348.author: stzuraski898
72348.body:
MgrCapGrant::expand_profile() cached its profile->grants expansion in
profile_grants and used `if (!profile_grants.empty()) return;` as the
"compute once" guard. Several valid profiles legitimately expand to zero
grants: "osd" and "mds" (and "rgw") push nothing and return, and the
"rbd"/"rbd-read-only" path returns early when it rejects an unrecognized
argument key. For all of these profile_grants stays empty, so the guard
never trips and expand_profile() re-runs its full evaluation on every
call. Since get_allowed() calls expand_profile(nullptr) on every
authorization check, these profiles were re-expanded per check.

Root cause: the "compute once" contract was inferred from
profile_grants.empty(), which cannot distinguish "not yet expanded" from
"expanded to zero grants". The empty-guard dates back to the original
port in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/6350bee5c873cb1cef0ca1345b89bff66817e0c1 ("mgr: stop re-using MonCap for handling MGR caps").

Fix: track expansion completion explicitly with a mutable counter
(profile_grants_expansions) and gate on it, so zero-grant profiles are
memoized after their first expansion. The observable authorization result
is unchanged (zero-grant profiles still grant nothing); only the
redundant re-computation is eliminated.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81016
Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8

72349.title: mgr/MgrCap: surface parse failures during decode
72349.author: stzuraski898
72349.body:
MgrCap::decode() called parse(s, NULL): it ignored parse()'s bool return
value and passed NULL as the error stream. A stored capability whose
decoded text no longer parses -- a grammar failure, or a
profile-evaluation failure (tracker #81015, e.g. an obsolete profile
after a downgrade) -- was therefore accepted silently, leaving the caller
no error signal and, on the profile-evaluation path, a partially
populated cap (stale text and retained grants).

Root cause: the NULL error stream and ignored return value have been
present since decode() was introduced in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/6350bee5c873cb1cef0ca1345b89bff66817e0c1 ("mgr: stop
re-using MonCap for handling MGR caps"); the profile-validation error
path added later (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/9193d8762347af65bebdaea673175113f7ccd01a) was never wired through to decode().

Capture parse()'s return value and error stream. On failure, log the
diagnostic via derr (guarded on g_ceph_context) and clear grants and
text so a failed decode never leaves a partially-populated cap behind.
The clear() is local to decode() and does not duplicate the parse()-side
grant-clearing fix tracked separately in #81015.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81017
Assisted-by: Claude Code (Claude Opus 4.8)

72350.title: mgr/PerfCounterInstance: remove undefined get_current() declaration
72350.author: stzuraski898
72350.body:
PerfCounterInstance.h declared `uint64_t get_current() const;` (private) but no definition exists in PerfCounterInstance.cc or anywhere else, so any call to it would be an undefined-reference/link error.

Root cause: commit 90463754ed6 (Jan Fajerski, 2018) removed the get_current() definition from DaemonState.cc -- "This function was wrong (should return buffer.back().v) and unused" -- but left the declaration behind. Commit 35f6dd06dd0 later extracted the PerfCounters classes into PerfCounterInstance.{h,cc} and carried the orphan declaration into the new header verbatim.

There are no callers of PerfCounterInstance::get_current() in the tree, so the declaration is dead. Remove it. The whole build links cleanly with no undefined-reference error; a runtime unit test is not applicable since the function has no definition and no callers.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81018
Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8

72352.title: mgr/PerfCounterInstance: guard get_latest_data() against empty buffer
72352.author: stzuraski898
72352.body:
## Summary

`PerfCounterInstance::get_latest_data()` returned `buffer.back()` with no
emptiness check. `buffer` is a `boost::circular_buffer`, and `back()` on an
empty buffer is undefined behaviour (it dereferences an invalid iterator).

## Fix

Return a zero-valued `static const DataPoint` sentinel when `buffer.empty()`,
otherwise `buffer.back()`. The const-reference, zero-copy contract is preserved.

## Reachability / likelihood

Low. `DaemonPerfCounters::update()` inserts a new instance and pushes its first
sample atomically under `daemon->lock`, and readers
(`ActivePyModules::with_perf_counters`) take the same lock, so an instance
present in the map has always received at least one sample by the time it is
queried. Dispatch also routes scalar vs. avg counters to the matching buffer.
The empty-buffer state is therefore not observable on the normal path; it is
only reachable if report decoding throws after the insert but before the push
(a corrupt/truncated `MMgrReport`). This is defensive hardening against genuine
UB rather than a routine crash.

Note: the companion avg accessor `get_latest_data_avg()` has the same latent
issue and is addressed in #72353 (see coordination note below).

## Tests

Adds a regression test for the empty-buffer path. The test file
(`test_perfcounterinstance.cc`) and CMake target are cherry-picked from #71237.

> Coordination: #72353 adds the same test file and
> `unittest_mgr_perfcounterinstance` CMake target. To avoid a duplicate-file /
> duplicate-target build break, the scaffolding will be owned by a single PR and
> the other rebased to add only its test cases.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81019

72353.title: mgr/PerfCounterInstance: guard get_latest_data_avg() against empty/zero-capacity avg_buffer
72353.author: stzuraski898
72353.body:
## Summary

`PerfCounterInstance::get_latest_data_avg()` returned `avg_buffer.back()` with
no emptiness check. `avg_buffer` is a `boost::circular_buffer`, and `back()` on
an empty (or zero-capacity) buffer is undefined behaviour.

## Fix

Return a zero-valued `static const AvgDataPoint` sentinel when
`avg_buffer.empty()`, otherwise `avg_buffer.back()`. `empty()` also covers the
zero-capacity case. The const-reference contract is preserved.

## Reachability / likelihood

Not reachable on current code; this is a latent defect / defense-in-depth.
All callers gate on `PERFCOUNTER_LONGRUNAVG`, so a scalar instance (the only
case where `avg_buffer` is zero-capacity) is never passed to this accessor. For
avg instances, `DaemonPerfCounters::update()` inserts and calls `push_avg()`
atomically under `daemon->lock`, and readers take the same lock, so an avg
instance is never observable with an empty `avg_buffer`. The guard prevents UB
if a future code path reaches this accessor without the gate.

## Tests

Adds regression tests for the empty/zero-capacity path. The test file
(`test_perfcounterinstance.cc`) and CMake target are cherry-picked from #71237.

> Coordination: #72352 adds the same test file and
> `unittest_mgr_perfcounterinstance` CMake target. To avoid a duplicate-file /
> duplicate-target build break, the scaffolding will be owned by a single PR and
> the other rebased to add only its test cases.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81020

72354.title: mgr/ThreadMonitor: return false from read_thread_stat() on parse failure
72354.author: stzuraski898
72354.body:
## Summary

`ThreadMonitor::read_thread_stat()` parses `/proc/<tid>/stat` to extract a
thread's utime/stime. It had two defects on malformed input:

1. **Unchecked extraction.** `ss >> utime >> stime` was not checked. On a short
   line the extraction fails and, per C++11 [istream.formatted.arithmetic],
   writes `0` into the targets. The function still returned success, so the
   caller (`process_thread_stats()`) computed a bogus CPU percentage from the
   zeroed values (e.g. `0 - last.utime` underflowing to a huge unsigned delta).
   This is defined-but-wrong behaviour, not undefined behaviour.

2. **Out-of-range substr.** `line.substr(end + 2)` (skipping the comm field's
   closing `")"`) threw `std::out_of_range` if the line ended at or just after
   the `)`. Because `read_thread_stat()` runs on the monitoring `std::thread`,
   an uncaught exception there would terminate the ceph-mgr process.

## Fix

- Parse into local temporaries and assign the out-parameters only after both
  extractions succeed; return false otherwise (out-params left unmodified).
- Bounds-check before `substr` and return false on a truncated line.
- Correct the header contract to "on a false return the out-parameters are
  not modified."

## Reachability / likelihood

Low. `/proc/<tid>/stat` is kernel-generated with a stable format and read
atomically, so a malformed or truncated line is not expected in normal
operation. The pre-existing worst case was a single wrong CPU-percentage
sample (self-correcting the next cycle); the `substr` path would only throw on
a line truncated exactly at the comm `)`. This is defensive hardening that also
makes the helper's return contract honest, rather than a fix for an observed
field failure.

## Tests

Adds the first `ThreadMonitor` unit-test target with cases for a well-formed
line, a truncated line (returns false, no throw), and the
"outputs unchanged on failure" contract. The test scaffolding/CMake target is
cherry-picked from #71237 and will be reconciled when that lands.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81337

72355.title: mgr/ThreadMonitor: return false from read_process_statm() on parse failure
72355.author: stzuraski898
72355.body:
## Summary

`ThreadMonitor::read_process_statm()` reads `/proc/self/statm` for the process
RSS. The open-failure path already returned false, but the field extraction
(`statm_file >> vsize_pages >> rss_pages`) was unchecked: on a parse failure
the stream writes `0` into `rss_pages` (C++11), yet the function returned
success. The caller then published `mem_rss_current = 0` to every module for
that cycle. The zero value was still emitted at `dout(20)`, but there was no
error indication that the read had actually failed.

## Fix

Route extraction through a small `parse_statm()` helper, return false on
extraction failure, and log the malformed input. This mirrors the "return
false" contract already used for the open-failure path.

## Reachability / likelihood

Essentially theoretical. `/proc/self/statm` always exists while the process is
running (no race with process exit) and the kernel always emits a well-formed
seven-field line, so a parse failure of the first two fields is not expected on
a normal Linux host. The realistic failure (/proc not mounted / not openable)
was already handled. This change is defensive hardening and makes the return
contract consistent; it is not a fix for an observed field failure.

## Tests

Adds the first `ThreadMonitor` unit-test target covering a well-formed line and
a malformed line (returns false). Test scaffolding/CMake is cherry-picked from
#71237 and will be reconciled when that lands.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81338

72356.title: mgr/PyModule: fix inverted use_main_interpreter guard in destructor
72356.author: stzuraski898
72356.body:
~PyModule() guarded the interpreter teardown with `if (use_main_interpreter)`,
so it called Py_EndInterpreter() on the shared main interpreter's thread state
for every module running in the main interpreter -- the default for all modules
not listed in mgr_subinterpreter_modules. Ending the main interpreter is a
Python fatal error ("Py_EndInterpreter: thread is not current") that aborts the
ceph-mgr process on normal module teardown. Conversely, genuine sub-interpreter
modules (use_main_interpreter == false), which own a thread state created by
Py_NewInterpreter() in load(), were leaked because the guard never fired for
them.

Root cause: the condition was inverted when it was introduced in
https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/239b0dc8a9c42449ee1faa1bf78bdcc380345ae2 ("mgr: add mgr_subinterpreter_modules config"). It must only tear
down interpreters the module actually created, i.e. sub-interpreter instances.

Invert the condition to `if (!use_main_interpreter)` so Py_EndInterpreter()
runs only for sub-interpreter instances; the main interpreter's borrowed thread
state is left intact, matching load()'s pMyThreadState setup.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81339
Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8

72357.title: mgr/MgrOpRequest: fix mark_finish_mon_command to pass flag_finish_mon_command
72357.author: stzuraski898
72357.body:
mark_finish_mon_command() was copy-pasted from mark_start_mon_command()
without updating the flag constant: it passed flag_start_mon_command
(0x08) to mark_flag_point() instead of flag_finish_mon_command (0x10).

As a result the finish bit (0x10) was never set in the op-tracker flag
word and latest_flag_point was left at the start value, so after a mon
command completed:
  - op-tracker dumps reported "start mon command" instead of
    "mon command finished" for the finishing op, and
  - any code checking the flag_finish_mon_command bit to detect command
    completion never fired.

The method is reachable in production via DaemonServer.cc (mark_finish_mon_command
is called at DaemonServer.cc:1043). The one-line fix passes the
already-defined flag_finish_mon_command constant; the switch statements in
the header already map that bit to the correct "mon command finished"
string.

The copy-paste was introduced in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/66efcaae7a05abaefb12758239b0e1ad5cbd85c9 ("mgr: integrate optracker
in ceph-mgr") and never corrected.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81340
Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8

72358.title: mgr/MgrOpRequest: set last_event_detail in mark_flag_point_string()
72358.author: stzuraski898
72358.body:
mark_flag_point_string() advanced the flag state (hit_flag_points,
latest_flag_point) and logged the event, but never stored its detail
string parameter into last_event_detail -- unlike the const char*
overload mark_flag_point(), which does. Because _get_state_string()
returns last_event_detail for the flag_reached_module state, any flag
set through the string overload caused the op-tracker state string to
report the previous (stale or empty) detail instead of the string that
was just passed in. This surfaces in dump_ops_in_flight /
dump_historic_ops as a "reached module" op with a missing or wrong
module name.

Root cause: the asymmetry between the two overloads was introduced when
the mgr op-tracker was first added in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/66efcaae7a05abaefb12758239b0e1ad5cbd85c9 ("mgr: integrate
optracker in ceph-mgr") and never corrected.

Fix: persist the detail string into last_event_detail in
mark_flag_point_string(), mirroring mark_flag_point().

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81341
Assisted-by: Claude Opus 4.8 (Claude Code)

72359.title: cephfs-mirror: stop copying extents after the first I/O error
72359.author: LiShengG
72359.body:
When a blockdiff callback returns several extents, `copy_to_remote()` only leaves the inner I/O loop when `preadv`/`pwritev` fails. The next extent's `should_backoff()` call resets `r` to 0, so the error is lost and the incomplete snapshot is committed.

Use a separate variable for the backoff check and stop at the first failed extent, so the sync attempt fails and is retried.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81370

Tested locally with vstart_runner by injecting one EIO into the first of two extents, for reads and for writes. On main, the second extent is still copied and the replayer tries to commit the snapshot. With this change the attempt fails, `last_synced_snap` is unchanged, and the retry produces an identical snapshot. The LD_PRELOAD fault-injection harness is not included; if a test is wanted, I can add one through a debug config option.

72362.title: qa/cephfs: do not empty a mounted file system from vstart_runner, and fix the flag rank_fail() retries with
72362.author: xiubli
72362.body:
Two qa fixes that make CephFS tests fail for reasons that have nothing to do with the code under test. 

1. qa/vstart_runner: do not empty a mounted file system from LocalContext.__del__

   LocalContext.__del__() runs shutil.rmtree(test_path), and the test's ceph-fuse mount lives under test_path. With Python 3.14 a LocalContext can be collected while the test still has the file system mounted, and rmtree then walks into the mount point and deletes the test's files and directories in the middle of the test. The failures look like MDS bugs: directories that were just created vanish, subtrees disappear from get subtrees, and the MDS log shows the unlinks coming from the test's own client. Seen with several test_exports and test_fragment tests under vstart_runner. test_path is now left alone while anything is mounted under it.
2. qa/cephfs: fix the flag rank_fail() retries "mds fail" with

   Since 4f333e1d06f, Filesystem.rank_fail() retries mds fail with a confirmation flag when the monitor refuses it because of an MDS_TRIM or MDS_CACHE_OVERSIZED health warning, but the flag is spelled --yes--i-really-mean-it. The monitor rejects that as an unexpected argument (EINVAL), so the test fails instead of failing the rank. Seen in a failover test where a directory split into 64 fragments raised MDS_TRIM: mds fail 1:1 got EPERM, and the retry EINVAL. It now passes --yes-i-really-mean-it.


Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81396

72370.title: tools/neorados: stop reading when the object shrinks
72370.author: tchaikov
72370.body:
"neorados read" stats the object once, then reads it in chunks until it has read that many bytes, advancing the offset by what each read returns. This races with a writer: if the object is truncated or rewritten with less data after the stat, the remaining reads start at or past its new end. The OSD trims such a read to zero bytes and returns success, so the offset never moves.

The window is small, since the object has to shrink while it is being read. When it does, the output stops and "neorados read" hangs without reporting an error, sending the same empty read to the OSD over and over.

Stop when a read returns no data.

72374.title: cmake/boost: pass build properties to stage and install only
72374.author: tchaikov
72374.body:
`${b2}` is the command prefix of every b2 invocation, including the `headers` step. It mixed the b2 engine options (-j, -d0, --user-config) with build properties (toolset, python, the arm abi/architecture/ binary-format and valgrind). This only works because those are built-in b2 features. A property declared in a library's Jamfile makes the `headers` step fail with `unknown feature`, as `context-impl` did until the ASan properties moved to boost_features.

Keep only the engine options in ${b2}, and move the other build properties to boost_features, which only the stage and install commands use. Without `toolset=`, `b2 headers` picks the toolset declared in user-config.jam and produces the same output as before.

72375.title: crimson, osdc: on reply - route client ops directly to the PG's reactor core
72375.author: ronen-fr
72375.body:
Update: good performance results when combining with a separate change
(read - a separate almost-ready PR), assigning PGs to cores not by 'number of PGs
on a specific core' but rather using 'number of Primary PGs on a specific core.
And, yes - I am aware of the fact that the Primary might change with time, e.g. following
a split. I do not think that negates the benefits of this initial assignment.

## Summary

A Crimson OSD runs one reactor per core, and each PG belongs to one reactor. A
client, however, keeps a single connection per OSD, served by whichever reactor
Seastar assigned it to. Most client ops (about (S-1)/S with S reactors) are
therefore received on one reactor and forwarded to the PG's reactor, and the
reply is sent back the same way: two cross-core hops per op.

This PR adds an opt-in mechanism that lets clients send each op straight to the
reactor that owns its PG:

- **OSD:** with `crimson_osd_core_listeners`, the public messenger binds one
  extra listening port per reactor. A connection accepted on a reactor's port is
  served on that reactor.
- **Reply hint:** every client op reply (`MOSDOpReply` v9) carries an
  `osd_core_hint_t`: the reactor that owns the PG, and that reactor's listener
  address. It is sent only to peers advertising the new `OSD_CORE_HINT` feature
  bit. The OSD keeps no per-client state.
- **Client:** with `objecter_use_osd_core_hints`, the Objecter opens a
  connection to each hinted reactor (lazily, per OSD session), and sends a PG's
  ops on that connection.

Both options default to **off**, so behaviour is unchanged unless they are set.

## Design notes

- **Messenger (crimson/net):**
  - The per-core listeners are `ShardedServerSocket`s with a fixed target core.
  - The server side of the handshake uses the address the client actually
    connected to (HELLO check, ClientIdent target check, ServerIdent addresses).
  - The connection registry is keyed by (peer address, listener core), so one
    client's connections to different reactors coexist.
  - Per-core ports accept lossy (client) sessions only.
- **Objecter (osdc):**
  - `OSDSession::core_cons` holds the per-core connections, and
    `OSDSession::pg_routes` the hinted core per PG.
  - All of a PG's ops, including linger and watch ops, follow the PG's route.
  - **Ordering:** a PG switches connections only while none of its ops are in
    flight, so a PG's in-flight ops always share one connection.
  - **Resets:** a reset of a per-core connection is handled like a session reset,
    scoped to the PGs routed through it: their ops are resent in tid order on the
    main connection, and their lingers are re-registered.
- **Compatibility:**
  - Old clients get v8 replies without the hint.
  - Classic OSDs advertise the feature bit but never send hints.
  - The kernel client is unaffected.
- **Observability:**
  - New Objecter perf counters: `op_send_core`, `core_hint_change`,
    `core_route_switch`, `core_cons`, `core_con_open`, `core_con_reset`.
  - `objecter_requests` shows the core each op was sent to.

## Performance

Measured on 5 Crimson OSDs × 18 pinned reactors, each on its own NVMe with the
seastore random-block backend; fio `rados` engine, 4 KiB random reads, 512 ops
in flight. Full report:
https://gist.github.com/ronen-fr/5fe8c79764ab39ed2d5a5f874070d977

| Clients (one connection per OSD each) | Hints off | Hints on |
|---|---|---|
| 4  | ~457k IOPS | ~438k (-4%, client-bound) |
| 8  | ~530k IOPS | **~790k (+43-56%), median latency halved** |
| 16 | ~870k IOPS | ~764k (-12%), p99 tripled |

- **Helps when an OSD has fewer client connections than reactors.** Without
  hints, only that many reactors handle network traffic, and the rest of the OSD
  is under-used.
- **Hurts when enough clients cover all reactors.** The load then follows how
  primaries are spread across reactors, and the busiest reactors cap throughput.
  Better primary-to-reactor

72378.title: mon/MonClient: drop the ping connection before deleting its messenger
72378.author: aainscow
72378.body:
`MonClient::ping_monitor()` deletes its temporary messenger while its `ConnectionRef` is still in scope. The last reference is dropped when the function returns, and `~AsyncConnection` then reads `async_msgr->cct` from the freed messenger:

```
#0 ceph::logging::SubsystemMap::should_gather<30u, 20>
#2 AsyncConnection::~AsyncConnection (msg/async/AsyncConnection.cc:162)
#7 MonClient::ping_monitor (mon/MonClient.cc:331)
#8 librados::RadosClient::ping_monitor
```

On a vstart cluster with cephx, `ceph ping mon.X` segfaulted in 164 of 180 attempts, and `qa/workunits/cephtool/test.sh` failed in `test_mon_ping`. The teardown order is old, but until #71797 pings with cephx asserted earlier on debug builds and never reached the teardown.

This releases the connection before shutting the messenger down. With the change, 180 pings against the same cluster did not crash, and the cephtool workunits (`--test-mon --test-osd --test-mgr`, `--test-mds`) and `mon/pool_ops.sh` pass.

Testing: no new test. Catching a use-after-free like this deterministically needs a live monitor with cephx and a memory checker, so a unit test is not practical. The existing cephtool `test_mon_ping` and `src/test/pybind/test_rados.py::test_ping_monitor` (rados python workunit) exercise this path with cephx; `test_mon_ping` crashed without the fix.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81400

72379.title: qa/standalone: don't kill processes that are not the test's own
72379.author: aainscow
72379.body:
Four standalone tests kill processes that are not their own. This only matters when they are run locally next to something else, for example a vstart cluster in the build directory that `run-standalone.sh` runs them from, or other standalone tests. Teuthology runs them one at a time on dedicated nodes, so CI is not affected.

- `mon/osd-pool-create.sh` (`check_pool_priority`) and `osd-backfill/osd-backfill-recovery-log.sh` (`_common_test`) call `kill_daemons` without the test directory. `kill_daemons` then searches from the current directory and kills every daemon with a pid file under it. Pass `$dir`, as every other caller does.
- `osd/osd-fast-mark-down.sh` ends with `pkill -SIGTERM rados`, which matches any process whose name contains `rados`: `ceph_test_rados`, `radosgw` and rados clients belonging to anything else on the machine. The test's own `rados bench` runs in the foreground under `timeout`, so there is nothing of its own left to kill. Drop it.
- `osd/divergent-priors.sh` stops the rados commands it started in the background with `killall -9 rados`, which kills every rados process on the host. Kill only the test's own background jobs.

We hit both problems on a vstart cluster: `osd-backfill-recovery-log.sh` sent SIGTERM to the vstart mgr and OSDs, and `osd-fast-mark-down.sh` killed every `ceph_test_rados` workload running against it.

Testing: the four changed scripts pass. A dummy daemon's pid file under the working directory is killed by `TEST_pool_pos_only_prio` before the change and left alone after it; a dummy process named `ceph_test_rados` is killed by `osd-fast-mark-down.sh` before the change and survives it; a dummy process named `rados` survives `divergent-priors.sh` with the change.

72381.title: mon/OSDMonitor: keep size and bucket target for a pool created in degraded stretch mode
72381.author: aainscow
72381.body:
In stretch mode, a pool created while the cluster is in degraded stretch mode was given half the stretch pool size and a `peering_crush_bucket_target` of 1. Entering degraded stretch mode only lowers each existing stretch pool's bucket count, sets the mandatory member and halves `min_size`, and `trigger_healthy_stretch_mode()` undoes exactly those changes, so nothing restored the new pool's size or bucket target. Once the lost site was back the pool had size 2 and min_size 2: the stretch rule put both replicas in one zone, a bucket count of 2 could never be met, and every PG stayed clean+peered.

The fix gives a pool created in degraded mode only the changes the existing pools get, so the healthy transition brings it back to the full stretch size with the others.

The first commit adds a standalone reproducer, `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-pool-create-degraded.sh` (3 mons, 4 OSDs, two zones and a tiebreaker): it enables stretch mode, stops one zone's mon and OSDs, creates a pool, and brings the zone back.

Testing: run on a build of the stretchy-C development branch, whose stretch mode code behaves the same as main for replicated pools in a two-zone cluster. Without the fix the test fails on the size check (2, expected 4); with it the pool is back to size 4 / min_size 2 after recovery, its PGs go active+clean, and the data written during degraded mode reads back. Not yet run on a main build.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81390

72382.title: kv/RocksDBStore, tools/ceph-kvstore-tool: report read errors when iterating a sharded store
72382.author: aainscow
72382.body:
`ceph-kvstore-tool list` (and `list-crc`, `dump`, `store-crc`) and `store-copy` stop at the first block RocksDB cannot read and exit 0, so a store with a corrupt SST looks intact and a partial copy looks complete. We hit this on a BlueStore OSD whose RocksDB had a corrupt SST: the OSD aborted on a block checksum mismatch, while `ceph-kvstore-tool bluestore-kv <osd dir> list` printed 119086 keys and exited 0.

- The tool looped on `valid()` and never checked the iterator status. It now checks it, prints an error and exits 1.
- For a sharded store (the BlueStore default), the whole-space iterator, `WholeMergeIteratorImpl`, always returned 0 from `status()`. It now reports an error from the default column family iterator or any sharded prefix iterator.
- When the first shard of a sharded prefix could not be read, seeking the whole-space iterator failed `ceph_assert(current_shard->second->valid())` in `is_main_smaller()`, the assert reported in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/52187. An unreadable shard is now treated like an exhausted one, so the seek returns the error.

Testing: the new `KVTest.RocksDBShardingIteratorReadError` in `ceph_test_keyvaluedb` corrupts the first block of each SST of a store with a sharded prefix in turn and lists the store. Without the fix it fails the `status()` check, and asserts when the first shard is the corrupt one; with it, it passes. The rest of `ceph_test_keyvaluedb` and `qa/workunits/cephtool/test_kvstore_tool.sh` pass. On a copy of the corrupt OSD, `list` and `store-copy` now exit 1 with "error reading the store, the output is incomplete" / "... the copy is incomplete".

This issue was identified and fixed by Claude (Claude Code, Anthropic's AI coding assistant).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81415

72383.title: common/io_exerciser: fix four ceph_test_rados_io_sequence defects
72383.author: aainscow
72383.body:
Four defects in `ceph_test_rados_io_sequence`, found running it against replicated and erasure coded pools:

1. Seq16 issued a Consistency op after every TruncateWrite whether or not `--checkconsistency` was given. A replicated pool has no consistency checker, so any run on one that reached Seq16 failed `ceph_assert(cc)` in `RadosIo::applyIoOp()`. Seq16 now checks consistency only when asked, as the other sequences do.
2. The Consistency case in `RadosIo::applyIoOp()` had no `break`, so every consistency check also ran the Copy case and copied the primary object over the secondary one behind the model's back. Added the `break`.
3. Seq15 read its copy target while the `copy_from` and truncate were still in flight. With balanced reads the read could reach a replica first and return the object as it was before the copy, which the tool reported as a miscompare. Seq15 now issues a barrier after them.
4. When no object could start an I/O, the main loop of `run_automated_test()` never waited on its condition variable and spun on RadosIo's lock while any I/O was outstanding (about 65 CPU seconds a minute with `--parallel 1`, against 12 with the fix; a run left behind after its cluster went away spun for 14 hours). It now waits.

Testing: the new `unittest_io_sequence` steps every sequence to Done without a cluster. Its Seq16 test fails before the first fix and its Seq15 test (`NoReadWhileWholeObjectWriteInFlight`) fails before the Seq15 fix; both pass with the fixes. Checked commit by commit on a main build.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81389

72384.title: cephfs_mirror: fsync remote file before closing it
72384.author: LiShengG
72384.body:
Buffered writeback errors can arrive after `ceph_close()` returns and escape
the final `ceph_sync_fs()`. Mirroring can then create a remote snapshot with
missing file data that later incremental syncs do not repair if the source
file stays unchanged.

Call `ceph_fsync(..., 1)` before closing each copied remote regular file so
writeback errors fail the affected directory sync before snapshot creation.
Preserve the first error while closing both file descriptors.

## Performance

Each data worker now waits for a file's data writeback before processing the
next file. This reduces overlap across files and may lower throughput or
increase snapshot synchronization time, especially with many small files or
high-latency remote storage. Workers still run concurrently. Data-only fsync
avoids an additional per-file metadata durability wait; the final
`ceph_sync_fs()` remains.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81402

72386.title: client: report writeback errors from sync_fs and range flushes
72386.author: LiShengG
72386.body:
## sync_fs

Buffered writeback can fail after `close()`, when no `Fh` remains to receive the error. `_sync_fs()` also ignores the flush status, so `ceph_sync_fs()` returns success. cephfs-mirror can then create a remote snapshot with missing data that later incremental syncs do not repair if the source file stays unchanged.

`Inode::set_async_err()` now also saves the error on the `Client`. `_sync_fs()` returns the flush error, or otherwise returns and clears the saved error. Per-handle reporting through `close()`/`fsync()` is unchanged.

## _flush_range

Ignoring range-flush errors lets O_SYNC/O_DSYNC buffered writes report success, blocking O_DIRECT reads return stale data, and O_DIRECT writes proceed despite dirty cached data that may later overwrite them.

`_flush_range()` now returns the error. Blocking direct reads and direct writes stop before issuing I/O. Buffered synchronous writes retain their cached data and metadata updates, but return the error without advancing the file position.

The last commit adds range-flush tests, skipped when `client_oc` is disabled, and can be dropped if preferred.

## Limitation

The saved error is shared per mount: one caller consumes it, so others may miss it. Linux `syncfs()` tracks errors per open file description (`f_sb_err`); equivalent tracking would require a libcephfs API extension.

cephfs-mirror shares a remote mount across directory syncs. #72384 adds per-file `ceph_fsync(..., 1)` before close so errors reach the affected directory sync. The two PRs can be applied independently.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81401

72387.title: tentacle: rgw-bucket-logging: handle presigned SigV2 requests
72387.author: nbalacha

Adds a test to check that the log record AuthenticationType is correctly set to QueryString for SigV2 presigned URLs.
This is not a cherry-pick as the original fix was part of the s3-tests repo before the tests were moved into the ceph repo.

72390.title: osd/scrubber: check EC CRCs only with every data shard and P0
72390.author: aainscow
72390.body:
Deep scrub of an optimized (FastEC) erasure coded pool checks each shard's data CRC through the erasure code. CRC32C is linear only over XOR, so that check is valid only when every data shard and the first parity shard, their XOR, are present. When a shard's scrub map lacked an object, `setup_ec_digest_map()` either decoded the missing CRCs through the plugin, which for ISA `reed_sol_van` uses GF(2^8) arithmetic whenever more than XOR is needed and reports healthy shards as mismatched, or, when it skipped the decode, still looked up every data shard and P0 and threw `std::out_of_range` ("Key not found") from `shard_id_map::at()`. On an OSD that is an abort in scrub. `match_in_shards()` tested only that the shards could be decoded.

This adds `stripe_info_t::can_check_crcs()` and skips the CRC check in both places unless every data shard and P0 are present. A shard missing the object is still reported missing.

Testing: the unit test is in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72425, stacked on this PR. `TestECFailoverWithPeering.ScrubObjectMissingFromOneShard` moves an object off each non-primary shard in turn, deep-scrubs, and expects the object reported missing on that shard and nowhere else. On a main build, without this fix all five ISA configurations throw "Key not found" (the five jerasure configurations pass, as jerasure does not check CRCs through the code); with it all ten pass, and so does the rest of `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering` (228 tests).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81332

72391.title: osd/PrimaryLogPG: mark omap dirty when copy_from replaces an object
72391.author: aainscow
72391.body:
`copy_from` onto an existing object removes the target and recreates it from the source, but `PrimaryLogPG::finish_copyfrom()` marked the omap dirty in the log entry's clean regions only when the source had omap. With a source that has no omap the entry claimed the omap was clean, although the target's old omap was removed with the object.

Log-based recovery trusts the clean regions: a replica that missed the copy is updated in place with its omap left alone, so it keeps the old omap keys and header while the primary has none. Deep scrub then reports `omap_digest_mismatch`, and a later omap write can make the stale keys readable on that replica. This has been the case since partial recovery was added in Octopus.

The fix marks the omap dirty whenever the existing target is removed, as `_delete_oid()` and `_rollback_to()` already do.

Testing: the new `TEST_copy_from_over_omap_recovers_omap` in `qa/standalone/osd/osd-copy-from.sh` gives an object omap and an omap header, takes the replicas out of the acting set, copies an object without omap over it, brings the replicas back and deep-scrubs the PG. On a main build it fails without the fix and the whole script passes with it. On an erasure coded pool the same sequence recovers correctly and deep scrub is clean.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81367

72399.title: crimson/osd: avoid shard-0 from PG, send core hit to clients
72399.author: perezjosibm
72399.body:
This PR makes these changes:
- **Reactor 0** handles only OSDSingletonState, OSDMap updates, and control messages
- **All PGs live on reactors 1..N** (never placed on reactor 0)
- **Clients skip the `get_pg_mapping` pipeline stage** entirely after the first `MOSDShardMap` exchange, eliminating the most common source of cross-core traffic on the hot path

#### Improvement 1 — Client PG→Shard Lookup Table

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [`src/messages/MOSDOp.h`](src/messages/MOSDOp.h) | Added `shard_hint` field, `get_shard_hint()`/`set_shard_hint()` accessors; bumped `HEAD_VERSION` to 10; added v9/v10 encode+decode split gated on `SERVER_TENTACLE` |
| [`src/msg/Message.h`](src/msg/Message.h) | Added `#define MSG_OSD_SHARD_MAP 137` |
| [`src/messages/MOSDShardMap.h`](src/messages/MOSDShardMap.h) | New message — carries the OSD's `spg_t → core_id` table to clients; includes `bind_epoch` for cache invalidation |
| [`src/crimson/osd/osd_connection_priv.h`](src/crimson/osd/osd_connection_priv.h) | Added `last_shard_map_sent` epoch field to `OSDConnectionPriv` to track per-connection delivery |
| [`src/crimson/osd/osd.h`](src/crimson/osd/osd.h) | Declared `maybe_send_shard_map()`; added `MOSDShardMap.h` include |
| [`src/crimson/osd/osd.cc`](src/crimson/osd/osd.cc) | Implemented `maybe_send_shard_map()` (snapshots `pg_to_core`, sends if epoch stale); updated `handle_osd_op()` to fire-and-forget it; added `MOSDShardMap.h` include |
| [`src/crimson/osd/pg_map.h`](src/crimson/osd/pg_map.h) | Added `get_pg_mapping_pair()` returning `optional<pair<core_id_t, store_index_t>>` |
| [`src/crimson/osd/pg_shard_manager.h`](src/crimson/osd/pg_shard_manager.h) | Added fast-path in `start_pg_operation`: checks local cache first (no future, no cross-core), then passes `shard_hint` from `MOSDOp` as `core_expected` |

#### Improvement 2 — Avoid PGs on Reactor 0

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| [`src/crimson/osd/state.h`](src/crimson/osd/state.h) | Added `get_mapping_core()` inline function returning core 1 when smp > 1, else 0 |
| [`src/crimson/osd/pg_map.cc`](src/crimson/osd/pg_map.cc) | Replaced hardcoded `invoke_on(0, ...)` with `invoke_on(get_mapping_core(), ...)`; added `state.h` include |
| [`src/crimson/osd/osd.cc`](src/crimson/osd/osd.cc) | `pg_to_shard_mappings.start()` now passes `pg_min_core = 1` (when smp > 1) so reactor 0 is never populated in `core_to_num_pgs` |


### Architecture after changes

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    C[Client] -->|MOSDOp + shard_hint=3| R0[Reactor 0\nOSDSingletonState\nControl msgs only]
    C -->|MOSDOp + shard_hint=3| R3[Reactor 3\nPG 1.4, 2.7...]
    C -->|MOSDShardMap cached| C

    R0 -->|PG ops forwarded| R3
    R3 -->|MOSDOpReply + MOSDShardMap| C

    R1[Reactor 1\nPGs + MAPPING_CORE] -->|update broadcast| R2[Reactor 2\nPGs]
    R1 --> R3
    R1 --> R0
```

### Preliminary performance results
* Same configurations as described in [80545](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80545) -- same methodology: avg of three runs.
* No improvements for replica=3.

* replica=1 (randwrite 4k):

| _.Config | _.Before | _.After | _.Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 OSD |	IOPS=16.2k, 3.9 ms 	| IOPS=19.3k, 3.3 ms | +119.13%  |
| 3 OSD |	IOPS=25.7k, 2.48 ms 	| IOPS=38.5k, 1.6 ms | +149.80% |

* Please note: Delta indicates how *After* results compares with the *Before* results, so the net difference is that for 1 OSD the gain in performance is 20% and for 3 OSD the gain is 50%.

On FreeBSD every disk is a character device (GEOM providers, including zvols under /dev/zvol), and fstat() reports st_size == 0 for them. refresh_size() only queried the device size for S_ISBLK, so on FreeBSD a device came out as size 0 and ceph-osd --mkfs failed with a crash...
