72406.title: doc/start: add HDD Selection section (avoid SMR drives for OSDs)
72406.author: AdamDudley
72406.body:
## Description

The **Storage Devices** page has an *SSD Selection* section but no parallel *HDD Selection* guidance. This adds a short `HDD Selection` list-table covering the two HDD-specific decisions that most affect OSD behavior.

The primary recommendation is to **use CMR and avoid SMR (shingled) drives for OSDs**. SMR's drive-managed rewriting of overlapping tracks stalls under the sustained random writes that BlueStore, RocksDB compaction, and recovery/backfill generate — a well-known cause of slow recovery and, under load, stalled OSDs. Vendors rarely label the recording technology on the data sheet, so the note tells readers to confirm CMR before buying.

A second row covers capacity/cost, cross-referencing the existing *Choosing Between HDD and SSD* section.

## Rationale

Readers deploying bulk HDD OSDs currently get no warning about SMR anywhere in the docs (zero mentions repo-wide). This is a frequent, costly mistake in HDD-backed clusters.

## Notes

- Additive only: a new section inserted before *Choosing a Controller (HBA)*; no existing text changed.
- Commit is DCO signed-off per `SubmittingPatches.rst`.
- The capacity/cost row includes one external reference to a per-capacity cost-per-TB comparison as a sizing aid for CMR drives. Happy to drop it or replace it with a community CMR/SMR reference list if you'd prefer the section carry no external link.

72407.title: kv/RocksDBStore: abort when an iterator hits a read error
72407.author: aainscow
72407.body:
**Depends on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72382.** The first three commits are that PR's and are reviewed there; only the last five commits are new. This will be rebased onto main once 72382 merges.

### Problem

RocksDB reports a read error that it finds while iterating, such as a block checksum mismatch, only through `Iterator::status()`. `Valid()` becomes false, so the iteration looks finished. `RocksDBStore::get()` aborts on such an error, but the iterators only returned -1 from the seek or step. BlueStore never checks `status()` or those return codes, so an unreadable SST block silently truncates whatever BlueStore is iterating: fsck, `collection_list`, `omap_iterate`, NCB allocation recovery, the bitmap freelist init, `_deferred_replay` and `_clone` all treat the error as the end of the data.

Sharded prefixes (O, p and m by default) are worse. `ShardMergeIteratorImpl::seek_to_first()`, `lower_bound()` and `upper_bound()` returned at the first shard that failed, without seeking the later shards and without sorting. `valid()` and `status()` then followed `iters[0]`, usually a healthy shard, so the walk carried on over the healthy shards and reported success. A whole column family, about a third of the keys, dropped out.

This was seen on two OSDs whose SST had its first 4 KiB overwritten (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68060):
- On the first, the only SST of column family O-2 was unreadable from its first block. `ceph-bluestore-tool fsck` reported 8762 errors and no read error: 733 leaked extents, 7957 shared blob ref mismatches and a statfs mismatch for every pool. Its object walk had skipped all of O-2, and the "leaked" space is exactly the space of the O-2 objects it never visited, so `fsck --repair` would have freed it. `collection_list` of the meta collection left out the 112 objects whose onodes were in the bad blocks and returned success.
- On the second, the first blocks of p-2 held the omap of `purged_snaps`. fsck reported success with 0 errors, and `omap_iterate` returned 0 entries for an object with at least 118 readable ones.

Details, evidence and the list of affected BlueStore code paths: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81440

### What this changes

- **Iterators fail-stop** (`kv/RocksDBStore: abort when an iterator hits a read error`). A seek, `next()` or `prev()` that leaves a non-OK status now aborts with the RocksDB status text, for example `Corruption: block checksum mismatch: ... in <sst> offset 0 size <n>`. This is the same as `get()`. It applies to `CFIteratorImpl`, `ShardMergeIteratorImpl` and `RocksDBWholeSpaceIteratorImpl`; the last used to assert on IOError only, and only in some of its methods. `WholeMergeIteratorImpl` is built from these, so it behaves the same way. The callers' `valid()` loops are unchanged. `RocksDBWholeSpaceIteratorImpl::seek_to_last(prefix)` now checks the status of its seek past the prefix before it falls back to `SeekToLast()`, which used to reset it.
- **Opt-out for tools.** With the new `KeyValueDB::ITERATOR_NOABORT` option, errors come back through `status()` instead of aborting. Only ceph-kvstore-tool uses it: `StoreTool::traverse` (list, list-crc, dump, store-crc) and `copy_store_to` (store-copy), which check `status()` and exit 1 since #72382.
- **`ShardMergeIteratorImpl` keeps a shard error visible** (`kv/RocksDBStore: keep a shard read error visible after a sharded seek`). Each seek now seeks every shard and sorts before checking status. A failed shard iterator is moved to `iters[0]`, so the iterator is invalid and `status()` returns the error. `status()` now checks every shard, not just `iters[0]`. `prev()` no longer re-seeks a shard that became invalid with an error to its first key, which used to lose the error, and it checks status at both of its exits.
- **Multi-key `get()`** (`kv/RocksDBStore: abort on any read error in the multi-key get()`). It now aborts on any status other than OK and NotFound, as the single-key `get()` does. It used to abort only o

72408.title: mgr/dashboard: implement hardware monitoring hosts API with pagination
72408.author: afreen23
72408.body:
All details in tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81439 Add GET /api/hardware/hosts (paginated list) and GET /api/hardware/hosts/{hostname} (per-host detail) for the hardware monitoring integration. Both return the same per-host object: hostname, serial number, overall health, per-category health counts with their components, and installed firmware versions. Node-proxy reports are large and cephadm holds one per host. Instead of fetching every host's full report and paginating afterwards, the list endpoint asks cephadm only for the host names (new node_proxy_list_hosts()), paginates those, and then fetches the full report only for the hosts on the requested page. The cost per request depends on the page size, not on the number of hosts in the cluster. Add the HardwareNoReport orchestrator error, raised when a host has no usable node-proxy report. The list skips such hosts, the detail endpoint returns 404, and any other orchestrator error is still reported as an error. ```ts MOCK_HOST_BLOB = { 'host': 'host1', 'sn': 'ABC123', 'status': { 'storage': { '1': { 'disk-0': {'status': {'health': 'OK'}}, 'disk-1': {'status': {'health': 'Critical'}}, } }, 'fans': { '1': { 'fan-0': {'status': {'health': 'OK'}}, 'fan-1': {'status': {'health': 'Warning'}}, } }, 'processors': {'1': {'cpu-0': {'status': {'health': 'OK'}}}}, 'memory': {'1': {'dimm-0': {'status': {'health': 'OK'}}}}, 'network': {'1': {'nic-0': {'status': {'health': 'OK'}}}}, 'power': {'1': {'psu-0': {'status': {'health': 'OK'}}}}, 'temperatures': {'1': {'temp-0': {'status': {'health': 'OK'}}}}, }, 'firmware': { 'id-bmc': {'name': 'BMC', 'version': '2.14'}, 'id-bios': {'name': 'BIOS', 'version': '1.8.3'}, 'id-lc': {'name': 'Lifecycle Controller', 'version': 'unknown'}, } } ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD A["node-proxy on each host
reads the BMC via Redfish"] -->|"POST report every 5 min"| B["cephadm NodeProxyCache
NodeProxyRawData"] B -->|"list_hosts()"| C["dashboard HardwareManager"] B -->|"fullreport(host)"| C C -->|"RawHostReport"| D["HardwareHostResponse.from_raw()"] D --> E["HardwareHostResponse
HardwareStatus → Category → *Component"] E -->|"to_dict()"| F["JSON"] F --> G["GET /api/hardware/hosts"] F --> H["GET /api/hardware/hosts/{hostname}"] ``` **cephadm changes:** HardwareNoReport. This is a new exception in orchestrator/_interface.py: ```python class HardwareNoReport(OrchestratorError): """Raised when a host has no node-proxy data (unknown host or node-proxy not running).""" def __init__(self, msg: str) -> None: super().__init__(msg, errno=-errno.ENOENT) ``` NodeProxyCache._resolve_hosts() now raises it, instead of a plain OrchestratorError, for an unknown host.

72410.title: cmake: fix ceph_ver.h in a worktree with a detached HEAD
72410.author: dvanders
72410.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81316

Building in a git worktree that has a detached HEAD fails when the main
checkout is on a branch:

```
build/src/include/ceph_ver.h:4:25: error: expected '=', ',', ';', 'asm' or '__attribute__' before ':' token
#define CEPH_GIT_VER ref: refs/heads/main
```

`grabRef.cmake` switches `GIT_DIR` to the worktree's common dir to resolve
branch refs, and the detached-HEAD branch then copies `${GIT_DIR}/HEAD`,
which is the main checkout's HEAD. The fix copies the worktree's own HEAD,
already saved as `HEAD_FILE`. (If the main checkout is detached as well, the
build silently gets the wrong version instead of failing.)

Tested with a minimal CMake project that includes the module, with refs
packed by `git gc` (the case from e15946e22aa):

| layout | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| main checkout, on a branch | correct | correct |
| worktree, detached | `ref: refs/heads/main` | correct hash |
| worktree, on a branch | correct | correct |
| detached worktree, HEAD moved, rebuild | — | re-configures, new hash |

72411.title: mds: hold mds_lock while reading mdsmap/mds_rank in status asok
72411.author: vshankar
72411.body:
MDSDaemon::dump_status() runs on the admin socket thread and reads mdsmap and mds_rank without mds_lock; only the mds_rank->dump_status() call was locked. handle_mds_map() runs under mds_lock and swaps out mdsmap, leaving it null until the new map is allocated and decoded. A "status" asok command racing with an mdsmap update dereferences a null/partially decoded MDSMap and crashes the MDS:

  *** Caught signal (Segmentation fault) **
   in thread thread_name:admin_socket
   2: (MDSDaemon::dump_status(ceph::Formatter*)+0x1e0)
   3: (MDSDaemon::asok_command(...))

mds_rank is likewise created and destroyed under mds_lock. Take mds_lock once around all accesses to mdsmap and mds_rank.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81448
Related-to: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64717
Reported-by: Dan van der Ster <dan.vanderster@clyso.com>
Reported-by: Abhishek Lekshmanan <abhishek.lekshmanan@cern.ch>

72412.title: script/vstart_chaos: fault injection runs on a vstart cluster
72412.author: aainscow
72412.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81452

Scripts that run a vstart cluster under random faults while client workloads run, then check that the cluster ends clean. This is developer tooling: apart from a page in `doc/dev` nothing outside `src/script/vstart_chaos` changes, and nothing runs it in `make check` or teuthology.

- **setup_cluster.sh** recreates the vstart cluster with one test pool: erasure coded (2+1 by default, with or without `allow_ec_optimizations`) or replicated, in one zone or over two datacenters with an arbiter monitor. On main, two sites use global stretch mode (`ceph mon enable_stretch_mode`), which takes replicated pools only. Where the monitors support `osd pool create --num_zones` (not in main), the pool is a `--num_zones 2` pool instead, which may also be erasure coded. **make_snapshot.sh** and **upgrade_cluster.sh** move the cluster onto a copy of a build's binaries, so that the build tree can change during a run.
- **chaos.py** applies weighted random actions in cycles, keeping each zone within its failure budget: OSD kill and restart, mark down, out/in, reweight, primary affinity, pg_num split and merge, repeer, deep scrub and pg-upmaps, and for a pool over two sites whole and partial site failures that run across cycles while everything else goes on. Meanwhile it runs `ceph_test_rados` (plain, localized and balanced reads), `ceph_test_rados_io_sequence`, rbd round trips and I/O probes that report stalled operations. Every 30 cycles and at the end it quiesces: it revives everything, waits for clean PGs and deep scrubs every PG. It stops on a crash, a daemon it did not kill dying, a workload failure or miscompare, a stuck operation, an inconsistent PG or PGs that do not return to clean, and saves the PG evidence.
- **run_chaos.sh** does one complete run, from a fresh cluster to a summary. Before it destroys the vstart cluster in `$CEPH_BUILD` it prints that build directory and its version and asks (`-y` skips the question).

Two hours on two sites in global stretch mode with a replicated pool, from the source root of a full build:

```
CEPH_BUILD=$PWD/build src/script/vstart_chaos/run_chaos.sh -p replicated -z 2 -t 7200
```

Two hours on a single-zone EC 2+1 pool with `allow_ec_optimizations`:

```
CEPH_BUILD=$PWD/build src/script/vstart_chaos/run_chaos.sh -p erasure -k 2 -m 1 -t 7200
```

`doc/dev/vstart_chaos.rst` and `run_chaos.sh -h` describe the options and how to read the results.

Bugs on main that runs of these scripts have hit: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81367 (stale omap after `copy_from` and log-based recovery), https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81194 (balanced EC direct reads after PG changes), https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81136 (`ceph mon enable_stretch_mode` replying EINVAL), https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81389 and https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81606 (`ceph_test_rados_io_sequence`) and, in runs on the stretch EC development branch, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81611, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81630, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81632 and https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81634.

### Testing
On main (c9664d9cdfb) with https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72556 applied, 3 monitors and 8 OSDs on one host. Without that PR, `ceph_test_rados_io_sequence` aborted in Seq15 (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81606) after 16 minutes of the first run.
- Two sites in global stretch mode, replicated size 4 (`-p replicated -z 2 -t 3600`): pass. 206 cycles with 5 site failures (one flap, one with the OSDs revived first, three with OSD losses in the surviving site), pg_num splits and merges, 4 quiesces with deep scrubs.
- One zone, EC 2+1 with `allow_ec_optimizations` (`-p erasure -k 2 -m 1 -t 3600`): pass. 120 cycles, 5 quiesces with deep scrubs, pg_num splits and merges, plain, localized and balanced reads.

On the stretch EC development branch, whose monitors support `--num_zones`: a two-zone EC 2+2 run ended by SIGTERM during a quiesce passed (a flap and a monitor-only site fail

72413.title: mgr/cephadm: fix ingress daemon upgrades
72413.author: Shubhaj1810
72413.body:
**Summary**

mgr/cephadm: upgrade ingress daemons during orchestrator upgrades
Ingress daemons (haproxy and keepalived) were being skipped during ceph orch upgrade because they were not included in the upgrade ordering or non-Ceph image handling logic. Additionally, upgrade processing relied on service-type lookups that do not work for ingress daemon types.

**This change:**
- Adds haproxy and keepalived to the cephadm upgrade order.
- Treats ingress daemons as non-Ceph-image services during upgrade status tracking.
- Introduces daemon-type based lookups for ingress daemons to avoid upgrade processing failures.
- Adds rolling upgrade rate limiting so ingress daemons are upgraded serially rather than all at once.
- Ensures ingress daemon upgrade progress is correctly reflected in ceph orch upgrade status.

**Validation**

**Before fix**
- Upgrade completed at 20/26 daemons upgraded.

72414.title: mds: reset heartbeat in cache-wide walks during resolve and rejoin
72414.author: vshankar
72414.body:
recalc_auth_bits() (end of up:resolve) and rejoin_scour_survivor_replicas() (handling a weak rejoin, on both a rejoining rank and a survivor) walk the entire cache under mds_lock without resetting the MDS internal heartbeat. With a large cache (e.g. after replaying a very long journal) these walks take long enough for the heartbeat to time out:

  heartbeat_map is_healthy 'MDSRank' had timed out after 15.000000954s
  mds.beacon.X Skipping beacon heartbeat to monitors (last acked 4s ago); MDS internal heartbeat is not healthy!

The mons then mark the MDS laggy and, with a standby available, fail the rank -- which restarts recovery and hits the same walk again.

Reset the heartbeat every heartbeat_reset_grace() items, as is done elsewhere on the recovery path (e.g. trim_unlinked_inodes()).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81449
Related-to: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64717
Reported-by: Dan van der Ster <dan.vanderster@clyso.com>
Reported-by: Abhishek Lekshmanan <abhishek.lekshmanan@cern.ch>

72416.title: mon/OSDMonitor: add missing checks to the stretch pool and stretch mode commands
72416.author: aainscow
72416.body:
Three defects in the stretch pool and stretch mode monitor commands, found while testing stretch erasure coded pools on a development branch and shown on a main build:

1. `ceph osd pool stretch set` accepted an erasure-coded pool, although stretch pools must be replicated (`ceph mon enable_stretch_mode` refuses EC pools). `stretch set` and `ceph osd pool stretch unset` then applied whatever size they were given: a k=2 m=1 pool became size 6, which `ceph osd pool set size` refuses for an EC pool. `stretch set` now refuses an EC pool, with the message `enable_stretch_mode` uses. `stretch unset` can then only meet an EC pool that an older release stretched. Refusing it would leave no way to clear its stretch values, so it accepts such a pool only with size k+m and min_size between k and k+m, which also repairs a size the old `stretch set` changed.
2. `ceph osd pool stretch set` and `ceph osd pool stretch unset` configure an individual stretch pool, which doc/rados/operations/stretch-mode.rst ("Individual Stretch Pools") offers as the alternative to stretch mode: stretch mode for exactly two data centers, a stretch pool for a pool spread over more than two. The monitor nevertheless accepted both while stretch mode was enabled. Stretch mode sets every pool's stretch values itself and changes them in its degraded and healthy transitions, and a pool changed by hand does not follow them. For example, `stretch set` in degraded stretch mode gave the pool the healthy `peering_crush_bucket_count` of 2 while only one zone was up, so its PGs stayed undersized+peered and its I/O blocked until the lost zone returned. Both commands now fail with -EINVAL while stretch mode is enabled.
3. `ceph osd force_healthy_stretch_mode` only ends recovery stretch mode, but in any other state it did nothing and still replied "Triggering healthy stretch mode" with success. It now fails with -EINVAL outside recovery stretch mode.

Each fix is one commit together with the standalone test that shows the defect and its documentation (doc/rados/operations/pools.rst and stretch-mode.rst). The EC stretch cluster design (doc/dev/osd_internals/erasure_coding/ec_stretch_cluster.rst) is not changed here: its updates for these refusals are part of the stretch cluster work in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72643.

All the tests are in `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-commands.sh`. The EC tests run 3 mons without OSDs; the others run 3 mons and 4 OSDs in two zones plus a tiebreaker, in stretch mode. To restart a monitor on its existing data without copying `run_mon`'s ceph-mon arguments, `qa/standalone: split activate_mon out of run_mon` moves the command that starts the daemon into a new `activate_mon` in ceph-helpers.sh, as `activate_osd` does for OSDs; `run_mon` calls it after `--mkfs`.

Testing, on a main build, with ceph-mon rebuilt at each step:
- Each new test failed without its fix and passed with it (checked before the test, fix and doc commits were squashed into one commit per defect).
  - `TEST_stretch_set_ec_pool` fails because the monitor answers "pool ec stretch values are set successfully" for a k=2 m=1 pool (`TEST_stretch_set_replicated_pool` passes). With the fix, `stretch set` on the EC pool is refused, `stretch unset` fails with "pool ec is not a stretch pool", and the pool's size, min_size and bucket count are unchanged. The test checks only `stretch set`: with the fix no EC pool can be made a stretch pool, so the EC size check of `stretch unset` cannot be set up (next bullet).
  - `TEST_stretch_pool_commands_in_stretch_mode` fails because, in healthy stretch mode, `ceph osd pool stretch set stretched 2 2 zone replicated_rule 6 3` returns 0 ("pool stretched stretch values are set successfully"). A copy of the test without that step showed `ceph osd pool stretch unset stretched replicated_rule 3 2` accepted as well ("pool stretched is no longer a stretch pool, all stretch values are unset successfully"). With the fix both are refused ("... is

72418.title: tools/ceph-kvstore-tool: fail store-copy cleanly when the store cannot be created
72418.author: aainscow
72418.body:
`ceph-kvstore-tool bluestore-kv <path> store-copy <dest>` crashed with a segmentation fault. The target store type defaults to the source type, `KeyValueDB::create()` can only create rocksdb stores and returns nullptr for bluestore-kv (or any other type), and `StoreTool::copy_store_to()` dereferenced the result.

- qa/workunits/cephtool: `test_kvstore_tool.sh` now expects store-copy without a store type to fail with a message naming bluestore-kv, and store-copy to rocksdb to copy every key. `expect_false` alone would also pass on the crash, so the test also checks the message.
- tools/ceph-kvstore-tool: `copy_store_to()` returns -EINVAL with "cannot create a store of type '<type>'; pass a store type such as rocksdb", and the usage text says that bluestore-kv needs the type.
- doc/man: `ceph-kvstore-tool.rst` documents the store type argument of store-copy.

Testing: `qa/workunits/cephtool/test_kvstore_tool.sh`, run locally on a main build. With only the test commit it fails at the message check; running the same store-copy by hand ends in a segmentation fault (exit status 139) in `StoreTool::copy_store_to()`. With the fix it passes: store-copy without a type exits 1 with the message, and store-copy to rocksdb copies all 12 keys. The man page was not built.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81466

72419.title: mgr/DaemonServer: _check_offlines_pgs must not skip PGs whose last acting OSD is not in the set
72419.author: FredNass
72419.body:
Since cf54988c504 ("mgr/DaemonServer: Modify offline_pg_report to handle set or vector types"), `_check_offlines_pgs()` only evaluates a PG when its *last* acting OSD is among the OSDs being checked: the `std::visit` introduced there assigns `found = container.count(a)` on every iteration, so `found` no longer records whether *any* member of the acting set is in the set — it reflects the last member only — and `if (!found) continue;` skips every PG whose last acting OSD is not in the set, however many of its other copies are.

Example: PG acting `[1, 2, 3]`, `size 3 / min_size 2`. `ceph osd ok-to-stop 1 2` visits 1 (found), 2 (found), 3 (found = **false**) → the PG is never evaluated → rc 0, `"ok_to_stop": true`, although one copy would remain. `ceph osd ok-to-stop 2 3` (osd.3 is last) is evaluated and refused.

`osd ok-to-stop` is what cephadm's upgrade asks before restarting each OSD (`_wait_for_ok_to_stop`), what `osd ok-to-upgrade` builds its batches with (`_maximize_ok_to_upgrade_set`), and what admins call by hand before maintenance. Only the OSDs that *end* an acting set are protected today.

Affected: main, (Umbrella) v21.0.0, v21.0.1, v21.1.0, (tentacle) v20.2.2, 20.2.3 and 20.2.4. Squid still has the old code and is fine.

The fix makes `found` sticky again: a small `in_set` visitor answers for one OSD (keeping the set/vector handling of cf54988c504), and both loops set `found = true` when it says so.

No unit test covers `_check_offlines_pgs` in `src/test/mgr`; one with an acting set whose last member is outside the checked set would catch a regression here — happy to add it if reviewers want it in this PR.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81468

Discovered-By : Claude Fable 5.1 High.

72420.title: cephadm: staged switch for OSDs — restart every OSD of a CRUSH bucket in one go
72420.author: FredNass
72420.body:
Follow-up to #72111, which added the staged switch (stage the new deployment while the daemons serve, switch them with one restart) with an MDS policy. This PR adds the OSD policy announced there, and the `cephadm` changes it needs. Stacked on #72111: its commits show up here until it merges; the 11 last commits are this PR's. It is about the OSD phase of the upgrade only; MONs and MGRs are left to a separate PR.

> **Depends on a fix to `osd ok-to-stop` on main.** Since cf54988c504 (Feb 2026, part of the `osd ok-to-upgrade` work) `_check_offlines_pgs` only evaluates a PG when its *last* acting OSD is in the set being checked (`found` is overwritten on every iteration instead of being sticky), so `osd ok-to-stop` — and the regular OSD upgrade path, and `osd ok-to-upgrade` — can answer "safe" for a set that leaves PGs below `min_size`. This policy puts whole hosts behind that answer, so it must not merge before the fix: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81468, PR #72419 .

## Upgrade time of the OSD phase: stock vs staged switch (3 nodes, 72 OSDs)

| Method | Failure domain | OSD phase (s) | Time with OSDs down (s) | Outage windows |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| stock v18.2.8 | datacenter | $\color{red}{\textsf{505}}$ | $\color{red}{\textsf{436}}$ | 6–7 batches |
| stock v18.2.8 | rack | $\color{red}{\textsf{531}}$ | $\color{red}{\textsf{441}}$ | 8–10 batches |
| stock v18.2.8 | host | $\color{red}{\textsf{539}}$ | $\color{red}{\textsf{440}}$ | 8–9 batches |
| **staged switch** | datacenter | $\color{green}{\textsf{67}}$ (÷7.5) | $\color{green}{\textsf{24}}$ (÷18) | 3 datacenters |
| **staged switch** | rack | $\color{green}{\textsf{135}}$ (÷3.9) | $\color{green}{\textsf{44}}$ (÷10) | 6 racks |
| **staged switch** | host | $\color{green}{\textsf{124}}$ (÷4.3) | $\color{green}{\textsf{43}}$ (÷10) | 6 hosts |

Setup and method in [Testing](#testing) below.

## What it does

With `osd` added to `mgr/cephadm/upgrade_staged_switch_types`, the OSD phase of `ceph orch upgrade` no longer redeploys OSDs one at a time. A group is **every OSD still to upgrade under one CRUSH bucket** of the type given by the new `mgr/cephadm/upgrade_staged_switch_osd_crush_level` option (default `host`). At the start of the OSD phase, every OSD the policy will switch is **staged ahead** (#72111's `upgrade_staged_switch_stage_ahead`, on by default): `cephadm deploy --stage` writes the new config, keyring and unit files next to the live ones and runs the target image once, while the OSDs serve — **one `cephadm _orch deploy-staged` call per host** for all its OSDs (new in this PR: one cluster lock, one image check, one `daemon-reload`, the uid/gid and sysctl looked up once per call, no firewall reload), hosts in parallel. On the test cluster below, the 72 OSDs are staged in 14–15 s. Then, per serve() pass, the policy:

1. walks the buckets of that type and asks the monitors, with `osd ok-to-stop <ids> max=<len>` on the exact set of OSDs still to upgrade under the bucket, whether **every PG stays active** (keeps ≥ `min_size` copies) without them — the same criterion the regular path applies per OSD. The first bucket that passes is the group. While none passes, it asks again every 2 s, up to 45 s per pass;
2. re-stages only the OSDs of the group whose target image or generated configuration changed since they were staged ahead (none, normally);
3. sets `noout` on exactly those OSDs (`osd set-group noout`), asks `ok-to-stop` once more, and switches them: **one `cephadm switch-staged` call per host naming every OSD of the group on it**, so a host's OSDs go down and come back around a single `systemctl stop` / `start` (new in this PR: `switch-staged` takes `--name` several times and checks every daemon before stopping any — cephadm's per-host lock would otherwise serialize one restart per OSD);
4. waits until the osdmap shows every one of them up again with a new `up_from`, `osd metadata` reports the target `ceph_version_short` for each, and every PG each of them hold

72421.title: mon/OSDMonitor: fail force_recovery_stretch_mode unless it can start recovery
72421.author: aainscow
72421.body:
Depends on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72416; only the last three commits are new.

### Problem

https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81467

- `ceph osd force_recovery_stretch_mode --yes-i-really-mean-it` crashes the leader if it runs in degraded stretch mode while every monitor of the lost data center is still down. The handler in `OSDMonitor::prepare_command_impl()` called `Monitor::go_recovery_stretch_mode()` unconditionally. That function asserts when `dead_mon_buckets` is not empty:
  ```
  src/mon/Monitor.cc: 7210: FAILED ceph_assert(0 == "how did we try and do stretch recovery while we have dead monitor buckets?")
  ```
- The crash costs the cluster its quorum. The monitors left after losing a data center are a bare majority: 3 of 5 in the layout stretch-mode.rst documents, 2 of 3 in the test.
- The automatic path in `OSDMonitor::update_from_paxos()` has checked `dead_mon_buckets` first since https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/57017, but the command never did. stretch-mode.rst ("Forcing Recovery Stretch Mode") offers the command for when the automatic switch "does not happen or you want to enable recovery mode early", so it is likely to be run before the lost data center is back.
- In healthy stretch mode, in recovery stretch mode or without stretch mode, the command did nothing and still replied "Triggering recovery stretch mode" with success. `force_healthy_stretch_mode` behaved the same way before #72416 (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81429).

### What this changes

- **mon/OSDMonitor.** `force_recovery_stretch_mode` now fails with -EINVAL in three cases:
  - not in degraded stretch mode: "the cluster is not in degraded stretch mode"
  - already recovering: "the cluster is already in recovery stretch mode"
  - a monitor bucket is down: "monitor buckets {pze=b} are down; recovery stretch mode needs all monitor buckets up"

  These are the cases in which `go_recovery_stretch_mode()` either did nothing or asserted, so nothing that used to work is refused now. The checks come before the `--yes-i-really-mean-it` check, as in `force_healthy_stretch_mode`. The command's help text in MonCommands.h ("if currently degraded and all monitor buckets are up") now matches what it does.
- **Tests.** Two new tests in `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-commands.sh`. The cluster has 3 mons (mon.a in zone iris, mon.b in zone pze, tiebreaker mon.c) and 4 OSDs, 2 per zone, in stretch mode.
  - `TEST_force_recovery_stretch_mode_requires_degraded`: the command must fail in healthy stretch mode.
  - `TEST_force_recovery_stretch_mode_requires_mons_up`:
    1. Lose zone pze (kill mon.b, osd.2 and osd.3) and wait for degraded stretch mode.
    2. The command, run under `timeout 60`, must fail with "monitor buckets {pze=b} are down", and the quorum must still be `["a","c"]`.
    3. Restart only mon.b. The cluster must still be degraded and not recovering, with all monitor buckets up. This is the "enable recovery mode early" case from the doc.
    4. The command must now succeed, and the cluster must reach recovery stretch mode.
    5. A second run must fail with "already in recovery stretch mode".

  To restart only the monitor, the mon part of `restore_zone_pze` is split out into a new `restore_mon_pze`.
- **Doc.** doc/rados/operations/stretch-mode.rst ("Forcing Recovery Stretch Mode") now says when the command fails, including while the tiebreaker is down.

### Testing

The standalone tests ran one at a time from the build directory, with the environment `qa/run-standalone.sh` sets up, and with ceph-mon built by `ninja vstart-base` from the code under test.

- **Test commit (unfixed ceph-mon).** Both new tests fail:
  - `TEST_force_recovery_stretch_mode_requires_mons_up`: the command prints nothing and is stopped by the 60 s timeout. mon.a's log shows the crash:
    ```
    mon.a@0(leader).osd e49 prepare_update mon_command({"prefix": "osd force_recovery_stretch_mode", "yes_i_really_mean_it": true} v 0)
    mon.a@0(leader) e8 dead_mon_buck

72425.title: test/osd: add EC scrub test for an object missing from one shard
72425.author: aainscow
72425.body:
Adds a unit test for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81332, split out of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72390 so that PR carries only the fix.

**Stacked on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72390**: the first commit, "osd/scrubber: check EC CRCs only with every data shard and P0", belongs to that PR; only the last commit is new here. The test fails without the fix, so this PR should merge after https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72390.

Deep scrub of an optimized (FastEC) erasure coded pool checks each shard's data CRC through the erasure code, which is valid only when every data shard and the first parity shard (P0) are present. Without the fix, an object missing from one of those shards made scrub throw `std::out_of_range` ("Key not found") for every ISA configuration.

This adds `hide_shard_object()`/`restore_shard_object()` to `PGBackendTestFixture` to move a shard's copy of an object aside, and records each shard's errors from `scrub_object()`. The new `TestECFailoverWithPeering.ScrubObjectMissingFromOneShard` moves an object off each non-primary shard in turn, deep-scrubs, and expects the object reported missing on that shard and nowhere else.

Testing: on a main build, without the fix all five ISA configurations throw "Key not found" (the five jerasure configurations pass, as jerasure does not check CRCs through the code); with the fix all ten pass, and so does the rest of `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering` (228 tests). The tree at the head of this PR is identical to the previous head of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72390, which is what was tested.

72437.title: mds: CephFS change notification (MDS-side producer, Kafka endpoint)
72437.body:
This implements the MDS-side change-notification direction from tracker #77895
(and the reopened #62215): a stream of path-level events for CephFS namespace
operations and client write flushes, produced by the MDS, with a Kafka endpoint
that the OpenCloud/reva posixfs watcher (`cephfswatcher.go`) already consumes.
The point is that a stock Ceph can drive the sync/collaboration consumers that
exist today, with no consumer changes.

The event format follows what that consumer dispatches on: inotify-style mask
values, paths relative to a configured watch root, one action per message. The
unit tests in the series pin the records byte for byte.

## The series

1. Change-notification core: hooks on `Server::journal_and_reply()` (all
   journaled namespace operations) and `Locker::_do_cap_update()` (client
   write/truncate flushes, which bypass the journal choke point); the records
   and operation classification in `ChangeNotifyFormat.h`; a bounded in-memory
   queue drained by one thread per rank with a drop-the-newest policy and
   counters; the file endpoint used by tests; the `mds_notify_*` options;
   `notify status` / `notify enable` / `notify disable` on the admin socket;
   all of it under the new `WITH_MDS_NOTIFY` build option (off by default).
2. Unit tests for the wire format (`src/test/mds/TestChangeNotifier.cc`), which
   run in a default build.
3. The Kafka endpoint: a small fire-and-forget librdkafka producer behind the
   endpoint interface.
4. Multi-rank: each active rank emits for the subtrees it owns, messages are
   keyed `mds.<rank>`, and drops are counted by cause (`dropped_queue` vs
   `dropped_endpoint`).
5. TLS/SASL options with file-based secrets.
6. Teuthology coverage: a workunit, a `CephFSTestCase` and a suite entry.
7. Documentation (operator and design), the config reference, and the release
   note.

## Properties (what a reviewer should hold us to)

* The metadata path never blocks and never gates `MDLog::trim()`. There are no
  journal entries, no delivery acks and no retries of our own: a full queue
  drops the event and counts it, and a Kafka outage is invisible to the file
  system.
* Per-rank ordering, no cross-rank ordering.
* At-least-once for operations that are re-executed after a failover (a client
  retry is reported again); bounded, silent loss for what is still in a queue or
  in the endpoint's in-flight buffer when a rank dies. Consumers act
  idempotently on each event, and can bound staleness with `ceph.dir.rctime`, a
  stock vxattr.
* No filtering policy in the producer: dotfiles and application housekeeping
  paths are emitted; filtering is the consumer's job.
* librdkafka is already an optional Ceph dependency (RGW bucket notifications).
  Discovery moves to the top level so both components share one target; no new
  external dependency.

## Measurements from the working branch

Test setup: three VMs, MDS on its own host, mon/OSDs on another, client and
broker on the third; scripts and raw captures available on request.

* Latency: tight A/B, 8 alternating samples of 2,000 creates each, median delta
  -1.0%, i.e. inside the sample-to-sample spread. No measurable cost at ~2,000
  creates/s (~4,000 events/s).
* Throughput: a 20,000-file burst (40,002 events) was accepted and delivered in
  10.4 s with zero drops (~3,850 events/s sustained).
* Drop policy: with the broker stopped and a deliberately small in-flight
  bound, 39,970 of 40,002 events landed on the endpoint drop counter and 0 on
  the MDS queue, and the burst ran in the same time as with a healthy broker:
  the MDS does not slow down when the endpoint refuses.
* Failover: `kill -9` of the active rank mid-workload, 1,200 acknowledged
  creates: 0 lost, 496 duplicate CREATEs (~41%, each about 18 s after its first
  copy, i.e. the client's retry being re-executed), client-visible stall 17.9 s
  on vstart. On the lab, over a real network: takeover in 6 s, workload
  completed, nothing lost.
* Credentials: SASL_SSL with SCRAM-

72440.title: script/ptl-tool: add --subject-branch-history for QA tracker subject
72440.author: yuriw
72440.body:
## Summary

On `--update-qa`, `ptl-tool.py` now records the integration-branch history in the QA tracker **subject**. The newly built branch becomes the subject anchor and the previous branch(es) accumulate, newest-first, in a trailing parenthesized list:

```
wip-yuri-testing-20261006.163134-umbrella (wip-yuri-testing-20261005.175703-umbrella, wip-yuri-testing-20261003.180813-umbrella, wip-yuri-testing-20261002.125630-umbrella)
```

Previously the subject was frozen at the branch used when the tracker was first created, so the sequence of re-runs was only visible by opening the ticket and reading the journal notes. Now the full branch trail is visible at a glance in the tracker list view.

Behavior:
- **Idempotent** — a subject already in `<anchor> (<history>)` form is re-parsed and extended, never nested.
- The trailing `(...)` group is only treated as branch history when every entry matches a ptl branch name, so an arbitrary human subject that happens to end in `(...)` is left intact.
- Re-running with the same branch is a no-op.
- Capped at Redmine's 255-char subject limit by dropping the oldest entries (with a trailing `...`).
- `--create-qa` is unchanged; only the `--update-qa` path sets the subject.

## Test plan

New unit tests in `src/script/test_ptl_tool.py` cover: first update, newest-first accumulation across the real tracker #81324 re-run sequence, idempotent re-parse, same-branch no-op, non-branch parens left intact, and the length cap.

```
$ pytest src/script/test_ptl_tool.py -q
26 passed
```

Add a new `acl_support` configuration option to the share resource. Also add a new `share_defaults` subresource for the cluster and add an `acl_support` option to that, such that you can set the default behavior for all shares in one cluster.

72445.title: treewide: split osd_types.h and trim heavy includes
72445.author: aainscow
72445.body:
Split `src/osd/osd_types.h` (7,221 lines) into ten topical headers, make the rest of the tree include only the pieces it needs, and trim a few other heavy includes. The aim is faster builds, and much faster rebuilds after editing one OSD type.

**This PR is kept as one, as it is, for discussion.** Its commits are arranged so that it can later be split into separate PRs: the mechanical split (commits 1-2), which changes nothing the compiler sees and is checkable with git and coreutils, and the include narrowing and trims (commits 3-10), which is where the compile-time savings come from and where every difference in generated code comes from. Not intended for backport.

## Commits

Mechanical split, could be its own PR:

1. `osd/osd_types.h: reorder into the order of the headers it is split into`: moves blocks of `osd_types.h`, unchanged, into the order of the new headers, and puts each block's includes, and `pg_pool_t`'s forward declaration of `CrushWrapper`, in front of it.
2. `osd: split osd_types.h into topical headers`: cuts the reordered file into `osd_types_{core,stats,pool,peering,op,object,log,client,superblock,scrub}.h` (`#pragma once`). `osd_types.h` keeps its includes and the few OSD-internal leftovers, and includes the new headers in that order, so every user sees the same declarations in the same order.

Include narrowing, could be a second PR:

3. `treewide: include only the osd_types headers that are needed`: about 40 widely included headers include only the pieces they use; sources that relied on the umbrella include what they use.

Smaller trims, one header each, on top of commit 3; they could join the second PR or follow it:

4. `include/interval_set.h: do not include common/dout.h`
5. `common/hobject.h: forward-declare json_spirit::Value`
6. `osdc/Striper.h: forward-declare ObjectExtent`
7. `common/ceph_context.h: include only the cmdmap_t declaration` (new `common/cmdparse_fwd.h`)
8. `common/tracer.h: include span.h instead of provider.h`
9. `include: use boost container forward declarations in denc/encoding/types`
10. `rgw: drop includes rgw_op.h and rgw_rest.h do not use`

## Compile cost

Measured with clang 19, Debug, using main's compile database. Each compile ran as its own process, with main and this branch compiled concurrently on the same machine. Instruction counts (perf, user space) are the stable metric.

| 2282 affected compile entries | main | this PR | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Instructions | 88.7 T | 81.3 T | -8.4% |
| CPU time | 37,100 s | 34,409 s | -7.3% |

That is about 7% of a full build (102 T instructions). All of it comes from commits 3-10: after commits 1-2 alone, `osd_types.h` still includes all ten headers and the build does the same work.

Translation units rebuilt after editing a header:

| Header (example types) | main | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `osd_types_log.h` (`pg_log_entry_t`, `pg_missing_t`) | 1115 | 286 |
| `osd_types_peering.h` (`pg_info_t`, `PastIntervals`) | 1115 | 302 |
| `osd_types_stats.h` (`object_stat_sum_t`, `pg_stat_t`) | 1115 | 405 |
| `osd_types_pool.h` (`pg_pool_t`) | 1115 | 782 |
| `osd_types_core.h` (`pg_t`, `spg_t`, `eversion_t`) | 1115 | 935 |
| `json_spirit_value.h` | 1392 | 756 |
| `hobject.h` | 1160 | 980 |

### Commits 1-2: mechanical split

No judgement calls. The two textual checks need only git and coreutils.

#### The cut (commit 2), with git and coreutils

Replacing each `#include "osd/osd_types_X.h"` line in the new `osd_types.h` with that header, minus its licence block, its `#pragma once` and its includes of the other new headers, gives back commit 1's `osd_types.h`. The only difference is one blank line, the one before the first block, which ends up on both sides of the cut. Run in a checkout:

git show "$A1:src/osd/osd_types.h" > before.h
sed -n "1,18p" before.h > before.h.licence
git show "$A2:src/osd/osd_types.h" |
while IFS= read -r l; do
  case "$l" in
  '#include "os

72446.title: msg: put Linux's AF_INET6 on the wire on FreeBSD and macOS too
72446.author: dvanders
72446.body:
Follow-up to #71445, now merged.

- **test/test_addrs:** the two tests from my #71445 review. They pin the msgr2 AF_INET encoding byte for byte, and check that `entity_addr_t` and `entity_addrvec_t` reject an `elen` one byte too long.
- **msg: AF_INET6 on the wire:** the wire format uses Linux's AF_INET6 (10), but only Windows mapped to it. FreeBSD (28) and macOS (30) sent their own value, which Linux peers don't recognise. Now every platform maps it; on Linux this is a no-op. Two new tests pin the IPv6 encoding.
- **msg: entity_addrvec_t's msgr2 decode** (from @tchaikov's review): `entity_addrvec_t::decode()` had its own copy of the msgr2 address decode, which kept the wire family as is. It now calls the same `decode_after_marker()` as `entity_addr_t::decode()`, and a new test decodes an IPv6 address through it.

On macOS the new tests fail without the fixes and pass with them. @wjwithagen confirmed `unittest_addrs` passes on FreeBSD.

72451.title: mgr/cephadm: run one OSD create per host at a time
72451.author: tchaikov
72451.body:
"orch daemon add osd" runs `create_from_spec(force_apply=True)` while the serve loop may be applying an OSD spec to the same host. The first daemon add makes this likely, since `create_osds()` saves `osd.default` and kicks the serve loop just before its own create. On a v20.2.3 cluster the two "ceph-volume lvm batch" runs started 8 ms apart on the same disk, and the mgr deployed the OSD twice. Which run wins is down to timing, so the result is not reproducible. Later adds can race the same way with osd.default or osd.all-available-devices.

Keep the set of hosts with an OSD create in flight in `OSDService`. `create_osds()` reserves its hosts before saving the spec and holds them until its create returns, waiting if another create runs there. The serve loop does not wait. It skips a reserved host without recording the apply, so `osdspec_needs_apply()` still asks for it, and it is kicked when the host is released. By then the disk is in use, so ceph-volume skips it and exits 0. A `threading.Condition` guards the set, which the mgr command threads share with the cephadm event loop. The set lives only in memory; after an mgr failover the serve loop applies osd.default again and deploys any OSD that was prepared but not deployed, as before.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81505

72452.title: rgw/kmip: add socket I/O timeout for KMIP connections
72452.author: supriti
72452.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81490

Adds rgw_crypt_kmip_socket_io_timeout_sec (0-300 s, default 0 = no
timeout) to set SO_RCVTIMEO/SO_SNDTIMEO on KMIP connections, so a KMIP
server that stops answering no longer blocks requests indefinitely.

A connection that may be out of step (I/O failure, undecodable or
mismatched reply) is now closed instead of reused, so a late reply
can't be read by the next request.

Tested with a proxy holding PyKMIP's reply: unset waits as before;
with 5 s the request fails after ~5.7 s and the next request succeeds
on a new connection.

72453.title: python-common: keep per-path crush_device_class in DeviceSelection.to_json()
72453.author: tchaikov
72453.body:
6c6cb2f5130 let a `DeviceSelection` path carry its own `crush_device_class`, but `to_json()` still writes only the path strings. So "ceph orch ls --export" never shows the class, and cephadm's SpecStore, which persists specs with `to_json()`, loses it at the next mgr restart. An OSD created from the spec after that, e.g. one replaced with "ceph orch osd rm --replace", gets the spec level class or the one the OSD detects itself, and CRUSH rules for the intended class no longer pick it.

Write a path that has a class as the dict from_json() accepts, and keep the others as plain strings, so specs without per-path classes serialize as before.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81605

72454.title: tentacle: qa/cephadm: fix test_set_mon_crush_locations test
72454.author: kginonredhat
72454.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74523

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67436
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74523

## Summary

`task/test_set_mon_crush_locations` fails because it still requires `mon dump --format json` to report `crush_location` as the string `{datacenter=a}`.

`mon: add time_added to mon_info_t` (`c5239a4c46d` on tentacle) switched `MonMap::dump()` over to `mon_info_t::dump()`. That encodes the crush-location map with `encode_json`, so JSON now looks like:

```json
"crush_location": [{"key": "datacenter", "val": "a"}]
```

`jq` then compares that array to the string `{datacenter=a}` and exits 1, even when the location was applied. Plain `ceph mon dump` still prints `{datacenter=a}`. The sample in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67436 is a mon whose location was set correctly and would still fail the old check.

This is a clean `git cherry-pick -x` of 456eb5d2f65. It only updates the workunit to look up `crush_location[].key` and `.val`. No daemon or mgr code changes.

Umbrella already contains 456eb5d2f65. Squid has the same mismatch after its own `time_added` backport (`48ecc59c530`) and is updated in a separate PR.

## Test plan

- [ ] `rados/cephadm` workunit `task/test_set_mon_crush_locations` passes on tentacle
- [ ] `ceph mon dump --format json` shows `crush_location` key `datacenter` / val `a` for mon.a, and the rack entries for mon.b and mon.c

72465.title: mgr/cephadm: reconfigure NFS daemons on placement change
72465.author: Shubhaj1810
72465.body:
## Description

NFS daemons were not updating `CEPH_NODES_LIST` when NFS service placement changed.

The placement-derived Ceph node IPs were not part of the NFS daemon dependencies, so existing daemons did not enter the reconfiguration path after placement changes. Only newly deployed daemons received the updated node list.

This change:

- tracks resolved Ceph node IPs in NFS dependencies
- detects placement-only changes
- updates `ganesha.conf` through the normal reconfiguration path
- sends `SIGHUP` to `ganesha.nfsd` instead of restarting the container when `ceph_nodes` is the only changed dependency
- preserves the existing redeploy behavior for stronger dependency changes

## Before

NFS was initially deployed on `ceph-node-00` and `ceph-node-01`:

```text
nfs.nfs-cluster1.0.0.ceph-node-00
nfs.nfs-cluster1.1.0.ceph-node-01
```

Both daemons had:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101;
}
```

After adding `ceph-node-02` to the placement, the new daemon received:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101, 192.168.100.102;
}
```

while the existing daemons continued to contain only:

```text
192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101
```

and required redeployment to obtain the updated configuration.

## After

With the fix applied, placement was expanded from:

```text
ceph-node-00
ceph-node-01
```

to:

```text
ceph-node-00
ceph-node-01
ceph-node-02
```

The existing daemon container IDs remained unchanged:

```text
ceph-node-00 → 28bb2c8ca26b
ceph-node-01 → 2efa2f239426
```

and a new daemon was created on `ceph-node-02`:

```text
ceph-node-02 → f2ea1b78cd5f
```

All three daemons received the updated configuration:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101, 192.168.100.102;
}
```

This was verified on the existing daemons and the newly deployed daemon.  

Placement was then shrunk back to `ceph-node-00` and `ceph-node-01`. The `ceph-node-02` daemon was removed, while the existing daemon container IDs remained unchanged. 

The remaining daemons correctly received:

```text
CEPH_NODES_LIST {
    Ceph_Nodes = 192.168.100.100, 192.168.100.101;
}
```

Also validated manually on a live 3-node cluster:

- initial 2-node NFS deployment
- placement expansion 2 → 3
- existing daemon reconfiguration without redeployment
- placement shrink 3 → 2
- existing daemon reconfiguration without redeployment

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81517
Signed-off-by: Shubha Jain [SHUBHA.JAIN1@ibm.com]

72470.title: rgw: reject unrecognized query params in s3 requests
72470.author: cbodley
72470.body:
s3 uses query parameters to represent "subresources" and routes those requests to different rest apis. rgw supports lots of these subresources, but not all of them - and aws continues to add more

rgw does this routing in RGWOp factory functions like RGWHandler_REST_Bucket_S3::op_put(), where we check query parameters for the subresources we support, then fall back to the default resource like RGWCreateBucket_ObjStore_S3

the risk of this strategy is that requests for subresources we don't support get incorrectly mapped to the default bucket/object resource. this can result in data loss when a PUT request falls back to PutObject and overwrites an existing object, or when a DELETE request falls back to DeleteBucket and removes a bucket prematurely

to mitigate this risk, both for current subresources that we don't support and for subresources added to aws in the future, we can't fall back to the default resource if the request conains any unrecognized query parameters

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80921

<details>

72472.title: mgr: do not abort or pin PG stats on corrupted daemon reports
72472.author: lumir-sliva
72472.body:
A daemon can send the mgr a message that decodes fine at the messenger level but carries garbage inside. In the tracker below, one host corrupts msgr2 secure-mode payloads in whole 16-byte AES blocks, which still pass GCM, so the mgr gets well-formed MPGStats / MMgrOpen / MMgrReport with bogus contents. Two things in the mgr turn that into a cluster-wide problem:

- `DaemonServer::handle_open()` and `handle_report()` decode the config blob, and `handle_report()` the packed perf counters, without catching `buffer::error`. One corrupted MMgrOpen aborts the mgr in `ms_dispatch`; the daemon reconnects to the next mgr and can take that one down too.
- `ClusterState::ingest_pgstats()` skips reports older than what it holds. One corrupted `pg_stat_t` with a huge `reported_epoch:reported_seq` makes every later genuine report look older, so the PG sits in a garbage state (`stale+creating+...+snaptrim_error`) until the mgr fails over, while its primary reports `active+clean`.

This series:
- decodes the config before touching any daemon state, and drops the session when it or the perf counters don't decode: mark the connection down and forget it in `osd_cons` / `daemon_connections` (a local `mark_down()` doesn't go through `ms_handle_reset()`). The daemon reconnects and resends;
- ignores a `pg_stat_t` whose `reported_epoch` is beyond the epoch of the MPGStats carrying it, i.e. beyond the sender's own osdmap;
- lets a newer report from the OSD that sent the stored stats replace them even if the stored pair is higher. Only primaries report and one OSD's reports arrive in order, so that covers a corrupted `reported_seq`. Late reports from a previous primary are still skipped;
- adds unit tests for both cases and for the late-report case, in a separate commit so the fixes pick cleanly to squid and tentacle, which don't have `test_clusterstate.cc`.

Testing:
- `unittest_mgr_clusterstate`: the two new pin tests fail on main, 12/12 pass with the series.
- vstart on main, with one OSD's `EVP_EncryptUpdate` interposed to corrupt the odd 16-byte block before encryption. Without the series the mgr aborted 17 times in 8 minutes in `handle_open`, and a PG was pinned within a minute until `ceph mgr fail`. With it, 10 minutes of the same load gave no abort and no pinned PG; the mgr log shows `dropping session ... cannot decode its config`, `... but the osd is at e64, ignoring` and `had 1.32 from osd.0 at 64:44466389293371572, taking its 64:185`.

Not covered here: a garbage metric type in MMgrReport still hits `ceph_abort()` in `UnknownMetricPayload`'s DENC. I'll send that separately.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68550

72473.title: mgr: fail decoding an unknown metric type instead of aborting
72473.author: lumir-sliva
72473.body:
MetricReportMessage (in MMgrReport, decoded by the mgr) and MetricConfigMessage (in MMgrConfigure, decoded by OSDs and MDSs) turn a type they don't know into `UnknownMetricPayload` / `UnknownConfigPayload`, whose decoder calls `ceph_abort()`. Senders only encode types the peer supports (`should_encode()`), so an unknown type only shows up when the message got corrupted, and then a single message takes down the mgr, or an OSD or MDS.

The decoders now throw `buffer::malformed_input` for an unknown type. `decode_message()` handles that like any other malformed message: the messenger drops it and resets the connection, and the daemon's mgr session reconnects (the mgr resends MMgrConfigure on open).

Follow-up to #72472 (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68550): one host there corrupts msgr2 secure-mode payloads in 16-byte blocks that still pass GCM, which is how this decode path came up.

Testing: the new `unittest_mgr_metrictypes` garbles the type field of an encoded report and config message. On main the binary aborts at `MetricTypes.h:85` / `:259`; with this change both decodes throw `malformed_input`. `ceph-mgr` and `ceph-osd` build.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82867

72480.title: os/bluestore/Writer: don't leave reused released space marked unused
72480.author: ming1
72480.body:
With `bluestore_write_v2=true`, a deferred write may reuse space released earlier in the same transaction, while the rest of that AU stays marked unused. A later small write there goes direct, and an older deferred write still queued for the same disk bytes then overwrites it: the object fails its csum after an OSD restart.

Mark only freshly allocated space unused, so writes into a reused AU are deferred too and queued after the older one. The unit test reproduces the csum error with write_v2 and passes with the fix.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80982

72490.title: os/bluestore: reserve bdev label copies added by online expand
72490.author: ming1
72490.body:
An online expand (`bluefs-bdev-expand` on a running OSD) writes bdev label copies into the new space but gives the whole new range to the allocator. Object data can then be allocated over a label copy, and the next label write corrupts it. Give the new range to the allocator without the label blocks.

With bitmap based allocators that is not enough: `BitmapAllocator::expand()` already marks the new space free without accounting for it, so the label blocks stay allocatable, and the hybrid allocator ends up with the new space free twice after a spillover. Leave the new space allocated in `expand()`; callers free it with `init_add_free()`.

Unit tests cover bitmap and hybrid expand; the online expand test runs with the avl, bitmap, hybrid and hybrid_btree2 allocators.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80951

72502.title: qa/rados: reduce osd dispatch delay injection probability to 1%
72502.author: aainscow
72502.body:
`msgr-failures/osd-dispatch-delay` sets `osd_debug_inject_dispatch_delay_probability` to 0.1 with a 0.1 s duration. As well as `ms_fast_dispatch`, the delay is injected twice per item in `ShardedOpWQ::_process()` (`OSD.cc`, before and after `pg->lock()`), so every op queue item pays an expected 20 ms sleep. That includes client ops, sub-op replies, peering events and `NullEvt`s.

The compression objectstore facets limit OSDs to 1 shard × 2 threads (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72879). Combined with the injection, that caps each OSD at about 95 queue items/s.

## What goes wrong

pggrow thrashing on wide EC pools pushes arrivals past that cap:
- every map epoch queues a `NullEvt` to each of the 80–170 PGs on an OSD, and the thrasher toggles `noscrub`/`nodeep-scrub` about every 2 s, each toggle being an epoch;
- pool splits add bursts of notifies.

Peering events are served strictly ahead of client work (WPQ strict queue, mClock immediate class), so the backlog never drains. Client ops and EC sub-read replies then starve for more than 10 minutes.

Evidence from the debug-20 logs of two failures in one QA batch:
- **Runs:** `skanta-2026-10-03_10:12:06-rados-wip-bharath19-testing-20261002.123021-main-distro-default-trial/604392` (read, WPQ) and `…/603575` (write, mClock).
- **Throughput:** about 95 items/s, all of it peering class, for 11–13 minutes, with no client items dequeued in that window.
- **Backlog:** peaked at 6,000–6,700 items, about a minute of queue wait per item.
- **Worker time:** 99.6% in the injected sleep, with about 0.05 ms of real work per item.
- **Model check:** a fixed-capacity model fed only with the measured arrivals reproduces the measured backlog to within about 5%.

## History

Before `rados_osd_op_timeout` was set (#71861), this showed up as `wait_for_recovery` timeouts (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75216). Across all k=10 m=4 thrash-erasure-code jobs on trial200 from January to October 2026:

| dispatch-delay | compression=yes | jobs | `wait_for_recovery` failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| no | no | 60 | 0% |
| no | yes | 61 | 3% |
| yes | no | 72 | 0% |
| yes | yes | 159 | 49% |

With the client timeout it now shows up as `ceph_test_rados` `-ETIMEDOUT` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81135).

## This change

Lower the probability to 0.01. Replaying the measured arrivals from both runs against the capacity implied by 1% gives:
- about 580–720 items/s of capacity;
- 24–35% utilisation at the worst 10 s burst;
- no backlog.

The perturbation still happens, at roughly 2 sleeps/s per OSD at 100 items/s. This file also feeds `rados/thrash` and the other `thrash-erasure-code*` suites through their `msgr-failures` symlinks.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81629

72503.title: osd/OSDMap: skip calc_pg_upmaps when an up OSD has no weight
72503.author: aainscow
72503.body:
The mgr balancer in upmap mode can abort ceph-mgr with
`OSDMap.cc: FAILED ceph_assert(osd_weight.count(oid))` in `OSDMap::calc_deviations()`
(https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/48896). This happens when CRUSH maps a PG to an OSD
whose CRUSH weight is 0.

**How it happens.** straw2 returns the first item of a bucket when every item in it has
weight 0. The chosen leaf is then checked only against the OSD's reweight (in/out), not
its CRUSH weight. Take a rule with several `take` steps, such as the legacy stretch-mode
rule `take site1; chooseleaf ...; emit; take site2; chooseleaf ...; emit`. If every OSD
of one site is crush-reweighted to 0 while it is still in, the first OSD of that site
goes into every up set. `build_pool_pgs_info()` counts the PGs on that OSD, but
`get_osds_weight()` leaves the OSD out of the weight map. The other site keeps
`osd_weight_total` above 0, so the existing early return does not fire, and
`calc_deviations()` asserts. With one OSD per `take`, the PGs stay full size and
active+clean, so the balancer aborts the active mgr on every run. The same core shows up
now and then in `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-uneven-crush-weights.sh`, which
sets both OSDs of one zone to CRUSH weight 0.

**When it can happen.** Zero CRUSH weight alone is not enough. Adding OSDs at weight 0, or draining an OSD or a host, does not trigger it with the rules Ceph creates (`take default` followed by `chooseleaf` over hosts): straw2 never picks a zero-weight item while any sibling has weight. It also needs a manually created CRUSH rule whose `take` reaches only zero-weight items. Examples are a rule with one `take` per site (as written for stretch clusters) while a whole site is crush-reweighted to 0 but still in, or, from reading straw2 but not tested, a device-class rule whose class has only zero-weight OSDs.

**Fix.** `calc_pg_upmaps()` logs an error and returns without changes when an OSD in an
up set has no weight under the pool's rule. Upmaps cannot move those PGs to a weighted
OSD in the same subtree. `total_pgs` also counts the copies on the unweighted OSD, so
the targets for the rest of the pool would be wrong too. The mgr balancer and
`osdmaptool --upmap` call `calc_pg_upmaps()` for one pool at a time, so other pools are
still balanced.

**Relation to https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/53736** (closed without merging). That
PR kept zero-weight OSDs in the weight map. As its author found while writing a test,
this only moves the abort to `ceph_assert(target > 0)`: a zero weight gives a zero
target, and `calc_deviations()` divides by the target. He also could not find how a
zero-weight OSD gets into an up set, so there was no reproducer. This PR leaves the
weight map and both asserts as they are. Instead it skips the pool when its mapping does
not follow its weights, and the new unit test reproduces the trigger.

One commit, `osd/OSDMap: skip calc_pg_upmaps when an up OSD has no weight`, with the fix and
`OSDMapTest.BUG_48896`. The test builds a two-datacenter rule with one `take` per datacenter, sets
both OSDs of dc-0 to CRUSH weight 0 (still in), and checks that every PG still maps to osd.0. It
then runs `calc_pg_upmaps()` and checks that no PG is upmapped to a zero-weight OSD.

Testing (Debug build):
- `unittest_osdmap --gtest_filter=OSDMapTest.BUG_48896` without the `OSDMap.cc` change aborts with
  `FAILED ceph_assert(osd_weight.count(oid))` in `calc_deviations()`. With the fix it
  passes.
- Full `unittest_osdmap` with the fix: all 46 tests pass. Only the new test reaches the new
  early return.

72504.title: mon: fix use-after-free of MonSession in handle_auth_request
72504.author: aainscow
72504.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81565



Monitor::handle_auth_request()'s new-session branch hands the only reference to a freshly created
MonSession to the connection (con->set_priv(RefCountedPtr{s, false})) and then keeps using the bare
`s` pointer (start_session, the session dout, the later s->authenticated check and
ms_handle_fast_authentication).

handle_auth_request runs on an msgr-worker thread with the connection lock dropped
(ProtocolV2::_handle_auth_request). When the monitor shuts down (Monitor::shutdown ->
messenger->shutdown -> mark_down_all), a connection that is still authenticating is stopped from
the shutdown thread and its reset is delivered on the dispatch thread. Monitor::ms_handle_reset()
then drops the connection's reference and returns early because the monitor is shutting down,
which destroys the MonSession and its auth_handler. ms_handle_reset never takes auth_lock, and it
drops the reference before taking any lock, so nothing serialises the free against the concurrent
handle_auth_request. The worker then uses the freed session and auth_handler in start_session.

This was seen once as a ceph-mon SIGSEGV 12 ms after SIGTERM in msgr-worker, with the faulting PC
in the heap (a call through a freed object), in a teuthology run of
rados:thrash-erasure-code-stretch.

The more-input branch of the same function already holds the reference in a function-scope
RefCountedPtr and bails if it is null ("this can happen if the async ms_handle_reset event races
with the unlocked call into handle_auth_request"); the new-session branch did not. The fix keeps a
reference across the whole window there too.

How it was confirmed: a temporary local check (not included here) that aborted the mon whenever
the connection was the only owner of the new session right after set_priv fired on the first
client authentication without this change, and never with it (3 runs each). The mon unit tests
(config_map, moncap, monmap, pgmap, montypes, election, monmap_monitor) pass.

72507.title: mgr/devicehealth: give each serve pass its own db retry budget
72507.author: lumir-sliva
72507.body:
devicehealth fails with "Module 'devicehealth' has failed: disk I/O error" (or "unknown operation") every few days on long-running mgrs, and only a mgr failover clears it.

`MgrModuleRecoverDB` reopens the database up to `MAX_DBCLEANUP_RETRIES` (3) times when the wrapped call raises `sqlite3.DatabaseError`, which is what libcephsqlite raises once its lock renewal fails or its client is blocklisted, e.g. after the `.mgr` PG was unavailable for longer than `cephsqlite_lock_renewal_timeout`. devicehealth applied the decorator to `_do_serve()`, the loop that runs for the whole life of the module, while the retry count only lives as long as one call of the wrapped function. So the module could recover from three lost databases per mgr activation, however far apart, and the fourth failed it for good.

This moves the loop body into `_serve_once()` and decorates that instead, so the budget covers consecutive failures within one pass. A database that stays unusable still fails the module after 3 reopens.

Reproduced on vstart by repeatedly blocklisting the mgr's libcephsqlite client (`ceph mgr dump` -> `active_clients`), with `mgr/devicehealth/sleep_interval 2` and `scrape_frequency 4` so the module writes every few seconds:

```
main:
loss 1: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/2004544131, errors caught: 1, module running
loss 2: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/1237131041, errors caught: 2, module running
loss 3: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/1461716975, errors caught: 3, module running
loss 4: blocklisted libcephsqlite client 10.162.0.2:0/2254942036, errors caught: 4, Module 'devicehealth' has failed: disk I/O error

with this change:
loss 1 ... loss 10: module running; scraping continues afterwards
```

The new unit test fails without the change (`OperationalError: disk I/O error` on the 4th spaced failure) and passes with it.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72958

72508.title: rgw/compression: use compression type fixed at multipart upload init
72508.author: kchheda3
72508.body:
If the placement target's compression type changes (e.g. `radosgw-admin zone placement modify --compression ...` followed by a period commit) while a multipart upload is in progress, parts uploaded before the change are stored with the old compression type and later parts with the new one. CompleteMultipartUpload rejects the mix with `InvalidPart`, so a server-side config change breaks client uploads.

This resolves the compression type once at InitiateMultipartUpload and stores it in `multipart_upload_info`, the same way the checksum type is already handled. Every UploadPart (including UploadPartCopy) then uses the stored type instead of the live placement config.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79629

72522.title: tools/contrib: sync upmap-remapped.py with cernceph/ceph-scripts
72522.author: dvanders
72522.body:
Bring `src/tools/contrib/upmap-remapped.py` up to date with `tools/upmap/upmap-remapped.py` of [cernceph/ceph-scripts](https://github.com/cernceph/ceph-scripts) at f08c004d102e ([cernceph/ceph-scripts#51](https://github.com/cernceph/ceph-scripts/pull/51)). The file here is a straight copy of that version.

The fix that matters most: on erasure-coded pools the old ordering loop never terminates when the mappings form a cycle longer than two (e.g. `0->2, 2->7, 7->0`), which a pg split or new hardware can produce. The script then spins at 100% CPU and prints nothing. The new code emits the mappings as ordered chains and leaves cycles out, so those pgs stay remapped and backfill.

Checked by running `gen_upmap` from both versions on these EC cases:

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 3-cycle `0->2, 2->7, 7->0` | hangs | `[]` |
| cycle plus a chain | hangs | the chain, in order |
| 2-way swap | `[]` | `[]` |
| chain `1->2, 2->3` | `[(2, 3), (1, 2)]` | `[(2, 3), (1, 2)]` |

The rest of that series is error handling and cleanup: replicated pools never map onto an osd already in the up set, degraded+remapped pgs with mismatched set lengths are skipped instead of failing an assert, unknown pools are skipped, mon commands get a timeout and their failures are reported, argparse, and the librados connection is closed on every exit. The output format (the `ceph osd pg-upmap-items` lines and the peering waits) is unchanged.

72534.title: mgr/cephadm: seed OSD ok-to-stop with the OSDs still pending upgrade
72534.author: FredNass
72534.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81587

## Problem

When upgrading OSDs, cephadm runs `osd ok-to-stop <id> --max N` with a single OSD (N = `mgr/cephadm/max_parallel_osd_upgrades`) and upgrades the OSDs it gets back. The mgr grows that set in `DaemonServer::_maximize_ok_to_stop_set()` by walking up the CRUSH tree and adding sibling OSDs in ascending id order, without knowing which of them already run the target version.

After the first pass, the batch is therefore made of the requested OSD plus the lowest-numbered OSDs under the same parent, which are already upgraded. On a host with 40 OSDs and N=16, the first pass upgrades osd.0-15 and every following pass a single OSD: **25 passes instead of 3**.

## Fix

Seed `osd ok-to-stop` with the OSDs on the same host that still need to be upgraded, capped at `max_parallel_osd_upgrades`, so the batch the mgr returns is made of OSDs that actually need upgrading. If that set cannot be stopped together, drop OSDs from the end and retry, down to the single OSD cephadm used to request (no shrinking on `-EAGAIN`, where a smaller set would not help). PG safety is still decided by the mgr.

This only changes the default (non CRUSH bucket scoped) upgrade path.

## Tests

New unit tests in `src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/tests/test_upgrade.py`, with a fake `osd ok-to-stop` mimicking `_maximize_ok_to_stop_set()`:
- 40 OSDs / N=16 → 3 passes (`[0-15]`, `[16-31]`, `[32-39]`)
- `max_parallel_osd_upgrades` is respected
- the seed shrinks until the set is ok to stop
- batches stay on one host
- peer selection skips other hosts, non-OSDs, the OSD itself and OSDs already on the target image
- no shrink on `-EAGAIN`

72537.title: crimson/os/seastore,osd: report the real reason mkfs could not create a device
72537.author: ronen-fr
72537.body:
check_create_device() mapped every creation failure except EEXIST to input_output_error, and OSD::mkfs() turned that into ceph_abort(). An ENOSPC - the common case, since a seastore OSD creates one device file per cache and data device under the same mount point - surfaced as a SIGABRT, a core dump and the single line:

  OSD::mkfs error creating empty object store in /var/lib/ceph/osd/ceph-0: \
    Input/output error

Keep the condition instead: map ENOSPC, EACCES/EPERM and ENOENT to the matching errors (adding enospc to Device::access_ertr so it reaches the OSD), and on ENOSPC log the requested size against the space actually available. Have OSD::mkfs log and throw rather than abort, so mkfs exits non-zero instead of dumping core.

Also remove the partially created device file on failure: the open is exclusive|create, so a leftover file makes the next mkfs take the EEXIST "already exists" path and succeed with a device that was never fully allocated.

72541.title: .github/workflows: check permissions of pusher instead of PR author and don't run on reopen
72541.author: bluikko
72541.body:
Don't change CI approval labels if pusher has write permission to the repo.

When someone with a write access to the repository pushes into a PR authored by someone with no write access, the already added `ci-approved` label is removed and `needs-ci-approval` is readded.

If someone else than the PR author pushed to the PR, permission level of the pusher should be checked (probably) instead of the PR author.

To keep the bot 404 log message correct, test that the PR author is the pusher. In case author was not the pusher, fall back to the generic error log message.

Don't run on type reopened because GitHub does not allow reopening a PR on a branch that was pushed to while the PR was closed. Takes care of similar label reset problem when user with write permissions reopened a PR authored by someone with no write permission.

Assisted-by: Claude Sonnet 5

72544.title: osd/SnapMapper: stop rescanning purged_snaps per mapping key
72544.author: Antek74
72544.body:
`Scrubber::run()` opened a fresh `omap_iterate` over `purged_snaps`,
from its start, for every mapping key: `O(M*P)`.  On snapshot-heavy
OSDs this pinned a core for days.

Collect the `purged_snaps` rows once up front, sort them numerically by
(pool, begin), and merge overlapping and adjacent rows of one pool
into disjoint ranges. Then each mapping key needs only one binary
search: `O(M log P)` instead of `O(M*P)`.

The numeric sort also fixes missed strays: with pools ordered as
decimal strings, the old walk could stop at a pool-20 row and never
reach pool 3.

The sort is needed because the on-disk key order is not numeric in
the pool: the pool id is a decimal string, so pool 20 sorts before
pool 3. The merge is needed because the writer can leave rows that
overlap or touch: `record_purged_snaps()` merges a new interval only
with rows already on disk, so intervals carried in one call do not
see each other. Once the ranges are disjoint and sorted, the last
row that starts at or before the snap is the only one that can
cover it.

Adds `unittest_scrubber_run`, a unit test for `Scrubber::run()`: it
builds a SnapMapper over a MemStore and fills it through the same
writer methods ceph-osd uses (`record_purged_snaps()`, `add_oid()`),
then checks every stray the scrub reports.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81592
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81798
