72552.title: LRC: Store the layer plugin in the EC profile
72552.author: jamiepryde
72552.body:
### Problem
PR #58052 changed the default LRC layer plugin from jerasure to isa. For k/m/l-type LRC profiles, and explicit-layer LRC profiles that don't specify a plugin, the per-layer plugin is not stored in the profile (this was by design). It is re-derived when the plugin is initialized using the default on each OSD. This means that any pre-tentacle cluster that upgrades to tentacle or later will have its LRC pools silently switch from using jerasure to isa. Jerasure and isa produce the same first coding chunk using XOR, but subsequent coding chunks differ.

### Fix
Record the layer plugin explicitly in the LRC profile using a new layer-plugin key. This is resolved:
* on the OSD at runtime in build_pg_backend() during the upgrade window, before require_osd_release is committed. The tentacle OSD will continue using jerasure for a pre-tentacle LRC pool.
* in the mon when require-osd-release is committed in encode_pending(). 
* in the mon at profile creation (in both the normalize_profile() and the default EC profile paths).
The new key is a per-profile default. If a layer already has a plugin specified then that will continue to be used. If the key is absent, the default remains isa.

### Limitation
Clusters that have already upgraded to tentacle or later with pre-tentacle LRC profiles / pools cannot be automatically repaired. This fix only protects clusters that have not already upgraded.

### Testing
* New unit tests added to TestErasureCodeLrc to test setting layer-plugin.
* Mocked upgrade testing on a vstart cluster. Testing using the mon_debug_no_require_* flags to pin require_osd_release at squid, and fixed and unfixed versions of the OSD and mon. Daemons were swapped in place to simulate the upgrade. Checked that upgrading to unfixed tentacle hits the bug. Checked that upgrading to the fix stores jerasure as the layer-plugin for an existing LRC profile that does not have layer-plugin set.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81369

72554.title: cls/rgw: fix duplicate CURRENT null versions in versioning-suspended buckets
72554.author: k-keshava
72554.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81603

Problem

In a bucket with versioning suspended, concurrent PUT and DELETE (no version id) on the same key corrupt the bucket index. ListObjectVersions returns many VersionId=null entries with IsLatest=true, and "radosgw-admin bi list" shows leftover versioned list entries (<key>\0v<epoch>\0i, empty instance) that still carry FLAG_CURRENT. Running the same requests one at a time never triggers it.

On a vstart cluster with 8 concurrent clients x 200 PUT+DELETE iterations, main ends up with 6-14 list entries flagged CURRENT for one key, and v20.2.4 with 27 (350+ under heavier contention).

Root cause

Confirmed with debug_objclass=20 OSD logs, following one leaked entry from creation to orphaning.

1. Orphaned list entry. A null version's instance entry key (\x801000_<key>\0i) is reused by every null generation, and its versioned_epoch is the only way to find its list entry. When rgw_bucket_complete_op() removes that instance entry (a DEL, or a CANCEL after a racing delete marked it non-existent), only the instance entry is removed. prepare_op() then recreates it with versioned_epoch=0, so the next link_olh() computes the list key from epoch 0, misses the real one, and the old list entry stays with FLAG_CURRENT set.

   Observed sequence: PUT link_olh writes the list entry (CURRENT) -> a late complete_op DEL sets exists=false -> complete_op CANCEL removes the instance entry -> prepare_op recreates it with epoch 0 -> the next link_olh unlinks <key>\0v915\0i (which doesn't exist), orphaning the entry.

2. Version marker overwritten. When versions are listed, RGW sends dir_suggest_changes for the orphaned null entries. rgw_dir_suggest_changes() builds the key with encode_obj_index_key(), which for an empty instance is the plain <key>, so it overwrites the version marker. After that, read_key_entry() resolves null-version operations to the plain entry, and every later write leaks another list entry.

Changes

- cls/rgw: remove list entry together with its versioned instance entry. A new remove_key_entry() removes a versioned instance entry's list entry along with it. It is used by the CANCEL and DEL removal paths in rgw_bucket_complete_op(), and does nothing if the list entry is already gone. get_list_index_key() now takes a const reference.
- cls/rgw: dir_suggest_changes must not overwrite a version marker. Suggestions whose on-disk entry is a version marker are skipped.
- test/cls_rgw: regression tests.
  - index_null_version_racing_remove replays the sequence above at the cls level and checks that exactly one list entry stays CURRENT.
  - index_suggest_version_marker sends update and remove suggestions for a null version and checks that the marker survives.

Testing

Run on a vstart cluster (Ubuntu 24.04 arm64):

- New unit tests: fail without the fix (2 CURRENT entries; marker flags 8 -> 3), pass with it.
- ceph_test_cls_rgw (full suite, replicated + EC): 44/44 pass with the fix.
- ceph_test_cls_rgw_stats: passes with the fix.
- End-to-end reproducer (boto3; versioning suspended; 4-16 concurrent clients doing PUT+DELETE): without the fix, 6-14 CURRENT entries and the marker overwritten; with the fix, exactly 1 CURRENT entry and the marker intact, across 6 rounds.

With debug logging on, one 8x200 round hit the race 8 times, and the new code removed the list entry each time, so the clean results come from the fix actually running.

The same patch was also verified on v20.2.4 (tentacle). It applies there with only small test adjustments: the older TEST_F fixture, and an increasing olh_epoch, because there link_olh takes the epoch from RGW. Both tests fail on stock 20.2.4 and pass with the fix, the full suite passes, and the reproducer is clean (27 -> 1 CURRENT).

Notes for reviewers

- The fix restores the index invariant that a versioned instance entry and its list entry are removed together. I didn't change the RGW-side ordering that lets a la

72555.title: mon: preserve log acknowledgements and release rejected requests
72555.author: yulongshi0816
72555.body:
The unconditional no_reply() in preprocess_log() introduced by 56cb53db96380c917f4192c31cbdd0f0f3ef1fe9 releases a forwarded request before its log entries are committed. The later MLogAck is then dropped by the peon because the routed request no longer exists, leaving the client log queue untrimmed.

Restore the preprocessing flow so new log entries retain their routed request until _updated_log() sends the acknowledgement. Call no_reply() in prepare_log() when rejecting an MLog with a mismatched fsid, so the peon can release the routed request on the path that originally leaked.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81604
Related PR: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/61933

72556.title: common/io_exerciser: start Seq15 at its first stage
72556.author: aainscow
72556.body:
Seq15's `stage` member in `src/common/io_exerciser/IoSequence.h` has no initializer and the constructor does not set it, so a new Seq15 starts at whatever stage the reused heap memory holds. In a long `ceph_test_rados_io_sequence --parallel 4` run, one object's Seq15 issued `Create`, `Barrier`, `Swap`, `Truncate` and aborted:

```
src/common/io_exerciser/ObjectModel.cc: 153: FAILED ceph_assert(primary_created)
```

It started at `SWAP_TO_PRIMARY`, swapped to the secondary object it had never created and truncated it. Starting at `WRITE_SECONDARY`, `COPY_FROM_SECONDARY` or `READ_SECONDARY` also aborts, and the other stages skip part of the sequence.

Initialise `stage` to `WRITE_PRIMARY`. valgrind reports the uninitialised read in `Seq15::_next()` on a `--dryrun` of Seq15 without the fix, and no errors on a dry run of every sequence with it.

`Seq15IgnoresPriorMemoryContents`, added to `unittest_io_sequence` from #72383, builds a Seq15 in zeroed memory and one in memory that holds `SWAP_TO_PRIMARY`, and expects the same ops from both. Without the fix the second one runs `Create`, `Barrier`, `Swap`, `Truncate`; with it both run the full sequence.

Depends on #72383: this branch is stacked on it, and only the last two commits belong to this PR.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81606

72563.title: rgw: graceful, bounded and staggered realm reload on period commit
72563.author: RaminNietzsche
72563.body:
`radosgw-admin period update --commit` makes every gateway in the realm reload its configuration. The reload pauses the Beast frontend, and that pause is disruptive in three ways:

- By default, `AsioFrontend::pause()` closes all connections, so in-flight requests fail.
- With `rgw_graceful_stop=true` it waits for outstanding requests with no limit, so one slow transfer can stall the reload.
- All gateways reload at the same moment, so gateways behind one load balancer pause together.

This PR builds on the crash fixes from #68920 and #69713. Defaults are unchanged.

- **rgw/beast:** add `rgw_realm_reload_pause_timeout` (default 30s, 0 = no limit).
  - When `rgw_graceful_stop=true`, the pause waits at most this long, then closes the remaining connections like the non-graceful path does.
  - The logic lives in `rgw::asio::lock_or_close_on_timeout()` so that it can be unit tested.
- **rgw:** add `rgw_realm_reload_max_delay` (default 0).
  - `RGWRealmReloader::handle_notify()` schedules the reload after a random delay in `[0, max]`.
  - A reload blocked on a bad configuration is still woken up immediately.
- **test:** unit tests for the bounded pause, and a multisite test that reads a large object slowly across a period commit with `rgw_graceful_stop=true`.
- **doc:** document `rgw_graceful_stop` and the new options in the config reference and the multisite guide, plus a `PendingReleaseNotes` entry.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81524

## Testing

- `unittest_rgw_asio_frontend_connection`: 4 tests, `--gtest_repeat=50`, all passed.
- Multisite with `test_multi.py` and vstart, 2 zones with 2 gateways each:

| Run | Config | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_period_update_commit` | defaults | passed |
| `test_period_update_commit` | `rgw_graceful_stop=true`, timeout 5s | passed |
| `test_period_update_commit` | as above, plus `rgw_realm_reload_max_delay=5` | passed; reloads spread between 1.1s and 4.9s |
| `test_period_commit_graceful_inflight` | as written: graceful, timeout 60s | passed; 64 MiB read completed across the reload |
| `test_period_commit_graceful_inflight` | `rgw_graceful_stop=false` | failed as expected: `IncompleteRead` after 11 MB |
| `test_period_commit_graceful_inflight` | graceful, timeout 2s | failed as expected; gateway log below |

```
00:55:12.019 frontend waiting up to 2s for outstanding requests to complete...
00:55:14.019 frontend outstanding requests did not complete within 2s, closed remaining connections
```

72579.title: rgw/dedup: fix dedup races with copy and delete
72579.author: benhanokh
72579.body:
Dedup modifies manifest on target object while keeping target object ref_tag and mtime intact (since logically they are the same).
This can race with Delete passing obsolete manifest to GC and Server-Side-Copy overwriting copy-target manifest.
 
 The same change was used on both cases - when preparing the operation (which includes read object MD, manifest etc) cache shared-manifest existence (boolean state). If it exits the object is part of a dedup chain already and won't be modified again by dedup so can continue like before.
 If shared-manifest state is false (the vast majority of the objects) then when removing head (DELETE) or setting new manifest (SS-Copy) add an atomic check that shared-manifest is still false (which means dedup didn't touch this object).
On failure (very rare as this is a race condition) retry operation from the top.

Dedup code was verifying TGT object state based on ref_tag and ETAG, which is probably enough today, but to be on the safe side it now also verifies mtime was not not modified.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80901

72581.title: crimson: shard-aware client op routing
72581.author: mohit84
72581.body:
Problem: A Crimson OSD runs N reactors and every PG lives on one of them. A client connection is accepted on whichever reactor `connection_distribution` picks, so an op whose PG lives elsewhere costs a cross-core hop (`submit_to`) to the PG's reactor and another for the reply. With fewer client connections than reactors
(a few heavy clients), roughly (N-1)/N of ops pay this.

Solution: A shard-aware client sends each op on a connection that the OSD accepted on the
reactor owning the op's PG, so the op is dispatched and served locally.

72582.title: test/osd: EC fixture fixes and tests for omap recovery
72582.author: aainscow
72582.body:
Tests for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81630 (Fast EC: omap update lost on a shard recovered while the PG is only peered), and three fixes to the EC peering test fixture that the tests need.

### Commits

- `test/osd: roll the peering fixture's PG log through the PG's backend`: `MockPeeringListener::get_log_handler()` handed `PeeringState` a log handler on the `MockPGBackend`, whose `ec_get_sinfo()` has k=0, so rolling forward an entry with an EC omap update divided by zero in `Trimmer::ec_omap()`. The PG's IO backend is now used, as in `PrimaryLogPG`.
- `test/osd: name recovery temp objects in MockPGBackendListener`: `get_temp_recovery_object()` returned an empty `hobject_t`, so every recovery that needs more than one push wrote its temp object as MIN.
- `test/osd: queue only the PeeringCtx transaction in prepare_write`: `MockPeeringListener::prepare_write()` also queued transactions that the caller queues itself, so the recovery push transaction in `recover_got()` was applied twice and the second pass removed the object the first had just renamed into place.
- `test/osd: add omap helpers to PGBackendTestFixture`: `write_omap()` sets and removes omap keys in one op; `get_shard_omap_keys()` reads one shard's ObjectStore omap.
- `test/osd: test EC omap removal across shard failure and recovery`: `TestECOmapRecovery` in `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`, for every optimized EC config with omap enabled. Keys are removed while a parity shard or the primary is down, then the shard is recovered.
- `test/osd: test EC omap recovery of the primary while the PG is peered`: the reproducer. Keys are set and removed while the primary is down; the primary comes back to a PG that can only peer (min_size raised to k+m, one more shard down), is recovered there, and the PG then goes active.
- `test/osd: roll EC omap test writes forward as an OSD does`: the fixture advances `pg_committed_to` on write commit only when `enable_log_trimming` is set, so the tests' later writes did not roll earlier entries forward; the entries were only applied when the PG activated. `TestECOmapRecovery` now sets it. The results are unchanged.

### Results on main (b8d62f134cb)

| test | result |
|---|---|
| `RemoveKeysWhileShardDownThenRecover` | passes, 10/10 configs |
| `RemoveKeysWhilePrimaryDownThenRecover` | passes, 10/10 configs |
| `SetKeysWhilePrimaryDownThenRecoverWhilePeered` | fails, 8/8 configs with m >= 2 (skipped for k=2 m=1) |

In the failing test the primary's shard ends with the old omap (keys a..e) instead of c, d, e, x, y; the other primary-capable shards are correct. 72586.title: mds: keep projected_version in sync when a dirfrag goes bad
72586.author: vshankar
72586.body:
When a dirfrag object is missing or its fnode header is corrupt, CDir::go_bad() marks the (non-fatally) damaged dirfrag complete and gives it a synthetic fnode with version 1 via reset_fnode(), leaving projected_version at 0. If that dirfrag is later part of a subtree being exported, Migrator::encode_export_dir() trips

  ceph_assert(dir->get_projected_version() == dir->get_version())

This is the same issue that was fixed for unlinked dirs in commit fcdee486697 ("mds: fix crash when exporting unlinked dir"), which introduced CDir::set_fresh_fnode(), but go_bad() was not converted. Use set_fresh_fnode() there too, which also handles the REJOINUNDEF state for a dirfrag opened during rejoin.

72600.body:
Hosts registered by FQDN get a crash daemon id of the short hostname (`crash.node1`), while the mgr creates the cephx key as `client.crash.<fqdn>`. 72611.title: mds: drop dirty_old_rstats of purged old inodes
72611.author: xiubli
72611.body:
With `mds_snap_rstat` enabled, the MDS can segfault while propagating the rstats of a stray directory:

```
 *** Caught signal (Segmentation fault) **
 in thread mds-log-trim
 2: (MDCache::project_rstat_inode_to_frag(...)+0x32e)
 3: (CDir::assimilate_dirty_rstat_inodes(...)+0x10e)
 4: (CInode::finish_scatter_gather_update(int, ...)+0x1c2e)
 5: (Locker::scatter_writebehind(ScatterLock*)+0x467)
 6: (Locker::scatter_nudge(ScatterLock*, MDSContext*, bool)+0x567)
 7: (LogSegment::try_to_expire(...)+0xb16)
 8: (MDLog::try_expire(...)+0x66)
 9: (MDLog::trim()+0x5b5)
```

The standby that takes over crashes the same way.  It is hit by `qa/tasks/cephfs/volumes/test_clone_stats.py`, which sets `mds_snap_rstat=true`.

### Root cause

1. The stray dirs live in the global snaprealm, so once any snapshot has been taken, `cow_old_inode()` cows an old inode for them.  As the rstat of that old inode is not fully accounted, its snapid is also recorded in `dirty_old_rstats`.
2. Committing the `~mdsN` dirfrag calls `CInode::purge_stale_snap_data()` on the stray dir.  No snapshot covers the old inode, so it is purged, but its `dirty_old_rstats` entry is left behind.
3. The next nest scatter of `~mdsN` runs `project_rstat_inode_to_frag()`, which does `cur->get_old_inodes()->at(p)` for each `dirty_old_rstats` entry.  `old_inodes` is now null, so the MDS crashes.  If only some of the old inodes had been purged, `at()` would throw `std::out_of_range` instead.

### Fix

Drop the `dirty_old_rstats` entries of the old inodes that `purge_stale_snap_data()` purges.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81672

72614.title: qa/cephfs: really drop the generic kernel spec from the job yaml
72614.author: ronen-fr
72614.body:
3-kernel.yaml exists so that a run scheduled with "-k <branch>" does not
install that kernel on every node: only the kclient facets (k-testing,
k-stock) are supposed to reinstate it, for the client roles alone. It has
never actually worked.

The script empties the kernel dict, but after all postmerge scripts have
run the scheduler calls

    update_key('sha1', parsed_yaml, self.base_config)

(teuthology/suite/run.py), and update_key() recurses into every nested dict
the two have in common (teuthology/misc.py). The emptied "kernel" mapping is
still a dict, so it gets the kernel sha1 put right back. A bare sha1 is all
Teuthology's kernel task needs to fetch and install a kernel, so the job ends
up doing exactly what this fragment is meant to prevent.

Remove the whole mapping once it has been emptied, leaving update_key()
nothing to recurse into. Jobs that do want a client kernel still carry
kernel.client from k-testing/k-stock, so their dict is not empty and is kept.
Only done for a custom kernel: with "-k distro" (the default) the re-injected
"sha1: distro" is what we want on all nodes, so that case is unchanged.

72615.title: build(deps): add krb5-devel/libkrb5-dev for make check (gssapi wheel build)
72615.author: senolcolak
72615.body:
## Fixes

Building Ceph with `make check` fails during `install-deps.sh`:
the bucket notification tests bring in the Python `gssapi` package
(`gssapi>=1.8.0`) via `src/test/rgw/bucket_notification/requirements.txt`,
which `install-deps.sh` pip-installs into the `install-deps-python3`
virtualenv (`preload_wheels_for_tox`).

The `gssapi` source distribution builds a non-pure-Python wheel and
needs `krb5-config`, which is provided only by the Kerberos development
packages. When they are missing, pip fails with:

```
/bin/sh: line 1: krb5-config: command not found
subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command 'krb5-config --libs gssapi' returned non-zero exit status 127.
```

This regression was exposed by commit
[803f698200edd784e3eaab86cb18aeee05b1a5ed](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/commit/803f698200edd784e3eaab86cb18aeee05b1a5ed),
which added `gssapi` to the bucket-notification test requirements.

Related: [tracker #80240](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80240) and
[#71519](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71519), which proposed the
Debian/Ubuntu dependency. This PR retains that fix under the
`pkg.ceph.check` profile and adds the corresponding RPM dependency.

## Changes

- **ceph.spec.in**: add `BuildRequires: krb5-devel` to the `make check`
  dependencies for Fedora/RHEL/openEuler (this is picked up by
  `dnf builddep` in `install-deps.sh` when `FOR_MAKE_CHECK=1`).
- **debian/control**: add `libkrb5-dev <pkg.ceph.check>` to `Build-Depends`
  so Debian/Ubuntu `make check` builds get the same dependency.

`krb5-devel`/`libkrb5-dev` are only pulled in for `make check` builds,
matching the existing pattern used for other test-only dependencies.

## How tested

Reproduced the failure on a CentOS 9 (el9) host: `./install-deps.sh`
failed while building the `gssapi` wheel because `krb5-config` was
missing. Installing `dnf install krb5-devel` resolves it; this PR makes
the dependency declared so `install-deps.sh` installs it automatically.

72616.title: rgw/s3vectors: return a distinct error when the backing bucket is missing
72616.author: jiaweien
72616.body:
With the rgw s3vector backend, LanceDB stores the vector data in a regular S3 bucket with the same name as the vector bucket (see the "Backing Buckets" section of doc/radosgw/s3vectors.rst). When that bucket is missing - either it was never created before `CreateVectorBucket`, or it was deleted after the vector bucket was created - every vector operation that requires the backend fails with a bare 404 "NoSuchKey", identical to the response for a vector bucket that does not exist. `ListIndexes` additionally returns a misleading empty list while `GetVectorBucket` still reports the bucket as healthy.

This change maps such failures, at the operation layer, to a dedicated 404 "VectorBucketBackendNotFound" error with an actionable message, by verifying the existence of the backing bucket when an operation fails with `-ENOENT`. The plain "NoSuchKey" behavior for a vector bucket or an index that does not exist, and the empty index listing of a vector bucket without a backend, are kept unchanged.

**Before:**
```json
{"Code": "NoSuchKey", "Message": ""}
```

**After:**
```json
{"Code": "VectorBucketBackendNotFound", "Message": "backing S3 bucket 'my-vectors' does not exist; recreate it via the S3 API"}
```

(verified on a live 21.3.0 deployment; the outputs above are actual responses)

Notes:
- `ListIndexes` intentionally keeps its existing semantics (200 + empty index list for a vector bucket without a backend), so that a vector bucket without a backend can still be deleted.
- PR #72143 changed the semantics of duplicate `CreateVectorBucket` requests; this change is orthogonal: it addresses the error reporting of operations failing because the backing bucket is missing.
- Improvement to an unreleased feature; no backports apply since s3vectors has not been part of any release.

72620.title: cmake: select the linker with CMAKE_LINKER_TYPE
72620.author: Doracly
72620.body:
## Summary

`-DCMAKE_LINKER_TYPE=BFD|LLD|MOLD` selects the linker and makes lld usable. Of
the three, lld links Ceph fastest and with the least CPU and memory (numbers
below). It replaces `WITH_MOLD`, which is in no release and is removed rather
than deprecated.

The linker is passed as `-fuse-ld`, as CMake honours `CMAKE_LINKER_TYPE` itself
only from 3.29 on.

The last two commits group the build speed-ups in the developer guide under one
section and document the option there, ahead of ccache: it needs only a package
and costs neither disk space nor memory. The grouping commit is identical to the
one in #71901, so the two PRs merge cleanly in either order.

## Fixes to the mold support from #69711

- mold drops the base-version symvers in `librados_c.cc`, so a mold-linked
  librados exported `rados_connect` and friends as `LIBRADOS_PRIVATE` and lost
  the four compat definitions; lld rejects them outright. librados now always
  links with ld.bfd where it uses symvers.
- That, not `--exclude-libs`, is what hid `rados_*` under mold, so the
  workaround that disabled `--exclude-libs` for mold is dropped.
- The `rados_*`/`_rados_*` globs added to `librados.map` made every build,
  including ld.bfd ones, export the 250 internal `_rados_*` functions behind the
  C API. A separate commit removes them, restoring the previous export list.

## `--copy-dt-needed-entries` in the libcephfs and fs tests

#71494 passes the option only where `check_linker_flag()` accepts it. That caches its result, so a tree configured with ld.bfd keeps passing the option after switching to lld or mold, which reject it. The first commit checks with `try_compile()` instead, which reruns on each configure.

## Testing

Clang 21 + lld (with crimson) and GCC 15 + mold, Debug, before the rebase onto #71494:

- `all` builds; every binary and library loads with all symbols resolved
  (`ldd -r`), apart from plugins that take symbols from their host
- librados exports match ld.bfd (`rados_*` versions unchanged, no `_rados_*`)
- vstart cluster: `HEALTH_OK`, rados put/get, rbd create, Python `rados`,
  `rbd`, `cephfs` and `rgw` import, `ceph-dencoder list_types`
- all `unittest_*`: 252/252 passed with both
- configure: default, `BFD`, `LLD`, `MOLD`, unusable linker

After the rebase: configuring one tree with `BFD`, then `LLD`, then `BFD` again passes `--copy-dt-needed-entries` to 10, 0 and 10 targets.
With mold, `ceph-dencoder` additionally needs #71814.
Not tested: CMake < 3.29.

## Link performance

Clang Debug (`-O0`), idle 24-thread machine, outputs on tmpfs, the default 13
parallel links:

| linker      | 62 vstart binaries (2.5 GiB) | 336 test binaries (15.4 GiB) | CPU (tests) | peak heap (tests) |
|-------------|------------------------------|------------------------------|-------------|-------------------|
| ld.bfd 2.46 | 10.7 s                       | 50 s                         | 768 s       | 13.5 GiB          |
| lld 21.1.8  | 1.8 s                        | 11 s                         | 236 s       | 1.7 GiB           |
| mold 2.40.4 | 2.1 s                        | 24 s                         | 565 s       | 5.4 GiB           |

mold is faster only one link at a time (the vstart set in sequence: mold 5.4 s,
lld 7.0 s, ld.bfd 46 s) and is CPU-bound from four parallel links on.
lld 17 to 21 perform the same. With `-Og` objects all three link faster
(ld.bfd about 2x).

72621.title: mgr/dashboard: rgw: expose LIST and DELETE rate limits in dashboard backend API
72621.author: pujaoshahu
72621.body: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f286b44-9785-4c2d-8c2a-28a0c4dced9c Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81695 Signed-off-by: pujaoshahu Summary: The backend change lets the dashboard API save RGW's dedicated LIST and DELETE rate limits. RGW already stores max_list_ops and max_delete_ops; the dashboard could read them, but a rate-limit update never sent them to radosgw-admin. RgwRateLimit.set_rateLimit() used to call ratelimit set with only the four older limits: read ops, write ops, read bytes, and write bytes. The user and bucket PUT endpoints (/api/rgw/user/{uid}/ratelimit and /api/rgw/bucket/{uid}/ratelimit) now accept max_list_ops and max_delete_ops (default 0, which means unlimited) and pass them through as --max-list-ops and --max-delete-ops. 72642.title: squid: cephfs_mirror: fix incremental sync after directory rename
72642.author: lumir-sliva
72642.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81279

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70757
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78910

this backport was staged manually

Both commits needed a hand resolution, the logic is unchanged:

- The fix. Main's SnapDiffSync::get_entry() was reworked by the datasync thread series (it queues files and creates remote directories itself); squid's still returns every entry to do_synchronize(). The same block goes in front of init_directory() here: stat the path in the previous snapshot, traverse in full if it is absent there, purge the remote and traverse in full if it changed type or inode. Squid already turns pic into sync_check=false, so files below such a directory are copied whole, as on main.
- The test. Squid has no setup_mount_b() and its check_peer_status_idle() does not retry, so the secondary mount is set up inline and sync_and_verify() waits 30s after each snapshot, like the other squid tests.

Besides the silent loss in #78910, the same snapdiff of a moved directory can fail outright on squid: if a subdirectory inside it was renamed or removed between the two snapshots, the client stats the old entry with a HEAD-relative path (#<dir-ino>/<old-name>), gets ENOENT, and the dir_root fails on every retry with "readdir_snapdiff error: (2) No such file or directory". This was hit on a 19.2.5 cluster. The full traversal avoids the snapdiff for such directories, so it fixes that too.

Tested on a vstart cluster built from v19.2.5, with and without the fix commit (src/tools/cephfs_mirror is the same in v19.2.5 and squid), using a standalone reproducer with the qa test's three scenarios plus a moved directory with renamed subdirectories:

| scenario | v19.2.5 | v19.2.5 + fix |
|---|---|---|
| same-parent rename (`mv dirB dirB-renamed`) | `dirB-renamed/sub/deeper/unchanged` missing on the remote | synced |
| cross-parent move (`mv d1/X d2/Y`) | `d2/Y/sub/deeper/unchanged` missing on the remote | synced |
| same-name replacement (`rm -rf replace/B; mv replace/A replace/B`) | not isolated (same run, earlier misses carry over) | synced, stale `old-only` removed |
| moved dir with renamed subdirectories, cold client cache | sync fails: `readdir_snapdiff error: (2) No such file or directory` | "is absent from the previous snapshot; using full traversal", synced |

The ported qa test also passes locally with vstart_runner.py on the same build (`Ran 1 test in 239s, OK`) and fails without the fix at the first rename step (`sync_and_verify('snap1', 2)` -> `verify_snapshot`: source and remote snapshot differ).

Squid is EOL soon, so it'd be great to squeeze this into the last squid release if there's still room. Squid users with mirrored directories that get renamed lose data on the backup without any error until then.

72643.title: mon,osd,osdc: EC stretch cluster (stretch pools with num_zones)
72643.author: aainscow
72643.body:
This PR lets a pool, replicated or erasure coded, be stretched over `num_zones` zones (CRUSH buckets, `datacenter` by default). Each zone holds a full copy of the data, `replica` copies of a replicated pool or a whole set of k+m shards of an erasure coded pool, and `min_size` applies to each zone. In this release a pool has one or two zones, and an erasure coded pool over two zones must be FastEC (`allow_ec_optimizations`). `ceph mon enable_stretch_mode` and `disable_stretch_mode` now change every pool as `ceph osd pool set <pool> num_zones` does; individual stretch pools (`ceph osd pool stretch set`) are kept for clusters with more than two zones.

- Feature tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82982. The test results attached there list every test run for these PRs, with its status and evidence, and the tests still to run.
- Design: `doc/dev/osd_internals/erasure_coding/ec_stretch_cluster.rst`, which says for each part whether it is in this release or a later one.
- User documentation: `doc/rados` (`stretch-mode.rst` and `pools.rst`); upgrade notes in `PendingReleaseNotes`.
- Tests: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72644, based on this PR. The two PRs go in together.

### Dependencies
Depends-on: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/68773

Until it merges, it is carried as the three `PREREQ:` commits at the start of this PR.

### Commits
After the `PREREQ:` copies come 25 commits, one per subject, building the feature up. Each commit's author is the author of most of its lines, and everyone who contributed lines to a commit has a Signed-off-by on it. Some monitor commits do not compile on their own; the PR as a whole builds and its tests pass. `FIXUP:` commits at the end name the commit they will be squashed into. The PR is functionally frozen: fixes found now go to separate pull requests, each with a tracker.

### Known issues
- Feature bit 54 (`OSD_STRETCH_ZONES`), OSDMap flag bit 24 (`stretch_zones`) and `pg_pool_t` version 34 are not reserved on main. https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69112 (pool migration) also takes version 34.
- The design puts these in this release, but they are not implemented yet: a dense EC direct read that hits a media error returns EIO instead of going to the primary (fixed by https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72292, which is not carried here), and some of the inter-zone statistics (per pool, the dashboard, `osd pool stats` and the local/remote read ratio).
- FastEC deep scrub checks a stripe from the shards' CRCs, which reach only the first (XOR) parity shard. So with m >= 2 a corrupt later parity shard is not detected, as on main. In a pool over zones the two copies then differ, and nothing says which is good, so the scrubber reports both and repair rebuilds both.
- On main, a client's Objecter can keep its previous `crush_location` after a run-time change, depending on the order in which the config observers run. The librados zone tests here move their client between datacenters, so they can fail intermittently until that fix is merged.

### Follow-ups
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82959 Umbrella compatibility: require one client feature, pool migration and incompatible clients, the upgrade commit after a backport, and Umbrella clients' split reads.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82960 show an erasure coded pool's settings in `ceph osd pool ls detail`.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82973 cancel an upmap that crowds a replicated PG over zones into one zone.

72644.title: qa: EC stretch cluster tests and suites
72644.author: aainscow
72644.body:
This is the QA half of the EC stretch cluster work (stretchy-C, https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67879). It needs the code half, https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72643, so the two go in together. This PR changes only `qa/`.

### Reading the commits
The commits before this PR's own are the code PR, https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72643, with its `PREREQ:` copies of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/68773; it describes them. This PR's own commits are the ones that change only `qa/`, after the code PR's last commit:
- The story commits, below.
- `FIXUP:` commits from review and testing, each naming the story commit that it is to be squashed into before merge. Approved FIXUPs are squashed into their story commits. Where several FIXUPs of one story commit still await review, they are combined into one whose message lists them in order.

Each commit's author is the author of most of its lines; every contributor will be credited in the Signed-off-by lines.

### The story
One commit per subject. The fixes and tests added while testing this split, and the fixes from earlier reviews, are squashed into the commit of their subject; newer ones are the `FIXUP:` commits on top.

- qa/tasks: create pools over zones in teuthology
- qa/suites/rados: add zone maps to EC thrash
- qa/standalone/crush: test stretch rules and pools over zones
- qa/standalone: test pools over zones, pool defaults and stretch mode
- qa: add stretch mode teuthology tests for erasure coded pools
- qa: add stretch_zone_thrash and the thrash-erasure-code-stretch suite
- qa/suites/rados/upgrade: check stretch pool fields after an upgrade
- qa: add thrash-stretch suite for stretched replica pool zone thrashing
- qa/suites/upgrade: stretch upgrades from Tentacle, with a zone lost before the commit

The `.qa` links of the new suite directories are in the commits that create the directories.

The upgrade suites commit with `require-osd-release vampire`, the release at which the code PR converts the stretch pools. The umbrella-x and the new tentacle-x suites check the pool fields across that commit; tentacle-x/stretch-zone-loss also runs a client load through a zone loss before the commit and commits while the zone is down.

### Testing
These standalone suites pass, run one at a time on a GCC Debug build of this branch's code: all 24 in `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/`, plus `crush/crush-stretch.sh`, `mon/osd-pool-create.sh` and `mon/osd-erasure-code-profile.sh`. The last run also covered the new `TEST_commit_warns_of_unconverted_pools` and `mon/misc.sh`; it was on code without three later code FIXUPs (`osd pool set replica` with an OSD failure domain, the raw used rate of EC pools over zones, and the dashboard and osdmaptool flag lists).

Teuthology, on an earlier push: `upgrade/umbrella-x` 2az and 3az passed. The three `upgrade/tentacle-x` jobs failed on bugs in the suites, fixed by a FIXUP that is now squashed into the tentacle-x story commit: the stretch suites lacked `upgrade_ignorelist_health.yaml`, and a `;` in an `echo` of stretch-zone-loss stopped that job at the first zone loss. A rerun on 2026-10-29 passed all three. With this branch's QA FIXUPs, rados/singleton's `mon-stretch-ec-pool` passed 3 of 3: https://pulpito.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-11-02_11:16:48-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-stretch-poolmig-qa-261030-distro-default-smithi/

Every QA FIXUP is now squashed into its story commit, on Callum's "good to merge everything"; a FIXUP whose lines a later story owns went into that story. The last push changed no file.

### Known issues (not fixed here)
- rados/singleton's `stretch-ec-mode-5-mons-8-osds` cannot pass as written: its profile has the host failure domain with 2 hosts in each zone.
- The thrash suites have not been run in teuthology.
- Main's `TEST_stretch_set_ec_pool` in `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-commands.sh` (from https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72416) expects the refusal message that the code PR changes. This PR's version of the test replaces

72645.title: RGW Posix - Escape '.' in object names
72645.author: dang
72645.body:
'.' is usually not a problem for object names, but a few specific cases can cause problems:  The single names "." and ".." can cause path problems, and we use ".<namespace>" internally to reprecent namespaces.

To avoid these issues, always escape '.' in addition to '/' for PosixDriver.

To accomplish this, add a new "path_encode()" equivalent to "url_encode()" that should safely escape everything dangerous in POSIX paths.  If anything is missed, it can be added in the future, and be automatically picked up.

72646.title: mgr/cephadm: complete filtered orch upgrades without cluster-wide gate
72646.author: kginonredhat
72646.body:
## Summary

Fixes a hang in **staggered / filtered** `ceph orch upgrade` steps (`--daemon-types`, `--services`, `--hosts`, `--limit`) where `ceph orch upgrade status` stayed `in_progress: true` indefinitely even after the filtered daemons were on the target image.

Root cause (seen in Teuthology job **614344** on `wip-rkachach-testing-2026-10-07-1110`):

1. `_do_upgrade()` still upgraded **monitoring stack** daemons (e.g. grafana) when the CLI filter was **`--daemon-types mgr`** only.
2. `_mark_upgrade_complete()` always required **all** mon/mgr/OSD/mds daemons cluster-wide before clearing upgrade state, so scoped steps never finished (`Cannot mark complete` loop).

Signed-off-by: Kobi Ginon <kginon@redhat.com>

## Failure context (Pulpito 614344)

| Item | Link |

72651.title: osd: serve an EC direct read only from this shard's own data
72651.author: aainscow
72651.body:
Each shard of an EC split read gets the same ro extent and works out its own data within it.
`ECBackend::extent_to_shard_extent()` got this wrong for a single-chunk extent of another shard: it gave
this shard's chunk in the same or the next stripe, so the OSD replied success with data from another
offset of the object, or with a short or empty buffer when that position is past the end of the shard's
object.

Clients without the fix for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80836 (#72016) send such reads: an op whose
reads are each within one chunk, in chunks of different data shards, goes whole to the shard of the
first read. These are clients built from main since #66459 and the v21.0.1, v21.1.0, v21.1.1,
v21.1.2 and v21.3.0 tags.

- test/osd: `TestBackendBasics.DirectReadOfOtherShardsChunk` reads half of each chunk of a two-stripe
  object from every data shard; it fails before the next commit.
- osd: `extent_to_shard_extent()` returns only this shard's data within the extent, with zero length
  when there is none, through the new `stripe_info_t::ro_range_to_shard_range()`.
  `ECUtil.ro_range_to_shard_range` checks it against `ro_range_to_shard_extent_set()`.
- osd: `PrimaryLogPG::do_op` replies -EINVAL to an EC direct read op with a READ/SPARSE_READ extent that
  holds none of the shard's data. Such an op is a client bug: failing it shows the bug, where having
  the client resend it to the primary would hide it. Clients without the 80836 fix get -EINVAL for these
  ops rather than wrong data. Reads from fixed clients and from the split path always include the
  shard's own data, so they are not affected. `PGBackend::check_direct_read()` makes the check. The
  backend test harness's new `direct_read()` applies it as `do_op` does, and
  `TestBackendBasics.DirectReadRefusedForOtherShardsData` checks that reads of other shards' chunks,
  a zero-length read and the op of such a client get -EINVAL.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81736

Tested: full build including tests (clang, Debug, -Werror). `unittest_backend_basics`: 1048 passed;
`DirectReadOfOtherShardsChunk` fails in all 80 optimized EC configurations without the fix, and
`DirectReadRefusedForOtherShardsData` fails in all 80 if the guard replies -EAGAIN.
`unittest_ecutil`, `unittest_ecbackend`, `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering`, `unittest_ec_omap_journal`,
`unittest_ec_transaction`, `unittest_ec_with_crush`, `unittest_osd_types`, `unittest_peeringstate`,
`unittest_pglog`, `unittest_scrubber_be`, `unittest_split_ops_ut` pass. Not yet run on a cluster.

72652.title: [DNM] rgw/s3vectors: test lancedb-c#69 (C API on runtime worker threads)
72652.author: aaltshuler
72652.body:
**Do not merge.** This is the validation PR @yuvalif asked for in https://github.com/lancedb/lancedb-c/pull/69#issuecomment-5571046583: RGW built against lancedb-c#69, with the `lancedb_run_on_stack()` calls removed, so the change can be tested with a real client before #69 merges.

With lancedb-c#69, every C API call runs its async work on the lancedb-c runtime's worker threads (8 MiB stacks by default) and the caller only blocks until it completes, so RGW no longer needs to grow the coroutine stack around LanceDB calls. #69 removes `lancedb_run_on_stack()` and the `stacker` dependency.

## Changes

- `src/rgw/lancedb-c` submodule: `a4ac1c0` → `11e8072` (#69 head; it also brings in the explain-plan FFI already on lancedb-c `main`). `.gitmodules` points at the `aaltshuler/lancedb-c` fork, because `11e8072` is not on an upstream branch yet. Both revert to upstream once #69 merges.
- `src/rgw/rgw_s3vector.cc`: `create_index`, `remove_indexes`, `create_vector_bucket` and `put_vectors` call their `*_impl` functions directly.
- `src/rgw/Cargo.lock`: removes `stacker` and the three packages only it used (`psm`, `ar_archive_writer`, `object`). Generated with `cargo update --workspace`, no other changes.

## Testing

Not built locally; I'm relying on `make check` for the build and the existing unit tests. Neither `unittest_rgw_s3vector` nor `unittest_rgw_lancedb_store` calls these four operations, so the real check is the `rgw/s3vectors` teuthology suite. Could you schedule it on this branch?

One thing to watch under load: `lancedb-rgw-store` calls into SAL synchronously inside its async `ObjectStore` methods. With #69 those calls run on the runtime's worker threads (one per CPU by default), so concurrent object-store I/O from LanceDB is bounded by the worker count. RGW does not call `lancedb_runtime_configure()` here, so it gets the defaults.

72653.title: tools/bluestore: force discard when explicitly trimming free space
72653.author: YiteGu
72653.body:
The trim command in ceph-bluestore-tool calls try_discard() with async=false when iterating over free extents in the BlueStore and BlueFS allocators. This selects synchronous discard, but does not bypass the bdev_enable_discard configuration setting.

Since bdev_enable_discard defaults to false, explicitly invoking trim on a discard-capable device can iterate over all free extents without issuing any discard requests. The command nevertheless reports "trim done". This defeats the intended use case of performing an offline trim while leaving discard disabled during normal OSD operation.

Pass force=true to try_discard() in both BlueStore::trim_free_space() and BlueFS::trim_free_space(). This allows explicit trim requests for the main block device and dedicated DB/WAL devices to bypass the online discard configuration setting while retaining synchronous execution and the device discard capability checks.

The change does not modify the process configuration, persistent configuration, or the behavior of normal online discard operations. Existing handling of underlying discard errors remains unchanged.

72659.title: crimson/os/seastore: return from operator<< for all enum values
72659.author: tchaikov
72659.body:
GCC warns about operator<<() for write_policy_t and backend_type_t, because neither switch has a default:
```
  seastore_types.cc:1236:1: warning: control reaches end of non-void function [-Wreturn-type]
  seastore_types.cc:1297:1: warning: control reaches end of non-void function [-Wreturn-type]
```
`write_policy_t` only exists in memory, so a value outside its two enumerators would be a bug. End that printer with `std::unreachable()`.

backend_type_t is decoded from device_spec_t on disk, so a corrupted or newer superblock can hold a value we don't know. Print it as invalid, like the placement_hint_t printer does, instead of running into undefined behavior while logging it.

72665.title: os/bluestore: don't relocate misreferenced extents onto false-free blocks
72665.author: ming1
72665.body:
fsck repair relocates misreferenced extents into space from an allocator built from the freelist, before it checks the freelist against the blocks in use. With a bitmap freelist that also has false-free blocks, the relocation can pick a block another object still uses and overwrite its data; the false-free fix then allocates the same block again and the freelist toggles it back to free.

Before relocating, take every block fsck found in use out of the allocator, so the relocation only gets truly free space. The unit test injects both corruptions, repairs, and checks the victim object and a clean fsck.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81430

72666.title: osd: revert #70377 "Set projected_size to current_size on cache invalidate."
72666.author: aainscow
72666.body:
Reverts #70377 (a970eae8efa, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78465).

With that change, `ECExtentCache::Object::invalidate()` replays from `current_size`, so a rollback replayed behind another op re-adds the rolled-back data as a growth hole in `do_not_read`. Writes queued behind the rollback then skip reading that data and zero-fill the parts of their pages they do not overwrite (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81611).

The tentacle backport is reverted by #72650. Reverting on main too keeps the two branches the same, so the replacement fix backports cleanly.

The first commit disables the three tests from #70371 that were written against the reverted change (`CloneInvalidateStaleSize`, `TruncateGrowWithSuspendedReads`, `RollbackInvalidateRealistic`): without it the extent cache test fails and the two backend tests hit `ceph_assert(reads_sent)`, which aborts the rest of `unittest_backend_basics`. A follow-up PR re-enables them with the replacement fix.

The replacement fix, with a description of the whole problem, is tracked in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81754.

72668.title: crimson/os/seastore/omap: check only live log keys in the trim walk
72668.author: shraddhaag
72668.body:
## Problem Primary OSD asks for a replica's `pg_query_t::LOG` since X. While building the dup list from the replica's pglog entries older than X, the OSD aborts. It asserts as the oldest pglog entry version is less than what is expected by the OSD's pglog. And so it asserts with `ceph_assert(i->version > other.tail)`. Why is there a mismatch between what the OSD expects the pglog to be and what it really is? When a client write comes along with a trim to a replica, the OSD trims the pglog in the memory heap and requests the same from seastore. Due to a bug in seastore's `remove_kvs`, it does not mark those entries as removed on disk. A divergence is created between the in memory pglog and the one on disk. The problem only becomes noticeable when the OSD is restarted and the pglog is loaded from disk and doesn't match what the OSD expects. Initially it only results in a `log bound mismatch` log but ultimately results in an assert when the primary requests for `pg_query_t::LOG` since pglog version X.
Full RCA for https://pulpito.ceph.com/xuxuehan-2026-04-27_04:29:46-crimson-rados:thrash-wip-new-128-distro-debug-trial/179259/ There is a peering request for PG 3.a from primary OSD.0 to OSD.1 asking for `pg_query_t::LOG` since `50'0`: ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,188 [shard 0:main] ms - [0x7c36b01e0840 osd.1(cluster) v2:10.20.193.125:6805/2658048002@51993 >> osd.0 v2:10.20.193.125:6802/1684756780] <== #17,14 === pg_query2(3.a 3.a query(log 50'0 ec=19/19 lis/c=49/45 les/c/f=50/46/0 sis=53 epoch_sent 53) e53/53) v1 (131) ``` In the replica OSD.1, `PeeringState::fulfill_log` is triggered to build the reply: ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - pg_epoch 53 pg[3.a( v 50'80 (46'71,50'80] local-lis/les=49/50 n=23 ec=19/19 lis/c=49/45 les/c/f=50/46/0 sis=53) [0,2,1] r=2 lpr=53 pi=[45,53)/1 (log bound mismatch, actual=[34'38,50'80]) crt=50'80 lcod 0'0 unknown NOTIFY PeeringState::fulfill_log log request from 0 DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - pg_epoch 53 pg[3.a( v 50'80 (46'71,50'80] local-lis/les=49/50 n=23 ec=19/19 lis/c=49/45 les/c/f=50/46/0 sis=53) [0,2,1] r=2 lpr=53 pi=[45,53)/1 (log bound mismatch, actual=[34'38,50'80]) crt=50'80 lcod 0'0 unknown NOTIFY PeeringState::fulfill_log sending info+missing+log since 50'0 ``` Notice the `pg[3.a( v 50'80 (46'71,50'80]` and `(log bound mismatch, actual=[34'38,50'80])`. This means OSD.1 expects the pglog to start from beyond the tail `46'71`, but we see that the actual pglog is `[34'38,50'80]`, ie it starts way before the expected `46'71`. `PeeringState::fulfill_log` invokes `copy_after`, which is responsible for building the reply with log entries since `50'0` and dups (pg's complete dup list + pg log entries that are less than `50'0` also get added as dups). ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - copy_after v 50'0 dups.size()=0 other.dups.size()=71 ``` In the reply, the only pglog entry greater than `50'0` is `50'80`, which gets added. Then `_handle_dups` is invoked to build the dup list for reply. First, all the dups in PG 3.a get copied over. We see dups being copied from `22'1` to `46'71`: ``` DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - _handle_dups earliest_dup_version 0 DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,365 [shard 0:main] osd - copy_up_to/copy_after copy dup version 22'1 .... DEBUG 2026-04-27 05:58:17,366 [shard 0:main] osd - copy_up_to/copy_after copy dup version 46'71 ``` Now, from the PG 3.a's pglog (which the OSD expects to start from beyond `46'71` but in reality starts from `34'38`), pglog entries before `50'0` need to be added as dups. It starts iterating from the oldest entry, `34'38`, finds it to be smaller than expected `46'71` and asserts: ``` ERROR 2026-04-27 05:58:17,366 [shard 0:main] osd - /ceph/rpmbuild/BUILD

72669.title: rgw/multisite: never distribute an uncommitted staging period
72669.author: lumir-sliva
72669.body:
A failed `period update --commit` on the master zone still notified the realm. At that point the period carries the staging id `<realm_id>:staging`, so the period pusher sent it to every other zone, and they made it their current period. The real period that follows has a lower epoch and gets dropped, every later master change is refused, and in my tests both zones ended up master of their own copy (split brain).

The notify became unconditional in ab303922097 (#57640), when it moved out of `rgw::commit_period()`. Squid isn't affected.

The fix has three layers. Each one stops the leak on its own, so a zone that still leaks can't poison a zone with the fix:
- `commit_period()` in radosgw-admin notifies only after a successful commit
- `RGWPeriodPusher::handle_notify()` refuses to push a staging id
- `RGWOp_Period_Post` rejects a pushed staging id with -EINVAL

Tested on two tentacle 20.2.4 clusters (4 gateways per zone) with a genuine refusal: metadata sync stopped on zone B, master moved A -> B -> A, then promoting B without `--yes-i-really-mean-it` was refused with "2 period(s) behind". Each layer was switched on alone:
- no layer: 4 staging pushes reach A 0.07 s after the refusal, HTTP 200
- full fix: nothing sent
- only the pusher check (old radosgw-admin): 4x "not pushing uncommitted staging period", 0 pushes
- only the receiver check (old sender): 32 pushes in 120 s, all HTTP 400, A keeps its period

The receiver check protects the peer's state but not period delivery. An old pusher that leaked a staging period has recorded its realm epoch, so it drops the real period from the next commit as "not newer" and keeps retrying the staging one (backoff capped at 30 s) until its gateway restarts or a later period comes along. In a mixed-version realm, the zone that runs `period update --commit` needs the new radosgw-admin or the new gateways. If a commit fails on a zone that hasn't been upgraded yet, restart that zone's gateways before retrying.

A zone that already took the staging period as current doesn't recover by itself after the upgrade: the real period with the same realm epoch is refused as a fork in the period history. In my tests, running `radosgw-admin realm pull --url <master>` on that zone, then `metadata sync init` and a gateway restart on both zones, got it back.

The second commit adds two tests to `rgw_multi/tests.py`:
- `test_failed_period_commit_not_distributed`: `period update --commit` on the master leaves the staging period one epoch behind, so a following `period commit` is refused on the epoch check. The test checks that no zone switches to the staging period.
- `test_staging_period_push_rejected`: sends the master's staging period to a secondary's `/admin/realm/period` the way an older pusher does, and expects HTTP 400 with the secondary keeping its period.

On a 3-zone mstart realm, 2 runs each: without the fix both fail (the second zone takes `<realm_id>:staging`, and the push gets HTTP 200). With the fix both pass, the refused commit sends nothing, and the receiver logs "rejecting uncommitted staging period". The pusher check has no test of its own, because with the radosgw-admin fix in place nothing can trigger it.

Built on current main (504b1a2b334, `radosgw` and `radosgw-admin`). The lab runs were on a v20.2.4 backport of the same fix, and the test runs on a build carrying the same three files.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81760

Backport: tentacle.

72670.title: rgw/multisite: fix metadata sync of past periods
72670.author: lumir-sliva
72670.body:
Two bugs in how a secondary catches up on past periods after a master change. Both leave metadata missing on the zone while `sync status` reports it caught up.

**More than 100 entries behind on a shard** (first commit). `RGWMetaSyncShardCR::incremental_sync()` leaves a past period when `period_marker <= mdlog_marker`. But `RGWCloneMetaLogCoroutine` clones the remote shard up to its tip and moves `mdlog_marker` there, while each pass applies at most 100 entries. So on the second pass the period ends and everything after the first batch is never applied. Compare against `max_marker`, the position actually read, instead. This dates back to 574ff5f5df6 (2017).

The second commit adds `test_multi_period_incremental_sync_backlog`: the third zone is down while the master moves, 150 buckets are created whose mdlog entries all hash to the same shard, and after the master moves back the third zone must have all of them. It works with the default shard count. Without the fix it fails (3 of 3; 50 of 150 buckets missing), with it it passes (3 of 3). It takes about 8 minutes, most of it the two master changes and the checkpoints.

**More than one gateway running the sync thread** (third commit). `RGWMetaSyncCR` advances to the next period only once every shard of the past period completed in the same process. `RGWMetaSyncShardCR` returns -EBUSY for a shard this gateway doesn't hold the bid for (#45958), before the "finished syncing current period" check, and `RGWBackoffControlCR` retries that forever. So a gateway only gets out if it wins the bid on every shard, and with more than one sync gateway the secondary stays on the old period for good.

The fix:
- a gateway that loses the bid on a past-period shard, or wins it but can't take the lease because another gateway holds it while syncing that shard in a later period, reads the shard marker from rados and treats the shard as done if the owner already reached the period marker or a later realm epoch;
- the owner writes that marker when it finishes a past period, while it still holds the lease. That part is needed because a shard can finish a period without applying anything, in which case the marker tracker never writes (compare https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/55770). If the lease ran out while the last entries drained, the owner retries the period instead, and it never moves a marker that's already on a later realm epoch back;
- a gateway that takes the lease with a stale marker checks the stored one first and finishes the shard without replaying the period.

This end-of-period write is why the first commit comes first: it is based on the position actually read.

Every gateway now advances through past periods on its own, and each writes the unversioned sync info, so one that finishes a period later can store an earlier, still valid period over a later one until it catches up. It's in the commit message; happy to switch that write to a version-checked one if you'd rather. The fix only fully applies once every gateway running the sync thread in the zone has it.

Tested with `test_multi_period_incremental_sync` (3 zones, 2 gateways per zone), which reproduces the multi-gateway stall once https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80439 (#71707), https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81760 and https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81758 are fixed:
- on 504b1a2b334 with those fixes: without this PR it fails (every gateway of zones 2 and 3 stays on realm epoch 2); with only the lost-bid part, 1 of 3; with this PR, 5 of 5
- on current main (04ba07e56c8, same fixes, `rgw_rest_conn_connect_to_resolved_ips=false` to avoid https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81756): 5 of 5

An earlier version of the third commit also passed 3 of 3 failover/failback runs on two tentacle 20.2.4 clusters with 4 sync gateways per zone.

Teuthology runs one gateway per zone, so the multisite suite can't hit the second bug; the existing test does with `gateways_per_zone = 2` in the test config.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81759

72671.title: rgw/multisite: keep the period id when pulling a period from the master
72671.author: lumir-sliva
72671.body:
`RGWPeriodPuller::pull()` fetches a period the zone doesn't have yet from the metadata master and stores it. Since the configstore refactor in 976889ff3ac it first gives the pulled period a new random id and resets its epoch to 1, which looks like a copy of the "create a new period" step of a period commit. Every gateway that pulls a period stores it under its own made-up id.

The pull path runs when a zone missed a period push, for example a zone that was down while the master moved. Its metadata sync then walks the period history with that made-up id, finds no mdlog for it on the master, and stays on that realm epoch for good.

The fix stores the pulled period as it came, as `store_info()` did before the refactor. Not in squid or tentacle, so no backport.

Tested with `test_multi_period_incremental_sync`, where the third zone is down while the master moves and then pulls the latest period:
- without the fix (1 gateway per zone): fails, the third zone walks realm epoch 3 under a random id instead of the real one; with 2 gateways per zone the two gateways of that zone log two different ids for the same period
- with the fix (together with the metadata sync fixes for more than one gateway per zone in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72670): the third zone walks the real ids for epochs 2, 3 and 4, 5 of 5 runs pass

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81758

72672.title: cephadm: add systemd timer for pushing RGW bucket usage to pushgateway
72672.author: ujjawal-ibm
72672.body:
Depends-on: https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/66671
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81767

## Problem:
We need a way to periodically export per-bucket/per-user RGW usage metrics to Prometheus. Currently there is no mechanism in cephadm to push these stats, so operators have no visibility into bucket-level storage consumption through their monitoring stack.

## Solution:
This PR adds support for an optional systemd timer-based cron job that pushes RGW bucket usage metrics to a Prometheus pushgateway.

### New RGWSpec fields:
- `metrics_push_enabled` -> enables the metrics push timer for the RGW service
- `metrics_push_interval` -> how often the job runs (default: 3600s, minimum: 60s)
- `metrics_push_timeout` -> max time the job can run before being killed (default: 300s, minimum: 30s)

### How it works:
1. The MGR orchestrator discovers a running pushgateway daemon and passes its URL to cephadm during RGW deployment.
2. cephadm generates a bash script (from a Jinja2 template) that executes into the RGW container, resolves the zone ID, and runs `rgw-export-bucket-usage` to push metrics.
3. A (systemd timer + oneshot service) pair is installed to run the script at the configured interval.
4. (timer, service, script) is automatically cleaned up when the RGW daemon is removed.

### Example usage:
```yaml
service_type: rgw
service_id: myrealm.myzone
spec:
  rgw_realm: myrealm
  rgw_zone: myzone
  metrics_push_enabled: true
  metrics_push_interval: 3600
  metrics_push_timeout: 300
```

## Testing:
**1.Deployed RGW with `metrics_push_enabled: true`, created 3 S3 buckets with objects, and verified the full pipeline.**

**2.Timer is active and firing on schedule.**

**3.Oneshot service runs successfully (exit code 0)**

$ systemctl status ceph-6318a164-c7af-11f1-988a-525400d3b5c0-metrics-push@rgw.testrealm.testzone.ceph-node-3.mntabo.service

TriggeredBy: ● ceph-6318a164-c7af-11f1-988a-525400d3b5c0-metrics-push@rgw.testrealm.testzone.ceph-node-3.mntabo.timer
```

**4.Status file**
```

{"status": "ok", "ts": 1791973182}
```


**3. Pushgateway receives per-bucket metrics with correct labels**
```
$ curl -s http://localhost:9091/metrics | grep '^ceph_rgw_bucket'
ceph_rgw_bucket_usage_bytes{bucket="test-bucket-1",instance="",job="rgw-bucket-usage",owner="testuser",tenant="",zone="91d001c9-1dce-4ffa-b8c7-d8b3b47f0f24"} 62464

72673.title: osd: Preserve op ordering when requeuing into waiting_for_coro_op
72673.author: MattyWilliams22
72673.body:
## Problem

With allow_ec_optimizations enabled, ops containing CEPH_OSD_OP_CALL run in a
coroutine that yields during async backend reads. While it is in flight
(coro_op_in_flight == true), PrimaryLogPG::do_op() parks every incoming op on
waiting_for_coro_op with push_back().

That breaks ordering in the following sequence:

1. An earlier op (e.g. tid 994) is parked in obc->waiters, waiting for an
   object rw-lock.
2. A coroutine starts, and newer ops (e.g. tid 997) are queued on
   waiting_for_coro_op.
3. The rw-lock is released, and release_object_locks() calls requeue_ops().
   Op 994 is dequeued by the shard thread while coro_op_in_flight is still
   true, so do_op() push_back()s it behind 997.
4. When the coroutine completes, on_coroutine_complete() requeues
   waiting_for_coro_op, and 997 runs before 994.

The OSD then aborts on the "bad op order" assertion at PrimaryLogPG.cc:4461.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81661

## Fix

requeue_op(), requeue_ops() and requeue_object_waiters() now take an
OpWaitingList argument identifying the waiting list the op came from. The enum
lists the waiting lists in pipeline order (MAP, PEERED, FLUSH, ACTIVE, READABLE,
CORO, SCRUB, CACHE_NOT_FULL, PRIMARY_REPAIR, UNREADABLE_OBJECT,
DEGRADED_OBJECT, BLOCKED_OBJECT, OBJECT_LOCK), followed by IN_PROGRESS for ops
that were not on any waiting list.

requeue_op() checks the gates an op can hit on the way back in (waiting_for_map,
waiting_for_readable, waiting_for_coro_op). If the op's previous list is
earlier in the pipeline than the gate, the op has not yet reached that gate and
goes to the back (push_back). Otherwise it is older than anything already
parked there and goes to the front (push_front). If no gate applies, the op is
enqueued on the scheduler as before.

Other changes:

- waiting_for_coro_op and coro_op_in_flight move from PrimaryLogPG to PG, so
  PG::requeue_op() can see them. The coroutine-specific state (active_coro_op,
  coro_resumer, active_coro_ctx) stays in PrimaryLogPG.
- PG::requeue_ops() is now a plain loop that delegates to requeue_op(). The
  special-case splice into waiting_for_readable is removed, because
  requeue_op() now handles that gate.
- Call sites that requeue from waiting_for_readable now swap
  the list into a local list first. This keeps requeue_op() from treating the
  source list as a gate for its own ops.
- In on_change(), the interrupted active_coro_op is placed at the front of the
  coro list before requeueing, so it stays ahead of ops that queued behind it.
- All requeue call sites now pass an explicit OpWaitingList. There is no
  default, so a new caller has to say where its ops came from.

72674.title: ceph-crash: fix the auth name fallback and add tests for it
72674.author: tchaikov
72674.body:
Since 3a0f9ee5, ceph-crash gives up on the first auth name unless it fails with EACCES. But a name without a keyring fails with EPERM, so a host without a keyring for `client.crash.<host>` never posts its crashes. rados/singleton/all/test-crash fails this way on every run, see https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76470.

With this change, ceph-crash tries the next name after any error, and only stops early if the command itself failed or the cluster rejected the dump. The startup ping uses the same names instead of client.admin. `--connect-timeout 5` makes a name the monitors don't know fail within 5 seconds instead of waiting for the 30s `timeout(1)`, and the name that worked last is tried first.

`post_crash()` and `scrape_path()` are now covered by unit tests, with `subprocess.Popen` mocked.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76470

72683.title: osd/ECExtentCache: hold reads behind a cache invalidation, pin growth holes
72683.author: aainscow
72683.body:
Stacked on #72666 (the revert of #70377); only the last two commits are new to this PR. The tests are in #72684.

Fixes two defects in the Fast EC extent cache. The full description is in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81754.

**1. Reads replayed after a cache invalidation overtake the invalidating write.** An op that invalidates the cache (a clone or rollback onto the object, a remove and recreate, a shrinking truncate) waits at the head of the queue. Then `ECExtentCache::Object::invalidate()` replays the ops queued behind it on the same object and sends their reads at once. The invalidating op's sub-writes are only sent once all the cache ops of its transaction are ready, after those reads. Unless the invalidating op reads something itself, the queued writes read the object as it was before it:
- below the old size, they get the old data instead of the clone's data, or instead of the zeros a truncate or recreate leaves, and write it back silently;
- past the old size, the reads are dropped, and a write with no other reads hits `ceph_assert(reads_sent)`.

The reverted #70377 turned the assert into zero-fill (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81611). Now the reads of the replayed ops wait for `write_done()` of the invalidating op, which runs after its sub-writes are sent and sets `current_size`.

**2. A growth hole is erased by an older op's cache line** (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81315, from #72331, unchanged). The growing op now pins every line its hole spans. This matches the `ceph_assert(reads_sent)` crash reports on https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78465 (tentacle 20.2.1/20.2.2).

Both commits cherry-pick cleanly onto tentacle after #72650.

Supersedes #72331 (fix) and, with #72684, #72332 and #72566 (tests).

Results with the tests from #72684, on main with #70377 reverted (10 optimized EC configurations per peering test):

| Test | main + #72666 | + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.Rollback` | abort, `ceph_assert(reads_sent)` | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.CachedRollback` | old data, 10/10 fail | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.TruncateGrow` | old data, 10/10 fail | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.CachedRecreate` | old data, 10/10 fail | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.Recreate` | abort | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.TruncateGrowShortShard` | abort | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECInvalidateReplay.UnalignedTruncate` (control) | pass 10/10 | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECRollbackPartialWrites.*` (4 tests; 3 zero-fill with #70377) | pass 10/10 | pass 10/10 |
| `TestECFailoverWithPeering.ExtentCacheGrowthHoleErasedByLineDeath` | abort | pass 10/10 |
| `ECExtentCache.HoleErasedByOlderOpLineDeath`, `HoleErasedBeforeReadDoneSendReads` | abort | pass |
| `ECExtentCache.CloneInvalidateStaleSize` | abort | pass |
| `TestBackendBasics.TruncateGrowWithSuspendedReads`, `RollbackInvalidateRealistic` | abort | pass 96/96 |

With this PR and #72684 merged into main, all of `unittest_ecfailover_with_peering` (338), `unittest_backend_basics` (888), `unittest_extent_cache` (12), `unittest_ecbackend`, `unittest_ec_with_crush`, `unittest_ec_transaction`, `unittest_ecutil`, `unittest_ec_omap_journal` and the `_l` variants pass. The new and rollback tests passed 600/600 over 5 repeats. Locally, the ctest unit tests pass (218/219: `run-cli-tests` fails only on `radosgw-admin/help.t`, as RGW was not built), as do `smoke.sh`, `safe-to-destroy.sh`, `crush_weights.sh` and `run-rbd-unit-tests-*`.

These are the tests for the Fast EC extent cache defects fixed in #72683. They combine the tests from #72566 and #72332, which this PR supersedes, with new tests for the remaining cases.

72685.title: [DNM] crimson: replication throughput work (testing/eval branch)
72685.author: Matan-B
72685.body:
edit: This PR would be splitted into separate PRs

---

This branch collects ongoing work around Crimson replicated write throughput.
It is not meant to be merged as-is.

Once the work is ready, it will be split into separate PRs by area.
Until then, this branch is used to run all fixes together and measure
their combined impact.

**The layers depend on each other.** While one bottleneck is limiting
throughput, improvements above or below it **usually won't show up in the
results**. Because of that, the work is done one layer at a time.

The numbers below were measured with the stats from #72580. Those
commits are intentionally kept out of this branch so the two don't
conflict.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80545

#### Approach:

1. Take the backend out of the way: run on CyanStore (cyanstore fixes included here)
2. Use stats to identify where a write spends its time (client stages,
   local commit, repop round trip, waiting for replicas) and which
   reactor is busy.
3. Use perf to understand where the CPU time is going.
4. Fix the biggest issue/bottleneck in replicated write path, rerun and repeat.

Fixes so far:
* cyanstore write path overhead
* sharding the OSD<>OSD msgr
* mclock immediate throttle
* batch acks
 
Results (3 OSDs, 4 reactors each, size 3, 4k randwrite, single runs):

So far, the CyanStore work increased throughput from about **19K IOPS to
nearly 30K** IOPS with replication enabled, while maintaining 1.71 ms
primary write latency.

More results, including SeaStore measurements, will be shared once the
branch is ready.

72686.title: osdc: send a single direct op holding primary-only ops to the primary
72686.author: aainscow
72686.body:
SplitOp sends an op whose reads all fall in one chunk whole to the shard holding that chunk, as an EC direct
read. When the op also holds ops only the primary may run (CALL, STAT, GETXATTR(S), CMPXATTR, CHECKSUM, or a
version request), its reads must be in raw shard 0's chunk, and the op goes to the OSD of shard 0 without a
check that this OSD is the primary. It may not be: when primary affinity rejects the OSDs of all the data
shards, a parity shard becomes primary while shard 0 is up and acting, and `ceph osd primary-temp` can name
any OSD. The OSD then runs the CALL on a shard that is not the primary.

- test/osdc: `TestSingleDirectOpTarget` gives an Objecter an OSDMap where primary affinity makes the parity
  shard primary. `CallGoesToPrimary` fails before the next commit: an op of a read and a CALL goes to the
  shard 0 OSD. `ReadGoesToItsShard` and `CallGoesDirectToPrimaryShardZero` check the direct reads that stay.
- osdc: `prepare_single_op()` sends an op holding primary-only ops direct only when the read's shard is the
  primary's shard; otherwise the op goes to the primary as usual. `validate()` also returns whether the op
  holds such ops.

Introduced by #66459. #72016 changes the same validation but keeps the rule; both add tests to
`test_splitop.cc`, so whichever merges second needs a rebase.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81773

Tested: full build including tests (clang, Debug, -Werror). `unittest_split_ops_ut`: 22 passed;
`CallGoesToPrimary` fails without the fix. Not run on a cluster.

72694.title: doc: Simplify the Assisted-by tag to match the Linux kernel
72694.author: aainscow
72694.body:
Depends on #66788

This PR is stacked on #66788 (the AI coding assistants guidance currently before the Ceph Steering Committee). Only the last commit is new.

The guidance is based on the Linux kernel's `Documentation/process/coding-assistants.rst`. Linux has since dropped the agent and model name from its attribution tag in [816d9992d9ed](https://github.com/torvalds/linux/commit/816d9992d9ed) ("coding-assistants: simplify attribution", merged for 7.3), so the tag records only that an LLM was used. This changes the Ceph guidance to match:

```
Assisted-by: LLM [TOOL1] [TOOL2]
```

replacing `AGENT_NAME-AGENT_VERSION[:MODEL_NAME] [TOOL1] [TOOL2]`. The optional analysis-tool list and the rule against listing basic development tools are unchanged.

The model name was discussed on #66788 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/66788#discussion_r3647807333), and the wording approved by https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79745 keeps it. As the guidance requires, this change needs its own Ceph Steering Committee motion before merge.

72695.author: aainscow
72695.body:

This adds a unit test for https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72674, which fixes https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76470: since 3a0f9ee5099, `post_crash()` moves on to the next auth name only when `ceph` exits with `EACCES`, so a host whose `ceph.keyring` has no key for `client.crash.<host>` (EPERM, exit status 1) never tries `client.crash` or `client.admin`, and `rados/singleton/all/test-crash` fails on main. - reports a failure when every name fails;

and that `scrape_path()` posts the crash with the fallback.

72696.title: common/admin_socket: only wait for the hook being unregistered
72696.author: aainscow
72696.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This fix has NOT BEEN REVIEWED by a human. It is being done with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. This is why the commits have no Signed-off-by.







`AdminSocket::unregister_commands()` waits until no admin socket command is running, whatever hook the running command belongs to. If that command blocks on a lock held by the thread doing the unregister, both wait forever.

`OSD::init()` hits this (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/59079). It holds `osd_lock` while BlueStore mounts, and the mount destroys an allocator whose `SocketHook` unregisters its commands. If an admin socket `config set` arrives during the mount, `handle_conf_change()` waits for `osd_lock`, and the OSD never boots. In teuthology this shows up as `wait_for_all_osds_up` timeouts, mostly in `rados/singleton/all/recovery-preemption`, where the OSD restarts after `kill -9` with a large store to mount.

This PR replaces the global `in_hook` flag with a multiset of running hooks. `unregister_commands()` waits only while the hook it is removing is running, which is the case the wait exists for.

Testing:
- New `AdminSocketRunningHook` tests in `unittest_admin_socket`: unregistering another hook while one runs (hangs without the fix, then fails after 30 s), and unregistering the running hook still waits for it.
- The whole `unittest_admin_socket` suite passes with the fix.
- teuthology `rados/singleton` `all/recovery-preemption` on a ceph-ci batch with all of these RADOS QA fixes (`wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014`): 10/10 passed, 7 of them with the facets every recent QA failure had (`mon_election/connectivity`, `msgr-failures/few`, `msgr/async-v1only`): https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:28-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_14:46:26-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_16:18:45-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.
