72698.title: qa/valgrind.supp: suppress rocksdb thread pool queues at exit
72698.author: aainscow
72698.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The rocksdb records are hidden on main behind the monitor OpenSSL leak, which teuthology reports first (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71606 suppresses it).
> - teuthology with https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71606 and this PR: none of the 6 monitor valgrind logs of the two `rados/verify` valgrind jobs has an error, and mon.a's suppression counts show the new entry matched the two rocksdb records: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:33-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/. Those jobs failed only on the OSD coroutine leak that https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72704 fixes.
> - `rados/valgrind-leaks` `2-inject-leak/none` passed: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:55:32-rados:valgrind-leaks-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.







This builds on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71606, which suppresses the OpenSSL records the monitors report under valgrind (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79831). It includes that PR's commit until it merges; only the last commit is new.

Since the rocksdb 9.11 update (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/70807), `Env::Default()` is never destroyed, so the queues of its thread pools stay reachable when `ceph-mon` exits. The mons in `rados/verify` and `rados/valgrind-leaks` run with `--show-reachable=yes` and report two records:

```
operator new[] < deque::_M_push_back_aux<BGItem> < rocksdb::ThreadPoolImpl::Impl::Submit
  < DBImpl::CompactRange < RocksDBStore::compact_thread_entry
```

Teuthology reports only the first error, an OpenSSL record that https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71606 suppresses, so these stay hidden until that PR merges. This PR adds a suppression next to the other rocksdb ones.

Testing: teuthology on a batch with https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71606 and this suppression (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:33-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:55:32-rados:valgrind-leaks-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/):
- `rados/valgrind-leaks` `2-inject-leak/none` passed.
- In both `rados/verify` `validater/valgrind` `tasks/rados_api_tests` jobs no monitor reported a valgrind error. They failed only on an OSD coroutine stack leak, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81777, which https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72704 fixes.

72699.title: qa/tasks/mgr: keep the class setup config across tests
72699.author: aainscow
72699.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - On main, `test_list_enabled_module` failed in 91 of the 92 `rados/dashboard` jobs of the 46 main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16.
> - teuthology with this PR: both `rados/dashboard` jobs passed all 290 tests (1 skipped), including `test_list_enabled_module`: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_15:03:51-rados:dashboard-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/. Both passed again in https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_06:56:10-rados-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/.







`CephTestCase.tearDown()` resets the config to the epoch saved when the cluster came up. That also removes what a test class set in `setUpClass()`: the per-mgr module ports from `setup_mgrs()` (`MODULE_PORTS`) and `_assign_ports()`, and settings such as the dashboard password policy in `UserTest`. The running mgrs keep the old values, so nothing shows until they respawn and lose them.

In `rados/dashboard`, `test_list_enabled_module` enables iostat, all mgrs respawn, and each starts the dashboard on the default port 8443:
- the test keeps polling the active mgr on its old port and fails;
- the two mgrs that share a host collide on 8443 ("Port 8443 not free"), which raises MGR_MODULE_ERROR.

Both dashboard jobs fail this way in almost every main batch, filed as https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/70669, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75358 and https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/62972. Since the run stops at the first failure, about half of the dashboard API test modules had not run in teuthology for a long time. With the ports kept, one of them fails the same way: `UserTest.setUpClass()` enables the password policy, the first test's reset removes it, and after a later mgr respawn `test_validate_password_fail_name` finds the username check off.

This PR saves the config version when a class's first test starts, after `setUpClass()`, and resets only that far back after each test, so every test still starts from the state `setUpClass()` left. The class resets to the saved cluster epoch at the end, as before.

Testing:
- teuthology `rados/dashboard` with the first version of this change, which kept only the ports: `test_list_enabled_module` passed, no "Port 8443 not free", and all 285 tests ran, with one failure, `test_validate_password_fail_name`, explained above. The mgr log shows the password policy removed by the first test's `config reset` and lost at the next respawn.
- teuthology `rados/dashboard` with this version, both jobs: all 290 tests passed (1 skipped), including `test_list_enabled_module` and `test_validate_password_fail_name`: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_15:03:51-rados:dashboard-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.

72700.title: mon/MonmapMonitor: do not call an election from update_from_paxos
72700.author: aainscow
72700.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The new `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-command-replies.sh`, run with `CEPH_CLI_TEST_DUP_COMMAND=1` as teuthology sets it, on main of 2026-10-28 (with https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72711): without the fix, the stretch mode test and both disallowed-leader tests fail in 3 of 3 runs; with the fix, all four tests pass in 3 of 3.
> - On main, `mon/mon-stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds.sh` failed in 15 of the 46 `all/stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds` jobs of the main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16 (one job per batch), including all 6 in October. In the first QA batch with https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72711, the same job got past `enable_stretch_mode` and failed on `disable_stretch_mode` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82182).
> - teuthology with this PR on main of 2026-10-21: all 6 jobs passed, including `all/stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds` with both election strategies (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-21_13:40:46-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-21_13:40:50-rados:singleton-wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021-distro-default-trial/) and `rados/standalone` `workloads/mon-stretch`, which runs the new tests (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-21_13:41:08-rados:standalone-wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021-distro-default-trial/). All runs: https://pulpito.ceph.com/?branch=wip-aainscow-mon-commit-waiters-v3-261021.








Every monmap command that changes the elector's disallowed leaders (`enable_stretch_mode`, `disable_stretch_mode`, `add/rm disallowed_leader`, `set_new_tiebreaker`) loses its reply and runs a second time (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81930). The second run fails or reports the command's own change. The stretch mode job failed with `Error EINVAL: stretch mode is already engaged` in every main QA batch in October (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81136), and now fails with `Error EINVAL: stretch mode is already disabled` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82182).

When a committed monmap changed the disallowed leaders, `notify_new_monmap()` started an election in the middle of `Monitor::refresh_from_paxos()`. The election restarts every service, which completes the commit's waiters with -EAGAIN; since a2230c9b0d2 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71248) those waiters run only from `post_refresh()`, after the election. The command was then dispatched again, or resent by the peon that forwarded it, and ran against the updated monmap.

That election is not needed: every caller of `notify_new_monmap()` bootstraps afterwards, and `bootstrap()` applies the disallowed leaders again and holds the election. So `notify_new_monmap()` no longer calls an election, and its `can_change_external_state` parameter goes away. The notification stays in the refresh rather than moving to `MonmapMonitor::tick()`, because the bootstrap's election starts before the next tick and would run with the elector's old election strategy and ranks.

https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72711 (merged) makes a repeated `enable_stretch_mode` succeed, but the command still runs twice: its reply says "stretch mode is already engaged", and `disable_stretch_mode` still fails. The teuthology jobs' deliberate duplicate commands (`CEPH_CLI_TEST_DUP_COMMAND`) do not need it: when the CLI's second attempt fails, it prints a warning and still exits 0.

The backports of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71248 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71968, https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71969) bring the regression with them unless this goes in alongside them.

Testing:
- `qa/standalone/mon-stretch/mon-stretch-command-replies.sh`, run with `CEPH_CLI_TEST_DUP_COMMAND=1` as teuthology sets it, on main of 2026-

> - The new `unittest_client_command_reset` fails on main (the command is not resent after the session reset) and passes with the fix.
> - On main, the cephtool workunit failed in 15 of the 91 `rados/singleton-bluestore` `all/cephtool` jobs with `msgr-failures/many` in the 46 main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16. With this PR and https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72702, 6 of 6 passed: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_14:23:11-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_16:18:51-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/. The hang hits about 1 job in 6, so the unit test is the stronger evidence.







`ceph tell mds.<id> ...` can wait forever. `rados/singleton-bluestore/all/cephtool` hangs until the 3 h timeout this way when it runs with injected socket failures (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72888).

When the MDS answers the client's reconnect with RESETSESSION, the messenger discards the unacked messages, including an outstanding MCommand, and calls `ms_handle_remote_reset()`. The client aborts only one-shot commands there. The CLI's commands are not one-shot, and a client without a mount has no MDSMap, so `cancel_commands()` never runs either: `ceph_mds_command()` waits on its condition with no timeout.

This PR resends the remaining commands on that connection from `ms_handle_remote_reset()`, as MonClient, MgrClient and Objecter already do for their commands after a reset. One-shot commands are still aborted with -EPIPE.

Testing:
- New `unittest_client_command_reset` runs a `Client` against a fake MDS connection, discards what was sent as RESETSESSION does, and calls `ms_handle_remote_reset()`. Without the fix the outstanding command is not resent; with it, it is resent with the same tid and its reply completes the caller. A second test checks that one-shot commands are still aborted. The first test fails on main and both pass with the fix.
- `Client::mds_command()` needs monitors and an FSMap, so the test registers commands directly; `command_lock` and `command_table` become protected for that.
- teuthology `rados/singleton-bluestore` `all/cephtool` with `msgr-failures/many`, the facet of every recent QA failure, on a ceph-ci batch with all of these RADOS QA fixes (`wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014`), including https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72702: 6/6 passed, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_14:23:11-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_16:18:51-rados:singleton-bluestore-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/.

72704.title: osd: free the stack of a coroutine that completes without yielding
72704.author: aainscow
72704.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The new `unittest_osd_coroutines`: `CompleteWithoutYieldFreesStack` fails when `start_coroutine()` keeps no reference (as on main), and valgrind then reports the 128 KB stack definitely lost in `create_control_block`, the same stack as the teuthology jobs. With the fix it passes with no valgrind errors.
> - teuthology: the two `rados/verify` valgrind `rados_api_tests` jobs that showed this leak on every OSD (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:33-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/) were re-run with the same seed and the fix. No OSD or monitor log of either job has a valgrind error: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_19:18:46-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v3-261014-distro-default-trial/. One job passed; the other failed only on an unrelated test race (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72744).







`PrimaryLogPG::do_op()` runs a CALL op on a pool with EC optimizations in a coroutine. `coro_resumer` owns the coroutine, and the coroutine body ends with `on_coroutine_complete()`, which resets `coro_resumer`. Since https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71327, `CoroHandles` keeps only a `weak_ptr`, so `coro_resumer` is the only strong reference. When the op completes without yielding, the reset destroys the coroutine while it is still running on its own stack. Boost then never unwinds the fiber, and its 128KB stack leaks once per such op. (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81777)

A coroutine that yields is safe: the `objects_read_sync()` completion resumes it through a locked `weak_ptr`, which keeps it alive until it returns.

`rados/verify` valgrind jobs show the leak as `Leak_DefinitelyLost`/`Leak_PossiblyLost` in `create_control_block<...push_coroutine...>` from the `do_op` lambda. Teuthology reports only the first valgrind error, and on main that is usually the monitor `CRYPTO_malloc` leak (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79831), so this one has been hidden. For example, jobs 629993 and 604377 have it on every OSD. With the monitor leak suppressed, it is the remaining failure.

This PR moves the coroutine start into `start_coroutine()` in `osd/Coroutines.h`. It holds a local reference while the coroutine runs, so a completed coroutine is destroyed after it returns, outside its own stack.

The in-body reset was introduced by 52f862cebbc (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67079). https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71327 (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79515) fixed the use-after-free in `on_change()` but kept this reset.

Testing:
- New `unittest_osd_coroutines` counts the stacks a coroutine started by `start_coroutine()` allocates, and checks they are freed when it completes without yielding, completes after a yield, or is destroyed while suspended. Without the fix, `CompleteWithoutYieldFreesStack` fails, and valgrind reports `131,072 bytes in 1 blocks are definitely lost` in `create_control_block`, the same stack as the teuthology jobs. With the fix, the test passes and valgrind reports no errors.
- teuthology `rados/verify` `validater/valgrind` `tasks/rados_api_tests`, the same two jobs (same seed) that reported this leak in https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_13:56:33-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-261014-distro-default-trial/, re-run with this fix: no valgrind errors in any OSD or monitor log of either job (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_19:18:46-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v3-261014-distro-default-trial/). One job passed; the other failed only on `LibRadosPoolIsInSelfmanagedSnapsMode.FreshInstance` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64056), where a fresh client read the osdmap from a monitor one epoch behind the pool deletion.

72711.title: mon: make enable_stretch_mode idempotent
72711.author: kamoltat
72711.body:
Problem:
Enabling stretch mode updates the monmap and can trigger an election
before the client gets a reply. When the command is replayed after the
election, stretch mode is already enabled and we return EINVAL even
though the original command succeeded.

Solution:
Return success if stretch mode is already enabled without changing the
existing configuration. If enablement is still pending, wait for the
commit and retry instead of returning success on uncommitted state.

Add regression coverage in both the standalone stretch test and the
five-monitor workunit used by
rados/singleton/all/stretch-mode-5-mons-8-osds. Repeat the enable command
and verify that it succeeds without changing the monmap.

Also remove obsolete CRUSH rule min_size/max_size fields and enable the
pool application in the standalone test to avoid unrelated health warnings.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81136
Signed-off-by: Kamoltat (Junior) Sirivadhna <ksirivad@redhat.com>

72712.title: rgw: avoid no-op dynamic reshard reduction and scale versioned limit_check
72712.author: trukhinyuri
72712.body:
In `RGWBucketReshard::calculate_preferred_shards`, `calculated_num_shards == current_num_shards` was checked before rounding up to `nearest_prime(calculated_num_shards)` and before clamping to `min_layout_shards`. In addition, the reduction condition only checked `current_num_shards > min_dynamic_shards` rather than `current_num_shards > std::max(min_dynamic_shards, min_layout_shards)`. When a bucket was already at `min_layout_shards` (or when `nearest_prime` rounded `calculated_num_shards` back to `current_num_shards`), `calculate_preferred_shards` set `need_resharding = true` with `*suggested_num_shards == current_num_shards`. Because `RGWReshard::process_entry` only dropped reduction requests when `suggested_shard_count > current_shard_count` instead of `>=`, RGW could execute a no-op reshard to the same shard count.

Also scale `safe_max_objs_per_shard` by one third for versioned buckets in `RGWBucketAdminOp::limit_check` (`radosgw-admin bucket limit check`) to match `RGWRados::calculate_preferred_shards`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/55546
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/69464

72713.title: mon: retry pings to dead peers after reconnect
72713.author: kamoltat
72713.body:
Problem:
A full messenger session reset can drop the last queued monitor ping.
Once the peer is marked dead, dead_ping only updates its connection
score without sending another ping.

This leaves the peers waiting on each other and can keep MON_NETSPLIT
active even after all monitors reconnect and rejoin quorum. This happened
during the monitor restarts in rados/singleton/all/mon-stretch-pool.

Solution:
Send another ping on each dead_ping interval so the peers can resume
pinging after reconnecting. Keep the peer marked dead until we hear from
it, and stop probing if its rank is no longer valid in the monmap.

Add unit tests for repeated dead-peer probes, keeping the peer marked
dead without a response, and stopping probes for invalid peer ranks.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79814
Signed-off-by: Kamoltat (Junior) Sirivadhna <ksirivad@redhat.com>

72714.title: DNM: rgw/datum: data operation core
72714.author: chardan
72714.body:
Datum is a powerful foundation for building clear, composable data-handling code in Ceph.

It provides shared operations for selecting and observing data, reducing the separate helpers needed for byte ranges, record fields, keys, lenses, and traversal. Datum supplies vocabulary such as `byte_extent`, `byte_mapping`, and `byte_query` for components that gather, splice, and move data. Operations such as `copy` accept ordinary storage and fragments.

The library provides interval queries and coverage, composed comparisons for standard Ranges algorithms, record projections, explicit ownership, traversal and continuation, resource budgets, and diagnostic field selection. These operations make it easier to pass data through components using views and projections, avoid unnecessary copies, and reuse transformations across data domains. Applications retain control of I/O, transactions, authorization, and storage policy.

Datum's core depends only on the standard library. Shared domain headers, including `ceph-datum.h`, adapt these operations to native Ceph types. Optional adapters provide Ceph framing, RGW key wire vocabulary, diagnostics, formatting, and binary codecs. Consumers such as CLS and libfdb can build on the same operations and supply their own domain policies; their integrations and migrations are outside this PR.

Documentation: This is one of the most exciting parts!! There is a tutorial that even has cats!
Eighteen unforgettable lessons, an interval interlude, enchanting runnable examples, and SO MUCH more! Amaze your friends! Confound your enemies! Further bewilder the befuddled! [Datum tutorial and design (PR preview)](https://ceph--72714.org.readthedocs.build/en/72714/dev/radosgw/datum/)

The core requires C++23; optional reflection and native framing facilities use C++26. Datum targets are registered as part of normal RGW builds when `WITH_RADOSGW` is enabled. Language requirements are scoped to the relevant Datum targets.

PR organization:

The commits are arranged in review order:

1. Documentation, tutorials, examples, and publishing support.
2. Pure C++23 Datum core and compatibility machinery.
3. Diagnostic vocabulary and formatting adapters, with dedicated tests.
4. zpp codec adapter, with codec and pipeline tests.
5. Ceph buffer and framing vocabulary, with native buffer tests.
6. RGW key wire vocabulary.
7. Remaining core and cross-domain tests, with shared test registration.

Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-6

Signed-off-by: Jesse F. Williamson <jfw@ibm.com>

72715.title: tools/cephfs_mirror: close directories by kind in finish_crawl
72715.author: lumir-sliva
72715.body:
SnapDiffSync::finish_crawl() closes every directory left on the sync stack with ceph_close_snapdiff(). Directories that are traversed in full instead of diffed (new, moved-in or replaced directories, purged or itype-changed subtrees) are opened with opendirat() and have no snapdiff handle, so closing their uninitialized ceph_snapdiff_info segfaults the daemon.

finish_crawl() runs whenever the crawl stops early, so any of these crashes cephfs-mirror while such a directory is on the stack:
- a sync error, e.g. a remote mkdir failing with EDQUOT. The daemon restarts and retries the same snapshot, so a persistent error turns into a crash loop
- stopping or restarting cephfs-mirror (SIGTERM)
- `ceph fs snapshot mirror remove` of the directory
- the mirror client getting blocklisted (same branch, not tested)

The fix closes the leftover entries with fini_directory(), which already picks ceph_closedir() or ceph_close_snapdiff() per entry when a directory is finished normally.

The qa test replaces a synced directory under the same name, so the next sync walks it in full, and makes its remote mkdir fail with a file quota. Without the fix the daemon dies at the failed mkdir and the test times out waiting for the sync failure; with it the sync fails, the daemon stays up, and the snapshot syncs once the quota is lifted. The SIGTERM and mirror-remove routes aren't covered by the test, there's a vstart reproducer for all three on the tracker.

squid and tentacle have the same loop in finish_sync(), so the backports need a small hand adjustment there.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81573

72716.title: tools/cephfs_mirror: resume a failed sync only from its base snapshot
72716.author: lumir-sliva
72716.body:
Depends on #72715, its two commits are in here because the new tests need that fix. Only the last two commits are new.

cephfs-mirror stores the snapshot it's about to sync in ceph.mirror.dirty_snap_id on the remote dir_root. When that id equals the snapshot being synced, an earlier attempt didn't finish, and the daemon resumes it with a snapdiff from the newest remote snapshot (prev). That only works if the earlier attempt diffed from the same prev. If the base gets deleted between attempts and the deletion is mirrored, prev moves back to an older snapshot while the remote tree still reflects the deleted one. Entries that only existed in the deleted snapshot are in neither side of the new diff, so they stay on the remote, in the remote snapshot and in every later one, and the sync is reported as successful.

The value is now written as "<current>:<base>" (base 0 for a remote scan), and an interrupted attempt is only resumed with a snapdiff when its base is still prev. Anything else falls back to a remote scan, same as any other mismatch. Side effect: a remote scan that fails is redone as a remote scan instead of being continued as a diff from prev.

Mixed versions:
- older daemons parse the value with atoll() and read the leading id, so they behave exactly as before
- a bare id from an older daemon still matches prev, so idle directories keep syncing incrementally after an upgrade
- a directory whose sync was interrupted by the upgrade has no recorded base and syncs its current snapshot once with a remote scan
- the MDS already allow-lists the xattr without validating the value, so no MDS change is needed

I checked both directions on vstart by swapping the daemon binary between failed attempts, steps and results are on the tracker.

Two qa tests make every attempt at a snapshot fail before it reaches the entries it removes, delete the base, then let the sync finish: once with the daemon mirroring the deletion itself, once with the base already gone on both sides. Both fail on main (the removed entries stay on the remote) and pass with the fix.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81572

72717.title: mgr/prometheus: iterate over a copy of the rbd_stats pool ids
72717.author: anthonyeleven
72717.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81782

`get_rbd_stats` deletes stale entries from `self.rbd_stats['pools']` while iterating over its keys. When a tracked pool is dropped from `rbd_stats_pools`, is deleted, or loses its rbd application, the next loop step raises `RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration`, and that metrics collection fails.

This iterates over a list of the keys instead, as the code a few lines below already does for `pool_ids`.

72718.title: mon,osd: send the HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL metric only while a level is high
72718.author: lumir-sliva
72718.body:
## Summary
Follow-up to #68442. The OSD, crimson OSD and monitor attach a `HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL` health metric to every report they send to the mgr, with a count of 0 when nothing is elevated and even when the guard is disabled (the default). This PR only attaches it when at least one subsystem is at or above `high_debug_level_threshold`.

## Problem
A mgr that predates the metric doesn't have a collector for it, so `DaemonHealthMetricCollector::create()` returns nothing and `DaemonServer::send_report()` logs

    mgr.x sent me an unknown health metric: 3

for every report from every daemon that sends it. During a rolling upgrade (mons first, then mgrs) that is one error line per upgraded daemon every few seconds until the mgr itself is upgraded, for a feature nobody turned on. It also matters for the tentacle/umbrella backports of #68442, where a point-release upgrade would hit this on every cluster.

## Fix
Wrap the `emplace_back` in `if (count > 0)` in `OSD::get_health_metrics()`, `Monitor::get_health_metrics()` and the crimson `OSD::get_health_metrics()`.

An absent metric reads the same as a zero one for the new mgr:
- `DaemonServer` replaces a daemon's `daemon_health_metrics` wholesale on each report (`DaemonServer.cc:872`), and `send_report()` rebuilds the checks from scratch each time.
- `HighDebugLevel::_update()` already ignores entries with a count of 0.

So the warning still raises while a level is high and clears once it drops, the threshold is removed or the level is reverted. With the guard on and a level actually elevated, an old mgr still logs it, which is expected.

One visible side effect: `ceph_daemon_health_metrics{type="HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL"}` from mgr/prometheus is now absent at idle instead of 0. Nothing in `monitoring/` or the tests reads it, and since #68442 hasn't shipped in a release yet, nobody can depend on the 0 series.

## Test
3-OSD vstart (MON=1, MGR=1, OSD=3), `debug_mgr 10`, counting `handle_report daemon_health_metrics` lines in the mgr log:

    before, idle, threshold 0:     37/38 lines carry HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL(0|(0,0))
    after,  idle, threshold 0:      0/28
    after,  threshold 10:          12/13, HEALTH_WARN HIGH_DEBUG_LEVEL
    after,  config rm threshold:    0/8,  HEALTH_OK within 10s

`qa/workunits/mon/debug_level_guard.sh` passes (warning raised, auto-revert, warning cleared, warn-only, disabled) and `unittest_debug_level_guard` 9/9. The crimson hunk wasn't built locally, it's the same one-line change as the classic OSD.

72719.title: mgr: add an osd_map_pools getter for rbd_support
72719.author: anthonyeleven
72719.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81783

The mirror snapshot and trash purge schedule handlers in rbd_support each call `get_rbd_pools` once a minute, even when no schedules exist. `get_rbd_pools` fetches `osd_map` only to read pool ids, names and applications.

Dumping `osd_map` holds the GIL while it converts every OSD and every `pg_upmap_items` entry to Python objects. It also computes a read balance score for each replicated pool, and each score copies the OSDMap and maps every PG of the pool. On a Reef cluster with 10,130 `pg_upmap_items` entries, Python module commands stalled for about 6 seconds every 66 seconds.

This gives `OSDMap::dump_pool()` a `with_read_balance` parameter, as #73045 does, and adds an `osd_map_pools` getter that returns the list of pools, dumped through `dump_pool()` without the read balance scores. `get_rbd_pools` and `TaskHandler.resolve_pool_name` use the getter. Other modules that only need pools, such as the prometheus module's `get_rbd_stats`, could use it too.

The new key is not added to the mgr API cache, since dumping only the pools is cheap.

72720.title: mgr/MgrClient: send keepalives on the mgr session
72720.author: anthonyeleven
72720.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81784

The mgr sends nothing back on a daemon's lossy mgr session, and `AsyncConnection`'s idle check counts only received traffic. So every OSD and MDS faults its mgr session once it has been open for `ms_connection_idle_timeout`, even though it reports every `mgr_stats_period` seconds. It then reconnects, authenticates again and declares all of its perf counters again. Daemons that connected together after a mgr failover stay in step, so they all reconnect to the mgr at the same moment.

MonClient avoids this by sending keepalives. After a report, `MgrClient` now sends one if half of the daemon's own `ms_connection_idle_timeout` has passed since the last, so the ack arrives well before the timeout. With the default 900 s timeout that is one keepalive every 450 s, not one per report. The mgr's messenger answers the keepalive itself, so nothing new reaches the mgr's dispatch path.

An earlier revision sent the keepalive from the mgr, so that daemons of any release would be fixed once the mgrs were upgraded. It is back in `MgrClient` because the daemon's idle timer is what closes the session, and only the daemon knows that timer's setting.

72723.title: qa: test lock requests interrupted after the MDS grants them
72723.author: vshankar
72723.body:
(This PR doesn't include the user-space driver fix yet -- raised it to link it in the kernel driver fix as a reproducer link)

A blocked fcntl/flock request can be interrupted after the MDS has granted the lock but before the client has seen the grant. The MDS keeps the lock, since an interrupt request only cancels a waiting lock. If the client discards the grant, the lock is orphaned on the MDS: the process that asked for it is gone and nothing unlocks it until the client releases its caps on the inode.

The test runs the lock holder and the waiter on the same mount so the holder's unlock and the waiter's interrupt queue up in order on one MDS session while the MDS is stopped. On resume, the unlock grants the lock to the waiter before the interrupt is processed. Another client then checks that the lock is free.

This reproducer is based on @deshpandevaishnavi20 reproducer report.

Reproduces: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81698

72726.title: crimson/osd: implement the purged-snaps mechanism
72726.author: ronen-fr
72726.body:
Crimson lacked Classic's purged-snaps machinery. Removed snaps were trimmed but never
recorded in the PGs' `purged_snaps`, so the monitor never marked them purged and
`removed_snaps_queue` never drained. There was also no purged-snaps scrub to catch
clones left mapped to purged snaps.

This PR ports the mechanism, following Classic (with changes based on Ante Kuspilic's
https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72544:
- PGs record trimmed snaps in `info.purged_snaps`.
- The OSD records the osdmaps' `new_purged_snaps` in the `purged_snaps` meta object,
  and fetches missing epochs from the monitor before booting.
- A periodic scrub (also the `scrub_purged_snaps` admin command) finds stray clones
  and requeues their snaps for trimming. The `reset_purged_snaps_last` admin command
  is ported as well.

Differences from Classic:
- Crimson keeps a snap-mapper object per PG, so the scrub runs per PG.
- The lookup uses the fixed algorithm from the #72544 review: rows sorted numerically
  and merged, so the decimal-string pool order on disk doesn't matter.
- The writer never leaves overlapping or adjacent rows. Classic's can, when one update
  covers several epochs.
- An unanswered request to the monitor is re-sent after 30 s.

The format helpers live in a new store-independent header (`osd/purged_snaps.h`),
covered by `unittest_purged_snaps`. Classic only switches to these helpers; its
behaviour is unchanged.

72727.title: mgr: free erased MgrMapCache python objects
72727.author: NitzanMordhai
72727.body:
MgrMapCache<PyObject*>::erase() and insert() dropped erased, replaced and evicted entries through Py_AddPendingCall(). That only queues the call for the main thread of the main interpreter, and the ceph-mgr main thread never runs Python, so the queue is never drained; once it is full the call fails and erase() ignored the failure. Either way every erased entry kept its reference. With prometheus scraping a 10K PG cluster, each invalidated pg_dump leaked about 90MB and the mgr grew ~400MB per minute.

erase() runs from notify paths that hold ActivePyModules::lock without the GIL, so queue the objects there and drop them on the next get() or insert(), which already require the GIL. insert() now drops replaced and evicted entries directly.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81794

Assisted-by: Claude

72728.title: test/mgr: add fake OSDs for mgr scale testing
72728.author: NitzanMordhai
72728.body:
ceph_test_mgr_fake_osd boots into the osdmap like a real OSD (MOSDBoot with bluestore-like metadata, beacons, pg create acks) and reports to the mgr through MgrClient, but has no object store, peering or heartbeats. Each fake reports the PGs it is acting primary for as active+clean, so a vstart cluster can carry hundreds of OSDs and a large pgmap at ~115MB per fake.

fake-osd-cluster.sh starts a 1 mon / 1 mgr vstart cluster, launches the fakes and creates a pool, waiting until all PGs are active+clean. It also works around vstart with OSD=0 creating size 0 pools, which corrupt the mon heap once crush has a device.

Example, from the build dir:

  ninja ceph_test_mgr_fake_osd vstart-base
  ../src/test/mgr/fake-osd-cluster.sh start -o 10 -p 10000 -s 3
  ../src/test/mgr/fake-osd-cluster.sh add 5
  ../src/test/mgr/fake-osd-cluster.sh status
  ../src/test/mgr/fake-osd-cluster.sh stop --all

10 fake OSDs with a 10000 PG pool reach active+clean in about 10s.

Resources measured with 10 fakes and 10000 PGs (debug build):
- each fake: ~115MB RSS, 14 threads, ~0.3% of one core
- each fake binds 2 ports from ms_bind_port_min..max (6800-7568 by default), so about 370 fakes per host unless the range is raised
- the fakes recompute their PG list once per osdmap epoch, so CPU spikes briefly on every map change, growing with PG count

72739.title: mgr/orchestrator: accept device paths that contain colons
72739.author: guits
72739.body:
`ceph orch daemon add osd` splits the host:device argument on every colon. PCI by-path names such as pci-0000:cd:00.0-nvme-1 contain extra colons and the unpack then fails with "too many values to unpack".

Only the first colon separates the host from the device spec.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81800

72740.title: mgr/prometheus: Fix stale health-check severity and missing messages
72740.author: AnuragRaut08
72740.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81799
Signed-off-by: Anurag Raut <anuragtraut08@ibm.com>

PR Description

The `ceph_health_detail` metric has two issues:

- **Stale severity:** The metric can report outdated severity when a health check changes severity.
- **Missing messages:** The `message` label remains empty even when an active health check has a summary message.

This PR addresses these issues by:

- Updating the stored severity when it changes.
- Exposing the current summary message for active non-scalar checks.
- Keeping messages empty for inactive checks and `OSD_DOWN` to preserve compatibility with existing Prometheus alert rules.

Regression tests cover severity changes, persistence, and message handling.

72742.title: mon/MonClient: ping without a key when no auth method needs one
72742.author: aainscow
72742.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The new `unittest_mon_client` case fails on main with -ENOENT and passes with the fix. `qa/standalone/mon/mon-bind.sh` also fails on main and passes with the fix.
> - On main, mon-bind.sh failed in 14 of the 46 `rados/standalone` `workloads/mon` jobs of the 46 main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16, including all 6 from October.
> - teuthology with this PR: the two jobs cited on the tracker, re-run with the same seed, passed: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_06:56:10-rados-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_07:01:46-rados-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/.







Since 20b8a72b5f3, `MonClient::ping_monitor()` returns the key loading error, so `ceph ping mon.X` fails with ENOENT before connecting on a cluster with `auth_client_required=none` and no keyring. `qa/standalone/mon/mon-bind.sh` fails this way on main (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80756):

```
mon-bind.sh:83: TEST_mon_client_connect:  ceph ping mon.a
[errno 2] RADOS object not found (error calling ping_monitor)
```

`init()` fails only when no auth method is left after `refresh_config()` has dropped cephx for the missing key. This PR does the same in `ping_monitor()`. It replaces the sleep in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72165.

Testing:

- `qa/standalone/mon/mon-bind.sh` fails on main with the error above and passes with the fix, as does `mon-ping.sh`.

72743.title: qa/tasks/workunit: tolerate a failed keyring import
72743.author: aainscow
72743.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - On main, the keyring import failed in 35 of the 46 `rados/thrash-old-clients` `1-install/reef` `workloads/rbd_cls` jobs of the 46 main QA batches from 2026-07-24 to 2026-10-16.
> - teuthology on main without this PR fails with the tracker's error: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_11:41:18-rados:thrash-old-clients-main-distro-default-trial/.
> - With this PR, both jobs passed, and `test_cls_rbd.sh` ran as `client.2` and passed 68 tests: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_11:41:12-rados:thrash-old-clients-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v6-261015-distro-default-trial/.







The workunit task merges the client's and `client.admin`'s keyrings into the cluster keyring with the host's `ceph-authtool`. In `rados/thrash-old-clients` that tool comes from reef, which cannot decode the aes256k `client.admin` key already in `/etc/ceph/ceph.keyring`. The first import fails with `error reading file /etc/ceph/ceph.keyring`, so every `1-install/reef` + `workloads/rbd_cls` job fails before the workunit runs (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79948). Only the `client.admin` import was allowed to fail.

This PR allows either import to fail. The client then finds its own key in `/etc/ceph/ceph.client.N.keyring`, as it did before the merge step was added. When the host's `ceph-authtool` can read the keyring, both imports succeed as before, so nothing changes for other jobs.

This is a narrow fix for the merge step. It does not touch how the auth ID reaches the workunits (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78881), and it does not make `client.admin` aes. In the reef `rbd_cls` job below, the test ran with `CEPH_ID="2"` and every monitor command it sent came from `client.2`, using the aes key provisioned for it, not `client.admin`. Workunits that run as `client.admin` regardless of `CEPH_ID` still need 78881. The `upgrade-clients` failure reported on the tracker (`ceph-authtool ... --name=mgr.x` in `qa/tasks/ceph.py`) is a different code path and is not fixed here.

Testing: `rados/thrash-old-clients` `1-install/reef` `workloads/rbd_cls`, with the reef client pinned to v18.2.8 because the current reef build has no package metadata on shaman:
- main without this PR: the job fails at `ceph-authtool /etc/ceph/ceph.keyring --import-keyring /etc/ceph/ceph.client.2.keyring` (`error reading file`), the tracker's failure (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_11:41:18-rados:thrash-old-clients-main-distro-default-trial/).
- with this PR, in a batch with other QA fixes: both imports fail and are logged, `test_cls_rbd.sh` runs as `client.2` and passes 68 tests, and both jobs pass (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_11:41:12-rados:thrash-old-clients-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v6-261015-distro-default-trial/).
- in non-reef workunit jobs of the same batch, both imports still succeed.

72744.title: test/librados: retry fresh instances in PoolIsInSelfmanagedSnapsMode
72744.author: aainscow
72744.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. What has been shown so far (more under Testing below):
>
> - The cause was found in the logs of job 638584 (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_19:18:46-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v3-261014-distro-default-trial/): the fresh client read the osdmap from a monitor one epoch behind the pool deletion.
> - teuthology with this PR: `FreshInstance` passed in both `rados/verify` `tasks/rados_api_tests` jobs: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_06:56:10-rados-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_07:04:07-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/.
> - The race is rare, so these runs show that the retry does not break the test, not that the failure is gone.







`LibRadosPoolIsInSelfmanagedSnapsMode.FreshInstance` connects a new client after each pool change and expects it to see the change at once. A new client takes its first osdmap from whichever monitor it connects to, and a peon that has accepted the new version but not yet received the commit still serves the previous epoch (`Paxos::is_readable()` is true while updating). `wait_for_latest_osdmap()` would not help: the peon answers the version request with the same old epoch. (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64056)

In https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-14_19:18:46-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v3-261014-distro-default-trial/ (job 638584), the pool delete was committed in epoch 35 (reply at 20:01:17.071). The fresh client connected to mon.b 70 ms later, got epoch 34, and still found the pool:

```
snapshots_cxx.cc:591: Failure
Expected equality of these values:
  -2
  cluster2.pool_is_in_selfmanaged_snaps_mode(pool_name)
    Which is: 1
```

This PR retries with a new instance each time, for up to 30 seconds, until it sees the expected result. Each attempt is still a fresh instance, so the test still checks that a new client fetches the map before answering.

Testing: in a batch with other QA fixes, `FreshInstance` passed in both `rados/verify` `tasks/rados_api_tests` jobs (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_06:56:10-rados-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_07:04:07-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/). The race is rare, so this only shows the retry does not break the test.

72745.title: qa/tasks: ignore out-of-order full ratios set by the thrasher
72745.author: aainscow
72745.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - Replaying the cluster log scan of job 577494 (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/skanta-2026-09-24_03:23:39-rados-wip-bharath10-testing-20260924.010810-main-distro-default-trial/), with its 488 ERR/WRN/SEC lines and the job's ignorelist: without this PR 2 lines fail the job; with it, none.

`OSDThrasher.thrash_cluster_full()` sets the full ratio to .001 for about a second. While it is below the backfillfull ratio, the monitors raise `OSD_OUT_OF_ORDER_FULL`. The "Health check failed" line is already ignored by `\(OSD_`, but if the monitor writes its health detail to the cluster log inside that window, two more lines appear and fail the job (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/69497):

```
cluster [ERR] [ERR] OSD_OUT_OF_ORDER_FULL: full ratio(s) out of order
cluster [ERR]     full_ratio (0.001) < backfillfull_ratio (0.9), increased
```

In job 577494 (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/skanta-2026-09-24_03:23:39-rados-wip-bharath10-testing-20260924.010810-main-distro-default-trial/) the 10-minute forced health dump landed in the window.

This PR adds both to `qa/tasks/thrashosds-health.yaml`. In the thrash suites only the thrasher sets the ratios.

The change also ran in a batch of thrash jobs with other QA fixes (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_08:22:09-rados:thrash-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v6-261015-distro-default-trial/), which passed.

72746.title: mon/MonClient: do not reopen a session after shutdown()
72746.author: aainscow
72746.body:
`MonClient::shutdown()` clears its connections and sets `stopping`, but `_reopen_session()` does not check `stopping`. Any `renew_subs()` after `shutdown()` therefore opens new hunting connections. `OSD::shutdown()` shuts the MonClient down before the Objecter, and the Objecter tick renews the osdmap subscription every 10 s when idle, so an OSD can reconnect during shutdown. Those connections stay in `pending_cons` until the `MonClient` in `main()` is destroyed, after `main()` has deleted the messengers. valgrind then reports (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75133):

```
InvalidRead  AsyncConnection::mark_down() < MonConnection::~MonConnection() < ... < MonClient::~MonClient()
Address is 192 bytes inside a block of size 2,032 free'd   by operator delete[] in main
```

osd.1 of job 581641 (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/skanta-2026-09-25_03:59:04-rados-wip-bharath29-testing-20260924.231744-main-distro-default-trial/) logged the sequence: `monclient: shutdown`, then 1 ms later from the Objecter timer thread `_renew_subs`, `_reopen_session rank -1` and three `picked mon` lines. On main this error has been hidden behind the monitor OpenSSL leak (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79831), because teuthology reports only the first valgrind error.

This PR makes `_reopen_session()` return when `stopping`, as the other entry points that drop work after `shutdown()` already do. This covers every caller and every daemon. `init()` clears `stopping`, so a re-initialised MonClient still connects. https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72378 fixes a different `MonClient` messenger lifetime (`ping_monitor()`) and does not cover this.

Testing:
- New `unittest_mon_client_shutdown` points `mon_host` at a plain listening socket. `RenewSubsConnects` (control) checks that `renew_subs()` connects. `RenewSubsAfterShutdownDoesNotConnect` checks that it does not after `shutdown()`. It fails 5/5 without the fix and passes 5/5 with it, and is clean under valgrind.
- The race is timing-dependent. In a batch with other QA fixes, the OSD valgrind logs of the 3 `rados/verify` jobs had no errors (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_06:56:10-rados-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/, https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_07:04:07-rados:verify-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v5-261015-distro-default-trial/).

This PR and https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72742 both add a test to `src/test/mon/CMakeLists.txt`, so whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.

72747.title: qa/tasks/ceph_manager: thrash whole hosts in and out
72747.author: aainscow
72747.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This fix has NOT BEEN REVIEWED by a human. It is being done with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. This is why the commits have no Signed-off-by.







The host thrashers (`thrashers/*_host`, `min_in: 2`) take hosts out as a whole but bring OSDs back one at a time. With `2-size-2-min-size` they can leave, for example, one in OSD on each of two hosts. CRUSH (`chooseleaf firstn 0 type host`) then maps about 7% of PGs to a single OSD, and those PGs stay `undersized+peered`, which is inactive. The clean interval waits for recovery without marking any OSD in, so `wait_for_recovery` times out (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/70279).

In job 593732 (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/skanta-2026-09-30_04:36:41-rados-wip-bharath14-testing-20260930.003013-main-distro-default-trial/), after `Removing all OSDs in host trial142` only osd.12 and osd.13 were in, on different hosts. radosbench created a 16-PG pool, PGs 6.0, 6.4, 6.c and 6.e mapped to `up [12] acting [12]`, and recovery never finished.

`crushtool --test --num-rep 2` on a 4-host x 4-OSD map gives the share of PGs mapped to one OSD:

| In OSDs | PGs mapped to 1 OSD |
|---|---|
| 1 OSD on each of 2 hosts (job 593732) | 6.8% |
| 1 whole host + 1 OSD of another | 3.5% |
| 2 whole hosts | 0 |

This PR keeps hosts whole. A new `in_host()` revives and marks in every OSD of a host with out OSDs, and the host thrashers use it instead of `in_osd()`. `out_host()` also requires at least `min_in_hosts` (default 2) other hosts with in OSDs. https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67860 (opt-in min_size protection when killing OSDs) is complementary.

Testing:
- New `qa/tasks/tests/test_thrash_hosts.py` drives `choose_action()`'s in/out actions on a mocked 4x4 cluster and checks that every host is all in or all out, with at least two hosts in. Without the fix it fails (`host2 is partly in`); with the fix it passes.
- teuthology `rados/thrash` with `2-size-2-min-size` and each of `pggrow_host`, `default_host`, `careful_host` and `mapgap_host`: all passed, and `in_host()` ran 25 times (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_08:22:09-rados:thrash-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v6-261015-distro-default-trial/ and the three runs after it). The original failure is intermittent, so this shows the change works, not that the failure is gone.

72748.title: librbd/deep_copy: keep clone whiteouts beyond a shrunk migration source
72748.author: aainscow
72748.body:
> [!WARNING]
> This PR was generated with AI assistance (Claude Code) to aid the productivity of the PR owner. It has not been reviewed by a human yet, which is why the commits have no Signed-off-by. The fix has been shown to work as follows (more under Testing below):
>
> - The new `TestMigration.CloneDiscardSnapShrink` fails on main for RBD_FEATURES 1, 61, 109 and 127, and passes with the fix.
> - `TestMigration.Stress` and `StressLive`, which hit this at random: 1 failure in 247 runs without the fix, 0 in 328 with it.
> - teuthology with this PR: `rbd/librbd` `c_api_tests_with_defaults` passed all 457 tests, including the 54 TestMigration tests: https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_08:32:08-rbd:librbd-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v6-261015-distro-default-trial/.







`ObjectCopyRequest::compute_zero_ops()` decides whether a clone's object is copied as a whiteout, an empty object that hides the parent data. It prunes the destination snapshot's parent overlap with `prune_parent_extents(..., migration_write=false)`, which clamps the overlap to the parent's size. During a migration the destination's parent is the migration source opened at HEAD. If the source shrank after a snapshot, the objects between the new size and that snapshot's overlap get no overlap, and their whiteouts are not copied. Reads before commit still go through the source, so the data looks right. After commit, that snapshot reads the parent's data instead of zeros (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/70847):

```
after commit snap: snap2, block 79691776~4194304 differs
```

Write paths already pass `migration_write = true` for migrating images. This PR does the same in `compute_zero_ops()` for migration copies (`OBJECT_COPY_REQUEST_FLAG_MIGRATION`). Other deep copies (`rbd deep cp`, rbd-mirror) are unchanged.

Testing:
- New `TestMigration.CloneDiscardSnapShrink`: write the last object in the parent, snapshot and clone, discard that object in the clone, snapshot, shrink to half, migrate. Without the fix it fails for RBD_FEATURES 1, 61, 109 and 127; with the fix it passes.
- `TestMigration.Stress` and `StressLive`, which hit this at random: 1 failure in 247 runs without the fix, 0 in 328 with it. TestMigration.*, TestDeepCopy* and the deep copy mock tests pass for RBD_FEATURES 0, 1, 61, 109 and 127.
- teuthology `rbd/librbd` `c_api_tests_with_defaults` in a batch with other QA fixes: 457 tests passed, including all 54 TestMigration tests (https://pulpito-ng.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-10-15_08:32:08-rbd:librbd-wip-aainscow-rados-qa-fixes-v6-261015-distro-default-trial/).

Not covered: `io::CopyupRequest::compute_deep_copy_snap_ids()` also prunes with `migration_write=false` on a migrating image. It may have the same clamp, but I have not reproduced a failure from it.

72749.title: cephadm: Properly support bootstrap of an IPv6-only cluster
72749.author: wido
72749.body:
When trying to deploy a IPv6-only cluster using cephadm one can run into problems where cephadm does not properly parse the IPv6 addresses and thus deployment fails.

This PR addresses that problem as it allows for smooth deployment of IPv6-only environments and adds tests to ensure this functionality keeps working.

I verified this PR on a local test deployment where the nodes had no IPv4 connectivity at all.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/58644

# Initial deployment
```sh
cephadm --image quay.io/ceph/ceph:v21 bootstrap \
    --mon-ip 2a14:9b80::2001 \
    --shared_ceph_folder /root/ceph \
    --skip-monitoring-stack --skip-dashboard \
    --ssh-user root
```

# Add nodes
```sh
cat /etc/ceph/ceph.pub >> /root/.ssh/authorized_keys   # on ceph02, ceph03

ceph orch host add ceph03 2a14:9b80::2003   # explicit address
ceph orch host add ceph02                   # hostname only
```

# Add OSDs
```sh
ceph config set mgr mgr/cephadm/use_agent true
ceph orch daemon add osd ceph01:/dev/sdb
ceph orch daemon add osd ceph02:/dev/sdb
ceph orch daemon add osd ceph03:/dev/sdb
```

# Ceph Health
```

72757.title: osd: fix the lower bound of the purged snaps request to the monitor
72757.author: ronen-fr
72757.body:
OSDMonitor::preprocess_get_purged_snaps() treats MMonGetPurgedSnaps'
'start' as an exclusive bound: it seeks with upper_bound(). But
OSD::_get_purged_snaps() sent purged_snaps_last + 1. Thus the purged
snaps of epoch purged_snaps_last + 1 were never fetched, while the
reply still advanced purged_snaps_last past that epoch.

This happens, for example, after the OSD missed some OSDMaps: from
then on, handle_osd_map() stops recording purged snaps (its new maps
do not start at purged_snaps_last + 1), and the next boot fetches them
from the monitor - skipping the first missing epoch. The OSD then has
no purged_snaps rows for that epoch's snaps, so the purged snaps scrub
cannot detect stray clones of those snaps.

Send purged_snaps_last itself.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81806

72759.title: debian: fix ceph-mgr restarts and missing modules after the mgr module split
72759.author: ThomasLamprecht
72759.body:
Since ceph-mgr-modules-core was split into per-module packages, every module package restarts a running ceph-mgr from its postinst. One upgrade configures about twenty of them, which exceeds the StartLimitBurst=3 of ceph-mgr@.service, so the manager then stays down with start-limit-hit, while apt reports success.

The first commit drops these restarts, in line with the --no-restart-after-upgrade used for all other daemons.

The second commit makes the ceph meta-package depend on ceph-mgr-modules-standard to ensure that hosts that don't install recommended packages also lose the modules formerly shipped in ceph-mgr-modules-core.
Using the meta package avoids a dependency loop with the module packages, which would come from depending on it in ceph-mgr itself.

72761.title: mon: clear stale health checks after re-election and rebuild the aggregate check
72761.author: kamoltat
72761.body:
Problem:
MON_DOWN can stay in the cluster health status after all monitors have rejoined quorum. The aggregate health checks may retain the old warning even when the leader and peon health checks no longer report it.

e.g.,
When mon.e went down, the leader reported MON_DOWN and the health
service committed it in the aggregate health checks.

After mon.e rejoined quorum, the current peon and leader health
checks no longer included MON_DOWN, but the committed aggregate still
did. Since the health tick only proposed an update when the source
checks changed, it could miss this inconsistency when those checks were
already clear. As a result, ceph health continued to report the old
MON_DOWN warning.

Solution:
Compare the aggregate health checks against the current leader and peon checks during health ticks. Rebuild the aggregate from current checks when proposing an update, so cleared checks like MON_DOWN are removed. Add unit tests for removing stale checks while keeping current checks.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81206
Assisted-by: Copilot 
Signed-off-by: Kamoltat (Junior) Sirivadhna [ksirivad@redhat.com](mailto:ksirivad@redhat.com)

72774.title: mgr/cephadm: split service implementations into dedicated modules
72774.author: rkachach
72774.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81831

## Description

This PR reorganizes the cephadm service implementations to improve code organization, readability, and maintainability.

Currently, `cephadmservice.py` contains both the common service abstractions and multiple concrete service implementations, while `monitoring.py` contains all monitoring service handlers in a single file.

The changes introduce a clearer separation between shared service infrastructure and individual service implementations.

### Changes

- Move concrete service handlers (`MonService`, `MgrService`, `RgwService`, etc.) from `cephadmservice.py` into dedicated Python modules.
- Keep shared service abstractions and helpers in `cephadmservice.py`.
- Move monitoring service handlers into a new `services/monitoring/` package, with one module per service.
- Update affected imports and unit tests.
- Add regression coverage for service discovery and registration.
- Preserve the existing `@register_cephadm_service` decorator and service registry mechanism.

### Scope

**This is a code organization/refactoring change only. No functional or behavioral changes are intended.**

The existing service implementations, configuration generation, deployment logic, and lifecycle behavior are preserved.

The goal is to make individual services easier to navigate, review, test, and maintain without changing how cephadm operates.

### Testing

- Updated existing unit tests to account for the new module locations.
- Added regression tests for service registration and discovery.
- Verified Python syntax and patch consistency.

This PR enhances the NVMe-oF Dashboard UI to support configuring network masks at the **Gateway Group** level and automatically inheriting them during **Subsystem creation**, following backend changes introduced in https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72466.

  * It is **checked by default**.

  * On submission, the subsystem inherits the group's network masks automatically.
* **Condition B (User opts out to specify a custom subnet mask):**

72776.title: rgw/multisite: pass the data sync status to the shard control coroutine
72776.author: lumir-sliva
72776.body:
## Summary
When a bucket's full sync fails during a data sync full sync, the bucket is dropped for good: failed full sync obligations never reach the error repo. Since 1985a16a62d (v18.0.0), so reef, squid, tentacle and main.

## Problem
- `RGWDataSyncShardControlCR` takes the data sync status in its constructor and has a member of the same name, but never initialises it, so `RGWDataSyncShardCR` and the full sync coroutines get an empty copy.
- `timestamp_for_bucket_shard()` finds no marker in it and returns 0 for every bucket shard.
- `RGWDataSyncSingleEntryCR` only parks obligations with a timestamp, and the "Write N to error repo" writes in `RGWDataFullSyncSingleEntryCR` are no-ops (`rgw::error_repo::write` is a `cmp_set_vals` GT against 0).
- The shard goes incremental and removes the full sync index; the bucket only syncs after a later write to it or a `bucket sync run`.

## Fix
Store the status. Full sync obligations then carry their datalog shard's `last_update`, as 1985a16a62d intended, and a failed one is retried by the incremental sync's error repo pass like any other failed obligation.

## Test
Two zones on one box: `data sync init` on the secondary, every object sync failing with `rgw_sync_data_inject_err_probability=1` until the data sync shards are incremental, then cleared over the admin socket.

| | main | with the fix |
|---|---|---|
| objects on the secondary after clearing | 0 of 30 after 210 s, 3 of 3 runs | 30 of 30 after ~55 s, 3 of 3 runs |
| error repo | nothing written | obligation parked with the shard's timestamp, retried once |

No multisite suite test: the suite has no fault injection for a full sync failure. The reproducer script is on the tracker.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81830

72777.title: rgw/multisite: defer datalog entries a stale period cannot resolve
72777.author: lumir-sliva
72777.body:
## Summary
A zone that comes back after the metadata master moved can lose, for good, the objects written to buckets that were created on the new master while it was away. No error, nothing in `sync error list`, and `sync status` says caught up.

## Problem
The returning zone starts on its local period, in which it is still the metadata master itself. The new master's period push only lands later, because the pusher backed off while the zone was unreachable (`rgw_period_push_interval_max`, 30 s by default). Until then:

- data sync processes the new master's datalog, finds no local instance for the new bucket, and `RGWSyncGetBucketInfoCR` fetches it from `get_master_conn()`, i.e. from itself. Its own access log shows the `GET /admin/metadata/bucket.instance/...` answered 404.
- `RGWMetaSyncSingleEntryCR` takes the 404 as "deleted", `RGWGetBucketPeersCR` tolerates the `-ENOENT`, the pipe set comes back empty and `RGWRunBucketSourcesSyncCR` completes with `r=0`.
- the shard marker moves past the entry, nothing is written to the error repo, and nothing ever revisits it.

The same happens without a restart when a link cut heals after the master moved.

## Fix
Before giving a bucket up on that 404, read the realm from the zone that logged the entry (`GET /admin/realm` over the data sync source connection) and compare realm epochs:

- source on a newer realm epoch than our current period: the 404 came from a master the realm no longer has. Return `-ESTALE`; `RGWDataSyncSingleEntryCR` writes the entry to the error repo and completes it, so it's retried on the error repo's backoff until the period push lands and the realm reload restarts sync.
- equal epochs: the 404 is authoritative and the bucket is skipped as before, so a bucket deleted on the master still converges.
- realm read fails: return that error, not `-ENOENT`.

The instance is never fetched from the source zone, which would resurrect buckets deleted on the master and not yet on the source.

The parked entry completes instead of failing because a failed entry fails the whole data sync shard: the restarted shard retries its entire error repo at once, and with writes still arriving on the new master that repeats on every poll. Out-of-band notifications carry no timestamp and can't be parked; they complete as well, since their datalog entry follows and is parked then.

In full sync the deferral only gets parked once full sync obligations carry a timestamp, which they currently never do: #72776 (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81830). Without it the full sync case behaves as it does on main.

## Test
Two zones from `test-rgw-multisite.sh` on one box: zone 1 (master) stopped, zone 2 promoted, a bucket with 5 objects created on zone 2, zone 1 restarted. Zone 2's push is delayed with `rgw_period_push_interval{,_max}=120` so that zone 1's data sync always gets to the entry first.

| | main | with the fix |
|---|---|---|
| bucket created during the outage | lost in 5 of 5 runs | 0 lost in 2 runs |
| same, client writing to the bucket and to 10 new ones during the 232 s window, `rgw_data_notify_interval_msec=200` | | 105 of 105 objects, 10 of 10 buckets, 0 shard restarts, 0 entry errors |

Earlier iterations of the same approach lost nothing in another 11 runs. While the zone is stale, each entry touching an unresolvable bucket costs two extra requests (the self-lookup and the realm GET), 185 over the 232 s window above; they stop with the push.

The second commit adds `test_bucket_created_during_master_outage`, which raises the push interval on the secondary's cluster with `config set` to hit the window every time. On main it fails at `zone_bucket_checkpoint` after 526 s; with the fix it passes in 352 s. `test_multi_period_incremental_sync` passes with the fix (with #72671 on top for the unrelated https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81758).

72778.title: rgw/multisite: do not report metadata sync caught up on an old period
72778.author: lumir-sliva
72778.body:
## Summary
`radosgw-admin sync status` prints "metadata is caught up with master" for a zone whose metadata sync is still on an older period than the realm's current one, which is exactly the state an operator runs it for after a master change.

## Problem
`get_md_sync_status()` (`src/rgw/radosgw-admin/radosgw-admin.cc`) compares the sync's period with the zone's own current period, not the master's: the variable is called `master_period`, but it holds the local `get_current_period_id()`. Both cases reproduce with three zones on one box, zone 3's gateway down while the master moves from zone 1 to zone 2:

- Zone 3 missed the period push, so its local period is the old one too. Sync and local period match, the shards are compared against the master's mdlog of that old period, and the output says caught up with no hint at all.
- After `realm pull` on zone 3 (gateway still down) the local period is the new one. The command prints "master is on a different period", skips the shard comparison, counts nothing as behind and prints "metadata is caught up with master" right below.

## Fix
Ask the master for the realm's current period (`GET /admin/realm` over the master connection, the endpoint `realm pull` uses; the local period stays the fallback if the request fails) and compare the sync's period and realm epoch against it. When they differ, the output names the sync's period, the local one if that is stale as well, and the master's, says how many periods metadata sync is behind, and never says caught up. The shard comparison is unchanged and still only runs when the sync is on the local period, whose mdlog is the one fetched. The old "master is on a different period" line is replaced.

## Test
Case 1 before:
```
                incremental sync: 64/64 shards
                metadata is caught up with master
```
Case 1 after:
```
                incremental sync: 64/64 shards
                metadata sync is on period 52892c11-... (realm epoch 2)
                local period 52892c11-... (realm epoch 2) is not the master's current period
                master is on period 67fa9171-... (realm epoch 3)
                metadata is 1 period behind the master
```
Case 2 prints the same without the "local period" line.

The second commit adds `test_sync_status_metadata_period_behind`, covering both cases and checking that the output says caught up again once the zone is back (3 zones, 1 gateway each). On main it fails at `assert 'metadata is caught up with master' not in status`; with the fix it passes in 79 s. `test_multi_period_incremental_sync` fails on current main regardless of this change (zone 3 ends up on a period id the other zones don't have, https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81758); with #72671 on top it passes with this change as well.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81763

72779.title: doc/dev: design for EC direct reads with client-side decode
72779.author: aainscow
72779.body:
Design document for extending EC direct reads (Fast EC only) so that clients almost never need to go via the primary OSD for reads.

## Summary

- **Client-side decode:** when a needed data shard is unavailable in the client's OSDMap, `ECSplitOp` reads enough data and coding shards directly and decodes in the client.
- **Primary fallback:** `-EAGAIN`-class conditions (object missing on the shard, unstable write, interval change, torn-read version mismatch), shard errors, ordered (`RWORDERED`) reads and complex operations still go via the primary. Fallback happens at most once per op.
- **Shared code:** read planning and decode are extracted from `ECCommon::ReadPipeline` into `ECUtil` (`plan_read()` / `complete_read()`) and linked into both the OSD and `libceph-common`.
- **OSD/Mon:** new op flag for shard-space reads (needed for coding shards), gated by a new `ec_client_decode` pool flag that the monitor only allows once `require_osd_release` reaches V.
- **RGW:** covers all RGW data read paths, and proposes RGW requesting balanced reads and no object version on data reads.

The doc follows the design doc template, including requirements, user stories, CLI, failure modes, a correctness argument, upgrade, counters and the test plan. Open questions are listed at the end.

## Notes for reviewers

- The correctness argument (C1) depends on two existing mechanisms that need confirming: primary reads wait behind in-flight writes via the object-context lock, and `can_serve_read()` also covers coding shards.
- The doc points out that `SplitOp::assemble_rc()` currently returns non-`EAGAIN` shard errors (e.g. `-EIO`) to the application instead of falling back to the primary.

72782.title: script/build-with-container: rebuild the image when debian/control changes
72782.author: aainscow
72782.body:
`build-with-container.py` reuses a cached build image while the hash of the files in `_CONTAINER_SOURCES` is unchanged. On Debian and Ubuntu, `install-deps.sh` installs the `Build-Depends` of `debian/control`, but that file is not in the list. So a change to the build dependencies there does not rebuild a cached image.

https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72402 (merged 2026-10-16) added `autoconf-archive` to `debian/control` for the new qatlib's `autogen.sh`. Ubuntu images built before it still pass the source check, and the qatlib configure step then fails in them:

```
configure.ac:29: error: AX_PTHREAD not found. Please install autoconf-archive or place ax_pthread.m4 in m4/
```

Jenkins `ceph-pr-pipeline` runs 5168 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71449), 5185 and 5204 (https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72643) failed this way. In 5185 and 5204 the amd64 image was reused ("Container image ceph-build:origin-pr-72643-merge.ubuntu22.04.amd64 present", "Container passes source check") before the failure, and run 5190 of the same PR, which built a fresh amd64 image, passed the qatlib configure step.

This change adds `debian/control` to `_CONTAINER_SOURCES`.

Tested by hashing the sources with `_hash_sources()` before and after appending a line to `debian/control`: without this change the hash is the same, and with it the hash changes. There are no unit tests for this script.

72788.title: mgr/telemetry: fix crash in anonymize_entity_name() when salt is unset
72788.author: SohamDutta02
72788.body:
anonymize_entity_name() falls back to a temporary salt when self.salt has not been loaded yet, but the fallback assigns to the module-level NO_SALT_CNT without a 'global' declaration. Python therefore treats NO_SALT_CNT as a local variable and reading it raises UnboundLocalError, so the one case the fallback exists for always crashes.

self.salt is None until serve() calls load(), so a report compiled before that point (e.g. 'ceph telemetry preview' or the dashboard's get_report_locked() call racing mgr startup or failover) fails in the perf channel, where non-OSD daemon names are anonymized.

Use a random uuid4 as the one-off salt instead of the counter. This keeps the original intent of not persisting a temporary salt, and avoids the predictable 'no_salt_found_<n>' salt, which would make the resulting hashes easy to reverse for short daemon names.

Add regression tests for the salted and unsalted paths.

72789.title: build-with-container,install-deps: stop reusing CI build images with the wrong contents
72789.author: djgalloway
72789.body:
Two fixes for `build-with-container.py` images that passed its "source check" but did not match the sources, which ceph-pr-pipeline hit hard on 2026-10-16 (35 of 150 failed runs, 23 PRs, main/squid/tentacle):

1. **Hash `debian/`.** `Dockerfile.build` copies `debian/` into the image (install-deps installs the Build-Depends from `debian/control`), but `_CONTAINER_SOURCES` didn't include it, so a `debian/control` change never invalidated a cached image. 36c42fdc94e (autoconf-archive for the qatlib bump) merged at 04:26 UTC and every builder with an existing image for a PR kept using it: `configure.ac:29: error: AX_PTHREAD not found` in 13 runs within hours. Directories are now walked and each path name is hashed with its contents. Every existing image misses the new hash once and gets rebuilt — intended.

2. **Opt-in `REQUIRE_BOOST_PKGS`: fail when ceph-libboost can't be installed.** `install_boost_on_ubuntu` only `ci_debug`s when the shaman/chacra fetch fails and leaves boost to the submodule. That fallback is right for developers and package builds, but in CI it can yield an image without `/opt/ceph` boost that is kept for a week; ceph-pr-pipeline moves one build tree between builders, so a tree configured against `/opt/ceph` boost 1.87 lands in such an image and dies with `Could NOT find Boost: Found unsuitable version "0.0.0"` or `ceph-conf: error while loading shared libraries: libboost_thread.so.1.87.0` (~20 runs, 10 PRs).

   With `REQUIRE_BOOST_PKGS` non-empty, `install_boost_on_ubuntu` exits non-zero instead, so the image build fails while shaman is unreachable rather than succeeding with the wrong contents. It is **off by default**. `Dockerfile.build` takes it as a build arg and passes it to `buildcontainer-setup.sh`; CI turns it on with `build-with-container.py --build-arg=REQUIRE_BOOST_PKGS=1` (bwc's existing `--build-arg`). ceph/ceph-build#2748 does that for ceph-pr-pipeline only.

   *Changed after review:* the first version keyed this off `FOR_MAKE_CHECK`, which was the wrong signal — `run-make-check.sh` sets it for developers too, and the check also fired on bwc's `FOR_MAKE_CHECK=false` package-build images (`-n` on the raw value). `JENKINS_HOME` / `in_jenkins` doesn't work either, since `buildcontainer-setup.sh` sets it in every bwc image build.

Backports: ceph/ceph#72985 (squid), #72986 (tentacle), #72987 (umbrella), tracked in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81983. All three branches already have bwc's `--build-arg` (backported earlier), so `REQUIRE_BOOST_PKGS` works there once the ARG lands. *(An earlier version of this note said they lacked `--build-arg`; that was a mistake in my check.)*

Testing: the boost fallback with a stubbed `install_pkg_on_ubuntu` under every combination (unset, `FOR_MAKE_CHECK=1`, `FOR_MAKE_CHECK=false`, `REQUIRE_BOOST_PKGS=1` alone and with `FOR_MAKE_CHECK=false`, empty `REQUIRE_BOOST_PKGS`) — it fails only when `REQUIRE_BOOST_PKGS` is non-empty. A podman build of the edited `Dockerfile.build` stanza confirms the build arg reaches the setup step, defaulting to empty.
