73321.title: doc/cephfs: explain large omap objects in the metadata pool
73321.author: anthonyeleven
73321.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/43034

No CephFS page says what to do when `LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS` names an object in a metadata pool. The entry in `doc/rados/operations/health-checks.rst` covers only RGW bucket index objects. This adds a "Large omap objects in the metadata pool" section to `doc/cephfs/health-messages.rst` and links it from that entry.

- Cause: with the defaults, a fragment splits at `mds_bal_split_size` (10000 head and snapshot entries, `CDir::should_split()`) and stops taking creates at `mds_bal_fragment_size_max` (100000), both well below the 200000-key threshold. In practice, the warning comes from the 1 GiB value threshold, as in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77513.
- Object to path: dirfrag objects are named `<ino>.<frag>` (`InodeStoreBase::get_object_name`). A directory's backtrace is stored in the metadata pool on `<ino>.00000000` (`CInode::get_backtrace_pool`), and `ceph-dencoder` decodes it as `inode_backtrace_t`.
- Fix: `scrub start <path>` scrubs every fragment of the directory and calls `maybe_fragment()` afterward (`ScrubStack.cc:559`). That splits on entry count only, so for a fragment that is too large only in bytes, the section gives `dirfrag ls` and `dirfrag split`. Both need the directory in the cache of its auth MDS (`MDSRank::_command_dirfrag_get`).
- Directories the MDS won't fragment: root (`1.00000000`), stray directories (`MDBalancer::maybe_fragment`), mdsdir, and anything inside a stray directory (`MDCache::can_fragment`).
- RGW bucket index objects point to the dynamic resharding page.

A second commit adds to `LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS` in `doc/rados/operations/health-checks.rst` what the object usually is, by pool. It only adds lines after the existing paragraph, whose wording differs on tentacle, so both commits cherry-pick cleanly to umbrella and tentacle.
- In an RGW log pool, it's usually an untrimmed log. Usage logs (`usage.<n>`) need `usage trim`. `RGWSyncLogTrimThread` trims the metadata log, the data log, and bucket index logs every `rgw_sync_log_trim_interval`, but never the sync error log (`sync error trim` is manual).
- In an RGW index pool, it's a bucket index shard. Those need resharding, or, in multisite deployments, `bilog trim` after sync catches up. Beginning with the Vampire release, new buckets use FIFO bilogs in the log pool (`rgw_default_bucket_bilog_type`, `rgw_bilog.h`).
- In a CephFS metadata pool, it links the new section.
- It also says that changing `pg_num` doesn't help, since an object and its omap stay in one PG, and that the warning can outlast a split or merge until the next deep scrub.

It adds the `rgw-trim-usage` and `rgw-multisite-check-the-logs` labels so those sections can be linked.

@dparmar18's #72152 "mds: consider dirfrag size when splitting a dir" adds `mds_bal_split_bytes` and documents byte-based splits in `dirfrags.rst`. Once it merges, the "too large only in bytes" paragraph here can say that a scrub splits those fragments too. This PR doesn't touch `dirfrags.rst`, to stay clear of that one.

@vshankar @dparmar18, could you check the procedure, in particular that `dirfrag split` is the right tool for a byte-heavy fragment on current releases, and the advice for stray directories?

73322.title: mds: fix rejoin when a dirfrag holding replicated inodes is missing
73322.author: xiubli
73322.body:
When a dirfrag object is missing from the metadata pool and a surviving
rank holds replicas of inodes in it, the rank taking over the failed rank
never leaves `up:rejoin`.  The survivor rejoins those inodes, the
recovering rank invents them as REJOINUNDEF and has to load the dirfrag
in `open_undef_inodes_dirfrags()`, the object is gone, and:

- with `mds_dir_prefetch = true`, `go_bad()` marks the dirfrag complete,
  but the inodes stay undef; the next `rejoin_gather_finish()` fetches
  the complete dirfrag again and hits `ceph_assert(!is_complete())` in
  `CDir::fetch()` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/54205), on every
  standby that takes the rank over;
- with `mds_dir_prefetch = false`, the keyed fetch leaves the dirfrag
  incomplete, and since 97e43ee7956 wakes the parked dentry waiters, so
  `rejoin_gather_finish()` fetches the same missing object again, about
  once per millisecond, for ever.

Reproduction steps and logs are in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82399.

This PR:

- marks a dirfrag BADFRAG and complete in `go_bad()` after a keyed fetch
  too, so that the woken waiters find nothing left to fetch;
- skips complete dirfrags in `open_undef_inodes_dirfrags()` and
  `open_ino_traverse_dir()`;
- drops the undef inodes that cannot be loaded from the cache of the
  recovering rank (`rejoin_trim_undef_inodes()`, which had no caller), so
  that the rejoin ack does not carry their empty inode bases, and makes
  the surviving ranks drop the replica dentries left out of the ack.
  Without this, the survivor overwrites its replica with the empty inode
  and, for a hard-linked file, crashes on the snaprealm assert in
  `CInode::decode_snap()`.  A remote link to a dropped inode is left
  dangling and returns ENOENT;
- adds `TestDamageRejoin` to `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_damage.py`.

Testing (vstart_runner, release build):

| test | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `TestDamageRejoin.test_rejoin_undef_inode_missing_dirfrag` | assert in `CDir::fetch()` | ok |
| `TestDamageRejoin.test_rejoin_undef_inode_missing_dirfrag_no_prefetch` | stuck in `up:rejoin` | ok |

73324.title: common: count all slow ops across OpTracker shards
73324.author: anthonyeleven
73324.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/67317
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/45871

The SLOW_OPS health check often reports fewer slow ops than an OSD has, frequently 0, next to a plausible oldest op age: "0 slow ops, oldest one blocked for 129 sec, osd.285 has slow ops". `ceph daemon osd.N dump_blocked_ops` on the same OSD lists the slow ops.

`OpTracker::visit_ops_in_flight` copies every shard's in-flight list into one vector and visits it. The slow op counters in `OSD::get_health_metrics` and `OpTracker::with_slow_ops_in_flight` return false at the first op younger than the complaint time. Before 57ebdc2a77e merged the shards into one vector to fix a deadlock, tracker 42780, that ended only the walk of the current shard. Now it ends the whole walk. Ops are dealt to the shards round robin, so on a busy OSD the first shard nearly always holds a young op, and the count covers about one of the `osd_num_op_tracker_shard` shards. The MDS uses the same shard count and takes its slow request count from `check_ops_in_flight`, so `MDS_SLOW_REQUEST` can be missed as well. The mon uses one shard and is not affected.

This sorts the gathered ops by initiation time before visiting them, after the locks are released, so a visitor that stops at the first young op has seen every older one. The sort runs only when the oldest op is already past the complaint time.

The new `unittest_tracked_op` puts a young op in shard 0 and slow ops in the other shards. On unpatched main all three cases fail, with a count of 0 instead of 3. With this change they pass.

A later note on 45871 describes a down OSD that keeps showing "0 slow ops" with a frozen age. That is a separate stale metric on the mgr side, and this PR does not change it.

Question for reviewers: is sorting inside `visit_ops_in_flight` preferred over changing each visitor to skip young ops instead of stopping? Sorting keeps the early-exit contract for every caller.

73326.title: osd/PrimaryLogPG: take an op's PG log version after its ops have run
73326.author: aainscow
73326.body:
On a pool with EC optimizations, an op with a CALL runs in a coroutine, and a cls read in it yields until the EC read completes. `execute_ctx()` took the op's PG log version before running the ops. While the CALL waits, the PG lock is free, and work that does not go through `do_op()` can take versions: the snap trimmer, watch timeouts, and ops whose async reads complete. The CALL then submits a version that is already used, and the primary aborts in `issue_repop()`, on `at_version >= projected_last_update` or on PGLog's `e.version > head`.

The version is now taken in `prepare_transaction()` after `do_osd_ops()` returns, where the op can no longer yield.

The new `TestClsRbd.object_map_update_while_a_write_reads` reproduces it: on main its FastEC case aborts the primary at `PGLog.h:675`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82471

73327.title: osd: add POOL_MIN_SIZE_TOO_LOW health warning
73327.author: FredNass
73327.body:
Raise a `POOL_MIN_SIZE_TOO_LOW` health warning when a pool's `min_size` lets the cluster acknowledge writes with no redundancy left:

- replicated pools with `size >= 2` and `min_size == 1`
- EC pools with `min_size <= k`. For `m == 1` the message recommends a profile with `m >= 2`, because `min_size = k+1` would equal `size` there and block I/O on any single failure.

The warning can be muted (`ceph health mute POOL_MIN_SIZE_TOO_LOW`) or disabled (`mon_warn_on_pool_min_size_too_low = false`).

This picks up #65718 by @MattyWilliams22, which the stale bot closed. The original commit is kept with its authorship. On the tracker, the author explained that the PR was dropped because QA tests started failing. This PR adds what was missing:

1. **QA environments.** #65718 only disabled the warning in `qa/tasks/ceph.conf.template`. Test clusters also come from:
   - `qa/tasks/cephadm.conf`: cephadm-based suites, with a default EC profile `k=2 m=1`
   - `src/vstart.sh`: `osd_pool_default_min_size = 1`; used by make check and the API/dashboard tests
   - `qa/standalone/ceph-helpers.sh`: the `run_mon` defaults
   - the rook CI cluster spec

   The warning is now off in all of them, in the same places that already turn off `POOL_NO_REDUNDANCY` and similar warnings.
2. **Fewer false positives.**
   - Pools with `size 1` are skipped, since `POOL_NO_REDUNDANCY` already reports them.
   - Stretch pools are skipped while in degraded stretch mode, where Ceph lowers `min_size` on purpose (see Stefan Kooman's note on the tracker).
3. **Robustness.** An unknown pool type no longer reaches `ceph_abort_msg()` in a health check; the pool is ignored.
4. **Tests.** New `qa/standalone/mon/health-pool-min-size.sh` covering replicated and EC cases, mute/unmute and disabling the option.

Open question for reviewers: should EC pools with `m=1` warn at all? Ceph defaults them to `min_size = k`, so every `m=1` pool will warn. I think that is the point of the tracker (several data-loss cases we see in the field involve `k+1` / `m=1` profiles), but it could be split into a separate check code if preferred.

Not done yet: a teuthology run. I don't have Sepia lab access. Could a RADOS maintainer schedule `rados` (and ideally `orch:cephadm` + `smoke`) against this branch?

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/66641
Supersedes: #65718

73328.title: mds: create the lock cache for a client that wants Dc or Du
73328.author: anthonyeleven
73328.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82472

Since "mds: prevent new lock cache cons when invalidating an existing one" (#54581; the squid backport #56406 is in 19.1.0 and later), the MDS never grants Dc or Du on a directory, so kernel clients mounted with `nowsync`, the default since 5.16, never send async creates or unlinks. `Locker::create_lock_cache()` returns unless the client already holds the bit for the operation, but a directory's allowed caps include Dc and Du only once a lock cache has set them in `lock_cache_allowed`, so neither ever happens.

The first commit checks the caps the client wants as well as the ones it holds. A kernel client with async dirops wants Dc and Du on a directory it has recently changed (`__ceph_caps_file_wanted()` adds `CEPH_CAP_ANY_DIR_OPS`), so the MDS still creates no lock cache for a client that won't use one, which is what that commit's second paragraph was after. The second commit adds `TestMisc.test_async_dirops_caps`: a kernel client mounted with `nowsync` creates and then unlinks files in a directory no other client uses, and the test waits for the MDS to issue Fx with Dc, then Fx with Du, on it.

Tested on a single-node 19.2.6 cluster with a 6.8 kernel client mounted with `nowsync`: mkdir, then 40 creates and 40 unlinks in the new directory, with `debug_mds 10`. The client wanted `pAsLsXsFsxcral` on the directory throughout.

| MDS | Issued after the creates | Issued after the unlinks | `create_lock_cache` log lines |
|---|---|---|---|
| 19.2.6 | `pAsLsXsFsx` | `pAsLsXsFsx` | 40 creates and 40 unlinks: "client cap lacks rights for lock cache" |
| 19.2.6 with this change | `pAsLsXsFsxc` | `pAsLsXsFsxcr` | one lock cache for create, one for unlink |

With the change, 200 files written in a new directory over `nowsync` were all there, with their contents, after remounting with `wsync`, and the MDS logged no asserts. I haven't run the new test under teuthology.

#73312 adds a note to `doc/cephfs/posix.rst` that MDSes since 19.1.0 don't grant these caps. Once both have merged, the note needs the release with this fix.

@vshankar @batrick

73329.title: umbrella: monitoring/ceph-mixin: scope test queries per dashboard
73329.author: anthonyeleven
73329.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78085

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69937
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78083

Umbrella has the same exposure as tentacle (#73253): 12 of the 106 panel/legend pairs that `ceph-cluster.feature` checks share their name with a different query on another dashboard (IOPS Read/Write with `cephfsdashboard`; the MGR, Monitor and OSD counts with `ceph-cluster`). So `run-tox-promql-query-test` can pass or fail depending on readdir order on the builder, as it did for #73085 on tentacle. From the main PR:

`get_dashboards_data()` keeps every query in a single map keyed by "<panel title>-<legendFormat>", but that id is not unique: several dashboards have a panel titled "IOPS", "OSDs" or "Throughput". The dashboard read last overwrites the earlier entry, so one query shadows another and never gets tested. glob() walks the files in filesystem order, so which query survives, and whether the test passes, depends on readdir.

run-tox-promql-query-test hit this in "Test IOPS Read" (ceph-cluster.feature): the scenario feeds ceph_osd_op_r but the id resolved to a CephFS pool panel.
```
    FAILED:
      expr: "sum(rate(ceph_pool_rd{cluster=~"mycluster|",  pool_id=~"UNSET VARIABLE"}[1m]))", time: 1m,
          exp:"{} 2.5E+01"
          got:"nil"
    HOOK-ERROR in after_scenario: AssertionError:
```
pool_id is "UNSET VARIABLE" because the scenario does not set $mdatapool, and no ceph_pool_rd series were fed, so the query returns nil. It only fails when readdir returns `cephfsdashboard` after `ceph-cluster-advanced`, so the earlier change that walked nested rows and made the winner deterministic did not fix it; it fixed which query wins, not that the wrong one can win.

Key the queries per dashboard (`data['queries'][<dashboard>][<id>]`) and have each .feature name its dashboard in a Background step. The lookup is confined to that dashboard, so a title/legend used elsewhere no longer shadows it. A duplicate within one dashboard is still an error, unless it is in a collapsed row.

`ceph-cluster.feature` covers `ceph-cluster-advanced`; the rest map to one dashboard each.

Clean cherry-pick of 1 commit, with the same line changes as on main.

73330.title: squid: mds: fix rejoin hang when dirfrag object is missing on disk
73330.author: anthonyeleven
73330.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81886

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71022
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79454

Squid has the same `CDir::go_bad()`, so a takeover MDS there can stay in up:rejoin indefinitely when a dirfrag object is missing or corrupt. The tentacle and umbrella backports are #73027 and #73028. From the main PR:

CDir::fetch_keys() parks its completion contexts in waiting_on_dentry instead of in the IO callback chain, but CDir::go_bad() (missing/corrupt dirfrag object) only woke WAIT_COMPLETE waiters, leaving the dentry waiters stranded.

During rejoin, MDCache::open_ino_traverse_dir() relies on those contexts (C_MDC_OpenInoTraverseDir) to resume the traversal.  When the dirfrag object is ENOENT, the traversal never resumes, so OpenFileTable::_prefetch_inodes() never reaches num_opening_inodes == 0, process_imported_caps() never re-runs, rejoin_gather keeps the local entry, and rejoin_send_rejoins() delays forever, wedging the MDS in up:rejoin.

Drain waiting_on_dentry in go_bad() and complete the waiters with -EIO.  The traversal then takes the do_open_ino() error path, asks peers, and finishes gracefully (as it already does for other open errors), letting the rejoin machinery proceed with the dir marked STATE_BADFRAG and recorded in the damage table.

Clean cherry-pick of 1 commit, with the same line changes as on main.

73340.title: qa/cephfs: apply fscrypt dummy encryption to ceph-fuse only in fs:wor…
73340.author: vshankar
73340.body:
…kload

The fscrypt facet (tasks/0-fscrypt) is merged into every fs:workload job, but client_fscrypt_dummy_encryption is a libcephfs option: the kernel client ignores it, so kclient jobs are described as with-fscrypt-dummy without running fscrypt.

The facet disables EC for every job. Commit 72e7040f7f8 added "ec_profile: [disabled]" to it, since an EC layout cannot be set on an fscrypt file system (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73461).

Move the facet under the ceph-fuse mount (mount/fuse/fscrypt), the only mount it applies to, and let each ceph-fuse job pick at random between fscrypt and no fscrypt, so that ceph-fuse also runs on EC data pools. kclient jobs on the EC objectstore facets get their EC data pool back, and job descriptions only mention fscrypt where it runs. Other mounts can add their own fscrypt facet, since each enables it differently.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82490

73342.title: crush, mon: make MAX AVAIL size-aware for multi-take CRUSH rules
73342.author: limhan-storage
73342.body:
`CrushWrapper::get_rule_weight_osd_map()` (`src/crush/CrushWrapper.cc:2556-2589`) does not match the placement logic of `crush_do_rule()` (`src/crush/mapper.c`) for multi-take CRUSH rules:

1. **Asymmetric root weights across `take` steps (e.g. hybrid SSD+HDD rules):**
   Commit `3bd34683e797` ([tracker #56650](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/56650) / PR #47189) accumulates raw subtree weights across all `CRUSH_RULE_TAKE` steps into a single `sum` before calling `_normalize_weight_map(sum, m, pmap)`, without inspecting `CHOOSE*` or `EMIT` steps. When `take` roots have different total weights (e.g. taking 1 replica from `default~ssd` and 1 from `default~hdd`), merging their raw weights makes each tier's share proportional to its bucket weight rather than the number of replicas emitted by each `take` scope.
2. **`arg1 <= 0` (`firstn 0`, `firstn -1`) and `EMIT` truncation require pool `size` ([tracker #19818](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/19818), [tracker #38624](https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/38624)):**
   In `crush_do_rule()`, `arg1 <= 0` resolves to `numrep += result_max` (`src/crush/mapper.c:942`), and `CRUSH_RULE_EMIT` clamps emitted items to `result_max - result_len` (`src/crush/mapper.c:1017`). Without pool `size`, rules using `firstn 0` / `firstn -1` or rules truncated at `EMIT` (such as `"choose 2 + choose 2 but pool size may only be 3"`) cannot be weighted accurately.
3. **`take osd.N` (`n >= 0`) overwrites `sum = 1.0`:**
   At `src/crush/CrushWrapper.cc:2578-2580`, a `CRUSH_RULE_TAKE` targeting a specific OSD (`n >= 0`) assigns `sum = 1.0`, overwriting any `sum` accumulated from previous `take` steps.

## Fix

1. Add a `size`-aware overload `CrushWrapper::get_rule_weight_osd_map(unsigned ruleno, int size, map<int,float> *pmap) const` that normalizes each `TAKE` scope against its own subtree weight sum, weighted by the number of items it emits after resolving `arg1 <= 0` against `size` and clamping at `EMIT` (using `int64_t` for intermediate width multiplication to avoid signed overflow).
2. In `PGMap::get_rules_avail()`, pass the pool `size` to `get_rule_avail(osdmap, ruleno, size)` when all pools using `ruleno` share a single `size`. Since `PGMapDigest` (`v = 5`) caches `avail_space_by_rule` per rule, if multiple pools with different `size` values share the same rule, fall back to the existing 2-argument overload rather than letting the first visited pool's `size` win. (If reviewers prefer bumping `PGMapDigest` to `v = 6` to key by `(ruleno, size)` or `pool_id`, happy to update).
3. Leave `OSDMap` callers (`check_pg_upmaps()`, `get_osds_weight()`, and `calc_rbs_fair()`) on the existing 2-argument overload in this PR so that neither upmap cancellation nor balancer targets / PG placement change on upgrade; balancer callers can be switched in a follow-up after #71053 lands.

73343.title: tentacle: mgr/MgrClient: send keepalives on the mgr session
73343.author: anthonyeleven
73343.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82492

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72720
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81784

Tentacle has the same `MgrClient` and the same receive-only idle check, so its OSDs and MDSs fault and re-establish their mgr sessions every `ms_connection_idle_timeout` in the same way. The main PR passed RADOS QA (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82145). From the main PR:


The mgr sends nothing back on a daemon's lossy mgr session, and `AsyncConnection`'s idle check counts only received traffic. So every OSD and MDS faults its mgr session once it has been open for `ms_connection_idle_timeout`, even though it reports every `mgr_stats_period` seconds. It then reconnects, authenticates again and declares all of its perf counters again. Daemons that connected together after a mgr failover stay in step, so they all reconnect to the mgr at the same moment.

MonClient avoids this by sending keepalives. After a report, `MgrClient` now sends one if half of the daemon's own `ms_connection_idle_timeout` has passed since the last, so the ack arrives well before the timeout. With the default 900 s timeout that is one keepalive every 450 s, not one per report. The mgr's messenger answers the keepalive itself, so nothing new reaches the mgr's dispatch path.

An earlier revision sent the keepalive from the mgr, so that daemons of any release would be fixed once the mgrs were upgraded. It is back in `MgrClient` because the daemon's idle timer is what closes the session, and only the daemon knows that timer's setting.

Clean cherry-pick of 1 commit, with the same line changes as on main. No follow-up fixes on main.

73345.title: deb/cephadm: only move the home of a user that has none
73345.author: insatomcat
73345.body:
The home directory check added by 65e2a33ee7 (#66394) is inverted: `usermod --home /var/lib/cephadm -m cephadm` runs whenever the cephadm user already has a home, instead of only when it has none (`/nonexistent`).

- When the home is already `/var/lib/cephadm`, usermod returns early and nothing breaks.
- When the cephadm user was created beforehand with another home (e.g. `/home/cephadm`), usermod refuses to move the home of a user that owns processes. On a live cluster the mgr keeps an ssh session open as cephadm, so every package upgrade fails:

```
usermod: user cephadm is currently used by process 5215
dpkg: error processing package cephadm (--configure):
 installed cephadm package post-installation script subprocess returned error exit status 8
```

73347.title: rgw/sts: cache OIDC provider JWKS for AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity
73347.author: next0262
73347.body:
Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82494

Every AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity request fetches the provider's discovery document and JWKS again. This caches them for `rgw_sts_jwks_cache_ttl` seconds (default 300, 0 disables caching), reducing provider round trips during pod rollouts and credential refreshes.

Entries are isolated by account or tenant, provider registration, and issuer. Unknown or missing `kid` values fetch fresh keys. Cached certificates are checked against the current registered thumbprints, and requests requiring endpoint verification cannot reuse an unverified entry.

`radosgw-admin oidc-provider invalidate-jwks-cache --provider-url <url> [--account-id <id>]` bumps a generation stored on the provider. Each RGW refetches after reading the new generation, including when an older fetch completes after invalidation. Removing a key from the remote JWKS alone still leaves it accepted until expiry unless the cache is invalidated; already-issued STS credentials retain their own expiration.

Validation covered 22 passing cache unit tests, relevant object builds, and a two-RGW vstart run with account isolation, repeated invalidation, and admin argument errors. The final help output matches `help.t`; cram itself was unavailable. The tested tree and the pushed tree are identical.

73348.title: rgw/sts: do not crash on an unparsable certificate in is_cert_valid
73348.author: next0262
73348.body:
Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82495

`is_cert_valid()` passes the result of `PEM_read_bio_X509()` to `X509_digest()` without checking whether parsing succeeded. An unparsable certificate leaves a null pointer, which can crash radosgw when its digest is calculated.

With `rgw_enable_jwks_url_verification` disabled (the default), this input comes from the `x5c` entries in the OIDC provider's JWKS. A malformed entry can therefore crash the daemon during `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity`.

Return `false` when the certificate does not parse, as for a certificate whose thumbprint does not match.

Not built or tested locally.

73355.title: exporter, mgr/prometheus: name the unit in HELP for time and byte counters
73355.author: anthonyeleven
73355.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/78090

The HELP text of a latency sum such as `ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum` names no unit, so blog posts and how-tos have guessed milliseconds or microseconds, while Ceph's own Grafana dashboards treat the values as seconds. This puts the unit in the HELP text, as @afreen23 suggested on the tracker issue, rather than in the metric names, which would break existing dashboards and alerts.

- ceph-exporter and mgr/prometheus append ` (seconds)` to the HELP text of every time counter, and ` (bytes)` to every counter that declares `UNIT_BYTES`. For a long-running average the unit goes on `<name>_sum`; `<name>_count` stays a plain count. Timestamps kept as time counters get ` (seconds)` too, meaning seconds since the epoch.
- 34 counters that hold byte counts didn't declare `UNIT_BYTES`, for example `op_w_in_bytes` and `recovery_bytes` in the OSD and `omap_setkeys_bytes` in BlueStore. They now do, so their HELP text names the unit and `perf schema` reports `"units": "bytes"` for them. Their values, names and priorities don't change.
- A new make check test, `src/test/check-perf-counter-units.py`, scans the `PerfCountersBuilder` declarations and fails when a u64 counter named for bytes doesn't declare `UNIT_BYTES`, or when a latency is kept in a u64 counter without its unit in the name (`avg_read_lat_msec` passes). Without this PR it flags 26 counters on main, including `root_rbytes` in the MDS, which is declared here too.

```
# HELP ceph_osd_op_r_latency_sum Latency of read operation (including queue time) Total (seconds)
# HELP ceph_osd_op_w_in_bytes Client data written (bytes)
```

Thanks to @afreen23 for the direction, and to Somanchi Poorna Sobhita for tracing where the HELP text is built. The documentation side of the issue is covered by #72863.

Testing:
- `unittest_exporter`: all 6 tests pass, with the HELP expectations updated for the time and byte counters in its fixtures.
- `prometheus/test_module.py`: 76 passed.
- `ctest -R check-perf-counter-units`: passes.
- All 12 changed C++ files compile on main 0f8fa6b9ce7, including the RBD write-back cache (`WITH_RBD_SSD_CACHE=ON`).

73356.title: doc/rados: modernize PG Calc and add FD Calc
73356.author: anthonyeleven
73356.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82513
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64905

Two commits: a rewrite of PG Calc, and a new FD Calc page beside it.

### PG Calc

The PG Calc page restored in eaaf7225312 loads the old ceph.com WordPress theme stylesheets, jQuery, and jQuery UI from web.archive.org and Google, and `pgcalc.js` is the Wayback Machine's rewritten copy of the old script. The theme stylesheets restyle the docs page around the calculator, its table runs past the content column, and **Generate Commands** navigates to a `data:` URL, which current browsers block, so it does nothing.

This rewrites `pgcalc.js` in plain JavaScript with its own CSS and nothing loaded from other sites. The suggested PG count is unchanged for a given size: 200,000 random inputs give the same count as the previous code.

- Each pool has an application and is replicated or erasure coded, with its own *k* (at least 2) and *m* (at least 1). An erasure-coded pool counts *k+m* shards.
- **Generate Commands** creates a replicated CRUSH rule, and an erasure-code profile and CRUSH rule for each *k* and *m*, with a chosen failure domain and CRUSH root; then each pool with its rule, its size or profile, `allow_ec_overwrites` for erasure-coded RBD and CephFS pools, and its application (`rbd pool init` for replicated RBD pools). It shows them with Copy and Download buttons and leaves out removed pools.
- A pool is marked red, and left out of the commands, when OSD # is less than its size or *k+m*, so its PGs can't be placed. A pool is marked amber when it has fewer than three replicas or *m=1*. Erasure coding for an RGW index or metadata pool or a CephFS metadata pool draws a warning that a future release may support it but most deployments should stick with replication, and *k* above 8 draws one that writes and rebuilds slow down for diminishing savings in space, linking the EC overhead table in the latest docs.
- A column heading opens a native dialog to set that value for every pool, and **Add pool** adds a row directly.
- The RGW presets use the pools that RGW creates today (`.rgw.root`, `default.rgw.{control,meta,log}`, `default.rgw.buckets.{index,non-ec,data}`), the Infernalis-era presets are gone, CephFS and erasure-coded RGW presets are added, and All-in-One puts 100% of the data in `rbd` rather than 200%.
- The calculator renders into `pgcalc-root`, because Sphinx gives the anchor for the page's `pgcalc` label the id `pgcalc`, ahead of the calculator.

The instructions, field descriptions, and formula move out of raw HTML into RST, so the docs theme styles them and `:confval:` links work, and a new section describes the generated commands. The Target PGs per OSD guidance now cites `mon_target_pg_per_osd` and `mon_max_pg_per_osd`, which d34fa3316f0 raised to 200 and 500 for Umbrella, and says so in words that read right on tentacle, where they are 100 and 250. The page notes that many clusters do fine with the PG autoscaler once that target is at least 200, and that the calculator remains useful for internalizing the dynamics and where the autoscaler is infeasible or undesirable. It also notes that the calculator assumes OSDs of one size: with mixed sizes, the largest OSDs hold the most PG replicas, which calls for a generous `mon_max_pg_per_osd`.

### FD Calc

A new page, `doc/rados/operations/fdcalc`, with a calculator for how much of a cluster's raw capacity a replicated or erasure-coded pool can use, given the CRUSH weights of its failure domains. Each PG puts at most one shard in a failure domain, so none can hold more than 1/*n* of what a pool with *n* shards per PG stores, and capacity past that is stranded. For example, replica 3 across failure domains of 100, 100, and 1138 stores 95 and strands 78% of the raw. It shows:

- What a balanced placement stores at full_ratio, and what each failure domain uses, holds back, and strands.
- What CRUSH alone stores before the first failure domain fills, from straw2's chance of choosing e

73357.title: doc/cephadm: say that Ceph does not support downgrades
73357.author: anthonyeleven
73357.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/57046

Adds a "Downgrading" section to the cephadm upgrade page (`doc/cephadm/upgrade.rst`). No user-facing page said whether Ceph can be downgraded.

- Ceph does not support downgrading to an earlier major release. Cephadm refuses it, and it also refuses to move from a stable release to an rc or dev release (`src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/upgrade.py`, the "cannot downgrade" checks). Raising `require_osd_release` is one-way.
- Cephadm does not prevent a downgrade to an earlier point release, but such downgrades are not supported: they may work in some situations and fail in others, are not recommended, and are done at the administrator's risk. The section suggests instead a configuration workaround, an upgrade to a later point or major release, or a local custom container image of the running release with the needed fixes cherry-picked in.
- The way back to an earlier major release is a new cluster at that release, with the data migrated or restored into it.

The section doesn't link the `require_osd_release` page, which exists only on main and umbrella, so the same text can be backported to tentacle and squid. On those branches the following heading reads "Post upgrade actions", so their cherry-picks need a one-line context fix.

73360.title: doc/rados: explain where Manager module options can be set
73360.author: anthonyeleven
73360.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/58469

Adds a "Manager Module Options" section to the configuration page (`doc/rados/configuration/ceph-conf.rst`). The tracker issue asks how to put an option such as `mgr/cephadm/daemon_cache_timeout` in `ceph.conf`, and how these names relate to `ceph config-key`.

- Manager modules read `mgr/<module>/<option>` options only from the Monitor configuration database. `src/mgr/MgrStandby.cc` passes `mgr/` keys to the modules only from the Monitor config callback, so a `mgr/...` line in a local `ceph.conf` has no effect. The section says to use `ceph config set mgr ...`.

- The `mgr/<module>/` entries in the `ceph config-key` store, such as cephadm's SSH keys, are module data, not configuration options.

The section goes before "Configuration Commands", where the text is the same on umbrella, tentacle, and squid, so it cherry-picks cleanly to all three. Test merges with the two open main PRs that touch this file found no conflicts.

73365.title: mgr/cephadm: propagate multi-registry credentials to all hosts
73365.author: Shubhaj1810
73365.body:
Problem
When a Ceph cluster is bootstrapped with multiple registry credentials, newly added hosts may not receive all credentials in /etc/ceph/podman-auth.json. Registry login could also be skipped during daemon redeployment or when a host was removed and added back, causing image pulls and service deployments to fail.

Fix
Persist all registry credentials provided during bootstrap.
Ensure registry login runs during daemon deployment/redeployment whenever credentials are configured.
Queue registry login whenever a host is added, including hosts added back after removal.
Before fix : authentication file missing after redeploy

`[root@ceph-node-03 ~]# rm -f /etc/ceph/podman-auth.json
`
# Redeploy daemon
`ceph orch daemon redeploy node-exporter.ceph-node-03
`
```
[root@ceph-node-03 ~]# cat /etc/ceph/podman-auth.json
cat: /etc/ceph/podman-auth.json: No such file or directory
```

After fix : credentials restored after host re-add

```
[ceph: root@ceph-node-00 /]# ceph orch host rm ceph-node-03 --force
Removed host 'ceph-node-03'
```

```
[ceph: root@ceph-node-00 /]# ceph orch host add ceph-node-03 192.168.100.250
```

73366.title: mgr/cephadm: migrate user-provided grafana certificates from tentacle
73366.author: kginonredhat
73366.body:
Tentacle stored per-host grafana certificates in certmgr as `grafana_cert` and `grafana_key`. These are now `grafana_ssl_cert` and `grafana_ssl_key`, and the certificate used by the service is selected through the spec's `certificate_source`. The old entries are no longer loaded by the TLSObjectStore, so after upgrading a user-provided grafana certificate is silently replaced by a cephadm-signed one.

Add migration 11 -> 12 which reads the legacy entries straight from the mgr store and copies every valid user-provided cert/key pair to the new names as an editable, user-made pair. A certificate is considered cephadm-generated when it was not marked user-made and its issuer is either the cephadm root CA (tentacle and later, `CN cephadm-root-*`) or has organization `Ceph` (squid and earlier): since f967ac061eb the monitoring stack issued self-signed grafana certificates with `create_self_signed_cert('Ceph', <host fqdn>)`, and squid custom certificates were carried into the tentacle store without `user_made`, so the issuer organization is what tells them apart — the same rule `migrate_6_7` already uses. When every host running grafana ends up with a user-provided pair, the grafana spec is switched to `certificate_source: reference`; when some host does not, a `CEPHADM_MIGRATION_WARNING` health warning explains what is left to do.

Certificates are migrated as long as they are valid, even inside the renewal window: the user provided them, so they are kept and the regular certificate health checks report the remaining validity. Expired, unparsable or key-less certificates are not migrated, and entries already present under the new names are kept. Processed legacy entries are removed from the mgr store (nothing reads them on this release and `TLSObjectStore.load()` would discard them as unknown objects on every mgr start). The migration is wrapped like `migrate_10_11`: on failure it sets `CEPHADM_MIGRATION_FAILURE` and returns False so it is retried from the serve loop instead of breaking the module load.

The `orch/cephadm/upgrade` suite now also covers the migration end to end: when upgrading from tentacle, it registers a user grafana certificate with `ceph orch certmgr cert-key set`, checks that grafana serves it before the upgrade, and after the upgrade checks that it is stored under the new names, that the spec uses `certificate_source: reference` and that grafana still serves the same certificate. Upgrades from other releases skip both steps. Two details were needed to make the check work against a tentacle cluster:

- tentacle is detected through the mgr daemon metadata (`ceph_release`): `ceph versions` reports bare version strings that do not contain the release codename;
- the private key is generated as PKCS#8, as tentacle's `certmgr cert-key set` only recognizes `BEGIN PRIVATE KEY` PEM blocks.

An end-to-end verification on a 3-node tentacle v20.2.4 lab cluster (kcli) is documented in the comments below: the user-provided CA-signed grafana certificate survived the upgrade to an image built from main + this PR's `migrations.py`, stored under `grafana_ssl_cert`/`grafana_ssl_key` with `certificate_source: reference` and the same served fingerprint.

Replaces #73233 (same migration, taken over). The "grafana serves the migrated certificate" check relies on the per-host reference certificate lookup fixes from #73234, which should merge first; a teuthology run of `orch/cephadm/upgrade` is still requested for this branch.

Backport note: the certmgr rework (930280141e1) is already in umbrella, so tentacle -> umbrella upgrades hit the same bug and an umbrella backport is needed. It cannot reuse the 11 -> 12 numbering (main has 9_10/10_11 that umbrella lacks) and would land as umbrella 9 -> 10. The migration is idempotent: entries already provisioned under the new names are short-circuited by `cert_exists`, cephadm-generated pairs never cause a flip, and the spec flip only touches specs still on `cephadm-signed`, so umbrella -> mai

73371.title: doc/governance: add CSC participation and inactivity policy
73371.author: jmundack
73371.body:
Set a minimum participation expectation for CSC members (casting a ballot in CSC votes) and an objective inactivity rule: a member who misses two or more consecutive votes, with at least 60 days since the notice for the first miss, is removed without a CSC vote. The Co-Chairs send a notice on each missed vote, may grant exceptions, and publish the roster and a participation record each voting cycle. Removed members may be re-added. On adoption, current members confirm their continued interest instead of facing retroactive removal.

Removal follows a published criterion rather than a vote on a named colleague, so the CSC can keep quorum without that friction, and easy reinstatement keeps it low-stakes. The 60-day gate keeps a short absence from causing removal when votes are frequent.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76665

73381.title: make-dist: check the version against src/ceph_release
73381.author: anthonyeleven
73381.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82551
Related-to: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82496

21.2.0 was packaged from an umbrella tree whose `src/ceph_release` still read `dev`, and 21.1.0 through 21.1.2 were tagged from `dev` trees too. `src/CMakeLists.txt` documents the rule (x.0.z is dev, x.1.z is rc, x.2.z is stable), but nothing enforced it.

`make-dist` now exits before building the tarball when the version is x.1.z and the release type is `dev`, or the version is x.2.z and the type isn't `stable`. A tree that is ahead of its last tag passes, so a branch can move to rc or stable before the release is tagged. Other minor numbers, such as main's `v21.3.0` ordering tag, aren't checked. `CEPH_SKIP_RELEASE_TYPE_CHECK=1` skips the check for a version scheme that doesn't follow this.

I ran the new block alone against these version and release type pairs:

| Version | `src/ceph_release` | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 22.0.0-308-g8e3ba332 | dev | passes |
| 21.3.0-5-gabc | dev | passes |
| 21.1.0 | rc | passes |
| 21.1.2-3-gabc | stable | passes |
| 21.2.0, 21.2.1-4-gabc | stable | passes |
| 20.1.0-pre.ibm.0 | rc | passes |
| 21.1.0, 21.1.2-129-g0719e29c | dev | refused |
| 21.2.0 | dev, rc | refused |

A backport to umbrella would have to land with the 82496 fix or after it, because umbrella's dev builds (21.1.2-129-g0719e29c, `dev`) fail this check until `src/ceph_release` says `stable`.

@batrick: ceph-build's ceph-setup job passes the `git describe` version to `make-dist`. Is there any release path that builds the tarball without going through `make-dist`?

73382.title: cephadm: test that a stable release doesn't default to the main image
73382.author: anthonyeleven
73382.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82552
Related-to: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82496

21.2.0's cephadm defaulted to `quay.ceph.io/ceph-ci/ceph:main` with `DEFAULT_IMAGE_IS_MAIN = True`, so without `--image` it deployed the CI build of main. The existing tests pin the image string but don't know the release type, so a branch moved to `stable` without the matching `cephadmlib/constants.py` change still passes make check.

The new `tests/test_constants.py` reads `src/ceph_release`. When the release type is `stable`, it requires `DEFAULT_IMAGE_IS_MAIN` to be False, `DEFAULT_IMAGE` not to be a `ceph-ci` image, and `DEFAULT_IMAGE_RELEASE` to match the release name. On dev and rc trees it skips, so main is unaffected, and a branch can still switch its image during the rc phase, as tentacle did (94a83a1bf5b landed between `rc` and `stable`). A downstream build that changes `DEFAULT_IMAGE` still passes as long as the image isn't a ceph-ci one.

I ran it with `src/ceph_release` and `cephadmlib/constants.py` taken from each tree:

| Tree | Result |
|---|---|
| main (`dev`) | skipped |
| tentacle (`stable`, `quay.io/ceph/ceph:v20`) | passed |
| umbrella's constants, with `src/ceph_release` changed to `stable` and nothing else | failed on `DEFAULT_IMAGE_IS_MAIN` |

@phlogistonjohn @adk3798: is `tests/` the right home for this, or would you rather have it as a line in the `flake8` tox env next to the `quay.io` count?

73383.title: client: advance the iterator in _kick_stale_sessions
73383.author: anthonyeleven
73383.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82547

`Client::_kick_stale_sessions()` never advances its iterator. Commit 730dd8a87a3 "client: switch to use shared_ptr for mds_sessions" replaced `mds_sessions.erase(it++)` with `mds_sessions.erase(it->first)` and dropped the `++it` before the STALE check. Since then:

- The loop never ends while `mds_sessions` holds a session that is not REJECTED. Both callers hold `client_lock`, so the client hangs. One caller is the `kick_stale_sessions` admin socket command. The other is `Client::tick()`, when a blocklisted client reconnects because `client_reconnect_stale` is true.
- A REJECTED session is erased by key, and the loop then reads the erased iterator. A STALE session is erased inside `_closed_mds_session()`, which also leaves the iterator dangling.

The first commit erases through the iterator and steps past a session before closing it, as the loop did before that commit. I modeled the old and new loops in a standalone program with the same map, session states, and erase calls, built with AddressSanitizer. The old loop spins forever, and the fixed loop finishes with no errors.

The second commit adds `test_client_kick_stale_sessions` to `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_misc.py`. It runs the command against a ceph-fuse mount that has an open session, then checks that the mount still works. Without the fix, the command hangs and the test fails. I have not run it in teuthology.

Both commits cherry-pick cleanly to umbrella, tentacle, and squid with the same line counts. No open PR touches these lines.

@vshankar, please review.

73384.title: client: match the dump_subvolume_metrics_aggr command name
73384.author: anthonyeleven
73384.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82548

The client registers `dump_subvolume_metrics_aggr` with its admin socket, but `Client::CommandHook::call()` compares the command against `dump_subvolume_metrics`. The registered name never matches, so the command falls through to `ceph_abort_msg("bad command registered")` and aborts ceph-fuse or the libcephfs application. This came in with commit c376635d5d5 "client,mds: add support for subvolume level metrics".

The first commit compares against the registered name, which is the one that `help` lists.

The second commit adds `test_client_dump_subvolume_metrics_aggr` to `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_misc.py`. It runs the command against a ceph-fuse mount, checks that the output has `current_metrics` and `last_metrics`, and then checks that the mount still works. I have not run it in teuthology.

Both commits cherry-pick cleanly to umbrella with the same line counts. Tentacle and squid do not have the command. No open PR touches these lines.

@vshankar, please review.

73399.title: doc/radosgw: describe syncing selected buckets to a cloud sync zone
73399.author: anthonyeleven
73399.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/59075

Neither `doc/radosgw/cloud-sync-module.rst` nor `doc/radosgw/multisite-sync-policy.rst` says how to sync only some buckets to a cloud sync zone. This adds a "Syncing Selected Buckets" section to the cloud sync page and links it from Example 3 of the sync policy page.

- Sync policy applies to a cloud zone like any other destination. The cloud zone's RGW builds its bucket pipes from the policy handler (`RGWGetBucketPeersCR`, `rgw_data_sync.cc`), and `RGWBucketSyncPolicyHandler` has no special case for sync modules.
- The commands follow Example 3: a zonegroup group in the `allowed` state with a directional flow and a pipe to the cloud zone, plus `period update --commit`, then an `enabled` bucket group per bucket.
- An `important` note: a zonegroup policy replaces `sync_from` for every zone. `convert_old_sync_config()` runs only while the zonegroup policy is empty (`rgw_bucket_sync.cc:758`), so a deployment that also mirrors data zones needs a group for that.
- A cloud zone is never a sync source (`RGWAWSSyncModule::supports_data_export()` returns false), hence the directional flow.
- The module doesn't use pipe destination parameters (storage class, destination owner, ACL translation). Only the generic fetch path applies them (`rgw_data_sync.cc:2868-2892`). The module picks its tier-config profile by source bucket name (`rgw_sync_module_aws.cc:1636`). Pipe prefix filters do apply, because bucket sync checks them before calling the module, so the section doesn't mention filters.

It stays clear of lines 144 to 182 of `cloud-sync-module.rst`, which @supriti's #73242 changes. The commit cherry-picks cleanly to umbrella and tentacle, and the behavior it describes is the same on both.

@cbodley @smanjara, is "allowed at the zonegroup, enabled per bucket" the setup you'd recommend for a cloud zone, and is there anything about a cloud destination the section should warn about?

73400.title: doc/cephfs: refine the large omap objects section
73400.author: anthonyeleven
73400.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/43034

Follow-up to #73321, from a fact-check of its "Large omap objects in the metadata pool" section against the code:

- The example log line now shows the current format. Since 5e59c521f8d "osd/scrub: modify OMAP stats collection", the OSD prints only the placement group (`src/osd/scrubber/scrub_backend.cc:290`, on main and umbrella). Tentacle and earlier print the raw hash first and the placement group in parentheses (`scrub_backend.cc:275` on tentacle), and the section now says so, so the same text is right on every branch.

- Automatic splitting skips stray directories (`MDBalancer::maybe_fragment()`), but `MDCache::can_fragment()` refuses only directories inside them. The section now says that the MDS does not split stray directories on its own, instead of that it never fragments them.

It applies cleanly on top of the #73321 backports for umbrella, tentacle, and squid.

73401.title: umbrella: doc/rados: explain where Manager module options can be set
73401.author: anthonyeleven
73401.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82569

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73360
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/58469

Adds a "Manager Module Options" section to the configuration page (`doc/rados/configuration/ceph-conf.rst`). The tracker issue asks how to put an option such as `mgr/cephadm/daemon_cache_timeout` in `ceph.conf`, and how these names relate to `ceph config-key`.

- Manager modules read `mgr/<module>/<option>` options only from the Monitor configuration database. `src/mgr/MgrStandby.cc` passes `mgr/` keys to the modules only from the Monitor config callback, so a `mgr/...` line in a local `ceph.conf` has no effect. The section says to use `ceph config set mgr ...`.
- `ceph config assimilate-conf -i <file>` moves such options from a file into the database. That is why the `[mgr]` example for `cephadm bootstrap --config` in `doc/cephadm/operations.rst` works: bootstrap assimilates the file (`src/cephadm/cephadm.py`).
- The `mgr/<module>/` entries in the `ceph config-key` store, such as cephadm's SSH keys, are module data, not configuration options.

The section goes before "Configuration Commands", where the text is the same on umbrella, tentacle, and squid, so it cherry-picks cleanly to all three. Test merges with the two open main PRs that touch this file found no conflicts.

73404.title: umbrella: doc/cephfs: explain large omap objects in the metadata pool
73404.author: anthonyeleven
73404.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82564

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73321
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/43034

No CephFS page says what to do when `LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS` names an object in a metadata pool. The entry in `doc/rados/operations/health-checks.rst` covers only RGW bucket index objects. This adds a "Large omap objects in the metadata pool" section to `doc/cephfs/health-messages.rst` and links it from that entry.

- Cause: with the defaults, a fragment splits at `mds_bal_split_size` (10000 head and snapshot entries, `CDir::should_split()`) and stops taking creates at `mds_bal_fragment_size_max` (100000), both well below the 200000-key threshold. In practice, the warning comes from the 1 GiB value threshold, as in https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77513.
- Object to path: dirfrag objects are named `<ino>.<frag>` (`InodeStoreBase::get_object_name`). A directory's backtrace is stored in the metadata pool on `<ino>.00000000` (`CInode::get_backtrace_pool`), and `ceph-dencoder` decodes it as `inode_backtrace_t`.
- Fix: `scrub start <path>` scrubs every fragment of the directory and calls `maybe_fragment()` afterward (`ScrubStack.cc:559`). That splits on entry count only, so for a fragment that is too large only in bytes, the section gives `dirfrag ls` and `dirfrag split`. Both need the directory in the cache of its auth MDS (`MDSRank::_command_dirfrag_get`).
- Directories the MDS won't fragment: root (`1.00000000`), stray directories (`MDBalancer::maybe_fragment`), mdsdir, and anything inside a stray directory (`MDCache::can_fragment`).
- RGW bucket index objects point to the dynamic resharding page.

A second commit adds to `LARGE_OMAP_OBJECTS` in `doc/rados/operations/health-checks.rst` what the object usually is, by pool. It only adds lines after the existing paragraph, whose wording differs on tentacle, so both commits cherry-pick cleanly to umbrella and tentacle.
- In an RGW log pool, it's usually an untrimmed log. Usage logs (`usage.<n>`) need `usage trim`. `RGWSyncLogTrimThread` trims the metadata log, the data log, and bucket index logs every `rgw_sync_log_trim_interval`, but never the sync error log (`sync error trim` is manual).
- In an RGW index pool, it's a bucket index shard. Those need resharding, or, in multisite deployments, `bilog trim` after sync catches up. Beginning with the Vampire release, new buckets use FIFO bilogs in the log pool (`rgw_default_bucket_bilog_type`, `rgw_bilog.h`).
- In a CephFS metadata pool, it links the new section.
- It also says that changing `pg_num` doesn't help, since an object and its omap stay in one PG, and that the warning can outlast a split or merge until the next deep scrub.

It adds the `rgw-trim-usage` and `rgw-multisite-check-the-logs` labels so those sections can be linked.

Clean cherry-pick of 2 commits, with the same line changes as on main.

73407.title: umbrella: doc/cephadm: say that Ceph does not support downgrades
73407.author: anthonyeleven
73407.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82566

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73357
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/57046

Adds a "Downgrading" section to the cephadm upgrade page (`doc/cephadm/upgrade.rst`). No user-facing page said whether Ceph can be downgraded.

- Ceph does not support downgrading to an earlier major release. Cephadm refuses it, and it also refuses to move from a stable release to an rc or dev release (`src/pybind/mgr/cephadm/upgrade.py`, the "cannot downgrade" checks). Raising `require_osd_release` is one-way.
- Cephadm does not prevent a downgrade to an earlier point release, but such downgrades are not supported: they may work in some situations and fail in others, are not recommended, and are done at the administrator's risk. The section suggests instead a configuration workaround, an upgrade to a later point or major release, or a local custom container image of the running release with the needed fixes cherry-picked in.
- The way back to an earlier major release is a new cluster at that release, with the data migrated or restored into it.

The section doesn't link the `require_osd_release` page, which exists only on main and umbrella, so the same text can be backported to tentacle and squid. On those branches the following heading reads "Post upgrade actions", so their cherry-picks need a one-line context fix.

73410.author: kchheda3
73410.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82578

A client could renew its other tickets without the MGR ticket and then

73411.title: mgr/cephadm: check only the reporting host's failed daemons
73411.author: mmgaggle
73411.body:
`HostData.handle_metadata()` scans every daemon in the cluster three times for each agent report: `get_error_daemons()` before and after applying the host's `ls`, and `update_failed_daemon_health_check()`. Each report therefore costs time proportional to the size of the cluster, and the endpoint's total work grows with its square.

A report can only change its own host's daemons. This change compares that host's failed daemons before and after, and rebuilds `CEPHADM_FAILED_DAEMON` only when they changed. The serve loop still rebuilds the health check on every iteration.

The agent endpoint was benchmarked on a vstart cluster with simulated agents, each reporting 20 daemons every 20 s:

| hosts | mgr CPU per report (before / after) | reports answered within 10 s | peak reports/s, 8 senders |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000 | 13.5 ms / 3.4 ms | 100% / 100% | 56 / 221 |
| 2,000 | 33.5 ms / 2.8 ms | 5.4% / 76.2% | 0 / 148 |

The cephadm unit tests give 1,809 passed and 1 skipped, the same as the base commit. flake8 is clean.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82579

73412.title: osd: a pwlc rollback in peering supersedes the copies that peers hold
73412.author: vitaly-goot
73412.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82581

**Symptom.** After a whole-cluster restart of an optimized EC pool, replicas abort on the first write of the
new interval:

```
PGLog.h:673: ceph_assert(head.version == 0 || e.version.version > head.version)
PGLog::IndexedLog::add <- PeeringState::add_log_entry <- PeeringState::append_log <- ECBackend::handle_sub_write
```

The entry has the new epoch and a counter the replica's head already has: `40455'25505236` against a head of
`40412'25505236`. Seen on 12 and 22 OSDs of a 55-OSD v20.2.4 test cluster (8+3) after two all-OSD restarts in
September, and on 3 shards of one PG after an all-OSD SIGKILL on 2026-10-30, this time with a debug-10 primary
log that shows the whole sequence.

**Mechanism.** The primary's log head and pwlc are rolled back in GetLog: `proc_master_log()` finds the first
write of the previous interval divergent (it never reached the shard whose log is authoritative) and
`consider_adjusting_pwlc()` / `consider_rollback_pwlc()` roll every range back to the new head. The pwlc epoch is
left alone. A peer that logged the rolled-back write still holds its copy of the pre-rollback map, with that same
epoch and toversions one past the new head. `update_peer_info()` prefers the higher toversion within one epoch,
so when that peer's info reaches the primary again later in peering, the map grows past the head again and
`apply_pwlc()` advances the primary's view of the shards the ranges cover. In the traced run the info came as
a notify in WaitUpThru: a new osdmap epoch arrived while the primary waited for up_thru, the stray re-notified,
and `proc_replica_notify()` took it (the peer's own `last_update` differs from the primary's rewound view, so
it is not a dup). `activate()` then stamps the map with the activation epoch and sends it as the definitive
copy; a shard whose `last_update` equals a range's start applies it, advances its `last_update` and log head
past the primary's head, and the first write of the interval, which reuses that version, asserts.

PR #71579 (#80360) closed the same symptom on one path: `PGLog::proc_replica_log()` rolls the peer's copy back
when it rewinds the peer's log. The merge in `update_peer_info()` was still open for a copy that arrives any
other way.

**Fix.** Two small changes in PeeringState:

1. A rollback in `consider_adjusting_pwlc()` or `consider_rollback_pwlc()` on the primary gives the map the
   current osdmap epoch (`pwlc_rolled_back()`). Every copy a peer holds was stamped by an earlier activation or
   by a write of an earlier interval, so it loses the merge.
2. `activate()` trims the map to the log head before stamping it, as `proc_master_log()` does, so no range
   beyond the head is ever sent as definitive. It logs at level 1 when that trims anything.

**Test.** `PeeringStateTest.PwlcStaleCopyAfterRollback` (3+2 pool): a partial write committed on the primary and
one parity shard but never received by the other parity shard; a nonprimary shard replaced; the old parity
shard's log is authoritative, the write is rolled back; the map with up_thru is delivered to the stray first,
so its notify with the stale pwlc copy reaches the primary in WaitUpThru. The test checks the invariant: after
peering no pwlc range reaches past the primary's log head, and the covered shard's `last_update` and log head
do not either. Fails on main (pwlc 4'1,4'2 and shard 1 at 4'2 against a head of 4'1), passes with the fix;
the rest of the PeeringStateTest suite is unchanged.

**Validation.** Unit test as above. On the 55-OSD v20.2.4 test cluster (8+3, 512 PGs, the write path that triggered
the assert active), three rounds of SIGKILL of all 55 OSDs under load followed by a staggered restart at debug_osd 10:
0 asserts, 0 crash lines in the OSD logs, every PG active again (2026-10-31, build 20.2.4-122). The same procedure on the
build without the fix aborted three shards of one PG at PGLog.h:673 the day be

73413.title: mgr/cephadm: store each target of a scoped TLS object in its own entry
73413.author: mmgaggle
73413.body:
`TLSObjectStore` keeps every target of a service- or host-scoped TLS object in one config-key entry, and rewrites the whole entry on each save. Per-host cephadm-signed certs make that entry grow with the cluster: the agent's, and node-exporter's and ceph-exporter's when the monitoring stack is secured. With the default `mon_config_key_max_entry_size` of 64 KiB, the key entry stops fitting at about 19 hosts and the cert entry at about 34. The mon refuses every later save, and each newly active mgr reconfigures the whole service.

This change stores each target in its own entry, `cert_store.target.<cert|key>.<name>/<target>`. The per-name entry stays as an empty map, so that registered names are still found on load. On load, targets still in a per-name entry are moved to entries of their own. Such entries were written before this change, or by an older mgr since, so they win over existing per-target entries.

A cluster that has already hit the limit is expected to get one more reconfigure on the first mgr start after the upgrade, to regenerate the keys that were never saved. After that the entries are complete.

Testing:

- The cephadm unit tests give 1,813 passed and 1 skipped. flake8 and mypy are clean.
- I also ran a vstart cluster with the default limit and 40 fake hosts with simulated agents:
  - On main, a mgr failover found 15 certs without their key, reconfigured the agent service, and had 39 more saves refused.
  - With this change, the next failover moved the entries, and the mon then held certs and keys for all 40 hosts with no saves refused.
  - Two more failovers found nothing missing and left the stored entries byte-identical.

73414.title: mgr/cephadm: use ECDSA keys for the agent endpoint and agent messages
73414.author: mmgaggle
73414.body:
Every message the mgr sends to an agent generates a new cert with an RSA-4096 key, which costs 0.78 s of CPU on average. Pushes go to every agent after a failover to a mgr on another host, or during an upgrade, so at 1,000 hosts each such push spends about 13 minutes of mgr CPU on keys. The agent endpoint's own RSA-4096 key also costs a signature for every agent report, since agents open a new TLS connection each time.

This series:
- python-common: `get_certificate_info()` and `get_private_key_info()` now report EC keys; until now they only knew RSA.
- mgr/cephadm: `SSLCerts.generate_cert()` and `CertMgr.generate_cert()` take `ecdsa=True` to issue a cert for an ECDSA P-256 key, still signed by the RSA root CA. Renewing a cert keeps its key type.
- mgr/cephadm: the agent endpoint and the messages to agents use P-256 keys. When the module loads, it replaces a stored RSA endpoint cert from an earlier version. Agents verify the endpoint against the root CA, which doesn't change, and the endpoint cert isn't one of an agent's config deps, so no agent is reconfigured. The per-host certs that agents serve stay RSA.

On one core, a new key and its cert take 779 ms of CPU with RSA-4096, and 1.15 ms with P-256.

The endpoint was benchmarked with 2,000 simulated agents reporting every 20 s, together with the fix for https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82579:

| | RSA-4096 | ECDSA P-256 |
|---|---|---|
| TLS handshake, mean / p99 | 273 ms / 6.6 s | 164 ms / 3.3 s |
| report latency, mean | 1.30 s | 0.89 s |
| reports answered within 10 s | 87.5% | 89.1% |

The share of reports answered barely changes, because reports mostly wait for the endpoint to accept their connection. The bigger saving is the key generation on pushes.

Testing:
- cephadm unit tests: 1,811 passed and 1 skipped, including 2 new tests (ECDSA cert generation and renewal; the endpoint replacing a stored RSA cert).
- python-common tests: 586 passed.
- flake8 and mypy are clean.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82582

73417.title: mds: do not stall or give up an export of a busy directory
73417.author: xiubli
73417.body:
Exporting a directory that a client is busy creating files in either
stalls for a full `mds_tick_interval` while the subtree freezes, or is
cancelled once the subtree is frozen.

**The freeze waits for the tick.** The freeze waits for the subtree's
auth pins.  Some of them belong to updates that are already submitted to
the journal but not flushed: early-replied requests and client cap
flushes (`_do_cap_update()` keeps an auth pin until the update is
journaled).  Nothing flushes the log for the freeze, so it waits for
`MDSRankDispatcher::tick()`, and every request in the subtree waits with
it.  The first commit flushes the log when the export starts freezing
and has `_do_cap_update()` ask for a flush when the inode, or the
subtree it is in, is freezing.

**The frozen export is cancelled.** `export_try_grab_locks()` needs to
wrlock the directory inode's filelock and nestlock.  Under load the
filelock is often in the middle of a state change, and on an exporter
that only has a replica of the inode it can be stable in sync, which a
replica cannot change by itself.  The export is then cancelled.  An
export pin retries at the next tick, and `export dir` does not retry at
all.  The second commit moves such a lock towards mix the way
`wrlock_start()` does (`scatter_mix()` on the auth, `LOCK_AC_REQSCATTER`
from a replica) and waits for it to settle instead of cancelling, up to
four times per export.  The scatter updates skip frozen dirfrags, so
waiting while frozen is safe.  `find_stale_export_freeze()` cancels an
export that has waited for these locks for `mds_freeze_tree_timeout`.

The third commit adds `TestExports.test_export_busy_dir`: four threads
create files in a directory while `export dir` moves it back and forth
between two MDSs six times with `mds_tick_interval` at 10 s; every export
must finish in under 5 s.  It fails without the first commit on the
kernel client, and without the second commit on ceph-fuse.

### Results

vstart, two active MDSs, 3 OSDs on NVMe.  Four client threads create
4 KiB files in a new directory, which `export dir` moves to the other MDS
after 2 s; 20 directories per round, rounds before/after/after/before,
MDSs restarted between rounds.  Latency in ms.

Kernel client:

|                       |        | p50  | p90  | p95  | p99  | max  |
|-----------------------|--------|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| freeze                | before | 4017 | 4364 | 4396 | 4513 | 4513 |
|                       | after  |  118 |  315 |  617 | 1045 | 1045 |
| export, cmd to done   | before | 4740 | 5166 | 5283 | 5455 | 5455 |
|                       | after  |  923 | 1728 | 2219 | 2496 | 2496 |
| slowest create in dir | before | 4297 | 4726 | 4937 | 5087 | 5087 |
|                       | after  |  528 | 1447 | 1849 | 2713 | 2713 |

ceph-fuse:

|                     |        | done  | p50 | p90  | max  |
|---------------------|--------|------:|----:|-----:|-----:|
| export, cmd to done | before |  0/35 |   - |    - |    - |
|                     | after  | 35/35 | 667 | 1039 | 1500 |
| freeze              | before |       | 170 |  422 |  514 |
|                     | after  |       | 114 |  172 |  334 |

Before the change, 37 exports were cancelled for the directory inode's
locks; after it none was.

### Testing

- `test_exports` (ceph-fuse and kernel client), `test_multimds_misc`,
  `test_failover.TestShutdownKillpoints`: no failures that do not also
  happen without this change.
- `test_export_busy_dir` fails before and passes after, with both
  clients.

Related: #73171 (the same kind of wait for cross-MDS renames,
https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82190).  Both PRs touch the same
condition in `_do_cap_update()`; whichever merges second keeps
`in->is_freezing()`, which also covers `in->is_freezing_inode()`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82584

73421.title: mgr/cephadm: do the agent endpoint's TLS handshakes on the worker threads
73421.author: mmgaggle
73421.body:
Agents open a new TLS connection for every report. cheroot accepts the agent endpoint's connections on a single thread, and `BuiltinSSLAdapter.wrap()` completes each TLS handshake on that thread. In the mgr that thread also has to win the GIL back from 30 busy workers, so as the cluster grows, reports wait in line for it. A client that stalls before its handshake holds up every other connection until the server's timeout.

This series:
- **mgr:** adds `DeferredHandshakeSSLAdapter`, whose `wrap()` only sets up the TLS state, and `DeferredHandshakeConnection`, which completes the handshake on the worker thread before it reads the request. Like `BuiltinSSLAdapter`, it drops a connection whose handshake fails without logging an error, and answers plain HTTP with a 400. A `CherryPyMgr` server opts in with `'defer_handshake': True` in `ssl_info`, so the dashboard and service discovery are unchanged.
- **mgr/cephadm:** the agent endpoint opts in.

The WSGI environ of a deferred connection lacks the `SSL_*` entries describing the negotiated session; the agent endpoint doesn't use them.

The test cluster was vstart with simulated agents reporting every 20 s, together with #73411. This series doesn't depend on that PR, but without it the handler, not the handshake, is the limit at these sizes.

| hosts | handshakes on | answered within 10 s | answered/s (offered) | latency p50 / p99 | handshake p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2,000 | the accept thread | 67.2% | 68 (100) | 0.75 / 8.9 s | 6.6 s |
| 2,000 | the worker threads | 99.9% | 103 (100) | 0.11 / 4.2 s | 1.6 s |
| 3,000 | the accept thread | 42.3% | 64 (150) | 1.5 / 9.5 s | 6.6 s |
| 3,000 | the worker threads | 55.8% | 87 (150) | 4.5 / 9.6 s | 6.7 s |

At 3,000 hosts more reports are answered, but the backlog now waits in the worker queue, so the median latency rises.

In a small cheroot test server, a client stalled before its handshake held another client's request for 4.8 s with `BuiltinSSLAdapter`; with this series that request took 4 ms. Plain HTTP got the 400 response, and neither the stalled client nor one that connected and hung up logged anything.

Testing:
- New unit tests in `tests/test_cherrypy_mgr.py`, 13 passed in all:
  - the opt-in wiring;
  - `wrap()` returning before the client starts its handshake, with the handshake completing on the first read;
  - a failed handshake closing the connection quietly;
  - plain HTTP getting a 400.
- The cephadm unit tests give 1,809 passed and 1 skipped. flake8 and mypy are clean.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82590

73423.title: doc/rados: rewrite the inconsistent PG and pg repair sections
73423.author: anthonyeleven
73423.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/61739

Niklas Hambuechen filed 61739 after following the docs to fix "1 pg inconsistent" on his cluster. The old pg-repair page now lives in the "PGs Inconsistent" section of `doc/rados/troubleshooting/troubleshooting-pg.rst`, and every complaint in the tracker still applied. This rewrites that section from the scrub code on main:

- **"No scrub information available" from `rados list-inconsistent-obj`.** The primary keeps the error details in its scrub store, which it clears on every new interval (`PrimaryLogPG::on_change` calls `cleanup_store`) and at OSD start (`OSD::clear_temp_objects`). `num_scrub_errors` persists in the PG info, so the PG stays inconsistent with no details until a deep scrub regenerates them. This is also tracker 15781.
- **What `pg repair` does.** `select_auth_object` chooses the authoritative copy: the primary first, excluding copies with read, stat, object info or size errors, then the newest version, then the most digests. Digests don't choose it; they flag the other copies against its object info. `repair_object` marks the differing copies missing, `DoRecovery` recovers them, and an `after_repair` deep scrub follows, with `failed_repair` if errors remain. The old text said repair overwrites digests and that recovery is beyond its scope.
- **When the primary's copy wins.** A write that changes only part of an object clears its data digest, on BlueStore too. Differing copies then show only object-level errors, and the primary-first tie-break decides. The section says how to recognize that case before repairing.
- **I/O and backfill.** The flag is read only by the health and state code, so an inconsistent PG serves I/O. A client read that hits a bad copy on the primary goes through `rep_repair_primary_object`. `prepare_stats_for_publish` derives the flag from `num_scrub_errors`, which only a scrub updates, so a PG can stay inconsistent after its bad drive is replaced.
- **Scheduling.** An operator `deep-scrub` or `repair` (`operator_requested`, `must_repair`) doesn't wait for `noscrub` or `nodeep-scrub`, allowed hours, `osd_max_scrubs` or `osd_scrub_during_recovery`, but does wait for active+clean. The `after_repair` scrub waits for allowed hours and `osd_max_scrubs`, and honors `osd_scrub_during_recovery` (`scrub_job.cc`).

It also shows the current `ceph health detail` output, fixes the `list-inconsistent-pg` and `list-inconsistent-obj` mix-up, says the shard error names end in `_info` rather than `oi`, and replaces `ceph osd listpools` with `ceph osd lspools`. It drops the clock-skew paragraph, because scrub compares the object info that the primary wrote and never compares clocks. It also drops the Filestore-only text and walkthrough. `osd-config-ref.rst` gains `osd_deep_scrub_update_digest_min_age` and `osd_scrub_retry_pg_state`, so the section can link them.

@kuklaondrej's #71718 removes the same Filestore paragraphs and walkthrough on this page. This PR replaces the whole section, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase; if #71718 merges first, I'll rebase this one.

The scheduler rules it describes are the same on umbrella and tentacle. The cherry-pick to both conflicts with older wording of the same section, so the backports will take this section as a whole.

@ronen-fr, does this match how the scrubber behaves, especially the scheduling paragraph?

73424.title: doc/cephfs: describe pinning the subvolume trash folder
73424.author: anthonyeleven
73424.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/61902

61902 began as a code change: put `/volumes/_deleting` on rank 1 by default, so that large recursive deletes stay off rank 0. In the tracker discussion, the code change was dropped because of the per-subvolume trash and distributed ephemeral pins, and documenting it under recommended settings was suggested instead. This adds a "Pinning the Trash Folder" section after "Removing a Subvolume" in `doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst`, written from the code on main:

- **Where the load goes.** A removal with no retained snapshots renames the whole subvolume into `/volumes/_deleting` (`SubvolumeBase.trash_base_dir` and `Trash.dump`), and the purge threads `rmtree` it there (`Trash.purge`). So the unlinks go to the rank that holds `_deleting`, which is the rank that holds `/volumes`.
- **Subvolumes with their own pin.** `ceph fs subvolume pin` sets the pin on the subvolume's base directory (`SubvolumeBase.pin`), which is the directory that gets renamed, so that pin goes along and the subvolume is purged by its own rank.
- **Retained snapshots.** `SubvolumeV2.trash_incarnation_dir` moves the data to the subvolume's own `.trash` and puts only a symlink in `_deleting`. The purge follows the link (`purge_queue.py`), so the subvolume's rank does the work.
- **Empty folder.** `MDCache::trim` calls `Migrator::export_empty_import` on an empty imported subtree, which doesn't check the export pin, so the empty `_deleting` goes back to the rank that holds `/volumes`. `MDBalancer::handle_export_pins` exports a pinned directory only once it isn't empty, so the next removal moves it to the pinned rank again. This is the behavior that the description wanted to avoid with a placeholder file. The section doesn't suggest one, because the purge threads would delete it.

The section goes after "Removing a Subvolume" rather than in the pinning section, because @neesingh-rh's #68539 adds a note at the end of the pinning section. @rishabh-d-dave's #59713 changes other parts of the same page and doesn't touch this text.

@vshankar @batrick, does this documentation suffice for 61902, or is a code change warranted, for example the default pin on `_deleting` that the original description proposed?

73426.title: mgr: make map cache ownership explicit
73426.author: tchaikov
73426.body:
`MgrMapCache`  uses raw `PyObject` pointers with different ownership rules for insertion and lookup. Callers must track reference counts by hand, and cache operations must remember to drain pending releases. Changes to error paths or cache operations can easily miss one of these steps.

Use a move-only `PyObjectRef` to make ownership explicit. Insertion takes ownership; lookup returns a separate reference through `clone()`. Keep raw reference adoption and transfer at the Python C API boundary.

Notification paths hold manager locks without the GIL, so they cannot safely release Python references. Mark entries stale and keep at most one stale reference per key. The next lookup or replacement releases it with the GIL after dropping the cache lock. Clear, disable and shutdown extract references before destroying them with the GIL, preserving the caller's Python context. Finalizers can then re-enter the cache safely. Reclamation stays synchronous and no longer needs a pending-release queue.

Remove the unused generic `MgrMapCache` and use `LFUCache` as a member. Let LFUCache hold move-only values and return removed values for destruction outside its lock. Prefer stale entries for eviction and reject writes when capacity is zero.

This is an ownership cleanup on top of the existing leak fix.
