73663.title: mds: fix 5-20 s create stalls in directories spread over several MDSs
73663.author: xiubli
73663.body:
When many clients create files in one directory whose fragments are spread over several active MDSs, creates stall for 5 to 20 s at a time. The journal of one MDS stops for that long. Its early-replied requests keep their locks and auth pins until their events are safe, so the requests on the other MDSs wait for those locks. Three things make it worse, and each commit fixes one of them.

**1. Remote auth pins wait for the next tick** (`mds: flush the journal when an early-replied request holds remote auth pins`)

A create whose fragment is on another MDS than the directory inode can ask the inode's auth MDS to auth pin it, when the inode's filelock or nestlock is in the middle of a gather. The request is early-replied, so `journal_and_reply()` does not flush the log, and the auth pin stays on the other MDS until the next tick. Anything there that waits for those auth pins, such as freezing the dirfrag for an export, waits with it. The fix flushes the log after an early reply when the request holds remote auth pins.

**2. The auth's lock gather waits for the next tick** (`mds: flush the journal when the auth starts a lock gather that is held`)

When the inode's auth starts a mix->lock gather with `simple_lock()`, the gather also waits for the wrlocks held on the auth. With clients creating files, hundreds of those are held by early-replied creates until their journal entries are safe. The replicas flush their log when they get `LOCK_AC_LOCK`, so they reach "lock" within milliseconds. On the auth nothing flushes: the waiters are on the replicas, so `nudge_log()` is never called there, and the gather finishes only at the next tick. The fix flushes the log at the end of `simple_lock()` when the 

**3. Backtrace writes of expiring segments flood the OSDs** (`mds: limit the backtrace writes of expiring journal segments`)

To expire a segment, `LogSegment::try_to_expire()` writes the backtrace of every inode created or moved in it, and `BatchCommitBacktrace` issues all of those writes at once. With large segments and a create workload, that is 5,000 to 14,000 writes to the data pool at once. The journal writes of the same MDS then wait behind them on the OSDs. The journaler has to remove the object ahead of its write position before it can write further. That removal took up to 4 s in the OSD queue, and the journal stopped "too close to prezero_pos" until it finished.

The fix issues those writes at most `mds_log_expire_backtrace_max_inflight` at a time, across all expiring segments. The new option is runtime, defaults to 256, and 0 restores the old behaviour.

The last commit adds `test_backtrace_expire_max_inflight` to `test_backtrace.py`. It checks that every backtrace is still written with the limit at 1, when many small segments expire together, and when the limit is changed or removed at runtime.

**Results**

io500 `mdtest-hard-write` on one host: 3 active MDSs and a standby, 3 NVMe OSDs, 16 io500 tasks over 4 kernel client mounts, 300 s stonewall. The tree pin spreads the directories over the MDSs. These three changes were the only difference between the builds; each step adds one change, and each build ran once:

| | before | + auth pin flush | + gather flush | + backtrace limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mdtest-hard-write, kIOPS | 7.98 | 7.89 | 8.10 | 8.92 |
| creates of 10 s or more | – | 103 | 208 | 0 |
| longest create, s | 15.5 | 21.3 | 19.4 | 8.0 |
| longest journal commit, s | – | 13.6 | 14.5 | 7.7 |

The slow requests are counted from the 100 slowest requests per MDS per minute (`mds_op_history_size 100`, `mds_op_history_duration 60`).

- The two flush changes remove the waits for the next tick. For example, peer requests of 1 to 2 s went from 15 to 0.
- The longest stalls come from the journal stopping, which the third change fixes. Without these changes, five runs of `mdtest-hard-write` gave 7.9 to 8.4 kIOPS.
- The other io500 phases did not change beyond their run-to-run spread. An ABBA comparison with more runs, a

73664.title: os/bluestore: unpin an onode in the shard that holds it
73664.author: ming1
73664.body:
`maybe_unpin()` follows an onode to the shard a `split_cache()` moved it to while the caller waited for the lock, but then links it into this shard's LRU, stamps this shard's age bin and counts it in this shard's `num`, under the other shard's lock only. The last reference to an onode dropped while its PG is split can thus link it into the wrong shard's LRU with no lock held, or unlink it from the other shard's list through the wrong list head, leaving both shards' list sizes off by one and a later trim of either shard working on a corrupt list. In the tree since a3057f4c373 (v18.1.0).

Delegate to the shard that holds the onode now; it does the work under its own lock. The unit test promotes an onode in one shard, calls `maybe_unpin()` on another, and checks that the onode, its age bin stamp and the counts stay with the holding shard, which can still evict it.

Split out of #73273 at ifed01's suggestion.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82605

73668.title: cmake: link extblkdev via blk, drop --copy-dt-needed-entries
73668.author: Doracly
73668.body:
## Problem

`extblkdev` is in `ceph_common_deps`, although libceph-common uses nothing from it, so `libextblkdev.a` follows `libceph-common.so` on link lines. With ld.bfd and `--as-needed` (Ubuntu's GCC default), `libceph-common.so` is dropped when no object before it needs it, and a later archive member referencing it fails to link:

* GCC + `WITH_SYSTEM_GTEST=ON`: the C++17 system gmock leaves `std::string` members undefined, ld pulls the C++23 `ExtBlkDevPlugin.o` for them, and its libceph-common references fail, e.g. for `unittest_async_call`.
* With `libcephfs.so` on the link line, the same shows as "DSO missing from command line". c6ac71d398c worked around that with `-Wl,--copy-dt-needed-entries` (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/70498). 585b64d0777 then removed two of the archives behind it, json_spirit and erasure_code. extblkdev is the last.

## Fix

1. Link extblkdev from blk. Its only callers are KernelDevice (blk) and BlueStore (links blk). blk now links it regardless of libaio, since SPDK-only and FreeBSD BlueStore builds got it via ceph-common.
2. Drop the workaround from the libcephfs and fs tests, together with the linker check from #71494.

## Testing

* GCC 15 + ld.bfd, Debug with crimson, SPDK and rgw, on current main: `all tests vstart` builds; `unittest_async_call` with system gtest links and passes.
* The ten libcephfs/fs tests link without the option with GCC 11, 13 and 15 + ld.bfd, with and without the extblkdev move. GCC 11 and 13 were linked against GCC 15's libstdc++, which Ubuntu 26.04's system libraries need.
* With the move, no archive after `libceph-common.so` on their link lines references a symbol only libceph-common defines; before it, only `libextblkdev.a` did.

Not tested: jammy, where the original failure appeared.

## Relation to #72620

#72620's first commit makes the `--copy-dt-needed-entries` check rerun on each configure. If this PR merges first, that commit is dropped there.

73673.title: os/bluestore: keep at least one cache age bin
73673.author: ming1
73673.body:
Zeros in `bluestore_cache_age_bins_*` are documented as "no items at that priority", so an all-zero list means everything at the lowest priority. It also makes `import_bins()` call `set_bin_count(0)`: `circular_buffer::set_capacity(0)` frees the ring, `shift_bins()` then inserts nothing, and the next insert dereferences `age_bins.front()` of an empty ring. The OSD segfaults within a second of mount, for the data, meta and both rocksdb caches. An empty or malformed string parses to no bins and crashes the same way.

Clamp the ring to one bin in both `set_bin_count()` implementations. Valid lists are unchanged. The added store test sets all four lists to zeros, remounts and reads; it segfaulted before the fix and passes with it.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82941

73674.title: os/bluestore: flush replayed deferred writes before removing their keys
73674.author: lumir-sliva
73674.body:
## Summary

Since #69961, deferred replay at mount and in deep fsck/repair removes the deferred keys without flushing the data device first. On an HDD with a volatile write cache and a separate DB, a power loss right after the replay loses the replayed writes for good. This flushes the data device once replay has written everything, and restores the two `DeferredReplayTest` cases that fail on main since that PR.

## Problem

70a982dd1eb split replay into "apply the IO" (`_deferred_replay()`: `aio_write`, `aio_wait`) and "remove the keys" (`_open_db_and_around()`: `submit_transaction_sync` of the `L` removals). Between the two nothing flushes BlueStore's `bdev`: BlueFS has its own `BlockDevice` for the shared device, so its flushes are no-ops for these writes (`KernelDevice::flush()` returns early unless that instance wrote). Before, replay went through the deferred write path and the kv sync thread flushed before it removed the keys.

Reproduced on vstart with the data device on a ublk HDD model (64 MiB volatile cache) and a separate DB: leave deferred keys pending with a kill + rollback to the last flush (dm-log-writes), run `ceph-bluestore-tool fsck --deep`, roll back to the last flush again, fsck again. main, 3/3:

| pending keys | flushes logged during the replaying fsck | keys after | second fsck |
|---|---|---|---|
| 77 / 27 / 63 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | 44 / 27 / 8 errors |

    _verify_csum bad crc32c/0x1000 checksum at blob offset 0xe000, got 0x199830d7, expected 0xb72e3f09, device location [0x6f7ef000~1000], ...
    fsck error: #1:0d011fe3:::rbd_data.102a693c0ed7.00000000000001bc:head# error during read:  0~400000 (5) Input/output error

With this PR: 3/3 clean (65-76 keys replayed, one flush after the replayed writes, second fsck success).

## Changes

- `os/bluestore: flush the data device after replaying deferred writes`: one `bdev->flush()` after the last replay batch, only if something was written. It's in `_deferred_replay()` so it covers every caller (mount, fsck deep/repair, `mount_readonly`). `io_since_flush` is set in the aio thread before `aio_wait()` returns, so the flush is never skipped.
- `os/bluestore: replay deferred writes once in mount_readonly`: 75f56543eb7 added a replay at the end of `_mount_readonly()`, but `mount_readonly()`, its only caller, still replays too. Kept the one in `mount_readonly()`, which checks the result.
- `os/bluestore: count replayed deferred writes`: replay counts its writes in `submitted_deferred_writes` / `_bytes` again, as it did through the deferred write path.
- `test/objectstore: check deferred replay flushes its writes`: new case in `unittest_deferred`. A child leaves deferred writes pending; a second child mounts with `bdev_inject_crash` armed from `dtr_deferred_replay_start`, so a device flush exits 1, and `dtr_deferred_replay_end` exits 2. Auto compactions are off so BlueFS doesn't flush inside the window.

Not changed: `_open_db_and_around()` ignores `_deferred_replay()`'s `-EIO`, and a deferred txn that fails to decode has its key queued for removal anyway (noted on the tracker).

## Tests

- `unittest_deferred`: passes; with the flush commit reverted the new case fails ("deferred replay ended without a flush", exit 2).
- `ceph_test_objectstore` deferred set (`*StoreTestSpecificAUSize.Deferred*`, `ReproBug56488Test`, `DeferredReplayTest`, `DeferredWriteTest`): 26/26; both `DeferredReplayTest` cases fail on main.
- Power-cut reproducer above, before and after; also on plain loop devices with an 8 GiB DB (no disk model): main lost data 3/3 (17-63 fsck errors, no flush of the data device during the replaying fsck), this PR 3/3 clean. With a 2 GiB DB the loss is often hidden: a RocksDB compaction output lands on `db.slow` and BlueFS's fsync of it flushes the main device too.

#69961 is being backported (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68060: umbrella, tentacle, squid), so this has to go with it.

@aclamk since this touches the replay split.

Fixes: https://tracker.

73675.title: cephadm: add rgw-gap-list as a managed service
73675.author: ujjawal-ibm
73675.body:
### Issue: 
RGW's rgw-gap-list.py finds bucket index entries whose RADOS objects are missing. It is a manual run today, so nobody sees a gap until a client gets a 404. There is no cephadm way to run it regularly on a cluster. 

### Fix:
Adds a new rgw-gap-list service type to cephadm. Each daemon is a long-running container that just sleeps, plus a systemd timer on the host. When the timer fires, it does a podman exec into the container and runs the script. 

### Testing and validation:
- Created two buckets, one untouched and one with 3 of 8 RADOS objects deleted. The scan reported 0 gaps for the first and exactly the 3 missing objects for the second. A missing multipart tail object was also detected.
- The timer fired by itself and updated the status file. Changing the spec updated the timer.
- Bad specs were rejected through ceph orch apply and were not stored.
- Timeouts: the in-container timeout and systemd's TimeoutStartSec both kill a hung scan.
- count_per_host: 2, scaling from 2 to 1, restart, and ceph orch rm all worked. rm left no units, directories, containers or keys.

Dependent PR containing the Script (RGW): https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73548

73678.author: next0262

73682.title: compressor/zstd: keep the bundled libzstd's symbols local to the plugin
73682.author: dvanders
73682.body:
`libceph_zstd.so` statically links the bundled zstd but exports all 290 `ZSTD_*` symbols. Daemons also load the distro `libzstd.so.1` through libcurl (a dependency of libceph-common), so the plugin's calls bind to the distro library: with `LD_DEBUG=bindings`, every zstd entry point the plugin calls resolves to `/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libzstd.so.1` (1.5.5 on Ubuntu 24.04). The bundled zstd is effectively unused, and updating the `src/zstd` submodule doesn't change what daemons run.

Link the plugin with `--exclude-libs,libzstd.a`, so that it uses the copy it was built with. Packagers who want the distro library keep using `WITH_SYSTEM_ZSTD`. Not on Apple, whose linker has no `--exclude-libs`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82947

## Testing

On main, Ubuntu 24.04:
- exported `ZSTD_*` symbols of `libceph_zstd.so`: 290 before, 0 after;
- `LD_DEBUG=bindings` while `unittest_compression` runs: after the change the plugin's symbols bind to itself, libc, libstdc++ and libceph-common, and none to the distro `libzstd.so.1`;
- `unittest_compression`: 91 passed.

73683.title: zstd: update the submodule to v1.5.7
73683.author: dvanders
73683.body:
zstd 1.5.7 compresses small and medium blocks considerably faster at the fast levels Ceph uses (`compressor_zstd_level` defaults to 1). At BlueStore's default 64 KiB compression blob size, level 1, single core (AMD EPYC Milan, libzstd with a reused context), compress MB/s:

| data | 1.5.6 | 1.5.7 | |
|---|---|---|---|
| json-like | 686 | 1031 | +50% |
| logs | 466 | 612 | +31% |
| Silesia corpus | 392 | 456 | +16% |

and 20-28% at level 3 on 64-128 KiB blocks. Decompression, 1 MiB blocks and level 9 are unchanged.

This only reaches running daemons together with #73682: without it, the plugin's calls bind to the distro `libzstd.so.1` instead of the bundled copy.

Note for incremental builds: `BuildZstd.cmake` doesn't rebuild `libzstd.a` when the submodule moves; remove `build/zstd_ext-prefix/src/zstd_ext-stamp/zstd_ext-build` first.

## Testing

`libceph_zstd.so` built with 1.5.7 on main (Ubuntu 24.04); `unittest_compression`: 91 passed.

73684.title: osd/PeeringState: don't walk the pg log from both ends to trim it
73684.author: dvanders
73684.body:
`PeeringState::calc_trim_to_aggressive()` finds the trim point by walking the pg log list from the tail and from the head at the same time, until it has both the entry `num_to_trim` from the tail and the entry `target` from the head. The walk from the head is up to `target` entries of pointer chasing (about 4,700 with the default per-OSD budget and 64 PGs), and it never changes the result: versions grow towards the head and `num_to_trim` is at most `size - target`, so the trim point is always the entry `min(num_to_trim, size - target)` from the tail. Walk only that far.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82946

## Measured

main, memstore, one OSD on 8 cores, 4 `rados bench` clients (4 KiB, 32 in flight each), so the OSD is CPU-bound; median of 3 runs each, OSD CPU from /proc:

| | write IOPS | OSD CPU per write | rand read IOPS |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 58.6k | 104.8 µs | 112.7k |
| this PR | 64.0k (+9.1%) | 99.9 µs (−4.7%) | 113.1k |

In `perf`, the function goes from 5.6% to 0.2% of the OSD's CPU under writes; its samples were on the two pointer loads of the list walk. PG log lengths under load are unchanged (max 4,787 per PG either way).

## Tests

- New `PeeringStateTest.TrimLogAggressive`: on an active primary with `pglog_hardlimit`, `pg_trim_to` stays put while fewer than `osd_pg_log_trim_min` entries are over the target, then keeps exactly the newest `target` entries. It passes with and without the fix.
- `unittest_peeringstate` (56) and `unittest_pglog` (54) pass.

Not tested: teuthology, BlueStore (where the walk is a smaller share of each op), EC pools.

73685.title: rgw/s3vectors: Support Vector bucket quotas and accounting
73685.author: soumyakoduri
73685.body:
Implement quota, usage and chown functionalities for native vector buckets.

* Check effective bucket and owner quotas at the start of CreateIndex and PutVectors. 
* Include native vector buckets in user and account statistics, and keep vector request usage separate from ordinary S3 buckets.
* Route supported admin operations through the vector namespace

In addition, 
* add runtime config options that bound the number of logical S3-Vectors entities, mirroring the AWS S3 Vectors service limits:
   - rgw_s3vector_max_indexes_per_bucket (default 10000) is checked by CreateIndex against the vector bucket's current index count.
   - rgw_s3vector_max_vectors_per_index (default 2000000000) is checked by PutVectors against the target index's current vector count.

Assisted-by: Codex:GPT-6-Astra
Signed-off-by: Soumya Koduri <skoduri@redhat.com>

73686.author: next0262
73686.body:
CopyObject leaves the SSE headers out of the IAM environment. A bucket policy that denies writes without `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` therefore rejects copies even when the header is supplied.

This carries Raja Sharma's fix from #67238 unchanged and adds the requested s3test. The test checks that a copy without the SSE header is denied and one with `ServerSideEncryption='AES256'` succeeds.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74739

73687.title: cls/rgw_gc: stop listing expired entries at the first unexpired one
73687.author: next0262
73687.body:
We hit this with two groups of four RGWs deployed using Rook, sharing the same RADOS cluster and RGW zone. One group used `rgw_gc_obj_min_wait=3600` and the other used the default 7200. After deleting completed multipart objects, about 3.5 TiB of tail objects remained without their head objects. The GC queues were empty and no GC errors were reported.

Expired-only listing skips unexpired entries, but queue removal pops entries from the head by count. Different wait values can put an expired entry behind an unexpired one. For example, within one shard

```text
Entry  Enqueued  Wait    Expires
A      10:00     7200s   12:00
B      10:10     3600s   11:10
```

At 11:30, GC returns B and deletes its tail objects, then removes one queue entry from the head, A. A's tail objects remain, but their GC entry is gone.

Stop expired-only listing at the first unexpired entry and return `truncated=false`. This keeps listing aligned with removal by count. Entries behind it wait for a later pass once it expires. `radosgw-admin gc list` without `--include-all` follows the same boundary; full listing is unchanged.

Includes a regression test for out-of-order expiry. Earlier vstart validation on `e79f554d95b` passed all eight Replicated tests. FAST_EC was not run, and builds and tests were not repeated on this base.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82952

73688.title: rgw: remove the log sync module
73688.author: abrahamperz
73688.body:
Remove the `log` sync module from RGW. It only wrote a log line for each object a zone would sync and has no other use.

- Delete `rgw_sync_module_log.{cc,h}`, drop it from `src/rgw/CMakeLists.txt` and stop registering the `log` tier type in `rgw_register_sync_modules()`.
- Drop the mention of the `log` plugin from `doc/radosgw/sync-modules.rst`.

The shared stat-remote-object coroutines (`RGWStatRemoteObjCBCR`, `RGWCallStatRemoteObjCR`) stay, because the Elasticsearch and cloud sync modules still use them.

Verified that `radosgw` and `radosgw-admin` build with the module removed, and that the RGW unit tests `unittest_rgw_iam_policy`, `unittest_rgw_bucket_sync_cache` and `unittest_rgw_frontend_type` still pass. No other code, test or qa suite references the `log` tier type.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80892

73689.title: osd: Fix data corruption in ECTransactionL with write+truncate
73689.author: MattyWilliams22
73689.body:
When a client I/O request contains both a write and a truncate, the
incorrect calculation of append_after (using logical_to_prev_stripe_offset
instead of the stripe-aligned new_size) caused writes to be treated as
appends, overwriting existing data with zeros and destroying previously
written data in the stripe.

This PR contains a fix for this issue, as well as some changes to ceph_test_rados_io_sequence which allow for this fix to be tested.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82864

73690.title: umbrella: doc/cephfs: explain caps that cover every file system
73690.author: anthonyeleven
73690.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82955

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73559
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74356

The tracker issue asks what `fsname=*` means in an MDS capability, and how `allow rw fsname=*` differs from `allow rw`. The File System Information Restriction section of the client capabilities page shows only caps for a single file system. In the code there is no `fsname=*`: the MDS and Monitor cap grammars accept only `[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]` in an `fsname` value (`src/mds/MDSAuthCaps.cc`, `src/mon/MonCap.cc`), and the Monitor parses MDS caps when they're set (`AuthMonitor::valid_caps()`). A cap without `fsname` matches every file system (`MDSCapMatch::match_fs()`), and `ceph fs authorize '*'` writes exactly that: MDS and Monitor caps with no `fsname`, and the OSD cap `allow rw tag cephfs data=*`. This adds that to the section, with an example.

Tested on a one-Monitor Tentacle 20.2.5 cluster (the `fsname` grammar is the same on main):

- `ceph auth get-or-create client.star mds 'allow rw fsname=*' mon 'allow r'` fails with `Error EINVAL: mds capability parse failed, stopped at 'fsname=*' of 'allow rw fsname=*'`.
- `mon 'allow r fsname=*'` fails the same way (`mon capability parse failed`), and so does `fsname="*"`.
- `ceph fs authorize '*' client.alluser / rw` writes `mds "allow rw"`, `mon "allow r"`, and `osd "allow rw tag cephfs data=*"`, as in the new example.

Clean cherry-pick of 1 commit, with the same line changes as on main.

73697.title: msg/async: take the worker reference under pool_spin in get_worker()
73697.author: abrahamperz
73697.body:
`NetworkStack::get_worker()` scans for the least referenced worker while holding `pool_spin`, but increments that worker's `references` only after releasing the lock. A concurrent caller that takes the lock in that window still sees the old count and picks the same worker, so two connections land on one worker while another gets none. Later picks only partly compensate, and established connections are never rebalanced.

This change takes the reference before releasing `pool_spin`, so choosing a worker and reserving it happen in one step.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82667

## Testing

I added `GetWorkerBalanceTest` to `ceph_test_async_networkstack`. In each of 1000 rounds, the test starts one thread per worker, lets every thread call `get_worker()` once at the same moment, and then checks that each worker was picked exactly once.

- Without the fix, the test failed at round 13. A standalone loop running the same race failed in about 4–6% of rounds (`min 0 max 2` references).
- With the fix, the test passes. The standalone loop showed no imbalance in 100,000 rounds with 2 to 8 workers.
- `SimpleTest`, `ConnectFailedTest`, `ListenTest`, `AcceptAndCloseTest` and `ComplexTest` still pass. `StressTest` aborts in my environment with or without this change, so that failure is unrelated.

`ceph_test_async_networkstack` is not part of `make check`, so CI does not run this test automatically.

73698.title: osd/scrubber: do not reschedule a wiped scrub target to "never"
73698.author: paulreece42
73698.body:
This was tricky to reproduce on the vstart.sh dev cluster, without much data - 
the bug is much easier to see, on a production cluster.

start_scrub_session() resets the selected scheduling target (clearing its
not_before/scheduled_at times back to the utime_t::max() sentinel,
2106-02-07T06:28:15.999999) as soon as the scrub is committed - *before* the
replica reservations are granted. If a replica then rejects the reservation
request, requeue_penalized() -> delay_on_failure() adds the retry delay to the
wiped not_before value. As utime_t saturates at 2^32-1 seconds, the addition
leaves the target at the sentinel: the PG is never periodically scrubbed again
(at that level) until an operator command, a configuration change or a primary
change recomputes its schedule. Operators see this as PGs whose next deep-scrub
is "scheduled" at 2106-02-07.

The fix anchors the retry delay on the current time whenever the target no
longer carries a valid time. The commit-adjacent SchedTarget::scheduled_at of
the failed attempt retains the sentinel afterwards; that field does not
participate in eligibility or queue ordering, only not_before does.

## Evidence

Test commit `9411704c16f` reproduces the exact sequence on a vstart cluster
(4 OSDs, osd_max_scrubs=1, reservation queuing disabled): PG A holds the shared
replica's reservation; PG B's committed periodic deep scrub is rejected by that
replica. Without the fix, the test fails with:

    osd.3 scrub-job:pg[1.1]:delay_on_failure: delayed deep scrub due to replicas for 5s.
      Updated: 1.1/dp,nb:2106-02-07T06:28:15.999,(periodic-regular,tr:2106-02-07T06:28:15.999),q:-,issue:replicas
    B (1.1) deep target after the reservation failure: 2106-02-07T06:28:15.999999+0000
    FAIL: tracker issue #79134 reproduced

With the fix, the same sequence reschedules to a real retry time and the test
passes:

    Updated: 1.1/dp,nb:2026-11-09T18:42:54.989,(periodic-regular,tr:2106-02-07T06:28:15.999),q:-,issue:replicas
    B (1.1) deep target after the reservation failure: 2026-11-09T18:42:54.989252+0000

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79134
Signed-off-by: Paul Reece <reecep@frib.msu.edu>

73699.title: cls/rgw: don't log ENOENT from BIVerObjEntry::init() as an error
73699.author: abrahamperz
73699.body:
When a client deletes an object in a versioned bucket without a version id, RGW links a delete marker under a newly generated instance. That instance has no index entry yet, so `BIVerObjEntry::init()` gets `-ENOENT`, which `rgw_bucket_link_olh()` expects and handles. `init()` still logged it at level 0:

```
<cls> .../cls_rgw.cc:1482: ERROR: read_key_entry() idx=\x801000_obj ret=-2
```

This fills the OSD logs with misleading errors on every such delete. `rgw_bucket_unlink_instance()` already skips logging `-ENOENT` from `init()`, but the message from `init()` itself was still printed.

This change makes `init()` log `-ENOENT` at level 20 and leaves the decision to the caller. `rgw_bucket_link_olh()` now logs the failure itself when it is not linking a delete marker, so a real missing instance is still reported at level 0. Other errors from `init()` are logged as before.

It also adds `TestClsRgw.link_olh_delete_marker`, which links a delete marker to a new instance and checks that it becomes the current version. As far as I can tell, no existing test covered this path.

Testing: ran `ceph_test_cls_rgw` against a vstart cluster (1 mon, 3 bluestore OSDs). With the new test and without the fix, each delete-marker link printed the `ERROR: read_key_entry()` line above in the OSD log. With the fix, only the level-20 message remains, and all 50 `ceph_test_cls_rgw` tests pass (Replicated and FastEC).

This picks up the change from #48119, which was closed as stale.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/58886

73700.title: mds: do not pin the dirfrag while the export's sessions flush
73700.author: xiubli
73700.body:
Once an export has frozen its subtree, `Migrator::export_frozen()` flushes the sessions of the clients that hold caps in it. `C_M_ExportSessionsFlushed` waits for that flush, and it kept the dirfrag pinned with `PIN_PTRWAITER` until the last client acked.

That can take a while, because it depends on the clients, and the export can be cancelled meanwhile, for example when the importer fails. The cancel unfreezes the dirfrag, but the pin stays. A split or merge of the dirfrag in that window then trips the reference count check at the end of `CDir::finish_old_fragment()`, and the exporter crashes:

```
src/mds/CDir.cc: 1019: FAILED ceph_assert(get_num_ref() == (state_test(STATE_STICKY) ? 1:0))
 ...
 CDir::finish_old_fragment(...)
 CDir::split(...)
 MDCache::adjust_dir_fragments(...)
 MDCache::dispatch_fragment_dir(...)
 MDCache::fragment_frozen(...)
```

Right before the assert, the dirfrag still holds `ptrwaiter=1`.

**Fix** (`mds: do not pin the dirfrag while the export's sessions flush`)

Keep the `dirfrag_t` instead of a pinned `CDir*`, and look the dirfrag up again when the flush completes. Dropping only the pin is not enough, because the pointer would then dangle once the old fragment is gone.

If the dirfrag is no longer there, the export is gone as well. `export_sessions_flushed()` already ignores a dirfrag whose export was cancelled or restarted, through the tid check.

**Test** (`qa/cephfs: test splitting a dirfrag after its export was cancelled`)

`TestExportCancelFlushingSessions.test_fragment_after_cancel` in `test_exports.py` does the following:

1. It pauses the importer, so that the export waits in DISCOVERING.
2. It cuts the client's network. The client has already answered the cap revokes of the export's locks.
3. It resumes the importer. The importer acks the prep, and the exporter waits in WARNING for the session flush, which never ends.
4. It fails the importer, which cancels the export.
5. It splits the dirfrag on the exporter.

Without the fix, the exporter crashes in step 5. With the fix, the dirfrag splits into 2 fragments, the exporter stays up and every file is still there. The test needs the client in a netns, and is skipped otherwise.

**Testing**

- The new qa test, run with vstart_runner `--usens`:
  - without the fix, the exporter asserts in `CDir::finish_old_fragment()` and the test fails;
  - with the fix, the test passes.
- A manual reproduction with the client's replies to the MDSs delayed (ceph-fuse with `ms_inject_delay_type=mds`, `ms_inject_delay_max=60`), on 2 active MDSs and 1 standby. Steps: `export dir /d 1` on rank 0, fail rank 1 while the session flush is pending, then `dirfrag split /d 0/0 1`.
  - Without the fix, it crashed 2 times out of 2.
  - With the fix, `/d` was split in 2 runs out of 2, with all files listed and no assert.

Exports are cancelled more often where they are frequent, as with ephemeral or distributed pins and `max_mds` changes, so such setups are more likely to hit this.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82968

73701.title: squid: test/rgw/multisite: use boto3 in test_suspended_delete_marker_incremental_sync
73701.author: abrahamperz
73701.body:
`rgw_multi.tests.test_suspended_delete_marker_incremental_sync` fails on squid with:

```
    bucket.configure_versioning(True)
AttributeError: 's3.Bucket' object has no attribute 'configure_versioning'
```

This is a squid-only fix: main already has the boto3 version of this test (converted by 3438add3fc9 "qa/multisite: boto3 in tests.py"). The change switches the test to `zone.s3_client`, matching main.

Testing: I ran squid's `test_suspended_delete_marker_incremental_sync()` with a real boto3 `s3.Bucket` and a botocore `Stubber` client in place of a multisite cluster. Before the change it raises the same `AttributeError`; after it, the test passes and makes the expected `put_bucket_versioning` (Enabled, Suspended), `put_object` and `delete_object` calls. `pyflakes` no longer reports `new_key` as undefined. The sync behaviour itself is exercised by the rgw multisite suite.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82954

73702.title: umbrella: doc/cephfs: refine the large omap objects section
73702.author: anthonyeleven

73704.title: tools/rados: do not exit() on missing arguments after connecting
73704.author: abrahamperz
73704.body:
`rados list-inconsistent-pg`, `list-inconsistent-obj`, `list-inconsistent-snapset` and `lock` call `usage_exit()` when an argument is missing. By that point `rados_tool_common()` has already connected the Rados client, so `exit()` destroys static objects while the client's `io_context_pool` thread is still running. The command then intermittently aborts instead of printing the usage and failing:

```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range'
  what():  map::at
*** Caught signal (Aborted) **
 ...
 9: (std::__throw_out_of_range(char const*)+0x44)
 10: (md_config_t::update_legacy_vals(ConfigValues&)+0x10d)
 11: (md_config_t::set_mon_vals(...))
```

Some runs segfault instead. This change replaces those post-connect `usage_exit()` calls with `usage(cerr); return -EINVAL;`, so the client is shut down normally and the tool still exits with status 1. `usage_exit()` stays for argument parsing in `main()`, which runs before the client connects.

Verification on a vstart cluster (1 mon), built from main:
- Before: `rados list-inconsistent-pg` (no pool) and `list-inconsistent-obj`/`list-inconsistent-snapset` (no pgid) aborted or segfaulted in about half of the runs.
- After: 30 runs of each command printed the usage and exited with status 1, with no crashes. The `pool "nosuchpool" not found` path is unchanged.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82969

73707.title: mds: journal ambiguous imports that a peer claimed in subtree maps
73707.author: xiubli
73707.body:
An import stays open in the journal from its EImportStart until its EImportFinish. If the importer fails in between, the rank that takes over replays the EImportStart and holds the import as ambiguous.

The problem is in resolve:

- `MDCache::handle_resolve()` applies the exporter's claim on the import at once, which gives the subtree back to the exporter in cache.
- `disambiguate_my_imports()` logs the EImportFinish(false) that cancels each import only later, one import at a time.
- `MDCache::create_subtree_map()` journals only the subtrees whose auth is ours in cache. A subtree map journaled in between, such as the one that starts a major segment, therefore leaves out the imports that are still open in the journal.

The next replay of that journal applies the EImportStart, holds the import as ambiguous, and then finds it missing from the map:

```
replayed ESubtreeMap at 4955231 does not include cache subtree 0x10000000273
...
src/mds/journal.cc: FAILED ceph_assert(!mds->mdlog->get_debug_subtrees() || errors == 0)
```

When the subtree map check is armed, every daemon that takes the rank asserts on the same map, and the rank cannot come back. The check is currently armed even with `mds_debug_subtrees` off, see #73665.

#72265 runs into this (see https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72265#issuecomment-6759577727). There, fragments of tree-pinned directories moved back and forth between the ranks every few seconds. When rank 0 failed, two of its imports were still open, and rank 0 then asserted 18 times on the same map. The race itself is in main.

**Fix** (`mds: journal ambiguous imports that a peer claimed in subtree maps`)

`create_subtree_map()` now journals every import still in `my_ambiguous_imports` as an ambiguous subtree of ours, with the bounds it was imported with. That is how replay holds it at that point of the journal. The EImportFinish(false) that follows cancels it, as before.

**Test** (`qa/cephfs: test a claimed ambiguous import in the importer's subtree maps`)

`TestAmbiguousImportSubtreeMap.test_claimed_ambiguous_import_in_subtree_map` in `test_exports.py`:

1. Sets `mds_log_events_per_segment 1` and `mds_log_minor_segments_per_major_segment 4`, so that a subtree map is journaled every few events.
2. Pins ten directories to rank 1, then clears the pins.
3. Sets `mds_kill_import_at 7` on rank 0 and holds rank 0 while rank 1 starts exporting all ten directories to it. Rank 0 then journals their EImportStarts together and dies before it acks.
4. The standby takes over. In resolve, the exporter claims the imports back, and subtree maps are journaled while the EImportFinishes are logged.
5. Fails rank 0 again and waits for the MDS daemons.

**Testing**

On a vstart cluster built from main:

| | without the fix | with the fix |
|---|---|---|
| the new qa test | fails: "does not include cache subtree" errors, and every daemon that takes rank 0 asserts in replay, so `wait_for_daemons()` times out | passes |
| the same steps run by hand | rank 0 stays in `replay(laggy)`; the 7 imports left out of the map are reported | rank 0 replays and goes active |

In both builds, the journal of the rank that took over has subtree maps between the EImportFinish(false) events, at the same points.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82971

73709.title: mds: avoid orphaned client sessions after failover of a non-zero rank
73709.author: smolix
73709.body:
## What and why

After a failover of a non-zero active MDS rank, a kernel client can end up with a session on that rank that the client does not know about. Nobody renews it. After `session_autoclose` (300 s) the MDS evicts it and, with `mds_session_blocklist_on_timeout` (the default), blocklists the client, so the mount fails on every rank. We observed this on 20.2.4 and 21.2.0 with 8 active ranks, `ceph.dir.pin.distributed` and 6.8 kernel clients.

Both routes we found go through the same messenger behaviour. With `Policy::stateful_server`, a client that connects again with a new client cookie gets its existing server-side `Connection` reused ("found previous session ... peer must have reseted"). A remote reset and then an accept are queued for that `Connection`. `MDSDaemon::ms_handle_remote_reset()` marks it down when its `Session` is a closed bootstrap session.

**Route 1: accept after mark_down (commits 1-4)**
1. A client with no session to rank N sends `REQUEST_OPEN` while N is in up:reconnect. The MDS parks it until clientreplay.
2. The client resets and reconnects with a new cookie. The messenger reuses the `Connection` and queues a remote reset and an accept.
3. `ms_handle_remote_reset()` marks the `Connection` down. The queued `ms_handle_accept()` is still delivered, and it attaches a new bootstrap `Session` to the dead connection.
4. At clientreplay the parked `REQUEST_OPEN` finds that `Session`. The session is opened and journaled, and the OPEN reply is dropped. The result is an orphaned session.

Fix: add `Connection::is_closed()` (true once the `AsyncConnection` is in the terminal `STATE_CLOSED`). The MDS does not attach a session on accept of a closed connection, and drops a parked `REQUEST_OPEN` whose connection is closed. A new deterministic test, `MessengerTest.AcceptAfterRemoteResetMarkDownTest`, reproduces the ordering.

**Route 2: a refused reconnect's connection left in standby (commits 5-7)**
1. At the failover, the client's export-target reconnect to rank X is refused ("ignoring msg from not-open session"). X sends CLOSE, and the server-side `Connection` stays in STANDBY with a closed bootstrap `Session`.
2. Later (about 90 s in our trials), a subtree that holds the client's caps is exported to X. X force-opens a session. The client's new connection is grafted onto the STANDBY `Connection`, and `ms_handle_remote_reset()` marks it down.
3. The client answers the reset with a reconnect. X is up:active and denies it, but keeps the force-opened session. The client is blocklisted at autoclose.

Fix: mark the connection disposable in every deny branch of `handle_client_reconnect()`. When a reconnect is denied for a session that holds nothing that needs fencing (no caps, leases, requests or delegated inos), close that session. During up:reconnect and up:rejoin the decision waits until clientreplay or active. `_session_logged()` sends no second CLOSE and does not mark the new connection disposable for exactly that close (`deny_close_seq`). The remote-reset `mark_down` is now logged at level 1.

## Evidence (summary)

- We root-caused route 1 from MDS logs and kernel dynamic debug output on stock 20.2.4.
- With commits 1-4 applied, 2 of 33 exposures (non-zero-rank failovers with a cold kernel client) still orphaned a session, both through route 2. Route 2 also explains the 6 such cases in the stock baselines.
- Route 2 step 2 hit 109 of 110 late opens to a rank that had refused the client at the failover, and 0 of 349 other opens.
- We run this series in production on 21.2.0 (umbrella).

## Commits

1. msg: add Connection::is_closed()
2. test/msgr: accept delivered after mark_down from remote reset
3. mds: do not attach a session to a closed connection on accept
4. mds: drop session open requests from a closed connection
5. mds: drop refused reconnect connections and close denied sessions
6. mds: log the mark_down in ms_handle_remote_reset at level 1
7. mds: do not leave any refused reconnect's connection in sta

73710.title: os/bluestore: apply cache age bin option changes at runtime
73710.author: abrahamperz
73710.body:
BlueStore never applied a runtime change to the cache age bin options.

`BlueStore::get_tracked_keys()` registered the bin lists as `bluestore_cache_kv_age_bins`, `bluestore_cache_kv_onode_age_bins`, `bluestore_cache_meta_age_bins` and `bluestore_cache_data_age_bins`, but the options are named `bluestore_cache_age_bins_{kv,kv_onode,meta,data}`. Because no observer tracked the real names and the options lack the `runtime` flag, `md_config_t::_set_val()` rejected a new bin list with EPERM ("may not be modified at runtime"). `bluestore_cache_age_bin_interval` was tracked, but `handle_conf_change()` had no branch for it, so a new value was accepted and then ignored. In both cases the OSD kept the values it parsed at startup.

This change:
- tracks the options under their real names;
- moves the parsing into `_set_cache_age_bins()`. `handle_conf_change()` bumps `config_changed`, and the mempool thread re-parses the bins and the interval itself. It is the only reader of these values once the store is mounted, so they are never modified while it reads them;
- clears each vector before refilling it. `_open_bdev()` runs once for `is_rotational()` and again at mount, and the old code appended on each run, so every list was held twice and `import_bins()` read the duplicate entries as priorities 7-10.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82909

### Testing
- New unit tests in `unittest_bluestore_types`:
  - `BlueStore.tracked_keys_are_options` checks that every tracked key is a real option and that the age bin options are tracked.
  - `BlueStore.age_bins_can_change_at_runtime` checks that `set_val()` accepts a new bin list.
- Without the fix, both tests fail: 8 assertions fail on the misspelled and untracked keys, and `set_val()` returns EPERM. With the fix, the whole binary passes (158 tests).
- `ceph_test_objectstore` BlueStore `SimpleMetaColTest`, `SimpleObjectTest`, `BufferCacheReadTest` and `Synthetic` pass with `bluestore_cache_age_bin_interval=0.1`, which exercises the mempool thread's bin rotation.
- These tests did not change a bin list on a mounted store. Teuthology/integration CI still needs to cover that path.

73711.title: crimson/osd: spread the primary PGs evenly over an OSD's cores
73711.author: ronen-fr
73711.body:
A PG's core is chosen once, by PGShardMapping on core 0, when the OSD
    first sees the PG: the core with the fewest PGs. Primaries and replicas
    count alike, so which of a core's PGs are primaries is left to chance.
    But only the primaries serve the client reads: with about 11 primaries
    per core, the busiest core of an OSD typically serves 1.4-1.6 times the
    mean of the reads, and saturates first.
    
Choose a new PG's core by its role: a PG this OSD is the up primary of
    goes to the core with the fewest primaries, any other PG to the core
    with the fewest non-primaries; ties go to the core with the fewest PGs.
    Both counts end up balanced to within one PG.
    
The role is that in the OSD's current map, using the up primary (CRUSH
    and upmap), not a temporary acting one. The PGs loaded at startup, and
    split children (which stay on their parent's core), are counted too, so
    that new PGs balance against them. dump_store_shards shows the
    primaries of each core.

73716.title: librbd: mark objects dirty in HEAD object map after snapshot rollback
73716.author: fl189
73716.body:
## Description

With `object-map` and `fast-diff` enabled, `rbd snap rollback <image>@<snap>`
leaves the HEAD object map in a state where fast-diff considers rolled back
objects unchanged relative to the most recent snapshot. Every consumer of
fast-diff then misses the rollback for these objects:

* snapshot-based rbd-mirror (deep-copy between mirror snapshots),
* `rbd export-diff --whole-object` and `rbd diff --whole-object`,
* any other `diff_iterate(..., whole_object=true)` / deep-copy user.

The secondary image (or the incremental backup) keeps the data written
after the rollback target snapshot, while the primary has rolled back.
No error is reported anywhere.

### Root cause

1. `operation::SnapshotRollbackRequest` first calls
   `ObjectMap::rollback()`, i.e. `object_map::SnapshotRollbackRequest`,
   which reads the snapshot's object map and writes it with `write_full` as
   the new HEAD object map.
2. The snapshot's object map is a copy of the HEAD object map taken when
   the snapshot was created (`object_map::SnapshotCreateRequest` reads HEAD,
   writes it as the snapshot map, and only then flags `OBJECT_EXISTS` as
   `OBJECT_EXISTS_CLEAN` in HEAD). Objects that existed but were not written
   since the preceding snapshot are therefore `OBJECT_EXISTS_CLEAN` in the
   snapshot map, and after the rollback they are `OBJECT_EXISTS_CLEAN` in
   HEAD as well.
3. The objects themselves are then rolled back with
   `selfmanaged_snap_rollback` directly via `data_ctx.aio_operate()`,
   without any object map update. The OSD handles this as a modification
   of the HEAD object (`_rollback_to()` sets `ctx->modify` even if the HEAD
   object already matches the snapshot), so from the RADOS point of view
   the objects are dirty relative to the latest snapshot.
4. The next snapshot copies the HEAD object map, which still claims
   `OBJECT_EXISTS_CLEAN`. `object_map::DiffRequest` therefore keeps
   `DIFF_STATE_DATA` (instead of `DIFF_STATE_DATA_UPDATED`) for the
   interval [snapshot before the rollback, snapshot after the rollback] for
   objects that were clean in the rollback target snapshot and overwritten
   after it. `deep_copy::ImageCopyRequest` sets
   `OBJECT_COPY_REQUEST_FLAG_EXISTS_CLEAN` and `ObjectCopyRequest` skips
   the object, diff-iterate with `whole_object` does not report it.

### Fix

`object_map::SnapshotRollbackRequest` now decodes the snapshot object map
it read, converts every `OBJECT_EXISTS_CLEAN` entry to `OBJECT_EXISTS` and
writes the result as the new HEAD object map. `OBJECT_NONEXISTENT` and
`OBJECT_PENDING` are kept unchanged and the snapshot object map itself is
not modified. The on-disk CRC setting of the map is preserved (the
`BitVector` decoded from the raw object keeps it). If the snapshot object
map cannot be decoded, the request takes the existing read-error path
(snapshot and HEAD object maps are flagged invalid) instead of writing an
undecodable HEAD object map.

The in-memory HEAD object map needs no separate change:
`operation::SnapshotRollbackRequest` reopens the HEAD object map from disk
after rolling back the objects (`send_refresh_object_map()`) and swaps it
in. The fast-diff invalid flag handling is unchanged.

### Why this approach

* It is correct: every existing object receives a rollback op, which the
  OSD treats as a write, so "dirty since the latest snapshot" is the true
  state. It matches what `rbd object-map rebuild` computes from the
  snapsets after the rollback (`ObjectMapIterate` returns `OBJECT_EXISTS`
  for HEAD objects whose snapset seq is not older than the latest
  snapshot).
* It is conservative: an object is never reported as unchanged when it
  may have changed. The cost is a one-time full-object copy of all objects
  that exist at the rollback target on the next incremental sync / diff,
  which is the same as for any other write to these objects.
* It is local to the object map rollback and requires no on-disk format,
  cls or protocol change. Old clients are unaf

73719.title: os/bluestore: re-bin a buffer moved between 2Q cache shards
73719.author: abrahamperz
73719.body:
`Collection::split_cache()` moves the cached buffers of a split PG's onodes to the new collection's buffer cache shard with `_move()`. `TwoQBufferCacheShard::_move()` (the default `bluestore_cache_type = 2q`) never re-pointed `b->cache_age_bin`, so the moved bytes stayed counted in the *source* shard's age bins while the buffer sat on the destination's lists. Later `_touch()`/`_rm()`/`_adjust_size()` calls from the destination then updated a counter that belongs to the source shard while holding only the destination shard's lock.

This sets `b->cache_age_bin = age_bins.front()` in `TwoQBufferCacheShard::_move()` before adding the bytes back, the same as `_add()` and `LruBufferCacheShard::_move()` already do. The source's `_rm()` has already removed the bytes from the old counter.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82910

### Testing

Added `BufferCacheShard.move_rebins` to `unittest_bluestore_types`. It adds a 4 KiB clean buffer to one shard, `_move()`s it to a second shard, and checks both shards' `sum_bins()`, for both `lru` and `2q`.

- Without the fix: `lru` passes; `2q` fails with the source shard still at 4096 bytes and the destination at 0.
- With the fix: the test passes, and the whole `unittest_bluestore_types` binary passes (157 tests).

The concurrent-update race described in the tracker is inferred from the code and was not reproduced on a cluster.

73722.title: mount.ceph,test: fix -Werror build with clang 21 and glibc 2.43
73722.author: Doracly
73722.body:
Fixes three errors in a clang 21 `-Werror` build on Ubuntu 26.04 (glibc 2.43). CI doesn't see them: make check uses clang 19 and glibc 2.35, builds only the `tests` target, and uses `-Werror` for C++ only.

- **mount.ceph**: with `_GNU_SOURCE`, glibc 2.43 returns `const char *` from `strstr()` and `strchr()` for a const argument, so clang and gcc reject assigning the result to `char *`. The pointers into the device string are now const, and `parse_options()` takes the writable `optarg`. A missing `-o` is marked by `NULL` instead of the address of `EMPTY_STRING`, which is dropped; behaviour is unchanged.
- **test/fs**: `test_trim_caps` writes an uninitialized byte to a pipe (`-Wuninitialized-const-pointer`, new in clang 21).

Stacked on #72644 at 0a2c7309894, so only the 23 commits after it are new. Callum's essential review fixes are in #72644 itself: the thrasher's zone-keeping upmaps (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82980), five standalone scripts made executable, explicit legacy erasure coded pools in three tests, and three fixes to the upgrade workunits.

- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82973 osd/OSDMap: the monitors cancelled an upmap that splits an erasure coded pool's zone block across zones, but kept one that puts more of a replicated PG over zones in one zone than the pool keeps there. A PG in one zone cannot peer across zones, so it stayed clean+peered, not active. `keeps_zone_blocks()` now checks replicated pools over zones too, so `check_pg_upmaps()` cancels such an upmap. The new unit test fails without the fix.
- https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82981 osdc/SplitOp: a localized split read that asks for the object's version, as librados does on every read by default, still sent a sub-read to the primary, which for a pool over zones is in the other zone for about half the PGs. Past umbrella the version now comes from a read shard that can become primary or, if the read has none, from one extra sub-read to such a shard in the zone being read; the primary is still used up to umbrella and for operations with more than reads. The two zone tests of split reads again expect no sub-read in the other zone, and new unit tests fail without the fix.

The scripts move into three new directories, each with its own workload (`mon-stretch-rules`, `mon-stretch-pool-zones`, `mon-stretch-pool-rules`), and the four hand-rule num_zones tests into a script of their own, so each job stays well under the limit, also on slow nodes.

73725.title: librbd/deep_copy: propagate zeroed extents in incremental copies
73725.author: fl189
73725.body:
## Description

Snapshot-based rbd-mirror replicates each mirror snapshot with an
incremental deep copy (`src_snap_id_start > 0`). In that mode
`deep_copy::ObjectCopyRequest::compute_zero_ops()` drops every zeroed
extent that reaches the end of the object:

* `prev_end_size` starts at 0 because the size of the object as of the
  start snapshot is not known to the incremental copy,
* so `end_size` is 0 (or the end of the data written in the snapshot),
  every zeroed extent is classified as "zero interval at the object end",
* and the truncate is only emitted if `object_extent.offset <
  prev_end_size`, which never holds.

Two ways to hit this:

1. **Discards** (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/58852): a discard that
   removes an object, truncates it or zeroes a range up to its end is not
   replicated. The secondary keeps the old data and its allocation.
2. **Snapshot rollback** on the primary between two mirror snapshots (see
   the latest comment on the tracker): the rollback removes or truncates
   every object, or object range, that did not exist at the rollback
   target. `list-snaps` reports these ranges as `SPARSE_EXTENT_STATE_ZEROED`
   for the mirror snapshot taken after the rollback, the incremental copy
   drops them and the secondary keeps the data written after the rollback
   target. Unlike a missed discard this is silent data divergence: the
   secondary reports the mirror snapshot as synced, but its image holds
   different data than the primary. `rbd mirror image promote --force`
   rolls the image back internally as well, so a later resync in the other
   direction can run into the same situation.

`rbd export-diff | rbd import-diff` and the full deep copy are not
affected, only the incremental deep copy.

## Fix

All changes apply to incremental copies only (`m_src_snap_id_start > 0`).
The full copy takes exactly the same path as before.

* **Unknown start size.** The destination object already matches the
  source object as of the start snapshot, only its size is unknown. If the
  object existed at the start snapshot, `prev_end_size` now starts at
  `layout.object_size` (an upper bound) instead of 0. Zeroed extents inside
  the object stay zero ops (this is the case that went wrong in an earlier
  iteration of #52358: `blkdiscard -o 2M -l 4M` zeroed the whole second
  object on the secondary), zeroed extents up to the end of the object
  become truncate or remove ops. If the object did not exist at the start
  snapshot, `prev_end_size` stays 0 as before.
* **Use the truncation that list-snaps reports.** `ObjectListSnapsRequest`
  always walks the full object history from snap id 0 and reports a
  truncated object as a `ZEROED` extent `[new size, previous size)` and a
  removed object as `[0, previous size)`. Those are the only `ZEROED`
  extents it reports for snapshots after the start snapshot. The start of
  that extent is therefore the size of the source object in that
  snapshot, and `compute_zero_ops()` uses it as `end_size` instead of
  reconstructing it. A truncate within a partially written object (for
  example the last object of the image, or a rollback to a state where the
  object was smaller) is then copied as a truncate or remove and not as a
  zero op that leaves the object allocated.
* **Clones.** If the destination object is backed by its parent (parent
  overlap at the destination snapshot), a removal is copied as
  `create` + `truncate(0)` (whiteout), as the full copy does with
  `hide_parent`. A plain remove would let parent data show through on the
  destination after a discard in the clone, which librbd itself handles
  with a whiteout.
* **Object map.** The object map of the destination snapshot (for
  rbd-mirror the HEAD object map) was derived from the start snapshot and
  still flags a removed object as existing. The object is now flagged
  `OBJECT_PENDING` before the write and `OBJECT_NONEXISTENT` with
  `current_state = OBJECT_PENDING` once the remove has completed, the same
  seq

73726.title: erasure-code/jerasure: do not free a system libJerasure's fields
73726.author: abrahamperz
73726.body:
`debian/rules` builds with `WITH_SYSTEM_JERASURE=ON`, so the jerasure and shec plugins (and their legacy flavors) link the same shared `libJerasure`. They share `galois.c`'s table of default Galois fields. Each plugin's `jerasure_finish()` destructor frees those fields at exit but does not clear the table, so the second plugin frees them again. A monitor that has loaded both plugins corrupts its heap during shutdown, and tcmalloc segfaults under `gf_free()`, as in the tracker.

This change frees the fields only when the vendored jerasure is linked into the plugin, where each plugin owns its own copy. With the system library, the fields are left to the library.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82975

### How this was verified

- Reproducer: a small program that `dlopen()`s `libec_jerasure.so` and `libec_shec.so`, calls `jerasure_init()` in each and exits. With both plugins linked against the system `libJerasure`/`libgf_complete` (as in the Ubuntu packages), glibc aborts with `free(): double free detected in tcache 2`, and valgrind reports invalid reads/frees in `jerasure_finish()`. With this change: exit 0, valgrind `ERROR SUMMARY: 0 errors`.
- The vendored build is unchanged: the same reproducer is clean under valgrind before and after.
- A configure with `-DWITH_SYSTEM_JERASURE=ON` passes `-DWITH_SYSTEM_JERASURE` to `jerasure_init.cc`.
- `unittest_erasure_code*` (plugin, jerasure, shec, lrc; 12 tests) pass.

73727.title: test/libcephfs: initialize ceph_ll_io_info in async I/O tests
73727.author: vshankar
73727.body:
The nonblocking I/O tests declare struct ceph_ll_io_info on the stack and set only some of its fields. libcephfs reads write, fsync and syncdataonly from it, and write_fsync_io_callback() uses write to tell a write completion from a fsync completion.

In ConcurrentWriteAndFsync, fsync_func() never sets write. When the stack garbage there is non-zero, the fsync completion sets write_done instead of fsync_done. The writer, which was held in ceph_ll_nonblocking_readv_writev() by client_inject_write_delay_secs, then sees write_done already set, fails its result assertion and returns while its write is still in flight. When the write completes, the client calls the callback through the io_info on the writer's dead stack frame, and the test crashes with SIGSEGV on a NULL callback.

Zero-initialize every ceph_ll_io_info in the tests and set write explicitly in fsync_func(). The writer and fsync threads also share one condition variable, so notify_one() could wake the thread whose operation is still in flight and lose the other wakeup; use notify_all(), and reset the completion flags under the mutex.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73590

73729.title: osdc/Objecter: do not keep a stale crush_location after a change
73729.author: aainscow
73729.body:
The Objecter and the CephContext both observe `crush_location`. On a change, the Objecter copies the CephContext's parsed location, but the config proxy calls a change's observers in the order of their addresses, not the order they were added in. When the Objecter's observer runs first, it copies the previous location, so a client whose `crush_location` changes at run time stays one change behind and sends localized reads to the OSDs of its old location.

The Objecter now parses the option in its own observer before copying it. The new unit test runs the Objecter's observer before the CephContext's; it fails without the fix and passes with it. `unittest_splitop` now links `unit-main`, so the test has the global CephContext it needs.

Found by the librados zone split-read tests of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72643, which move their client between zones and failed in about 1 of 5 runs.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82994

73730.title: mon/OSDMonitor: let a repeer of an erasure coded PG change its acting set
73730.author: aainscow
73730.body:
A repeer maps an erasure coded PG to its primary, padded with holes to the pool size (since https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/66323, a3cc500a543). If the PG still has that pg_temp from an earlier repeer, a second repeer proposes the same pg_temp. That changes nothing, and it also replaces the primary's pending request to remove the pg_temp. The PG then waits forever for an acting set change.

When the repeer's pg_temp would match the current acting set, remove the pg_temp instead.

The new standalone test, TEST_repeer_twice_on_ec_pool, holds the pending map open and repeers twice in one epoch. It fails on main and passes with the fix:
- main: https://pulpito.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-11-09_09:23:11-rados:standalone-main-distro-default-smithi/
- fix: https://pulpito.ceph.com/aainscow-2026-11-09_10:55:43-rados:standalone-wip-aainscow-repeer-twice-261109-distro-default-smithi/

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82961

73731.title: ceph-volume: fix deadlock when a lot of debug logs are generated.
73731.author: redxef
73731.body:
When a process generates a lot of debug output stderr might fill up, blocking the called process from continuing and in the worst case generating no output on stdout, causing a deadlock.

Always call communicate to let it handle the IO and avoid the deadlock.

We encountered this when setting up debugging output for a unrelated issue on a cluster with encrypted OSDs. The OSDs failed to come up since the command to obtain the LUKS keys deadlocked.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82995

73732.title: client: accept Cap re-issue and drop stale CapReleases
73732.author: edwinzrodriguez
73732.body:
Under heavy trim, the client can queue a CapRelease, re-acquire the same inode Cap (e.g. via lookup) before the RELEASE is flushed, then keep the Cap locally while the MDS still honors the late RELEASE and issues a new cap_id at seq 1.  A later readdir Cap update hits add_update_cap's stale path (seq <= local seq) with a mismatched cap_id and aborts on ceph_assert(cap.cap_id == cap_id).

Only treat seq <= cap.seq as a delayed update when cap_id still matches; otherwise accept the MDS Cap re-issue.  On Cap (re)acquire, cancel any unflushed CapRelease items for that ino and complete the deferred pinned-icaps accounting so a RELEASE cannot race past re-issue.

73738.title: nvmeofgw: do not erase the current element inside a range-for
73738.author: evkuzin
73738.body:
`NVMeofGwMon::check_beacon_timeout()` erases the timed-out gateway's entry from `last_beacon` (a `std::map`) while iterating it with a range-based for. Erasing the element the loop is positioned at and then letting the loop increment is undefined behaviour. It runs on every beacon timeout, so on every NVMe-oF gateway failover. libstdc++ with `-D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` aborts on this shape with "attempt to increment a singular iterator"; release builds survive by luck because the freed node's links are usually still readable.

The fix iterates with an explicit iterator and advances with `it = last_beacon.erase(it)` on the timeout branch, the same idiom used elsewhere in `src/mon` (for example `MDSMonitor.cc`). Behaviour is otherwise unchanged. `process_gw_map_gw_down()` has no access to `last_beacon`, so the single pass remains valid.

Introduced by b49ac690d97 ("nvmeofgw: fast-failover changes"), shipped in v21.0.0 and backported to tentacle 20.2.1, so this needs backports to tentacle and umbrella.

Verification: no unit harness can construct `NVMeofGwMon` without a live monitor, so there is no new test. A standalone reproduction of both loop shapes over a `std::map` built with `-D_GLIBCXX_DEBUG` aborts on the old shape and completes on the new one.

A second instance of the same pattern exists in `NVMeofGwMap::check_all_gws_in_deleting_state()` (`src/mon/NVMeofGwMap.cc:209`), reached through `nvme-gw delete`; it will follow in a separate PR.

Introduced by b49ac690d97 ("nvmeofgw: fast-failover changes")

73740.title: test/librados: keep the cluster usable when creating an EC pool fails
73740.author: aainscow
73740.body:
`create_ec_pool()` and `create_ec_pool_pp()` work on a cluster handle that the caller owns and keeps using, but most of their error paths shut it down. After a failed `osd pool set <pool> allow_ec_optimizations true`, the error path also sends another mon command on the shut-down cluster. In C this uses the freed `RadosClient` and is followed by a second `rados_shutdown()`. That path's pool delete also looks the new pool up in a client osdmap that does not have it yet, so the pool is left behind. Whenever the set fails, the EC test binaries crash instead of reporting a failure.

The helpers leave the caller's cluster connected on every error path. `create_one_ec_pool()` shuts down the cluster it connected, as `create_one_ec_pool_pp()` does. The `allow_ec_optimizations` error path waits for the latest osdmap and removes the pool, profile and rule with `destroy_ec_pool()` or `destroy_ec_pool_pp()`.

Checked on one mon whose default EC profile cannot take EC optimizations, so the set always fails. Without the fix `ceph_test_rados_api_io_pp` segfaults, and valgrind shows `ceph_test_rados_api_aio` and `ceph_test_rados_api_watch_notify` using the freed `RadosClient`. With it all three fail cleanly with the monitor's error, valgrind reports 0 errors, and no test pools are left.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83011

73741.title: mon: answer a resent osd pool create once the pool exists
73741.author: aainscow
73741.body:
Stacked on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69112 (pool migration, at c5ced798ae1): only the last commit is new. It is the 82290 fix from https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73254, moved to its own PR so that each tracker has one. It can be taken into #69112.

https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82290 mon: with #69112, a create of a pool that is still pending answers "already exists" at once, so a client that resent its create can find no pool on its next command. 73744.title: mds: fetch only the wanted dentry when the cache has no room for the dirfrag
73744.author: xiubli
73744.body:
With mds_dir_prefetch (the default), a lookup that misses a dentry makes CDir::fetch() load the whole dirfrag, not only the wanted dentry. That pays off while the cache can keep the dirfrag until its other entries are looked up.

It stops paying off once the tree being walked is larger than the cache:

- The cache sits at its trim target, so each dirfrag loaded for one dentry pushes other entries out.
- Its own entries are trimmed again before most of them are used.
- Every lookup that misses then reads a whole dirfrag from the metadata pool and puts thousands of inodes through the cache.

In mdtest stat phases over 12M files, with 2 active MDS and a 16 GiB cache, each rank held about 5.3M inodes. Per rank, in 10 s:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────┐
│                                                 │         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────┤
│ lookups replied (mds.reply)                     │ 3,071   │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────┤
│ whole dirfrags fetched (mds.dir_fetch_complete) │ 275     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────┤
│ inodes trimmed (mds.inodes_expired)             │ 626,322 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┴─────────┘
```
That is about 300 lookups/s per rank, with the metadata pool read at about 34 MiB/s. The same test with 4.8M files, which fit in the cache, runs at 50–66k stat/s. Two heads of #72265 that are a week apart behave the same, and the code that does it is in main.

Fix (mds: fetch only the wanted dentry when the cache has no room for the dirfrag)

MDCache::cache_has_room_for(n) tells whether n more entries fit. It says no when:

- the cache is over its trim target, or
- trimming has lately dropped at least n entries (the decaying trim_counter). Trimming then keeps the cache just below its target, and a loaded dirfrag only pushes other entries out again. This is what happens in mdtest delete phases, where unlinks keep making a little room, or
- the dirfrag would take the cache over its target. An entry is taken to be as large as a cached entry on average. While the cache holds fewer entries than the dirfrag, that average says little, and the whole dirfrag is loaded only while the cache is less than half full.

On a lookup miss, CDir::fetch() loads only the wanted dentry (fetch_keys()) when the dirfrag does not fit. The number of entries comes from the dirfrag's fragstat, or from the directory's dirstat when a dirfrag that trimming closed comes back without its fnode.

Nothing changes while the cache has room. Readdir, and lookups with mds_dir_prefetch off, are not affected.

Test (qa/cephfs: test lookups that miss when the MDS cache is full)

TestDirPrefetchCacheFull in test_misc.py creates 1000 files in dir and drops them from the MDS cache:

- test_lookup_prefetches_dirfrag: with room in the cache, a lookup that misses loads the whole dirfrag.
- test_lookup_fetches_key_when_cache_full: with mds_cache_memory_limit at 8 MiB, filled by looking up 5000 files of another directory, lookups in dir load only their dentry (no complete fetch, one keyed fetch per lookup). Readdir still lists every file, and every file can be looked up.

Testing

qa on vstart:
```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────┐
│                                                                                                                                      │                     base                      │         this PR         │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────┤
│ TestDirPrefetchCacheFull

73748.title: cls/lock: use ceph::real_time and ceph::timespan instead of utime_t
73748.author: abrahamperz
73748.body:
Modernize cls_lock to use our `std::chrono` types instead of `utime_t`:

- `cls_lock_lock_op::duration` and the `cls_lock_client` interface (`lock()`, `Lock::set_duration()`) now take `ceph::timespan`
- `locker_info_t::expiration` is now a `ceph::real_time`
- the cls method computes and trims expirations with `ceph::real_clock`

These types encode the same way as `utime_t` (32-bit seconds + 32-bit nanoseconds), so the wire format of the ops and of the stored lock xattr doesn't change.

Callers in librados, libradosstriper, cephsqlite, librbd, rgw, the `rados` tool and the tests are converted. The `utime_t` overload of `Lock::set_duration()` is removed, so the compiler flags any caller that still passes a `utime_t`. Two spots keep printing through `utime_t` so their output doesn't change: `rados lock info` (a lock without expiration still prints `0.000000`), and the topic shard ownership stats in rgw_notify, which store a `utime_t`.

One small behavior fix falls out of this: `RGWSI_Cls::Lock::lock_exclusive()` built its `utime_t` as `utime_t(msec / 1000, msec % 1000)`, which treated the millisecond remainder as nanoseconds. It now passes the `timespan` through unchanged.

This is the follow-up to the discussion in #73596. That PR touches the same files, so whichever one merges second will need a rebase. I'm happy to rebase this one.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83005

Verification: I compiled every touched translation unit: cls_lock, cls_lock_client, librados, radosstriper, cephsqlite, librbd, rgw, the rados tool, and the cls_lock and librbd tests. I also ran `ceph_test_cls_lock` against a local vstart cluster (1 mon, 3 bluestore OSDs) and all 22 tests passed, including `TestLockDuration` and `TestRenew`, which exercise the expiration logic. 73750.title: rgw: report errors from bucket info before starting the response
73750.author: abrahamperz
73750.body:
`RGWBucketAdminOp::info()` called `flusher.start(0)` before it looked up the user, the account or the bucket stats. On the REST side, `RGWRESTFlusher::do_start()` sends the status line and headers right away, so when one of those lookups failed, `RGWRESTOp::send_response()` saw the flusher already started and could not report the error. The client got `200 OK` with an empty body.

The missing-bucket case is already covered: `RGWBucket::init()` fails before the flusher starts. A missing uid is not:

```
GET /admin/bucket?uid=nosuchuser&format=json
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Length: 0
```

This change starts the flusher in each branch only after the lookups that can fail have succeeded. That means after `bucket_stats()`, after `load_user()`, and after `load_account_by_id()`. The listing branches still start it before they begin streaming output. After the change, the same request returns `404` with an error body.

Also adds a `bucket-stats7` case to `qa/tasks/radosgw_admin_rest.py` for a non-existent uid.

Verified on a local vstart cluster (1 mon, 1 osd, 1 rgw). Before the change, `uid=nosuchuser` returned `200` with an empty body. After it, the same request returns `404`. Bucket listing by uid (with and without stats), stats for one bucket, the full bucket listing, and `bucket=nosuchbucket` (`404 NoSuchBucket`) behave as before. I didn't run the teuthology `radosgw_admin_rest` task locally.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/41355

73752.title: rgw: reject out-of-range epoch values in policy date conditions
73752.author: abrahamperz
73752.body:
`Condition::as_date()` turns a numeric policy date value (seconds since the epoch) into a `ceph::real_time` by casting the parsed `double` to `uint64_t`. For a negative, NaN, infinite or very large value that cast is undefined, and on x86-64 it yields a date far in the future. As a result, `{"DateLessThan": {"aws:CurrentTime": "-1"}}` (or `"-0.5"`) held as if the date were centuries away, so a statement meant to have expired still granted access.

This change range-checks the parsed number before the casts. A value that is not finite, is negative, or does not fit in a `ceph::real_time` (unsigned nanoseconds since the epoch) is now treated as unconvertible, the same way a malformed date string already is: the comparison skips it.

Testing: added `ConditionTest.DateEpochOutOfRange` to `unittest_rgw_iam_policy`. Without the fix it fails for all six out-of-range values (`-1`, `-0.5`, `nan` and `-inf` under `DateLessThan`; `inf` and `1e300` under `DateGreaterThan`). With the fix the whole suite passes (48 tests).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82411

73753.title: os/bluestore: re-bin a buffer moved between 2Q cache shards
73753.author: ming1
73753.body:
`TwoQBufferCacheShard::_move()` removes a buffer from the source shard, links it on the destination's list, and then adds its length back through `b->cache_age_bin`, which still points at the *source* shard's age bin. After a PG split the moved bytes stay counted in the source shard's age bins until the buffer is next touched, and until then the destination shard updates that counter under its own lock while the source shard updates it under another. `LruBufferCacheShard::_move()` already re-bins through `_add()`.

The fix points `cache_age_bin` at the destination's newest bin before the add. The second commit adds a gtest to `unittest_bluestore_types` that fails before the fix (source bins 4096, destination 0) and passes after.

Introduced by 56351838337 ("common/PriorityCache: Implement Cache Age Binning", v17.1.0).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82910

| after | 196.6 | 67.0 |

That is about 3 fewer allocations per op. I did not measure a CPU difference for these two commits alone; I expect it to be within noise. The measurement was made on ac9e87cc97e (main as of 2026-11-09, before fdfbeba70e3); the commits apply unchanged to current main, where I have not built them.
