73755.title: client: fix two deadlocks in the completion of a non-blocking read
73755.author: dvanders
73755.body:
Two deadlocks in the completion of a non-blocking read
(`ceph_ll_nonblocking_readv_writev()`), one commit each, then a test for
each.

A non-blocking read that goes to the OSDs is completed by
`C_Read_Sync_NonBlocking::finish()`. On a short read it re-verifies the file
size with `_getattr()`, which sends a getattr to the MDS and waits for the
reply when the client does not hold Fs (another client has the file open for
write). `finish()` runs in the Objecter's dispatch on a messenger worker
thread; if that worker also serves the MDS connection, the reply is never
read. The client hangs and the MDS evicts it.

Seen with Samba's vfs_ceph_new using async I/O
(`ceph_ll_nonblocking_readv_writev()`); backtrace in the tracker.

The fix runs the completion on a finisher. It is a new finisher, not
`objecter_finisher`: that one completes the client's own writes (ObjectCacher
writeback, and non-blocking writes through `C_Lock_Client_Finisher`), which
hold cap references. If the MDS has to revoke those caps to answer the
getattr, a read completion waiting on `objecter_finisher` would block the
write completions the revoke waits for. The cost is one more thread per
client and one thread hop per non-blocking sync read.

Alternatives not taken: hopping to the finisher only when the read is short
and Fs is not held (a second code path in a fix meant for three backports),
and making the size re-verification itself non-blocking (a larger change to
the client's request path).

The second commit puts the read's Fr cap reference when the OSD reply
arrives, before the completion is queued to the finisher. Otherwise an MDS
that must revoke Fr from this client before it answers the getattr (the
getattr's rdlock queued behind a truncate) waits for references that cannot
be put: the one of the read waiting in `_getattr()`, and those of the other
reads on the file whose completions are queued behind it on the finisher
(found by @xiubli in review; the first version of this commit covered only
the first). The blocking path in `_read()` likewise puts the reference
before its `_getattr()`. The owner of the read still puts the reference it
was created with, so `finish()` takes one back just before completing it;
no caps are waited for. The read always ends after the re-verification (see
the related tracker below); reading on would need `get_caps()`, which
belongs with the fix for the stale size, where it can be tested.

Shutdown: the new finisher is drained and stopped right after
`objecter_finisher`, before `objecter->shutdown()`. A read still in flight
then is in the same position as a non-blocking write completing through
`objecter_finisher` today. Checked by reading, not by a test.

Related, not fixed here: after the re-verify, `finish()` compares the
position with the size it read before the getattr, so it never reads on when
the file has grown (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83030).

The third commit adds a libcephfs test: one mount keeps a file open for
write, a second with `ms_async_op_threads = 1` does a non-blocking read past
the end of the file. The fourth adds one for the Fr reference: a short and a
full non-blocking read in flight on one file, their OSD replies delayed
(`ms_inject_delay_type = osd`), while the other mount sets the file's size.

Tested on main at 7f06b19a9c6 (Ubuntu 24.04, RelWithDebInfo, vstart with 1
mon, 1 OSD, 1 MDS, memstore):
- AsyncShortReadWithoutSizeCap (third commit) with the client code of
  7f06b19a9c6: fails 2 of 2 runs ("the non-blocking read did not complete"
  after 60 s). With the fixes: passes 10 of 10 runs.
- AsyncReadsWithSizeChange (fourth commit) with src/client/Client.cc of the
  first version of this PR (142b21a1036, the Fr reference dropped only
  around the getattr): fails 3 of 3 runs, neither read completes and the
  size change waits. With the fixes: passes 15 of 15 runs (about 3 s each,
  the injected delay).
- AsyncReadAndWriteMultiClient and ZeroSizeBufferAsyncReadFsync: pass.
- for the first test,

73761.title: mgr: hold the GIL when returning formatted Python objects
73761.author: lumir-sliva
73761.body:
## Summary
`get_daemon_health_metrics()`, `get_unlabeled_perf_schema_python()` and `get_perf_schema_python()` hand their result to Python without holding the GIL. A mgr built against debug CPython aborts as soon as the prometheus module collects, or on the influx self-test.

## Problem
All three functions hold a `without_gil_t` for their whole body and only take the GIL back around the Formatter calls. They then `return f.get()`, and `PyFormatter::get()` does `Py_INCREF` on the result while the GIL is still released. In the two perf schema getters the `PyFormatter` is declared after the `without_gil_t`, so `~PyFormatter()` also does its `Py_DECREF` without the GIL.

With `Py_REF_DEBUG` (debug CPython), `Py_INCREF` reads the current thread state, which is NULL here:

    Fatal Python error: _PyInterpreterState_GET: the function must be called with the GIL held, ... but the GIL is released (the current Python thread state is NULL)
     10: _Py_INCREF_IncRefTotal()
     11: (PyFormatter::get()+0x31)
     12: (ActivePyModules::get_daemon_health_metrics()+0x7f)

A release build gets away with it only because the dict isn't shared with another thread yet and its count never reaches zero in these functions.

## Fix
Take the GIL back before returning. `acquire_gil()` clears the saved thread state, so the `without_gil_t` destructor does nothing and the formatter is destroyed with the GIL held. No new lock ordering: the perf schema getters already take the GIL under `ActivePyModules::lock` to build the formatter.

## Test
vstart, MON=1 OSD=1; reproducer steps in the tracker.
- `ceph-mgr` built against debug CPython 3.12.3 in place of `mgr.x`: on main it aborts in `get_daemon_health_metrics()` when prometheus is enabled, and in `get_unlabeled_perf_schema_python()` on `ceph mgr self-test module influx`. With this change both run, and `/metrics` returns 132 samples.
- `qa/tasks/mgr/test_module_selftest.py` with a temporary check in `PyFormatter::get()` / `~PyFormatter()` that logs when the GIL isn't held: 60 violations on main, all in these three functions, 0 with this change. 14/16 pass both before and after; the 2 errors are known environment issues (vstart_runner's cluster log check, dashboard frontend not built).
- `unittest_mgr_pyformatter` 22/22, `unittest_mgr_pyutil` 7/7, `unittest_mgr_map_cache` 21/21.

The `get_daemon_health_metrics()` part fixes a regression from #71114, so its backports #72540 (tentacle) and #72539 (umbrella) need this as well.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83039

the checks for 1-, 2-, 4-, and 8-byte atomics only load the values. a load can link without libatomic even when an increment needs it.
use ++ to make the probe try an increment at each size, and initialize the values so the test can also be run.

the Debian patch fixed a riscv64 build of Ceph 16.2 this way. commit 4c726846e44884889bdf6f3e76f7dec574dd431e introduced a tagged-pointer probe for 16-byte atomics, and that already selects libatomic on riscv64 in current Ceph. so we don't have a known failure to fix here.

this should catch the same problem if another toolchain needs libatomic for the smaller operations.

Based on Debian patch 0013 by Eric Long.

73765.title: os/bluestore: track bluestore_throttle_trace_rate
73765.author: yulongshi0816
73765.body:
handle_conf_change() applies bluestore_throttle_trace_rate through BlueStoreThrottle::reset_throttle(), but the option was never added to get_tracked_keys(). So a runtime change does not reach BlueStore: the config shows the new value, and the OSD keeps sampling transactions at the rate it read at startup.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83042

73766.title: client: drop readdir_cache before freeing a cached dentry
73766.author: LiShengG
73766.body:
readdir_cache holds plain Dentry pointers, but unlink() can free a dentry that is still in it while the directory stays complete and ordered: trim_dentry() clears I_COMPLETE only for a dentry with an inode. A null dentry gets there e.g. when a rename overwrites a file that has other links and _try_to_trim_inode() nulls their dentries (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/69706). The next cached readdir then dereferences the freed dentry.

Clear I_COMPLETE in unlink() when the dentry is in readdir_cache, as the directory then no longer knows that name, and drop readdir_cache in clear_dir_complete_and_ordered() also when the directory is not complete yet, while a listing may still be filling it.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83036

73767.title: client: refresh readdir rstat in batches
73767.author: LiShengG
73767.body:
With client_dirsize_rbytes, readdir sends a GETATTR with CEPH_STAT_RSTAT for each subdirectory it returns from readdir_cache or from a kept readdir buffer, as rstat is not covered by caps: with readdir_r, a directory of 16 subdirectories costs 18 requests per listing.

Record in each inode which listing its last authoritative rstat was requested for (Inode::rstat_seq against dir_result_t::listing_seq, taken when a request is made; MClientQuota does not count), and refresh stale subdirectories through READDIR instead, whose reply covers a whole page: the same listing now costs 3 requests.

A listing that reads from the MDS anyway only loses the GETATTRs. A listing served from readdir_cache sends a READDIR only where at least one in 32 entries of the directory is a subdirectory (dirstat); below that, it keeps sending a GETATTR for each subdirectory.

Such a READDIR lists a complete directory from the start, which insert_readdir_results() checked with ceph_assert(); drop the cache when the reply does not match it instead.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83041

### MDS requests per listing

libcephfs `readdir_r`, one mount, directory of 20000 entries with S subdirectories (16 entries for S=16). vstart, 1 active MDS, debug client, localhost; main is 6fa99c01829. Counts are MDS `req_readdir` + `req_getattr`; hot times are the median of 5 passes.

**First listing (cold client cache)**

| S | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 1 + 18, 7 ms | 1 + 3, 2 ms |
| 200 | 16 + 203, 397 ms | 16 + 3, 288 ms |
| 1000 | 16 + 1003, 494 ms | 16 + 3, 239 ms |
| 5000 | 16 + 5001, 1969 ms | 16 + 3, 275 ms |
| 20000 | 16 + 19987, 8197 ms | 16 + 3, 274 ms |

**Relisting a complete directory (hot)**

| S | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 16 | 0 + 18, 4.4 ms | 1 + 2, 1.1 ms |
| 200 | 0 + 202, 113 ms | 0 + 202, 133 ms |
| 400 | 0 + 402, 194 ms | 0 + 402, 129 ms |
| 1000 | 0 + 1002, 227 ms | 16 + 2, 197 ms |
| 2000 | 0 + 2002, 443 ms | 16 + 2, 173 ms |
| 5000 | 0 + 5002, 1269 ms | 17 + 2, 210 ms |
| 20000 | 0 + 20002, 5235 ms | 23 + 2, 213 ms |

Cells are READDIR + GETATTR. With unmodified NFS-Ganesha V15.8 on top (`ls -f`, NFSv4.1, 5000 subdirectories) a listing goes from 50 + 23843 (8.2 s) to 50 + 2 (0.7 s).

### Where it helps

- **Cold listing**: the READDIR replies already carry the rstat, so the per-subdirectory GETATTRs go away at any density; no extra request.
- **Hot listing, at least 1 in 32 entries a subdirectory**: S serial GETATTRs become one READDIR pass.
- **Hot listing, sparser than that**: same requests as main (S=200 and S=400 above; the time difference there is noise). A READDIR page costs about as much as 32 GETATTRs here, and a real network only makes a GETATTR dearer.
- **No subdirectories**, or `client_dirsize_rbytes=false`: unchanged.

73768.title: common/StackStringStream: Move `destructed` out of Cache
73768.author: mkogan1
73768.body:
(reopen of @adamemerson 's PR https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/68705)

The thread local `Cache` contains a 'destructed' flag to warn users away from it. Accessing destructed objects is undefined behavior, and Clang has got aggressive about it.

To fix, replace `cache.destructed` with a thread local `cache_destructed`. Since bool is trivial it should last as long as the thread.
_Additionally, stackful coroutines may resume on a different thread. Mark the stream constructor and destructor [[gnu::noinline]] to prevent the compiler from retaining a thread-local cache address across a yield and accessing another thread’s cache after migration._

73769.title: umbrella: client: match the dump_subvolume_metrics_aggr command name
73769.author: anthonyeleven
73769.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82977

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73384
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82548

The client registers `dump_subvolume_metrics_aggr` with its admin socket, but `Client::CommandHook::call()` compares the command against `dump_subvolume_metrics`. The registered name never matches, so the command falls through to `ceph_abort_msg("bad command registered")` and aborts ceph-fuse or the libcephfs application. This came in with commit c376635d5d5 "client,mds: add support for subvolume level metrics".

The first commit compares against the registered name, which is the one that `help` lists.

The second commit adds `test_client_dump_subvolume_metrics_aggr` to `qa/tasks/cephfs/test_misc.py`. It runs the command against a ceph-fuse mount, checks that the output has `current_metrics` and `last_metrics`, and then checks that the mount still works. I have not run it in teuthology.

Both commits cherry-pick cleanly to umbrella with the same line counts. Tentacle and squid do not have the command. No open PR touches these lines.

73770.title: cephadm: wait for docker to remove the old container before a restart
73770.author: aainscow
73770.body:
With docker, a daemon's container runs as `docker run --rm -d` (since https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69146). `docker stop` returns once the container has stopped, and dockerd removes it afterwards; its name stays taken until that removal ends. On a restart, unit.run can start inside that window: its `docker rm -f` fails because a removal is already in progress, and `docker run` then fails with "Conflict. The container name ... is already in use".

cephadm bootstrap restarts the first monitor and fails when that restart loses the race. The window is wide with docker's containerd image store, the default for new docker 29 installs. In teuthology this fails many rados/cephadm jobs on Ubuntu gibba and smithi nodes (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81748, also reported as https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83018).

Make unit.run wait, for up to 30 seconds, until the old container is gone before it runs the new one.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/81748

73771.title: common: use 64-bit sizes on 32-bit hosts
73771.author: tchaikov
73771.body:
size_t can truncate BlueFS available space and neorados object offsets on 32-bit hosts. Use uint64_t through the BlueFS return path and for the neorados read and write offsets. Cast cephfs-mirror directory counts to the uint64_t type used by its service attributes.

This ports the relevant parts of Debian patch 0009. The snapshot timestamps already have explicit casts. The patch's change to `SimpleRADOSStriper::truncate(size_t)` would conflict with its current uint64_t declaration, so leave it out.

73772.title: Umbrella: mgr/dashboard: allow Fast EC pools as primary pool for RBD
73772.author: nmunet
73772.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83045
backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71651
parent tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79661

<hr/>

Fast EC pools (ec_optimizations enabled) now support OMAP, removing the historical blocker for using EC pools as the primary pool for RBD images and mirroring.


Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79661
(cherry picked from commit 9eb0c72b69889eb22700fc3a2ade00cd05dc941d)

73773.title: crimson/os/seastore: fix laddr_index_erase assert on retire of absent…
73773.author: amathuria
73773.body:
… extent

Cache::laddr_index_erase() unconditionally asserted that the retired extent was linked into laddr_index.
This is wrong for laddr-indexed types (COLL_BLOCK / ONODE_BLOCK_STAGED / LOG_NODE) that are retired by paddr while absent from Cache. In that case retire_absent_extent_addr() builds a placeholder via alloc_absent_extent(): it is initialized with the paddr only (laddr is never set), is never read through read_extent(), and is not a freshly committed node, so it is never inserted into the laddr_index. At commit, commit_retire_extent() -> laddr_index_erase() then trips the assert.

Make laddr_index_erase() idempotent and only unlink when the extent is actually linked.
laddr_index_replace() does not need the same change: it only runs for mutated extents (duplicate_for_write of a resident extent read via read_extent), where prev is always linked.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83046

73774.title: mgr/cephadm: don't redeploy nvmeof outside the staggered upgrade filters
73774.author: ShwetaBhosale1
73774.body:
The NON_CEPH_IMAGE_TYPES branch of _do_upgrade() reads the daemons to redeploy from the host cache, ignoring the --daemon-types/--services/--hosts filters. Now that nvmeof is a valid --daemon-types target, that redeploys every gateway in the cluster as soon as the ceph image daemons are done, before the user runs the nvmeof pass. Only reach into the cache for types no filter can name.

This PR depends on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71576

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83034

73775.title: cephadm: allow newer Jinja2 and MarkupSafe
73775.author: tchaikov
73775.body:
The upper bounds date from 2023, when cephadm still supported Python 3.6. Cephadm now requires Python 3.9. MarkupSafe 3.0 supports it, as does the current Jinja2 3.1 release. The MarkupSafe <2.2 bound now rejects a usable package, and neither cap records a known API break.

Remove the upper bounds from the regular pip and tox requirements. Keep the minimum versions and the separate Python 3.6 bounds. Build pip dependencies from source so the zipapp contains only Python code.

Based on Debian patch 0039 by Thomas Goirand.

73776.title: cephadm/build: use dpkg-query for Debian dependencies
73776.author: tchaikov
73776.body:
When Debian package support was added in 3ff9b0c, `build.py` asked apt-cache about each expected package. If that failed, dpkg -S tried to find the package that owned the Python module, to allow for a different Debian package name.

The three dependencies we bundle have known Debian names, and the build tests install those names. They do not exercise the fallback, which also searches for pyyaml* even though PyYAML installs yaml. Debian's reproducible-build tests lack apt-cache, so the precheck fails before it can inspect the installed packages.

Ask dpkg-query for the installed package and its version. Check the status too: `-W` also returns packages left in the config-files state.

73777.title: cmake/pybind: load Python ssl with Ceph's libcrypto
73777.author: tchaikov
73777.body:
ceph-mgr loads libcrypto before Python's ssl module. Comparing their OpenSSL version strings does not tell us whether that will work: different versions can load together, and matching versions can still fail. Preload Ceph's libcrypto in Python, then import ssl and create a context.

Skip the check with static OpenSSL and in cross builds, where a host Python process cannot reproduce the target's load order.

Based on Debian patch 0041 by Thomas Goirand.

73778.title: umbrella: mgr/cephadm: centralize service dependency calculation
73778.author: rkachach
73778.body:
backport tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/80709

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/71655

73779.title: messages/MOSDOpReply: optionally name the core owning the PG (v9)
73779.author: ronen-fr
73779.body:
A Crimson OSD runs each PG on one reactor core. A reply may now name that core, and the port on which it accepts client connections, so that a client can send the PG's later ops straight to it, instead of having them forwarded from the core that accepted its connection.

- osd_core_hint_t (osd_types): the core, and the port of its listener - on the IP of the OSD address the client already uses. Versioned, so that it may carry more later. Registered with ceph-dencoder.
- MOSDOpReply v9: an optional osd_core_hint_t (a presence flag, then the hint), appended after the trace. Every reply is encoded as v9; older decoders, the kernel client's included, stop before the hint.

Nothing sets or reads the hint yet.

Tests (unittest_osd_types): a hint's round trip; a reply without one; a hint sent whatever the peer's features; a v9 reply decoded as v8.

Co-authored-by: Mohit Agrawal <moagrawa@redhat.com>

73780.title: rbd: fail mirror pool peer remove for a nonexistent peer
73780.author: abrahamperz
73780.body:
`rbd mirror pool peer remove <pool> <uuid>` returned success even when no peer with that UUID existed, because removing a peer is idempotent in librbd (`Mirror::peer_site_remove()` ignores `-ENOENT` from `cls_rbd`). A typo or stale UUID therefore looked like a successful removal.

The rbd CLI now lists the pool's mirror peers first. If the UUID is not among them, it prints `rbd: mirror peer <uuid> does not exist` and exits with `ENOENT`. The librbd API keeps its idempotent behavior, so callers that rely on it (python bindings, mgr modules, retries in the rbd-mirror QA helpers) are unaffected.

`qa/workunits/rbd/cli_generic.sh` gets a `test_mirror_pool_peer_remove` case: removing an unknown UUID fails, removing the real peer succeeds and leaves no peers, and removing it a second time fails.

Verified by building `rbd` on top of current main and running the new workunit steps against a vstart cluster: the unknown-UUID removal now fails with ENOENT, and the existing peer is still removed normally.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/16986

73781.title: client: add ZeroCopyClient async bufferlist I/O with FSCrypt
73781.author: edwinzrodriguez
73781.body:
## Summary
- Add `ceph::ZeroCopyClient` and C ABI (`cephfs/ceph_buffer.h`, `ceph_ll_async_read` / `ceph_ll_async_write`) so callers (NFS-Ganesha) can move data as owned `bufferlist` pages without memcpy through iovecs.
- Filer → Objecter async path: `alloc_buffers` / `wrap_static` / `claim` / `claim_iov`, consume-at-submit writes (`CEPH_LL_WRITE_*`), read callback with owned bl, `aio_in_flight` accounting, and `cephfs-tool --zero-copy`.
- FSCrypt on the ZC path: plaintext-in/out ABI with RMW + encrypt on write and `prepare_data_read` / decrypt on read; per-op key validator; assemble claim_append/decrypt and Filer submit off `client_lock` under concurrent load.


## Test plan
- [ ] `unittest_zerocopy_client_buffer` / `unittest_zerocopy_io`
- [ ] `ceph_test_libcephfs` zerocopy + concurrent async I/O cases
- [ ] `ceph_test_libcephfs_fscrypt` aligned/unaligned ZC round-trips (`client_oc=false`)
- [ ] `cephfs-tool --zero-copy` alloc→write and async read smoke
- [ ] Confirm unmount / Fh lifetime (no leaked Fh refs)
- [ ] Ganesha-oriented stress (optional): ZC read BW + `client_lock` lockstat vs classic

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82299

73782.title: .helios: add CSC election voter list and Helios documentation
73782.author: batrick
73782.body: Add the Ceph Steering Committee (CSC) election voter list (`csc.csv`) and provide GitHub-flavored Markdown documentation (`README.md`) for voter authentication formats.

73783.title: mgr/smb: fix stored_cluster_ids ignoring alt_store
73783.author: avanthakkar
73783.body:
`stored_cluster_ids()` read the primary store inside the loop over alternate stores, so only the public store was checked when cleaning up removed clusters. A stale cluster namespace present only in the priv store was never removed.
This PR updates the loop to use alt_store instead to fix the issue. 

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83061

73784.title: rgw/metadata: keep the index generation of an existing bucket instance
73784.author: abrahamperz
73784.body:
`radosgw-admin metadata put bucket.instance:...` of a resharded bucket writes it back with index generation 0, so the bucket loses its index: listings and `bucket stats` show only objects written after the put, and in versioned buckets later overwrites can make GET/HEAD of a key return 404.

The JSON form of `RGWBucketInfo` carries `num_shards`, `bi_shard_hash_type` and `index_type`, but not `layout.current_index.gen` or the reshard target. `RGWBucketInstanceMetadataHandler::put_prepare()` already keeps the stored layout logs for an existing instance (fc7f5f96734), but not the current index, so a `metadata get`/`metadata put` round trip stored generation 0 and `put_post()` called `init_index()` for generation 0.

A local put to an existing instance now keeps the stored `current_index.gen`, `target_index` and `resharding` state. Puts from a remote zone are unchanged (they already keep the whole local layout), and the shard count, hash type and index type still come from the incoming JSON as before.

Testing: added `BucketInstanceMetadata.PreserveIndexGeneration` to `unittest_rgw_bucket_metadata`. It dumps a generation-2 bucket instance with a reshard in progress to JSON, decodes it the way `metadata put` does, and puts it back. Without the fix the test fails (stored generation 0, reshard target dropped, `init_index()` called for generation 0); with the fix it passes, along with the rest of the suite. I have not run the radosgw-admin reshard/get/put sequence from the tracker on a live cluster.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83035

73785.title: container: select the EPEL branch matching the base image's minor
73785.author: djgalloway
73785.body:
EPEL 10 is branched per RHEL minor. Rocky's epel-release resolves to the \`10z\` alias (newest RHEL minor). When RHEL 10.3 went GA on 2026-11-11, Fedora moved \`10z\` to 10.3 while the \`rockylinux:10\` image is still 10.2, so every rocky10 container build in ceph-dev-pipeline since then fails with:

```
nothing provides (python3.12dist(cryptography) < 50~~ with python3.12dist(cryptography) >= 49) needed by python3-pyOpenSSL-26.3.0-1.el10_3.noarch from epel
```

Rocky 10.2 ships cryptography 43; EPEL 10.3's pyOpenSSL needs 49. The same thing will happen on every future RHEL minor until Rocky catches up.

Rewrite the epel metalinks to `epel-$releasever_major.$releasever_minor`, which dnf derives from the installed rocky-release, so EPEL always matches the base image and moves with it when `rockylinux:10` becomes 10.3. CentOS Stream is untouched (no minor, `epel-10` already correct). Older minors remain resolvable through the archive mirrors.

Verified in a local `rockylinux:10` container: after the rewrite the epel repo resolves to `/epel/10.2/`, pyOpenSSL 25.0.0-1.el10_1 is offered and `dnf install python3-pyOpenSSL python3-cheroot` succeeds. The rewrite also handles Fedora's epel-release template (`${stream:+s}`), which is what ceph-build's builder container installs.

Related: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82884 (same mismatch on Sepia testnodes, fixed in ceph-cm-ansible #906).

73786.title: rgw: unify the two guard_reshard() retry loops
73786.author: abrahamperz
73786.body:
`RGWRados::guard_reshard()` and `RGWRados::Bucket::UpdateIndex::guard_reshard()` duplicated the same loop that retries a bucket index op while the bucket is being resharded (ENOENT retry, `block_while_resharding()`, retry reset after reshard completes, and the `InLogrecord` status check).

The only real difference was how each one gets its `BucketShard`:
- `UpdateIndex` reuses its cached shard (`get_bucket_shard()`) and invalidates it after ENOENT or a finished reshard.
- `RGWRados` reinitializes the shard from the bucket instance before every attempt.

This moves the loop into one `RGWRados::guard_reshard()` overload that takes `get_bs()` and `invalidate_bs()` callbacks. Both existing functions keep their signatures and call the new overload, so call sites don't change and each one keeps its current retry behavior and log levels. The local `NUM_RESHARD_RETRIES` macro becomes a `constexpr` in the shared loop.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/54260

Testing: built `radosgw`/`radosgw-admin` on top of current main and ran `qa/workunits/rgw/test_rgw_reshard.py` against a vstart cluster with `rgw reshard progress judge interval = 10` (as in `qa/suites/rgw/verify/overrides.yaml`). All cases pass, including the fault-injection, logrecord-recovery and unlinked-entries cases. The rgw log shows a write that went through the shared loop's blocking path ("resharding operation on bucket index detected" followed by "reshard completion identified").

73788.title: rgw: report x-amz-abort-date from the multipart upload's initiation time
73788.author: abrahamperz
73788.body:
When a bucket has an `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` lifecycle rule, CreateMultipartUpload returns an `x-amz-abort-date` counted from 1970-01-01 instead of from the upload's initiation time. For example, a rule with `DaysAfterInitiation` 1 gives `Sat, 03 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT` for every upload.

`RGWInitMultipart::send_response()` passes `RGWInitMultipart::mtime` to `rgw::lc::s3_multipart_abort_header()`. Before the zipper refactor, the meta object write filled `mtime` through `obj_op.meta.mtime = &mtime`. That write moved into `MultipartUpload::init()`, which records the time in the upload object, so the op's `mtime` was never set again and stayed at zero.

This change copies `upload->get_mtime()` into `mtime` after a successful `init()`. The rados and dbstore drivers set that time when they write the meta object. The lifecycle worker is not affected: it already uses the index entry mtime to decide when to abort.

Verified on a vstart cluster (1 mon, 1 OSD, 1 radosgw): I created a bucket with a 1-day `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` rule and sent CreateMultipartUpload at `Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:54 GMT`.

- Without the fix: `x-amz-abort-date: Sat, 03 Jan 1970 00:00:00 GMT`
- With the fix: `x-amz-abort-date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 00:00:00 GMT` (initiation time plus one day, rounded up to the next midnight UTC, as S3 does)

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82460

73789.title: cephadm/smb: don't log secrets during smb deploy
73789.author: avanthakkar
73789.body:
Several smb debug log lines wrote secrets to logs: 
- the cephadm binary logged external cluster keyrings
- mgr/cephadm logged the smb daemon keyring and TLS keys in generate_config
- mgr/smb logged whole resources during apply, including passwords, TLS keys, RGW and
cephx keys.
 
This PR masks or drops the secrets from those log lines and keeps them out of the sqlite db and the public spec backup. It also fixes `ceph smb show --password-filter hidden` for external cluster setups, which was not masking external cluster keys. Existing sqlite rows and spec backups are cleaned up the next time the cluster is updated.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83066

73790.title: mgr/MgrClient: cancel the pending report when stats_period goes to 0
73790.author: abrahamperz
73790.body:
`MgrClient::handle_mgr_configure()` did not cancel `report_callback` when the mgr set `stats_period` to 0. The pending report was still sent once. If the period went back to non-zero before that event fired, `_send_stats()` overwrote `report_callback` with a new event while the old one was still queued, and both kept rescheduling themselves. The daemon then sent two `MMgrReport`/`MPGStats` per period, and `reconnect()` could only cancel one of the two loops.

This change cancels the pending event when the period goes to 0, the same way `reconnect()` already does.

It also adds `unittest_mgr_mgrclient`, which feeds a `MgrClient` an `MMgrMap` and a sequence of `MMgrConfigure` messages, and counts the reports through the pgstats callback (the mgr address is unreachable, so the lossy session just drops them):

- `StopCancelsPendingReport`: period 1 → 0, then wait 1.5s. Without the fix a second report is sent (2 instead of 1).
- `RestartBeforeNextReportKeepsOneLoop`: period 1 → 0 → 1, then wait 2.5s. Without the fix there are 6 reports (two loops) instead of at most 4.

Both tests fail on current main and pass with the fix (3 runs in a row). The other `unittest_mgr_*` tests still pass.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83017

73791.title: mgr/rbd_support: skip pools without omap support in get_rbd_pools()
73791.author: abrahamperz
73791.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/54965

`get_rbd_pools()` returns every pool with the `rbd` application tag. The usual RBD setup pairs a replicated pool with an erasure coded data pool, and both carry the tag, but RBD images can't live in an EC pool without omap support, yet:

- the mirror snapshot and trash purge schedule handlers rescan it every minute, sending `rbd.namespace_list`/`rbd.mirror_image_status_list` calls to objects that can never exist there, and the task handler loads a task queue from it;
- `rbd trash purge schedule add --pool <ec-pool> ...` is accepted, then fails with `(95) Operation not supported` when the schedule is saved, while the schedule still shows up in `schedule ls` until the module restarts.

This skips pools that don't support omap, using the same test as `pg_pool_t::supports_omap()` and the dashboard's `isRBDCapablePool()`: replicated pools, plus EC pools that have `supports_omap` (FastEC). The perf handler matches I/O against the data pool since #67767, so it asks for the data-only pools with `include_data_pools=True` and `rbd perf image iostat` keeps reporting images whose data lives in an EC pool.

A schedule spec that names such a pool is now rejected up front with `<pool> is not an RBD pool`, as for any other pool that can't hold images.

#72719 also touches `get_rbd_pools()` (it switches the osd_map source), so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Testing

73794.title: mon, osd: require pool-migration clients by name, with one feature bit for pool migration and pools over zones
73794.author: aainscow
73794.body:
Stacked on https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/69112 (pool migration) and https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/72643 (pools over zones): the first commit after the merge of the two is this PR's. It gives the two features one connection feature bit, and lets an operator require clients that have it with `ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client`, as a feature rather than a release.

Tracker: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83075

## Summary

- **One feature bit for both.** Pool migration takes connection bit 54, incarnation 2 (`POOL_MIGRATION`), shared with `OSD_STRETCH_ZONES` of #72643, since the two ship in the same releases, backports included. A peer can follow a migration only if it sends that bit and `SERVER_OCTOPUS`; Luminous to Nautilus clients still send bit 54 with its old meaning. This replaces `SERVER_VAMPIRE` as the sign, which a backport to an earlier release cannot send.
- **`ceph osd set-require-min-compat-client pool_migration`** sets the `require_pool_migration` flag of the OSDMap after the same check of connected clients, MDSs and managers that a release gets (`--yes-i-really-mean-it` overrides). `ceph osd unset-require-min-compat-client pool_migration` clears it, except while a pool is being migrated. A flag changes no encoding, so it can be backported.
- **`ceph osd pool migrate` is refused** until the flag is set, and while any connected client, MDS or manager cannot follow a migration. The release gate on `require_min_compat_client vampire` goes.
- **While a migration runs,** the monitors and OSDs refuse new connections from clients that cannot follow it, and the OSDs fail such clients' ops to either pool with `EIO`. The flag alone turns no client away, as a release setting does not.
- **Two health checks** on each monitor's own sessions: `POOL_MIGRATION_INCOMPATIBLE_CLIENTS` (warning, while pool migration is enabled) and `POOL_MIGRATING_WITH_INCOMPATIBLE_CLIENTS` (error, while a pool is being migrated).
- **A finished migration no longer locks older clients out.** Found in upgrade testing: the renamed source pool stays a migration source until it is deleted, and #69112 required `SERVER_VAMPIRE` of every client while any pool migrated, so once a pool had been migrated no Umbrella client could connect. Now only a migration target requires anything, and it requires the feature set rather than a release marker.
- **Teuthology:** `qa/suites/upgrade/umbrella-x/pool-migration` (6 jobs) upgrades every daemon from Umbrella while the clients keep Umbrella packages, and checks each refusal and admission above around a real migration. Its last step would have caught the lock-out.

## The merge

The merge commit resolves #69112 against #72643: `pg_pool_t` keeps the migration fields at v34 (`SERVER_VAMPIRE`) and takes the zone fields at v35 (`OSD_STRETCH_ZONES`); `osd pool migrate` takes the same parameters as `osd pool create`, and a migration with no parameters gives the target the source pool's zones and replica too. It is here so the commits apply to both; it is not for review on its own.

## Testing

- Full build (gcc), no warnings in the changed files.
- Unit tests: `unittest_osdmap` (54, `PoolMigrationFeatures` also checks that no release marker is required and fails on the code before the last commit), `unittest_osd_monitor` (118), `unittest_osd_types` (109, zone encoding v35, migration v34), `unittest_pool_create_params` (129), `unittest_pool_defaults` (11), `unittest_features`, `unittest_mon_health_monitor`, `unittest_crush_wrapper`, `unittest_splitop`: all pass.
- `qa/standalone/mon/pool-migration-clients.sh` (new), 3 of 3 pass: a migration is refused until `set-require-min-compat-client pool_migration` is set; the command is refused while a connected client lacks the feature unless forced; `unset` is refused while a pool is being migrated; `ceph osd dump` shows `require_pool_migration`; connected clients that cannot follow a migration block `osd pool migrate` and raise `POOL_MIGRATION_INCOMPATIBLE_CLIENTS`, and r

73795.title: mgr/cephadm: don't deploy OSDs when db/wal devices select nothing
73795.author: FredNass
73795.body:
When an OSD spec defines `db_devices` or `wal_devices` but the filter selects no device on a host, cephadm deploys the OSDs anyway. They are created without the dedicated DB/WAL the spec asks for, collocated on the data devices, with no error, event or warning. If `block_db_size` is set, ceph-volume even carves a `block.db` LV on the data device (collocated LV split), which makes the issue harder to spot.

Common causes: a typo in a `model`/`vendor` filter, a `size` filter that doesn't match (ceph-volume reports base-1024 sizes labelled "TB"), a fast device that is unavailable or claimed by another spec, or a selector bug such as https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/72696.

This PR:

* adds `DriveSelection.unsatisfied_roles()`, which returns the dedicated roles (`db_devices`, `wal_devices`) defined in the spec but left empty while **new** data devices are selected. Data devices already backing an OSD (`ceph_device_lvm`) are not counted, so existing OSDs of a spec don't trigger the check. `journal_devices` is not checked, since it is never passed to ceph-volume.
* makes cephadm skip the host in that case, report it as a service event (ERROR) and a cephadm log warning, and record the apply so that the host is only re-evaluated once its inventory or the spec changes. Other hosts of the spec are not affected.
* reports the condition in `ceph orch apply --dry-run` as a preview note, without running ceph-volume.
* adds a new `allow_collocated_fallback` OSD spec option (default `false`), which restores the previous behaviour explicitly. The deployment is then reported as an INFO event.
* documents the behaviour and adds a PendingReleaseNotes entry, since this changes what happens with specs that relied on the silent fallback (e.g. a single spec covering hosts with and without SSDs).

Points open for review:
* the option name (`allow_collocated_fallback`);
* blocking by default vs. only reporting for one release before blocking.

A dedicated health check was intentionally left out of this PR; it can be discussed as a follow-up.

Tests: new unit tests in `python-common` (`test_disk_selector.py`, `test_drive_group.py`) and `cephadm/tests/test_cephadm.py` (apply blocked, fallback allowed, DB selected, dry-run preview). `python-common` tests and `cephadm` + `orchestrator` mgr tests pass locally. flake8 is clean; mypy reports no new errors.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83074

73796.title: mgr/cephadm: add 'ceph orch osd spec explain'
73796.author: FredNass
73796.body:
When an OSD spec doesn't create the expected OSDs, operators have no way to find out which criterion excluded which device: all the reasons are only logged at debug level in `DriveSelection.assign_devices()`, and with `filter_logic: AND` the evaluation stops at the first failing criterion. Operators end up editing and re-applying specs blindly.

This PR adds a read-only command that explains the device selection of OSD specs against the cached inventory, without running anything on the hosts:

```
ceph orch osd spec explain [<service_name>] [--host <hostname> ...] [--verbose] [--format ...]
ceph orch osd spec explain -i <osd_spec_file>     # before applying the spec
```

For each spec and host, it reports:
* whether cephadm can deploy OSDs on the host: placement, offline, maintenance, `_no_schedule` label, no inventory, inventory age;
* the devices selected for each role, with notes when `data_devices` selects nothing, when only existing OSDs are selected, or when `db_devices`/`wal_devices` selects nothing (see #73795);
* for each device and role, why it is not selected: **all** the failing filter criteria, with the expected value and the value seen in the inventory, or the obstacle when the filters match (unavailable with reject reasons, other spec, taken by an earlier role, being replaced, limit reached);
* hints for confusing mismatches: `size` compared to ceph-volume's base-1024 `human_readable_size` labelled "TB" (a 4 TB disk is seen as "3.64 TB"), case-sensitive `model`/`vendor`, `rotational` reported by the kernel.

```
osd.hdd_ssd_db
  host node1: eligible
    data_devices: 0 selected
    db_devices: 1 selected (/dev/sdc)
    NOTE: data_devices selects no device: no OSD will be created
    PATH      TYPE  SIZE     MODEL                 ROLE          SELECTED  REASON
    /dev/sdb  hdd   3.64 TB  ST4000NM0035          data_devices  no        size: '3.64 TB' (3.64e+12 B), expected >= 4TB (4e+12 B) [1]
                                                   db_devices    no        model: 'ST4000NM0035', expected contains 'MZ7L3'
    /dev/sdc  ssd   1.75 TB  SAMSUNG MZ7L31T9HBLT  data_devices  no        size: '1.75 TB' (1.75e+12 B), expected >= 4TB (4e+12 B)
                                                                           rotational: 0 (non-rotational), expected 1 (rotational) [2]
                                                   db_devices    yes       selected

[1] the size filter is compared to '3.64 TB', which ceph-volume computes in base 1024 (TiB, GiB) but labels TB, GB, while the filter uses base 1000 units. The device actually has 4000787030016 bytes and would match the filter in base 1000
[2] as reported by the kernel (/sys/block/<dev>/queue/rotational); RAID controllers and virtual disks may report it wrongly
```

Design notes:
* The selected / not selected outcome comes from the regular `DriveSelection`, and each criterion's result comes from the existing `Matcher.compare()`. The explanation therefore cannot diverge from what is actually deployed, and a test checks this.
* When a device doesn't match the filters of a role, the filter mismatch is reported as the reason and any other obstacle as a detail. Otherwise, every HDD would show up as "taken by data_devices" in the `db_devices` column.
* `SizeMatcher.compare()` is split so that the byte comparison can be reused; its behaviour is unchanged.
* The JSON/YAML output is meant to be reusable by the dashboard.
* Devices filtered out by `ceph-volume inventory --filter-for-batch` (partitioned or mounted devices) are not in the cephadm inventory and can't be reported; this is documented.

If #73795 is merged, the note about an empty `db_devices`/`wal_devices` will need a small follow-up to say that cephadm refuses to deploy unless `allow_collocated_fallback` is set.

Tests: new unit tests in `python-common` (`test_drive_selection_explain.py`, matchers and selection explanation), `cephadm/tests/test_cephadm.py` (explanation, host status, stored specs) and `orche

73797.title: qa/cephfs-mirror: fix em-dash in comment breaking yaml merge
73797.author: yuriw
73797.body:
A Unicode em-dash in a comment on this file (added in #70942) makes `teuthology-suite`'s yaml merge fail with:

73800.title: rgw: use current bucket attrs when retrying raced bucket writes
73800.author: abrahamperz
73800.body:
When `retry_raced_bucket_write()` loses a race (`-ECANCELED`), it reloads the bucket info and attrs and calls the write function again. Several callers built the attrs they write from `s->bucket_attrs`, which is the copy read when the request started, so the retry put stale values back for keys the request never meant to touch. For example, a PutBucketCors that raced with a PutBucketTagging restored the old tags.

This change makes those callers build the attrs from `s->bucket->get_attrs()` on every attempt, as RGWPutBucketTags and RGWPutBucketEncryption already do:

- RGWPutCORS, RGWPutBucketPublicAccessBlock and RGWPutBucketPolicy copy the current bucket attrs inside the retried function.
- RGWSetBucketVersioning no longer resets the bucket's attrs to `s->bucket_attrs` before `put_info()`.
- `put_swift_bucket_metadata()` starts each attempt from the request metadata and merges it with the current bucket attrs. Before, the attrs map was built once and reused, so a retry kept the stale values.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/51572

## Testing

I reproduced the race against a vstart cluster with a boto3 script. Each round sends PutBucketTagging (with a new value) and one of the other ops at the same time, then reads the tags back. Without this change, some rounds read the previous round's tag. With it, no tag update was lost:

| op racing with PutBucketTagging | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| PutBucketCors | 189/200 lost | 0/200 |
| PutPublicAccessBlock | 186/200 lost | 0/200 |
| PutBucketPolicy | 183/200 lost | 0/200 |
| PutBucketVersioning | 188/200 lost | 0/200 |

Each op still applies its own change, and Swift container metadata POST still adds and removes `X-Container-Meta-*` as before. I didn't run the Swift path under contention.

73801.title: crimson/osd: exclude absent PG mappings from placement counts
73801.author: yulongshi0816
73801.body:
`PGShardManager::start_pg_operation()` calls `get_or_create_pg_mapping()` for every PG op before it knows whether this OSD will hold the PG, so the PG->core mapping is created and the core's PG count is incremented up front. When the op is then dropped because the PG is not here (the create is canceled in `handle_pg_create_info()`, or `run_with_pg_maybe_wait()` discards it), neither is undone, and since the PG never existed, `remove_pg_mapping()` is never called for it. The count stays inflated until the OSD restarts, even after the pool is deleted, and new PGs are placed on cores by these counts.

A common trigger is creating a pool with size 3 and setting it to size 2 right away: a replica that gets the size 2 map before it handles the create from the primary leaves one such mapping per PG. On our 14-OSD cluster this added up to exactly the number of PGs in the cluster, real PGs per reactor ranged from 18 to 32, and the busiest reactor capped 4 KiB random writes.

This change keeps the mapping (so ops in flight still route to the same core, see https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/74084
), but:

- takes the PG out of the placement counts where such an op is dropped (`release_pg_count_if_absent()`), and counts it again when the PG is created on that core (`pg_created()` -> `claim_pg_count()`);
- does not decrement the counts again in `remove_pg_mapping()` for a released PG;
- after a new osdmap has reached every shard, removes the mappings of released PGs whose pool is gone;
- adds `num_mapped_pgs` and `num_uncounted_pgs` to `dump_store_shards`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83080

## Testing

14 crimson OSDs (SeaStore, 6 reactors each), crimson-osd built from eade23b6822 + #72916, with and without this change. To hit the race reliably, one OSD is paused with `kill -STOP` for 8 s (below the heartbeat grace) while a 256 PG pool is created with size 3 and set to size 2. Leaked mappings = sum of `num_pgs` in `dump_store_shards` minus the PGs whose acting set includes the OSD, summed over all OSDs:

| | without this PR | with this PR |
|---|---|---|
| run 1 (pause osd.13) | 256 | 0 (256 uncounted) |
| run 2 (pause osd.6) | 512 | 0 (256 uncounted) |
| after deleting the pools | 512 | 0 (0 uncounted, mappings removed) |
| 4 KiB random write IOPS | 109,514 | 111,046 |

The IOPS numbers show no obvious regression; they are not meant as a performance gain. With this PR, also checked (each twice): setting size back to 3 creates the PGs on the dropped replicas and counts them again; deleting the pool while the OSD is still paused leaves nothing behind. In every step, every OSD's PG counts matched its acting PGs, and no OSD restarted or crashed. On main, the affected files were compile-checked. Details and the reproduction steps are in the tracker.

73805.title: script/build-integration-branch: support resuming after merge conflicts
73805.author: rkachach
73805.body:
Until now, a PR that did not merge cleanly aborted the whole run (and, since `git pull` also exits with 1 on a merge conflict, could even be mistaken for a network error and retried forever). Building the branch again meant starting from scratch.

Split `git pull` into `git fetch` + `git merge` so fetch failures and merge conflicts are told apart. On a conflict the script now stops with the merge left in progress and prints how to carry on:

  ./src/script/build-integration-branch wip-yourname-testing
  git add <resolved-files>
  git merge --continue
  ./src/script/build-integration-branch wip-yourname-testing --continue

The initial run records the integration branch name, trailers and the PR list (including each PR's head sha) under $GIT_DIR. With --continue that state is reused instead of querying GitHub again: the branch is checked out if needed, PRs whose recorded head is already an ancestor of HEAD are skipped, and the remaining ones are merged. The same commits are merged as in the initial run even if a PR was updated in the meantime, and merge commit messages stay identical to what `git pull` produced. The state is removed once the branch is complete.

73807.title: mgr/cephadm: record OSD spec apply outcomes and add 'ceph orch osd spec status'
73807.author: FredNass
73807.body:
**Depends on #73796** (`ceph orch osd spec explain`), which this PR is based on. Until #73796 is merged, the commit list also shows its 5 commits. The commits specific to this PR are the last three:

* `mgr/orchestrator: add osd_apply status and 'orch osd spec status'`
* `mgr/cephadm: record the outcome of OSD spec applies per host`
* `doc/cephadm: document the outcome of OSD spec applies`

---

cephadm applies OSD specs in its serve loop, host by host, but keeps no record of what it decided or of what ceph-volume did. When OSDs are missing, nothing tells an operator whether a host was skipped, whether the spec selected no data device, whether ceph-volume failed or created nothing, or since when. `ceph orch osd spec explain` (#73796) answers "why", on demand and for the current inventory. This PR answers "what did cephadm do, and since when?", passively.

This PR:

* **records, per (OSD spec, host), the outcome of the last apply**, from `OSDService.create_from_spec()`:
  * the outcome: `deployed`, `up_to_date`, `nothing_selected` or `failed`. `failed` covers exceptions as well as ceph-volume not creating any OSD although new data devices were selected;
  * `since`, `last_attempt` and `inventory_refreshed`;
  * the number of selected devices per role;
  * the number of excluded devices per role and reason / failing criterion, from `explain_drive_selection()`;
  * when relevant: `osds_created`, `error`, `unsatisfied_roles`.

  The reports are persisted with the host, so that they survive mgr failovers, and the reports of removed specs are dropped. When the status is read, hosts that can't be scheduled (offline, maintenance, `_no_schedule`) are reported as `not_schedulable`, and hosts never evaluated as `pending`.
* **exposes the reports in `ceph orch ls osd --format yaml|json` as `status.osd_apply`.** The block counts all hosts but only lists the hosts that are not `up_to_date`, so that the output stays small on large clusters.
* **adds `ceph orch osd spec status [<service_name>] [--host ...] [--format ...]`**, a human-readable view of the same data:
  * it lists all hosts, most severe outcome first;
  * it flags the hosts that will be re-evaluated on the next pass;
  * it points to `explain` for the per-device details.
* **emits one service event per apply pass** listing the hosts whose outcome changed (e.g. `node1: deployed -> up_to_date`). The level is ERROR for `failed` and INFO otherwise.

```
$ ceph orch osd spec status osd.hdd_ssd_db
osd.hdd_ssd_db: 4 host(s) matched (1 failed, 1 nothing_selected, 1 deployed, 1 up_to_date)

HOST   OUTCOME           SINCE    LAST ATTEMPT  INVENTORY  DATA  DB  NEW  DETAIL
node6  failed            4h ago   4h ago        4h ago     3     1   3    ceph-volume lvm batch: 1 fast devices were passed, but none are available
node5  nothing_selected  34h ago  98m ago       103m ago   0     2   0    data_devices selects no device (size: 10 mismatches)
node4  deployed          6h ago   6h ago        6h ago     12    2   1    created osd.42
node1  up_to_date        5w ago   47h ago*      47h ago    12    2   0    -

73808.title: cmake: run gperf and protoc without waiting for libraries
73808.author: Doracly
73808.body:
With Ninja, a custom command waits for the dependencies of the target using its output. The gperf step for `rgw_iam_policy_keywords.frag.cc` thus waited for 52 targets, among them `libceph-common.so` and `librados.so`, and held back 352 compiles of `rgw_common` and the targets depending on it, although gperf needs none of them. The two nvmeof protoc steps likewise held back the 9 `ceph-nvmeof-monitor-client` compiles until `libmon.a`, `libclient.a` and others were built.

Each generator now has its own target without dependencies. A custom command shared by several targets only waits for their common dependencies, so gperf and protoc start right away. `add_dependencies()` lets Make run them early and keeps it from running gperf twice in parallel for `rgw_common` and `rgw_common_standalone`, both built by default.

Comparing `build.ninja` before and after: only the three generator commands lose dependencies; everything else only gains ordering on the new targets. `DEPENDS_EXPLICIT_ONLY` would also work, but needs CMake 3.27.

73814.title: msg/async: also replace standby connections on client restart
73814.author: tchaikov
73814.body:
A re-created monitor reuses its old address with a lower global_seq and a new client_cookie.  A peer that still holds the old connection in `STANDBY` rejects each new session as stale, and nothing reconnects over the standby, so the monitor keeps probing and never joins the quorum.

The restart detection from 1bd8e0c7ab2 skipped `STANDBY` connections on the assumption that the peer holding one would eventually reconnect itself.  That assumption fails for a monitor that was removed from the monmap: nothing connects to it.  Allow replacing `STANDBY` connections too, and keep excluding READY, where the peer may still be live.

The check is still a heuristic: a lower sequence with a different cookie does not prove a restart, since a delayed handshake from the same live peer looks the same.  The confusion needs two racing handshakes from one messenger, and a messenger keeps one connection per peer, so this rarely happens.  Even then, dropping a standby with an empty queue only costs its live owner one reconnect, which returns with a higher sequence.

Test this by recreating a client at the same address with a lower sequence.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83027

73816.title: crimson/os/seastore: abort on DPDK hugepage exhaustion
73816.author: Matan-B
73816.body:
Followup to https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/73142

With SPDK active every CachedExtent buffer comes from the DPDK hugepage heap, so the heap has to cover the extent cache of all shards rather than just in-flight I/O, and it runs out long before system memory does: 8 GiB sufficed for one shard and not for four.

When it does, spdk_dma_malloc() returns NULL and the std::bad_alloc thrown here escapes into a future nobody handles. Every dependent operation is left on a broken promise and the OSD wedges with no error reported anywhere. Abort naming the remedy instead, so the exhaustion is visible.

73818.title: mgr/cephadm: add HostCache.get_network_for_ip() helper
73818.author: abrahamperz
73818.body:
The ingress host filter (`has_interface_for_vip()` in `serve.py`) and keepalived config generation (`_get_valid_interface_and_ip()` in `services/ingress.py`) both looped over `HostCache.networks` to find the host subnet that contains a VIP. This PR moves that loop into `HostCache.get_network_for_ip(host, ip)`, which returns `(subnet, {iface: [ips]})` or `None`, and uses the helper at both call sites. Behaviour stays the same; the only addition is that the hostname is normalized, as other `HostCache` lookups already do.

Testing: added `test_get_network_for_ip` to `cephadm/tests/test_cephadm.py`. The full `cephadm/tests` suite (including the ingress and keepalived tests), flake8 and mypy all pass locally.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/62327

73819.title: crimson/osd: don't take create_or_wait_pg for ops that cannot create
73819.author: tchaikov
73819.body: An op waiting for a missing PG holds create_or_wait_pg, blocking other PGs on the same shard pipeline for as long as it waits.  Use a per-PG orderer for ops that cannot create a PG, and keep the shard-wide phase only for ops that can create one. Register the turn before completing the connection handle, so the shard-local path also releases get_pg_mapping before waiting for the PG.  Hold the turn until with_pg registers the op in its PG or object pipeline. This keeps a later lookup from overtaking an earlier waiter when a PG is published, while allowing other PGs to proceed.  The lookup path now releases the pipeline before calling with_pg, so ClientRequest no longer needs to release it before throttle admission.

73820.title: crimson/osd: do not report empty PG stats to the mgr
73820.author: ronen-fr
73820.body:
PeeringState::start_peering_interval() clears the PG's published stats. Until the PG publishes them again, PG::get_stats() returned a default-constructed pg_stat_t, and PerShardState::get_pg_stats() included it in the MPGStats report with reported_epoch raised to the current osdmap epoch. The mgr then accepted it as newer than the PG's last real stats, so for one stats period the PG showed as 'unknown' with no objects and with scrub stamps of 0, raising PG_NOT_SCRUBBED and PG_NOT_DEEP_SCRUBBED on a freshly created cluster.

Make PG::get_stats() return the optional stats and skip PGs that have none, as the classic OSD does in PG::with_pg_stats(). The mgr keeps the PG's last reported stats until the new ones arrive.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83087

73822.title: tentacle: rgw: timestamp-based olh epochs and decoupled olh op epochs
73822.author: fl189
73822.body:
backport trackers: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/73058 https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75997

---

backport of https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/62469 and https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pull/67661
parent trackers: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/68466 https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/75340

#67661 fixes a regression introduced by #62469 (see the discussion in #73185), so both are backported together.

All commits are cherry-picked with -x in the same order as on main, including the fixup!/squash! commits of #67661 as they were merged.

Conflicts, all outside the production code paths:
- src/test/rgw/rgw_multi/tests.py: tentacle imports the datetime module, so the new ObjVersion.mtime annotation uses datetime.datetime. The bucket delete tests keep their tentacle variants.
- src/cls/rgw/cls_rgw_ops.cc: tentacle still uses the pointer-list generate_test_instances(), so get_stales is set on the existing op.

Why tentacle needs this: with a versioned bucket in a multisite zonegroup, lifecycle noncurrent expiration on a secondary zone unlinks instances locally and increments the olh epoch there, and these unlinks are not logged, so the master never sees them. Once the secondary's olh epoch is above the epoch of the next write of the same key synced from the master, that write is not promoted to current on the secondary, which silently keeps the old version as current while sync reports no error. Lifecycle runs on every zone, so running it on a secondary is enough to hit this.

Testing (this branch applied with git am on tentacle 1520469d515, and v20.2.5 as the unpatched reference, two vstart zones a1/a2 on one host):

- [x] builds on tentacle (radosgw, radosgw-admin, cls_rgw, ceph_test_cls_rgw)
- [x] ceph_test_cls_rgw: 19 of 19 passed
- [x] src/test/rgw/rgw_multi with two zones: 12 of 12 passed, including test_versioned_lifecycle_deletes, test_timestamp_based_epochs, test_versioned_bucket_sync_disable_enable_object_delete and nine existing versioning and delete marker tests
- [x] reproduction of #68466: versioned bucket, lifecycle on a2 removes two noncurrent versions of a key, then a new version of that key is written on a1. On v20.2.5 a2 keeps the old version as current in two fresh runs (olh epoch 6 on a2 against epoch 5 of the new version). With this backport the current version matches on both zones. A single local unlink on a2 only brings the epochs level and does not show the issue on either build. Deleting versions on a2 with DeleteObject and a versionId does not show it either, because that delete is synced to the master and raises the epoch there as well.

73831.title: cls/otp: return the check result from the check op
73831.author: abrahamperz
73831.body:
`OTP::check()` sent the `otp_check` write and then a separate `otp_get_result` read to learn the outcome. Now that writes can return data, the `check` method encodes the result in its reply and the client sets `RETURNVEC` on the write, so an MFA check takes one OSD op.

- The reply (`cls_otp_check_otp_reply`) carries only the result and its timestamp, about 15 bytes. It does not echo the token, so it stays well under `osd_max_write_op_reply_len` (64 bytes by default) no matter how long the token is.
- The result comes from the same `otp_instance::find()` lookup that `get_result` uses, so the outcome is the same, including `OTP_CHECK_UNKNOWN` when the check was not recorded because there were too many attempts in the window.
- Mixed versions: when the reply is empty (an OSD running an older `cls_otp`), the client falls back to `get_result` as before. Older clients don't set `RETURNVEC`, so the OSD drops the new reply data and they keep reading `get_result`, which is unchanged. The unused `cls_otp_get_result_op` encoding in the client fallback is removed; `get_result` decodes the `cls_otp_check_otp_op` input, which is what the client already sent.

Testing: on a vstart cluster I ran `radosgw-admin mfa create`, then `mfa check` three times: once with a valid `oathtool --totp` PIN, once replaying the same PIN, and once with a wrong PIN.
- With this change: `ok`, then `EACCES` twice (results 1/2/2). The OSD log (`debug objclass = 20`) shows three `otp_check_op` calls and no `otp_get_result` call.
- With the OSD running the `cls_otp` from main and the new client: the same results, with one `otp_get_result` after each check, so the fallback works.

`ceph_test_cls_otp` (new, run by `qa/workunits/cls/test_cls_otp.sh` in the rgw verify suite) covers the check op: a valid pin, a replayed pin, a wrong pin, a missing id and the attempt limit, plus that the `RETURNVEC` reply matches `get_result` and that a write without `RETURNVEC` returns no data. All 12 cases pass on a vstart cluster (replicated and FastEC pools).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/49866

73836.title: common/mutex_debug: make the lockdep id atomic
73836.author: abrahamperz
73836.body:
`mutex_debugging_base::_will_lock()` updates the lockdep `id` before the mutex is acquired, while the thread that currently holds the mutex may be updating the same field in `_locked()` or `_will_unlock()`. With lockdep enabled, ThreadSanitizer flags this as a data race, for example on the `Finisher` lock during `ceph-mon --mkfs` from vstart.sh.

This change stores the id in a `std::atomic<int>`, matching the neighboring `nlock` and `locked_by` members.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/67582

How I verified it:
- Built `mutex_debug.cc` with `-DCEPH_DEBUG_MUTEX -fsanitize=thread` and ran a small driver that locks the same mutex from two threads, the way `Finisher` does. Before the change, TSAN reported the race between `_will_lock()` and `_locked()` on every run. After the change, it reports nothing.
- `test_mutex_debug.cc` passes (4/4), both with and without TSAN.

73837.author: bstillwell

When creating upmaps with 'ceph osd pg-upmap-items' there are a number of cases where it reports success, but some of the mappings would be trimmed.

Examples:
- the source OSD is not in the PG's CRUSH mapping
- the source OSD was already remapped by an earlier pair
- the target OSD is already in the PG
- the target OSD is marked out or has a CRUSH weight of 0
- the source and target OSDs are the same
- the resulting mapping violates the CRUSH rule

This change reports an error in those situations.

73838.title: test/mgr: Continued ceph-mgr Unit Test coverage: MgrClient
73838.author: stzuraski898
73838.body:
Add a standalone unittest_mgr_mgrclient target that exercises MgrClient's command, tell-command, manager-map, daemon-service registration and status, health-metric, and stats/report behavior through the public API.

Reaching the on-wire paths needs a session, which a test's real client messenger never gets because it never sees an available MgrMap, leaving those branches dark. Two seams in TestMgr.h open them up: a RecordingConnection that captures every message instead of sending it, and an MgrClientTestHelper that injects a session backed by that connection and exposes the protected map, timer, and report-callback internals. The tests then assert on what MgrClient actually emits over the configure, command/tell-send, and _send_stats/_send_report paths. Tests that spin up a second client messenger start() it so its worker threads tear down deterministically.

Three known MgrClient bugs are captured as DISABLED regression tests that assert the fixed behavior; re-enable each once its bug is fixed:
  - #83015: start_tell_command() checks `name` after std::move(name), so a tell for a non-active mgr is sent to the wrong target instead of being queued.
  - #83016: shutdown() drops pending commands without completing their on_finish callbacks. The active shutdown-drop tests pin the current behavior and reclaim the leaked contexts so the suite stays leak-clean.
  - #83017: _send_stats() does not cancel the previously scheduled report event, orphaning it in the timer across a stats_period toggle.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/77535

73839.title: rgw/keystone: renew a rejected admin token for EC2 credentials
73839.author: LIII-XXII
73839.body:
## Problem

`EC2Engine::get_from_keystone()` sends the cached Keystone admin token to `/v3/s3tokens`. Keystone answers `401` both when the request signature is wrong and when the admin token is invalid. RGW maps every `401` to `SignatureDoesNotMatch` and never drops the cached admin token, so after Keystone revokes it, **every** S3 request authenticated with EC2 credentials fails until the token expires (24 h with the Keystone default) or RGW restarts.

Because `EC2Engine::authenticate()` *rejects* on `-ERR_SIGNATURE_NO_MATCH`, the strategy stops there and the local engine is not tried: with the default `rgw_s3_auth_order` (`sts, external, local`), S3 also fails for **local RGW users**.

Keystone revokes all tokens of a user when its password is set. Kolla Ansible sets the password of every service user on each run (`update_keystone_service_user_passwords: true` by default), also when it did not change. So on Kolla deployments with `rgw_keystone_token_cache_size > 0`, each Kolla run breaks S3 for up to a day.

The Swift `TokenEngine` already handles this (https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/64094, #55236). The EC2 path was not covered.

Seen on Ceph 20.2.1 (Tentacle), Keystone 27.0.1 (2025.1), Kolla Ansible 2025.1:
- Kolla sets the `ceph_rgw` password: `PATCH /v3/users/<rgw admin user>` at 19:49:39
- Keystone logs from all three RGW hosts from 19:49:44: `Authorization failed. The request you have made requires authentication.`
- All S3 requests (Keystone EC2 credentials and local users) fail with `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch` for ~31 h, across several Kolla runs, until RGW is restarted. In an earlier occurrence S3 recovered without a restart exactly when the cached admin token expired.

## Change

For `s3tokens`, a `401` is ambiguous. Blindly invalidating the admin token on every `401` (as the Swift path does) would make each request with a wrong signature issue a new admin token, i.e. a password authentication on Keystone, for any unauthenticated client. Instead, when `s3tokens` returns `401` and the admin token came from the cache:

1. Ask Keystone whether it rejects the admin token: `GET /v3/auth/tokens` with the admin token as `X-Auth-Token` and `X-Subject-Token` (a token may always validate itself).
2. Only if Keystone answers `401` or `404`: drop the cached admin token and retry once with a new one.

Connection errors and other statuses keep the current behaviour. A request with a wrong signature costs one token validation and does not evict the admin token.

## Testing

- Not built locally; relying on `make check`.
- Reproduction (RGW with Keystone, `rgw_keystone_token_cache_size` > 0, `rgw_s3_auth_use_keystone = true`):
  1. `aws s3 ls` with EC2 credentials of a project → works (caches the admin token).
  2. `openstack user set --password <same password> <rgw_keystone_admin_user>` → Keystone revokes the admin token.
  3. `aws s3 ls` again. Before: `SignatureDoesNotMatch` until RGW restarts or the token expires; local users fail too. After: works; with `debug_rgw=20` the log shows `invalidating admin_token cache due to 401`.
  4. `aws s3 ls` with a wrong secret key → `SignatureDoesNotMatch`, and the log shows `admin token validation returned 200` (the admin token is kept).

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/79931

73840.title: osd/PeeringState: share rebuild-stats onset/pause, not just close
73840.author: sseshasa
73840.body:
`arm_rebuild_span()`, `pause_rebuild_span()`, and the vulnerability-window's open branch in `prepare_stats_for_publish()` marked info dirty for local persistence, but gave replicas no guarantee that onset/pause would be shared before a primary handover. A promoted peer that never received it latched a fresh onset of its own instead of inheriting the true one, losing real exposure/rebuild time across the handover. The close path already closed this exact gap via `rebuild_stats_close_unshared`. This is now renamed to `rebuild_stats_unshared` and set on open/pause too, so `Active::react(AdvMap)` retries `share_pg_info()` for any of these transitions, not just close.

Tests:
1. Adds following unit tests mirroring the existing close-side coverage:
 - VulnerabilityWindowOpenSharesWithReplicasOnAdvMap,
 - RebuildSpanOpenSharesWithReplicasOnAdvMap,
 - RebuildSpanPauseSharesWithReplicasOnAdvMap

2. A deterministic standalone test, `TEST_rebuild_perf_replica_history_shares_handover_after_open`, using a primary-affinity handover instead of a kill so it doesn't inherit the timing-dependence of the test that originally caught this race.

73842.title: osdc: return split read throttle budget before posting its completion
73842.author: vobruba-martin
73842.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83105

With `split_reads` enabled on a pool, a librbd client (e.g. rbd-nbd) can deadlock once `objecter_inflight_op_bytes` or `objecter_inflight_ops` is exhausted.

The throttle budget of a split read is taken for the parent op and was returned only from `_finish_op()` in the handler that `op_post_split_op_complete()` posts to `Objecter::service`. librbd submits every IO from threads of that same io_context (`neorados::RADOS::get_io_context()`), so all of them can block in `_throttle_op()` while the handlers that would return the budget wait in their queue.

The first commit returns the budget as soon as the last sub-read completes, before posting the completion. The second commit does the same for the `-EAGAIN` redrive, which takes the budget back with the non-blocking `Throttle::take()`. This may push the throttle past its limit, by at most the budget of the split reads being redriven. The commits are kept separate so that the second one can be discussed or dropped independently.

Introduced by 4c4b905c493 ("osdc: Extend op_post_submit to cope with successful Ops and move SplitOp decision point.").

## Testing

- New unit tests in `unittest_objecter_direct_reads` check that the budget is returned before the posted completion/redrive runs, and that the redriven op takes it back and returns it when it completes. Both fail without the fix.
- `unittest_objecter_direct_reads` (11/11) and `unittest_splitop` (26/26) pass.

73867.title: ceph-crash: skip an unfinished dump instead of stopping the scan
73867.author: bhouse-nexthop
73867.body:
Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83155

scrape_path() returns when it finds a crash dump with `meta` but no `done`. Every dump listed after it is skipped, and because an unfinished dump never gets its `done` file (the daemon died while writing it), it blocks them on every pass.

This changes the `return` to `continue`. The unfinished dump is still picked up later if `done` appears.

73868.title: rgw: reject an x-amz-copy-source that decodes to nothing
73868.author: mheler
73868.body:
RGWPutObj only handled x-amz-copy-source when the url-decoded value was non-empty. A bad escape like %ZZ or an empty header decodes to an empty string, so UploadPartCopy stored the request body (or an empty part) and returned 200.

Parse the copy source whenever the header is present, so these fail with 400 InvalidArgument like CopyObject does.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83150

73869.title: mgr/orchestrator: add --format to orch upgrade ls
73869.author: abrahamperz
73869.body:
`ceph orch upgrade ls` always printed indented JSON, while `ceph orch upgrade status` already accepted `--format`. This adds `--format` to `upgrade ls`, so the list of available versions can be printed as YAML (or compact/pretty JSON). Without `--format` the output is the same indented JSON as before, so existing scripts that parse it keep working.

The `format` argument of `upgrade status` is now typed as `Format` instead of a plain string, so the CLI validates it against the known formats instead of raising a `ValueError` on an unknown value.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/54000

Testing: added `test_orch_upgrade_ls` in `orchestrator/tests/test_orchestrator.py`, covering the default output, `--format yaml` and `--format json`. It fails on main and passes with this change. The orchestrator tests, `cephadm/tests/test_upgrade.py`, flake8 and mypy pass.

73870.title: .github: create GH Copilot Code Review Skill
73870.author: epuertat
73870.body:
## Summary

Introduces a Ceph-specific code review skill for GitHub Copilot, adapting general code review practices to Ceph's architecture, conventions, and real-world engineering experience.

The skill provides a structured review approach focused on correctness, maintainability, compatibility, testing, performance, and security. It encourages reviewers to prioritize meaningful defects over stylistic preferences and to consider the operational implications of changes across Ceph components.

### Sources and rationale

The skill builds on three complementary sources:

1. **General code review practices** — Adapted from [awesome-skills/code-review-skill](https://github.com/awesome-skills/code-review-skill), providing the foundational review methodology and structure.
2. **Ceph community review discussions** — Derived from an analysis of the most-commented Ceph PRs ([Ceph PR review history](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/pulls?q=is%3Apr+sort%3Acomments-desc)). The analysis covers review discussions and more than 50,000 PR comments, identifying recurring patterns around architectural decisions, correctness, compatibility, testing, performance, and collaborative review practices.
3. **Ceph security advisories** — Informed by the [Ceph repository security advisories](https://github.com/ceph/ceph/security/advisories) and their associated metadata and discussions. These informed a cross-cutting security review section and component-specific security considerations.
