73876.title: .github/workflows: check-license works on PRs with large diffs
73876.author: aainscow
73876.body:
`check-license` fails on every PR whose diff is over 20000 lines, because GitHub refuses `gh pr diff` for it (`HTTP 406: Sorry, the diff exceeded the maximum number of lines (20000)`). #72643 and #72644 fail it this way now.

This adds a step that reads the changed files from the pull request files API instead, as proposed in #72135. The new step also:

- Searches in full, at the PR head, a file whose `patch` the API leaves out because its diff is too large. On #72643 that is `src/mon/OSDMonitor.cc` and `doc/dev/osd_internals/erasure_coding/ec_stretch_cluster.rst`.
- Fails if listing the files, or reading one of them, fails, rather than passing without having read anything.
- Skips removed lines, so that deleting text that names the license (e.g. removing `src/common/crc32c_ppc.c`) does not fail the check.
- Writes the license name in two parts, so that the workflow file does not contain it and is checked like any other file.
- Gets the PR number, repo and head SHA from `env` rather than having them expanded into the script.

### Why the old step is disabled rather than removed

The check that runs on this PR is the one on main (`pull_request_target`), and it searches the whole diff, including removed lines and context. The license name is on two lines of the old step, so this PR leaves those lines as they were, and no change is within 3 lines of them: the old step only gets `if: false`. The diff therefore does not contain the license name in any of git's diff algorithms, and this PR passes the check on main without an override.

Once this is merged, a follow-up can delete the old step. The new check skips removed lines, so the follow-up will pass too; I checked that deleting the step leaves the license name only on removed lines.

### Testing

I ran the step's script locally against live PRs:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| #72643 (two files with no `patch`) | passes, reading exactly those two files at the head |
| An earlier version of this PR (the license name only on removed lines) | passes |
| #72135 (the license name on added lines) | fails: license found in PR changes |
| A PR number that does not exist | fails: could not list the files |
| A head SHA that does not exist | fails: could not read the file |
| #72643, searching for a string that is only in an unchanged part of `OSDMonitor.cc` | fails: found in `src/mon/OSDMonitor.cc` (the #72135 version passes this) |

The new step itself has not run on GitHub yet; it first runs on PRs after this is merged.

### Known limits

- 21 files on main already contain the license text (`debian/copyright`, `COPYING-GPL2`, ...). A PR that changes one of them too much for the API to return its patch will fail the check.
- The files API lists at most 3000 files per PR, so files beyond that are not checked.

73878.title: rgw: don't record successful ratelimit info requests as failed
73878.author: abrahamperz
73878.body:
`GET /admin/ratelimit` sends a correct 200 response for the user scope, and for the global scope when no global limit has been stored yet, but radosgw records both requests as failed. The user branch falls through to the final `op_ret = -EINVAL`, and the global branch accepts `-ENOENT` from `read_period_config()` as "nothing stored" but leaves it in `op_ret`. The `op status=` and `req done ... status=` log lines then show -22 or -2 next to `http_status=200`.

This returns after the user scope response, like the bucket scope already does, and clears `-ENOENT` in the global scope before sending the defaults.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82558

Testing: on a vstart cluster with one RGW and no realm, `GET /admin/ratelimit?ratelimit-scope=user` (for a user with and one without a stored limit) and `?global=true` were logged with status -22, -22 and -2 on main, all with HTTP 200. With this change all three are logged with status 0 and return the same JSON. A missing user still returns 404 and an unknown scope still returns 400.

73879.title: mgr/cephadm: filter daemons before copying them in list_daemons()
73879.author: abrahamperz
73879.body:
`list_daemons()` walked `get_daemons_with_volatile_status()`, which copies every cached daemon in the cluster, and only then dropped the ones on other hosts or with another type, id or service name. Listing one host's daemons (`ceph orch ps --hostname`) or one service's (the prometheus module does this on every scrape) therefore cost as much as listing the whole cluster.

`get_daemons_with_volatile_status()` now takes an optional host and an optional predicate, and skips non-matching daemons before copying them. `list_daemons()` passes its filters through. The filters only look at fields the copy does not change (type, id, service name), so the result is the same as before. Making the copy itself cheaper is handled separately in #73533.

Added `test_list_daemons_filters_before_copy`, which checks the result and that only the matching daemons are copied. The test fails without the fix (every daemon gets copied), and the whole `cephadm/tests` suite, flake8 and mypy for cephadm pass with it.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/82583

73881.title: rgw: don't let an append extend an atomic manifest
73881.author: mheler
73881.body:
A copy, rewrite, transition or restore of an appendable object writes an atomic manifest with its first chunk in the head, but keeps the append part number attr. The next append removes the head object's data and merges its part onto the atomic rule. GET then fails with 404 while the index still lists the object at its full size.

Drop the attr when the atomic writer completes, so these objects become normal objects, like synced ones already do. Copies made before this still carry the attr, so also refuse an append when the manifest's first rule starts at part 0, as an atomic manifest's does.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83163

73882.title: rgw/dedup: skip the parts of multipart uploads in progress
73882.author: mheler
73882.body:
Dedup ingress lists the bucket index shards directly, so it also sees the `_multipart_` entries of uploads that haven't completed. A part has the same etag and size as an object with the same data, and passes every other ingress check, so dedup can pick it as a source or a target.

CompleteMultipartUpload builds the object's manifest from the part manifests in the upload's omap, not from the part heads that dedup rewrites:
- **Part as dedup target:** its tails are freed, and the completed object points at the freed rados objects.
- **Part as dedup source:** the wildcard on its tails is owned by the part's tail tag. Neither complete nor abort ever puts that tag, so the tails leak.

Skip index entries in a namespace, and add a dedup test that leaves an upload in progress across a dedup run. The test checks that nothing is deduped, that the completed object reads back its data, and that nothing is left in the pool after gc.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/TBD

73883.title: crimson/osd: include seastar help before bootstrap
73883.author: zchaffee1
73883.body:
Because Seastar help commands were handled within the daemon, a child worker process was spawned, causing the command `crimson-osd --help-seastar` to fail. To prevent this, you had to pass `crimson_cpu_set` or `crimson_cpu_num` with a command such as `crimson-osd --no-mon-config --crimson-cpu-num 1 --help-seastar`.

To fix this behavior, the help command needs to be called before ever reaching the daemon or spawning a subprocess. Within the bootstrap, `help-seastar` and `help-loggers` are intercepted, and if either is detected, runs the help command and terminates. `crimson-osd --help` was updated to also include `help-seastar` and `help-loggers`.

Testing was done by building the code, which completed successfully. The output was diffed against `perf-crimson-msgr --help-seastar` resulting in identical outputs. It was also tested with the inclusion of additional arguments, such as `crimson-osd -i 0 --help-seastar`, which also succeeded.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/76355

73885.title: rgw/rados: set_attrs() moves a restored object's internal mtime
73885.author: mheler
73885.body:
After a permanent cloud restore, peer zones go by the restore time instead of the object's mtime, so the 1ns bump on later tag, ACL, retention or legal hold changes is too small and those changes never sync. This bumps the restore time by 1ns too.

A two-zone vstart showed the bug, where the peer got a new tag on a normal object but not on the restored one. 

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83164

73886.title: rgw: PostObj notification uses the written object's mtime and version
73886.author: mheler
73886.body:
An `s3:ObjectCreated:Post` notification reported `eventTime` 0.000000 and an empty `versionId` on a versioned bucket, while the uploaded object had both. `RGWPostObj` writes through its own object but published the event from `s->object`, which it never loads or writes. It now takes the mtime from the processor's `complete()`, like `RGWPutObj` does, and the version from the object it wrote.

`test_post_object_upload_amqp` only counted events, so it passed with the bug. It now uploads to a versioned bucket and checks the event's `versionId` and `eventTime` against `head_object()`.

Fixes: https://tracker.ceph.com/issues/83166

73887.title: ceph-volume: add lvm migrate-block-devices command
73887.author: kginonredhat
73887.body:
## Description

Adds a new `ceph-volume lvm migrate-block-devices` subcommand that converts partition-backed `block.db`/`block.wal` devices of a single hybrid bluestore OSD to LVM volumes, in-place: the OSD id and the data device are preserved and no rebalancing happens.

`ceph-volume lvm migrate` only moves BlueFS data between existing logical volumes; there is currently no supported path for operators running hybrids with db/wal on raw GPT partitions to move them to LVM without purging and recreating the OSD. This fills that gap for one OSD per invocation (batch flows remain external automation, as agreed in the tracker).

The in-place flow is:

* preflight: LVM-based unencrypted bluestore OSD, requested roles exist and are partitions, backup path exists/is writable/has enough space, OSD is registered, cluster is `HEALTH_OK` (bypassable with `--force-unhealthy`), and a layout rule is enforced on the disk being touched: LVM-backed db/wal devices must form a prefix in partition order, so a raw db/wal pair below an LVM-backed one (common after a single-OSD recreate) is rejected before anything destructive happens
* set `noout`/`norebalance`/`nobackfill` (default on, `--no-maintenance-flags` to disable; they are unset only after fsck succeeds and the OSD is up, and are left set with explicit unset instructions on failure)
* stop the OSD
* back up the partitions as raw images (dd, 4M blocks) plus a JSON metadata file recording devices, sizes and PARTUUIDs
* wipe each partition and create a ceph-tagged PV/VG/LV on it, with tag parity with what `lvm prepare` sets on db/wal volumes
* restore the bytes into the new LVs, trimmed to the LV size when LVM metadata makes the LV smaller than the partition (the fsck/startup gates catch the unlikely case where BlueFS had allocated the tail)
* update the data LV tags and the OSD directory symlinks
* run `ceph-bluestore-tool` fsck (shallow by default, `--fsck deep|none`)
* start the OSD again and wait for it to come up

Also supported: `--what db|wal|db,wal` subsets, `--dry-run` (preflight and plan only), and idempotency (a second run on a migrated OSD is a no-op that exits 0). The `recreate-osd` strategy is a documented stub that refuses to run until implemented. Encrypted OSDs are rejected for now.

The tracker carries a full design review (goals, non-goals, failure/rollback semantics, open questions) in the notes.
